"The Beast will come out with the ring of Sulaymān and the staff of Mūsā. It will brighten the face of the believer and will mark the nose of the disbeliever with the ring, so much so that the people at a dining table will gather and one will say, 'Here, O believer,' and another, 'Here, O disbeliever,' and it will be said, 'This one is a disbeliever and this one is a believer.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Muʿāwiyah, and he said: Shall I not give you good news? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Ṭalḥah is among those who have fulfilled their pledge." This hadith is gharīb; we do not know it from the narration of Muʿāwiyah except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We memorized it from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ,
who said: ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not die until women were made lawful for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no caller who calls to anything except that he will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection, bound to it, never leaving it, even if a man called only one other man."
Then he recited the saying of Allah:
"And halt them; they are to be questioned. What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No people go astray after having been upon guidance except that they are given to disputation."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse:
"They cited him to you only for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Lineage and status lie in wealth, and nobility lies in piety."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is the brother of Ḥazm ibn Abī Ḥazm al-Quṭaʿī, from Thābit,
from Anas ibn Mālik,

from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said about this verse, "He is worthy of being feared and worthy to forgive": Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: I am worthy of being feared, so whoever fears Me and does not set up another god with Me, I am worthy to forgive him. Abū ʿĪsā said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb, and Suhayl is not strong in hadith; he alone narrated this hadith from Thābit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: You will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised."
A woman said: Will we see, or will some of us see, the private parts of others? He said: "O so-and-so,
'Each person among them on that Day will have a matter that occupies him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed:

"Then, on that Day, you will surely be asked about the pleasures," the people said: O Messenger of Allah, about which pleasures will we be asked, when they are only the two black things [dates and water], the enemy is present, and our swords are on our shoulders? He said:
"That will come to be."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise whose two banks are of gold, flowing over pearls and rubies. Its soil is sweeter-smelling than musk, its water is sweeter than honey and whiter than snow."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nothing is more honored by Allah, the Exalted, than supplication."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, that a man
said: O Messenger of Allah, the laws of Islam have become many for me, so tell me of something I can hold fast to. He said:
"Let your tongue never cease to be moist with the remembrance of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ said:

"Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the most pleasing to your Sovereign, the highest in your ranks, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better than meeting your enemy so that you strike their necks and they strike your necks?"
They said: What is that, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "The remembrance of Allah."
Muʿādh ibn Jabal said: A person has done no deed that saves him more from the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than the remembrance of Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best remembrance is 'There is no god but Allah,' and the best supplication is 'Praise be to Allah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are words to be said after prayer whose sayer is never disappointed: glorifying Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, praising Him thirty-three times, and declaring His greatness thirty-four times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us on the day of Badr:
"When they close in on you" meaning, when they are many against you "shoot them, and conserve your arrows."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Abyssinians were playing with their spears in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, ʿUmar entered,
and he reached down for some pebbles and threw them at them. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Leave them, ʿUmar."
ʿAlī added: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us: Maʿmar informed us: [this took place] in the mosque.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We visited Abū Umāmah, and he saw some silver ornamentation on our swords, and he became angry and said: "Lands were conquered by people whose sword ornaments were not of gold and silver, but of tin, iron, and leather straps."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went on a campaign with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ toward Najd, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ caught up with us in a valley full of thorny trees. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped beneath a tree and hung his sword from one of its branches. He said: The people scattered through the valley, seeking shade beneath the trees. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A man came to me while I was asleep and took the sword. I woke up with him standing over my head, and I only noticed the sword drawn in his hand. He said to me: 'Who will protect you from me?' I said: 'Allah.'
Then he said a second time: 'Who will protect you from me?' I said: 'Allah.'
He then sheathed the sword, and there he is, sitting."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not punish him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Jews will fight you, and you will be given power over them, until the stone says: 'O Muslim, there is a Jew behind me, so kill him.'"
He said: This hadith is good and sound.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Death be upon you."
ʿĀʾishah said: I understood it, so I said: "And upon you be death and the curse."
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Gently, ʿĀʾishah,
Allah loves gentleness in all matters."
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, did you not hear what they said?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I said: 'And upon you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Ṭufayl ibn ʿAmr al-Dawsī and his companions came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah,
Daws has disobeyed and refused,
so invoke Allah against them."
It was said: "Daws is destroyed." He said:
"O Allah, guide Daws and bring them [to Islam]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought a people, he would not attack until morning,
and if he heard the call to prayer, he would hold back,
and if he did not hear the call to prayer, he would attack after morning came.
We reached Khaybar at night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was rare for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to set out on a journey except on a Thursday.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of al-Ḥarrah, when the people were pledging allegiance to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥanẓalah, Ibn Zayd said: "On what is Ibn Ḥanẓalah taking the people's pledge?" He was told: "On death."
He said: "I will not pledge allegiance on that to anyone after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He had been present with him at al-Ḥudaybiyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī had stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ at Khaybar, as he had an eye ailment. He said: "Shall I stay behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" So ʿAlī set out and joined the Prophet ﷺ.
On the evening of the night at whose morning Allah granted the conquest,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I will give the banner" or "Tomorrow the banner will be taken by" "a man whom Allah and His Messenger love" or he said "who loves Allah and His Messenger; Allah will grant victory at his hands."
Then suddenly there was ʿAlī, whom we had not expected.
They said: "This is ʿAlī."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave it to him, and Allah granted victory at his hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Prophet ﷺ, we used to take the meat of sacrificial animals as provision to Medina,
and on more than one occasion he said: the meat of the sacrificial offerings.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It reached him from al-Qāsim, from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no vow in disobedience [to Allah]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the people of Basra, who said: I accompanied ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"Vows are of two kinds. A vow made in obedience to Allah is for Allah, and it must be fulfilled. A vow made in disobedience to Allah is for Satan, and it is not to be fulfilled; its expiation is what expiates an oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Women and perfume were made beloved to me from this world, and the coolness of my eyes was placed in prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Umm Salamah, do not trouble me concerning ʿĀʾishah, for by Allah, revelation has not come to me while I was in the bedcover of any woman among you except her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ from Allah while I was with him. I got up and closed the door between him and me. When it had lifted from him, he said to me:
"O ʿĀʾishah, Gabriel conveys greetings of peace to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She, meaning [one of his wives], brought food in a bowl of hers to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions. Then ʿĀʾishah came wrapped in a cloak, carrying a stone pestle, and she broke the bowl with it. The Prophet ﷺ put the two halves of the bowl together and said:
"Eat. Your mother was jealous."
[He said it] twice. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took ʿĀʾishah's bowl and sent it to Umm Salamah, and gave Umm Salamah's bowl to ʿĀʾishah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw a woman who prepared food like Ṣafiyyah. She sent the Prophet ﷺ a vessel with food in it, and I could not restrain myself from breaking it. So I asked the Prophet ﷺ about its expiation, and he said:
"A vessel for a vessel, and food for food."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a slave woman with whom he had relations. ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah kept at him until he forbade her to himself. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?} to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I looked for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and put my hand into his hair. He said:
"Your devil has come to you."
I said: Do you not have a devil? He said:
"Yes, but Allah helped me against him, and so he submitted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I missed him one night, and she related the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to us while we were in a tent in the mosque of Medina, and he said in it:
"It has been revealed to me that I should fight the people until they say: There is no god but Allah." Similar to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: His father Aws said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah. Then their blood and their property are protected, except by its right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Every sin, Allah may forgive, except for a man who deliberately kills a believer, or a man who dies as a disbeliever."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, the killing of a believer is greater in the sight of Allah than the disappearance of the world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man will come holding the hand of another man and say: My Lord, this man killed me.
Allah will say to him: Why did you kill him? He will say: I killed him so that might would belong to You.
Allah will say: Indeed, it is Mine.
Another man will come holding the hand of another man and say: This man killed me.
Allah will say to him: Why did you kill him? He will say: So that might would belong to so-and-so. Allah will say: It does not belong to so-and-so. So he will bear his sin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On the Day of Resurrection the slain man will come with his killer and say: Ask this one why he killed me. He will say: I killed him for the sovereignty of so-and-so."
Jundab said: So beware of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever comes worshipping Allah, not associating anything with Him, establishing prayer, giving zakāh, and avoiding the major sins, will have Paradise."
They asked him about the major sins, and he said:
"Associating partners with Allah, killing a Muslim soul, and fleeing on the day of battle."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, what are the major sins?" He said:
"They are seven. The greatest of them are associating partners with Allah, killing a soul without right, and fleeing on the day of battle." Abridged.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whatever man comes forth to split my nation, strike his neck."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: and the verse of those who wage war was revealed concerning them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this chain of transmission.
And he added: Shuʿbah said, "I asked Qatādah, 'Did you hear it from Anas?' He said, 'Yes, we asked him about it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he saw the Prophet ﷺ raise his hands when he entered the prayer and said the takbīr—Hammām described it as level with his ears—then he wrapped himself in his garment, then placed his right hand over his left. When he wanted to bow, he took his hands out of the garment, then raised them, then said the takbīr and bowed. And when he said:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him,"
he raised his hands. And when he prostrated, he prostrated between his palms.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah met me and said, "Shall I not give you a gift? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us, and we said, 'We already know how to greet you with peace, but how should we send blessings upon you?' He said:

'Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrāhīm; You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrāhīm; You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us, saying:
"Do not get ahead of the imam. When he says the takbīr, then say the takbīr; and when he says, 'wa lā ḍ-ḍāllīn,' then say, 'Āmīn.'
When he bows, then bow; and when he says, 'Allah hears whoever praises Him,'
then say, 'O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The imam is only a shield. So if he prays sitting, then pray sitting; and when he says, 'Allah hears whoever praises Him,'
then say, 'O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise.'
For whoever's words coincide with the words of the inhabitants of the heavens, his previous sins will be forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
they said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transfer of chain.) And Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated to us,
and Ḥarmalah ibn Yaḥyā,
both said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab informed me,
and Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that they both heard Abū Hurayrah
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Saying 'Subḥān Allāh' is for men, and clapping is for women."
Ḥarmalah added in his narration: Ibn Shihāb said, "I have seen men of knowledge say 'Subḥān Allāh' and gesture."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said:
"Why do I see you raising your hands as if they were the tails of unruly horses? Be still in prayer."
He said: Then he came out to us again and saw us in circles, and said:
"Why do I see you in scattered groups?"
He said: Then he came out to us again and said:
"Will you not form rows as the angels form rows before their Lord?"
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, how do the angels form rows before their Lord?" He said:
"They complete the first rows and stand closely together in the row."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them that he said:
"Straighten the row in prayer, for straightening the row is part of the excellence of prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw some people at the back of the mosque. Then he mentioned something similar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Do not prevent your women from the mosques when they ask your permission to go to them."
He said: Bilāl ibn ʿAbd Allāh said, "By Allah, we will prevent them."

He said: ʿAbd Allāh turned to him and rebuked him harshly, such as I had never heard him rebuke anyone, and said, "I tell you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and you say, 'By Allah, we will prevent them'?"
label: machine translation

He did not mention what comes after it.

label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Kūfah

complained about Saʿd to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and they criticized his prayer. So ʿUmar sent for him and he came to him. ʿUmar mentioned to him what they had found fault with regarding the prayer, and he said, "I lead them in the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, not falling short of it. I prolong the first two rakʿahs for them and shorten the last two."
He said, "That is what I expected of you, Abū Isḥāq."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said to Saʿd, "They have complained about you in everything, even in prayer."
He said, "As for me, I prolong the first two rakʿahs and shorten the last two, and I do not fall short in following the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said, "That is what I expected of you."
Or, "That was my opinion of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He heard the Prophet ﷺ recite in the Fajr prayer: {By the night as it departs}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was beating a slave of mine when I heard a voice behind me say, "
Know, Abū Masʿūd."
Ibn al-Muthannā said [that he said it] twice: "
Allah has more power over you than you have over him."
I turned around, and it was the Prophet ﷺ. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, he is free for the sake of Allah." He said, "
Had you not done so, the Fire would have scorched you," or he said, "the Fire would have touched you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: the qasāmah (oath procedure) existed in the Jāhiliyyah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ confirmed it as it had been in the Jāhiliyyah, and he gave judgment by it among some people of the Anṣār regarding a slain man whose death they claimed was caused by the Jews of Khaybar. Maʿmar differed from the two of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Eight men of ʿUkl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he mentioned something similar up to the words "he did not cauterize them," and he said, "They killed the shepherd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a man came leading another with a leather strap, and he said, "O Messenger of Allah, this man killed my brother."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Did you kill him?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, had he not confessed, I would have established the proof against him."
He said, "Yes, I killed him." He said, "How did you kill him?"
He said, "He and I were gathering firewood from a tree, and he insulted me and made me angry, so I struck him on the side of his head with an axe."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "
Do you have any property with which you can pay for yourself?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have nothing but my axe and my cloak."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "
Do you think your people would buy you [i.e. ransom you]?"
He said, "I am of less worth to my people than that."
So he threw the leather strap to the man and said, "Take your man."
When he turned away, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
If he kills him, he will be like him."
The people caught up with the man and said, "Woe to you! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
'If he kills him, he will be like him.'"
So he returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I was told that you said,
'If he kills him, he will be like him.'
Yet I only took him by your command." He said, "
Do you not want him to bear your sin and the sin of your companion?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Then that is so."
He said: That was how it was.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman struck her co-wife with a tent pole while she was pregnant and killed her. He said: One of them was from Laḥyān. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the blood money of the slain woman payable by the male relatives of the killer, and a ghurrah [a slave] for what was in her womb.
A man from the killer's male relatives said, "Shall we pay blood money for one who neither ate nor drank nor cried out [at birth]? Such a case is to be voided."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Is this rhymed speech like the rhymed speech of the Bedouins?"
He said: And he made the blood money binding upon them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
from Banū Makhzūm stole, and she was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. She sought refuge with Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "
By Allah, if it were Fāṭimah, I would cut off her hand." So her hand was cut off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Māʿiz ibn Mālik when he was brought to the Prophet ﷺ: a short, stocky man without a cloak. He testified against himself four times that he had committed adultery.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Perhaps you only kissed her."
He said, "No, by Allah, he has committed adultery," meaning the other one.
He said: So he had him stoned. Then he delivered a sermon and said, "

Whenever we go out in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, one of them stays behind, bleating like the bleating of a male goat, giving one of the women a small gift of milk. If Allah gives me power over any of them, I will certainly make an example of him to deter them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī delivered a sermon and said, "O people, carry out the legal punishments on your slaves, whether married or unmarried. A slave woman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ committed adultery, and he commanded me to flog her, but she had only recently given birth, so I feared that if I flogged her I would kill her," or he said, "that she would die. So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said, 'You did well.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: a man who had drunk wine was brought to him, and he struck him with two palm branches, about forty [strokes]. Abū Bakr did the same. When ʿUmar became [caliph], he consulted the people, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said, "[Make it] like the lightest of the legal punishments: eighty."
So ʿUmar ordered it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Syria there was a man who was known as Abū Muḥammad, and he used to say that the Witr prayer is obligatory.

Al-Mukhdajī said: I went to ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit and met him as he was going to the mosque, and I told him what Abū Muḥammad had said. ʿUbādah said: Abū Muḥammad has lied. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"Allah has made five prayers obligatory upon His servants. Whoever performs them, not neglecting any part of them out of disregard for their right, will have a covenant with Allah that He will admit him to Paradise. And whoever does not perform them will have no covenant with Allah: if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will admit him to Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not come until people boast to one another about mosques."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that mosques be built in the neighborhoods, and that they be kept clean and perfumed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"The muʿadhdhin will be forgiven as far as his voice reaches, and everything moist and dry will ask forgiveness for him. And whoever attends the prayer will have twenty-five good deeds recorded for him, and what is between the prayers will be expiated for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Give glad tidings to those who walk to the mosques in the darkness of the perfect light on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"Allah does not accept the prayer of a woman who has reached puberty except with a head covering."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ziyād ibn Abī al-Jaʿd took me by the hand while we were in ar-Raqqah, and he stood me before an old man called Wābiṣah ibn Maʿbad of Banū Asad. Ziyād said: This old man told me that a man prayed alone behind the row, while the old man was listening, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him to repeat the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was among ten of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, among them Abū Qatādah. Abū Ḥumayd said: I am the most knowledgeable among you of the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
They said: How so? By Allah, you were not more constant than us in following him, nor earlier than us in accompanying him. He said: Yes. They said: Then present it.

He said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for prayer, he would raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders, then say the takbīr until every bone settled in its place, upright. Then he would recite. Then he would say the takbīr and raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders, then bow and place his palms on his knees, then straighten, neither lowering his head nor raising it. Then he would raise his head and say:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him."
Then he would raise his hands until they were level with his shoulders, standing upright, and say: "Allah is the Greatest."

Then he would go down to the ground and keep his arms apart from his sides. Then he would raise his head, fold his left foot and sit on it, and when he prostrated he would spread the toes of his feet. He would prostrate and then say: "Allah is the Greatest."

Then he would raise his head, fold his left foot and sit on it until every bone returned to its place. Then he would do the same in the other [rakʿah]. Then when he stood up after the two rakʿahs, he would say the takbīr and raise his hands until level with his shoulders, as he did at the beginning of the prayer. Then he would do that for the rest of his prayer, until, when it was the prostration after which came the salutation, he would put his left foot forward and sit leaning on his left side.
They said: You have spoken the truth; this is how he ﷺ used to pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said: Shall I not lead you in prayer the way the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed? Then he prayed and did not raise his hands except the first time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for prayer, he would face the qiblah, raise his hands, and say: "Allah is the Greatest."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah: With what did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ begin the night prayer? She said: You have asked me about something no one has asked me before you. When he stood, he would say "Allahu akbar" ten times, "al-ḥamdu lillāh" ten times, "subḥān Allāh" ten times, and "lā ilāha illā Allāh" ten times, and seek forgiveness ten times, and he would say:
"O Allah, forgive me, guide me, provide for me, and grant me well-being."
And he would seek refuge in Allah from the distress of the standing place on the Day of Resurrection.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are two pauses that I memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn denied that and said: We memorized only one pause.
So we wrote to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb in Medina, and Ubayy wrote that Samurah had memorized correctly.
Saʿīd said: We asked Qatādah: What are these two pauses? He said: When he entered his prayer, and when he finished the recitation.
Then afterwards he said: And when he recited: "...nor those who go astray."
He said: He liked, when he had finished the recitation, to pause until his breath returned to him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said concerning a woman with irregular bleeding: "
She leaves the prayer during the days of her menstrual periods in which she used to menstruate, then she bathes, performs ablution for every prayer, fasts, and prays."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a woman in postnatal bleeding would sit [out of prayer] for forty days or forty nights after her childbirth, and we used to apply ḥūrs-dye to our faces, meaning for [skin] discoloration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ wanting to accept Islam, and he commanded me to bathe with water and lote-tree leaves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about menstrual blood that gets on a garment. He said: "
Scrape it off with a rib bone and wash it with water and lote-tree leaves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked his sister Umm Ḥabībah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray in the garment in which he had relations with her? She said: Yes, if he did not see any filth on it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She asked Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and said: I am a woman who lets my garment trail long, and I walk in dirty places.
Umm Salamah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
What comes after it purifies it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "

Jibrīl, peace be upon him, led me in prayer at the House [the Kaʿbah] twice. He prayed Ẓuhr the first time when the shadow was like the strap of a sandal; then he prayed ʿAṣr when everything was the length of its shadow; then he prayed Maghrib when the sun had set and the fasting person breaks the fast; then he prayed ʿIshāʾ when the twilight had disappeared; then he prayed Fajr when the dawn appeared and food became forbidden for the fasting person.

The second time he prayed Ẓuhr when the shadow of everything was its own length, at the time he had prayed ʿAṣr the day before; then he prayed ʿAṣr when the shadow of everything was twice its length; then he prayed Maghrib at its first time; then he prayed the last ʿIshāʾ when a third of the night had passed; then he prayed Ṣubḥ when the land had become bright. Then he turned to me and said: O Muḥammad, this is the time of the prophets before you.
And the time is between these two times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of people about the time of this prayer, the last ʿIshāʾ prayer. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray it at the setting of the moon on the third night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We prayed the ʿAtamah prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he did not come out until about half the night had passed. Then he said: "Take your seats."
So we took our seats, and he said: "

The people have prayed and taken to their beds, but you will remain in prayer as long as you are waiting for the prayer. And were it not for the weakness of the weak and the illness of the sick, I would delay this prayer until half the night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:

"O Allah, set right for me my religion, which is the safeguard of my affairs; set right for me my worldly life, in which is my livelihood; set right for me my Hereafter, to which is my return; make life an increase for me in every good, and make death a relief for me from every evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Say: O Allah, guide me and keep me on the right course. And by 'guidance', remember your guidance of the way, and by 'right course', the straightness of the arrow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shall I not inform you of the most beloved speech to Allah?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of the most beloved speech to Allah." He said:
"The most beloved speech to Allah is 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ looked into the Fire.
Then he mentioned [a narration] similar to the hadith of Ayyūb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbdullāh had two wives. He came from one of them, and the other said, "You have come from so-and-so." He said, "I have come from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, who narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'The fewest of the inhabitants of Paradise are women.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Ḥasan al-Ḥulwānī,
and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd,
said: Yaʿqūb narrated to us,
– meaning Ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd – my father narrated to us,
from Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān,
all of them from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar,
from the Prophet ﷺ, with the meaning of the hadith of Abū Ḍamrah from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah. They added in their narration: "and they went out walking."
And in the narration of Ṣāliḥ: "walking together."
Except ʿUbaydullāh, for in his narration is: "and they went out."
And he did not mention anything after it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr gave a sermon and said:

"Allah is more delighted with the repentance of His servant than a man who loaded his provisions and water onto a camel, then travelled until he was in a barren stretch of land. The midday heat overtook him, so he dismounted and rested beneath a tree, and sleep overcame him, and his camel slipped away. He awoke and hurried up a height but saw nothing; then he hurried up a second height but saw nothing; then he hurried up a third height but saw nothing. So he returned to the place where he had rested, and while he was sitting there, his camel came to him walking until it placed its halter in his hand. Allah is more delighted with the repentance of a servant than this man was when he found his camel in its same condition."
Simāk said: Ash-Shaʿbī claimed that an-Nuʿmān attributed this hadith to the Prophet ﷺ, but I did not hear it myself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah is more delighted with the repentance of His servant when he repents to Him than one of you who was on his mount in a barren land, and it got away from him, carrying his food and drink. He despaired of finding it, so he came to a tree and lay down in its shade, having lost hope of his mount. While he was like that, suddenly it was standing beside him. He took hold of its halter and then said, out of intense joy, 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord.'
He made a mistake out of intense joy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"If you had no sins for Allah to forgive you, Allah would bring a people who have sins, and He would forgive them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ and we mentioned Paradise and the Fire.
Then he mentioned [a narration] similar to their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father said to me: Qatādah narrated to us,
(Transfer of chain) And Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us,
al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us,
ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān; (Transfer of chain) and Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us,
Abū al-Walīd narrated to us,
Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us,
both of them from Qatādah,
all of them mentioned it with the chain of Shuʿbah, similar to his hadith. And in the narration of Shaybān and Abū ʿAwānah:
"A man among the people whom Allah had given abundant wealth and children."
And in the narration of at-Taymī:
"For he had not stored up any good with Allah."
He said: Qatādah explained it as: he had not saved up any good with Allah.
And in the narration of Shaybān:
"For by Allah, he did not store up any good with Allah."
And in the narration of Abū ʿAwānah: "he did not provide [any good]", with the letter mīm.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, stretches out His hand at night so that the one who did wrong during the day may repent, and stretches out His hand during the day so that the one who did wrong during the night may repent, until the sun rises from the west."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
With the same wording as the narration of Ḥajjāj, specifically the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, and he did not mention the hadith of Asmāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The believer has a sense of protective jealousy, and Allah has an even greater sense of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Hajj is the jihad of every weak person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "May I perform Hajj on behalf of my father?" He said:
"Yes, perform Hajj on behalf of your father. Even if it does not add any good for him, it will not add any harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Prophet ﷺ for a ruling about a Hajj that was due from his father, who had died without performing Hajj. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Perform Hajj on behalf of your father." And the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Likewise, fasting that was vowed is to be made up on behalf of the deceased."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, Hajj has become obligatory for my father, but he is unable to perform it except lying across [the mount]."
He was silent for a while, then he said:
"Perform Hajj on behalf of your father."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said:

"The place for entering ihram for the people of Madinah is Dhū al-Ḥulayfah; for the people of Syria it is al-Juḥfah; for the people of Yemen it is Yalamlam; for the people of Najd it is Qarn; and for the people of the East it is Dhāt ʿIrq."
Then he turned his face toward the horizon and said:
"O Allah, turn their hearts [toward us]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was beside the legs of the camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the tree, and when it stood up straight with him, he said:
"Labbayk, [I respond to You] with ʿUmrah and Hajj together."
That was during the Farewell Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no pilgrim in ihram who spends his day for Allah, saying the talbiyah until the sun sets, except that the sun sets with his sins, and he returns as his mother bore him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "We were with the Prophet ﷺ while we were in ihram. When riders met us, we let our garments down over our heads, and when they had passed, we raised them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The prophets used to enter the Sanctuary on foot and barefoot, and they would circumambulate the House and perform the rites barefoot and on foot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah during the day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced the Stone, then placed his lips on it and wept for a long time. Then he turned and saw ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb weeping, and he said:
"O ʿUmar, here is where tears are to be shed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at ease in the year of the Conquest, he circumambulated on his camel, touching the corner with a curved staff in his hand. Then he entered the Kaʿbah and found in it a dove made of wooden sticks, so he broke it. Then he stood at the door of the Kaʿbah and threw it down, while I was watching him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions when they wished to enter Makkah for his ʿUmrah after Ḥudaybiyah:
"Your people will see you tomorrow, so let them see you strong."

When they entered the Mosque, they touched the corner and jogged, with the Prophet ﷺ among them, until they reached the Yamani corner; then they walked to the Black Corner. Then they jogged until they reached the Yamani corner, then walked to the Black Corner. He did that three times, then walked the remaining four.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever circumambulates the House and prays two rakʿahs, it is like freeing a slave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ was asked about the Yamani corner,
while he was circumambulating the House. ʿAṭāʾ said, "Abū Hurayrah narrated to me that the Prophet ﷺ said:

'Seventy angels are assigned to it. Whoever says: O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in this world and the Hereafter; our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire—they say: Āmīn.'"
When he reached the Black Corner, he said, "O Abū Muḥammad, what has reached you about this Black Corner?" ʿAṭāʾ said, "Abū Hurayrah narrated to me that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever greets it is only greeting the Hand of the Most Merciful.'"
Ibn Hishām said to him, "O Abū Muḥammad, what about the circumambulation?" ʿAṭāʾ said, "Abū Hurayrah narrated to me that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say:

'Whoever circumambulates the House seven times and says nothing except Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, Allāhu akbar, and lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh, ten sins are erased from him, ten good deeds are written for him, and ten degrees are raised for him thereby. And whoever circumambulates and speaks [otherwise] in that state wades into mercy with his feet, like one wading in water with his feet.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the Hajj in the ifrād manner.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the Hajj in the ifrād manner.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She brought him dates and ghee. He said: "
Return your ghee to its skin
and your dates to their container, for I am fasting."
Then he stood in a corner of the house
and prayed a voluntary prayer,
and he made supplication for Umm Sulaym and her family.
Umm Sulaym said: "O Messenger of Allah,
I have a little something [to ask]." He said: "What is it?"
She said: "Your servant Anas."
So he left out no good of the Hereafter or of this world except that he supplicated for me with it. He said: "
O Allah, grant him wealth and children, and bless him in them."
And indeed I am among the wealthiest of the Ansar.
And my daughter Amīnah told me that, at the time Hajjāj came to Basra, more than one hundred and twenty of my own offspring had been buried.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ entered upon her on Friday while she was fasting, and said: "Did you fast yesterday?" She said: "No." He said: "
Do you intend to fast tomorrow?" She said: "No." He said: "Then break your fast."
Ḥammād ibn al-Jaʿd said: Qatādah heard: Abū Ayyūb told me that Juwayriyah told him, so he ordered her and she broke her fast.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade fasting on two days, the day of Fitr and the day of Adhā; and two ways of dressing, wrapping oneself completely in a garment [leaving no opening for the arms] and sitting with one's knees drawn up in a single garment; and prayer at two times, after the Fajr prayer and after the ʿAṣr prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿUmar when a man asked him, saying: "I vowed to fast every Tuesday or Wednesday for as long as I live,
and it happened to coincide with the Day of Sacrifice."
He said: "Allah commanded fulfilling vows,
but we were forbidden to fast on the Day of Sacrifice."
The man repeated [the question] to him, and he said the same,
adding nothing to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were discussing the Night of Qadr, so I went to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, who was a friend of mine, and said: "Will you not go out with us to the date palms?" He went out wearing a cloak. I said to him: "Did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention the Night of Qadr?" He said: "Yes. We observed iʿtikāf with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the middle ten days of Ramadan, and we came out on the morning of the twentieth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said: "

'I was shown the Night of Qadr, but I forgot it, or was made to forget it. So seek it in the last ten nights, on the odd nights. And I saw myself prostrating in water and mud. So whoever observed iʿtikāf with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, let him return.'"

He said: "So we returned, and we saw no patch of cloud in the sky. Then a cloud came and it rained on us until the roof of the mosque, which was made of palm branches, was flowing with water. The prayer was established, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrating in the water and mud, until I saw the mark of mud on his forehead."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to observe iʿtikāf every Ramadan,

and when he had prayed the morning prayer he would enter the place where he observed iʿtikāf. He said: ʿĀʾishah asked his permission to observe iʿtikāf, and he permitted her, so she pitched a tent in it.
Ḥafṣah heard of it, so she pitched a tent.
Zaynab heard of it
and pitched another tent.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left the next morning, he saw four tents and said: "What is this?" He was told about them, and he said: "
Did piety move them to this? Remove them; I do not want to see them." They were removed,
and he did not observe iʿtikāf in Ramadan until he observed it in the last ten days of Shawwāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and his wives were with him; then they got up to leave,
and he said to Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy: "
Do not hurry, until I leave with you."
Her house was in the quarter of Usāmah.
So the Prophet ﷺ went out with her,
and two men of the Ansar met him,
and they looked at the Prophet ﷺ and then hurried on. The Prophet ﷺ said to them: "Come here;
this is Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy."
They said: "Glory be to Allah, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "
Indeed, Satan runs in the human being as blood runs,
and I feared that he might cast something into your hearts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A time will come upon people
when a man will not care how he acquires wealth, whether from what is lawful or from what is unlawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If a woman spends from her husband's earnings without his order,
he receives half of the reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
May Allah have mercy on a servant who is generous when he sells, generous when he buys, and generous when he asks for repayment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaʿlā and Salamah, the two sons of Umayyah, said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the expedition of Tabūk, and with us was a companion of ours. He and another man fought each other while we were on the road.

He said: One man bit the hand of his companion, so his companion pulled his hand out of his mouth and knocked out his front tooth. Then he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking compensation for his tooth.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One of you sets upon his brother and bites him like a stallion biting, then he comes seeking compensation? There is no compensation for it."
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ nullified the claim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"This and this are equal."
He said: Meaning the thumb and the little finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah used to narrate that a man

came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Last night I saw a cloud of shade from which clarified butter and honey were dripping, and I saw the people scooping it up with their hands, some taking much and some taking little. And I saw a rope stretching from the sky to the earth, and I saw you, O Messenger of Allah, take hold of it and ascend. Then a man after you took hold of it and ascended. Then another man after him took hold of it and ascended. Then another man took hold of it and it snapped, then it was joined for him and he ascended with it."
Abū Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, by Allah, you must let me interpret it." He said: "Interpret it."

He said: "As for the shade, it is the shade of Islam. As for the butter and honey dripping, it is the Qurʾān, its softness and its sweetness. As for those taking much and those taking little, they are the one who takes much of the Qurʾān and the one who takes little of it. As for the rope reaching from the sky to the earth, it is the truth that you are upon; you take hold of it and Allah raises you up. Then another man after you will take hold of it and ascend by it. Then another man after him will take hold of it and ascend by it. Then another man will take hold of it and it will snap, then it will be joined for him and he will ascend. O Messenger of Allah, tell me: did I get it right or wrong?" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"You got some right and some wrong."
He said: "I swear by my father and mother, you must tell me what I got wrong." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not swear."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the elders of his people: that ʿAbd

Allāh ibn Sahl and Muḥayyiṣah went out to Khaybar because of hardship that had afflicted them. Then Muḥayyiṣah was told that ʿAbdullāh ibn Sahl had been killed and thrown into a pit or a spring at Khaybar. So he went to the Jews and said: "By Allah, you killed him."
They said: "By Allah, we did not kill him."

Then he came back to his people and told them of that. Then he, his brother Ḥuwayyiṣah, who was older than him, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sahl came forward. Muḥayyiṣah, who had been at Khaybar, went to speak, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Muḥayyiṣah: "Let the elder speak, let the elder speak,"
meaning in age. So Ḥuwayyiṣah spoke, then Muḥayyiṣah spoke. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Either they pay the blood-money for your companion, or they will be notified of war."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to them about that, and they wrote back: "By Allah, we did not kill him."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ḥuwayyiṣah, Muḥayyiṣah and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān:
"Will you swear oaths and thereby be entitled to the blood-money of your companion?" They said: "No." He said:
"Then shall the Jews swear to you?"

They said: "They are not Muslims." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid the blood-money himself, and sent them one hundred camels until they were brought into their dwelling. Sahl said: A red she-camel among them kicked me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Faith has seventy-some branches, or sixty-some branches. The best of them is the saying 'There is no god but Allah,' and the lowest of them is removing harm from the road. And modesty is a branch of faith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Marwān brought out the pulpit on the day of an Eid and began with the sermon before the prayer. A man stood up and said: "O Marwān, you have opposed the Sunnah. You brought out the pulpit on the day of Eid, though it was not brought out on it, and you began with the sermon before the prayer."
Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: "Who is this?" They said: "So-and-so, son of so-and-so."
He said: "As for this man, he has fulfilled what was upon him. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is unable, then with his tongue; and if he is unable, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Between a servant and polytheism there is nothing but abandoning prayer,
so when he abandons it, he has committed polytheism."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I had forbidden you to drink from skin containers, but now drink from any vessel, only do not drink anything intoxicating."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Abū Salamah ibn
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about bitʿ (a honey drink), and he said:
"Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me and Muʿādh to Yemen, and he said:
"Invite the people, give them good news and do not drive them away, make things easy and do not make things difficult."

I said: O Messenger of Allah, give us a ruling about two drinks that we used to make in Yemen: bitʿ, which is made from honey that is left to soak until it ferments, and mizr, which is made from corn and barley that is left to soak until it ferments. (The narrator said:) The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been given comprehensive speech, with concluding words that sum up everything. So he said:
"I forbid every intoxicant that keeps one from prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They mentioned nabīdh in the presence of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have nabīdh prepared for him in a waterskin (Shuʿbah said: from Monday night), and he would drink it on Monday and Tuesday until the afternoon. If anything was left over, he would give it to the servant to drink or pour it out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people asked Ibn ʿAbbās about selling wine, buying it,
and trading in it. He said: Are you Muslims? They said: Yes.
He said: Then it is not permissible to sell it, buy it, or trade in it.

Then they asked him about nabīdh, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on a journey, and when he returned some of his Companions had prepared nabīdh in green jars, hollowed palm-trunks and gourds. He ordered that it be poured out, and it was poured out. Then he ordered a waterskin, and raisins and water were put in it that night. By morning he drank from it that day, the following night, and the next day until evening. He drank and gave others to drink, and when morning came he ordered what was left of it to be poured out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met ʿĀʾishah and asked her about nabīdh,

so ʿĀʾishah called an Abyssinian slave girl and said: Ask this one, for she used to prepare nabīdh for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Abyssinian girl said: I would prepare it for him in a waterskin at night, tie its mouth and hang it up, and in the morning he would drink from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir,
from the Prophet ﷺ this hadith, except that he said:
"Turn the vessel upside down, or cover the vessel."
And he did not mention laying a stick across the vessel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Close the door."
Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of al-Layth, except that he said: "and cover the vessels." And he said:
"...the clothes of the people of the house would be set ablaze upon them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Except that he did not say:
"Mention the name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Like the narration of Rawḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Cover the vessel and tie the waterskin, for in the year there is a night on which a pestilence descends, and it does not pass by any vessel that has no cover or any waterskin that has no tie, without some of that pestilence descending into it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we were invited to a meal with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
he mentioned [a narration] with the meaning of the hadith of Abū Muʿāwiyah and said: "as if being driven." And about the girl: "as if she were being driven."
He placed the coming of the Bedouin in his narration before the coming of the girl, and added at the end of the hadith: Then he mentioned the name of Allah and ate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Sufyān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man ate in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his left hand, and he said: "Eat with your right hand."
The man said: I cannot. He said: "May you never be able to."
Nothing prevented him except arrogance.
He said: And he never raised it to his mouth again.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"None of you should drink while standing; whoever forgets should vomit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ lick his three fingers after eating.
Ibn Ḥātim did not mention "three."
And Ibn Abī Shaybah said in his narration, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaʿb, from his father:
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"If a morsel of food falls from one of you, let him pick it up, remove whatever dirt is on it, and eat it, and not leave it for Satan. And let him not wipe his hand with a towel until he has licked his fingers, for he does not know in which part of his food the blessing lies."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Satan is present with each of you in everything he does, even at his meal. So if a morsel falls from one of you, let him remove whatever dirt is on it and then eat it, and not leave it for Satan. When he has finished, let him lick his fingers, for he does not know in which part of his food the blessing lies."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ one night, and he began with Sūrat al-Baqarah. I thought, "He will bow at the hundredth verse."
Then he continued, and I thought, "He will pray it all in one rakʿah." He continued, and I thought, "He will bow with it."

Then he began Sūrat an-Nisāʾ and recited it, then he began Āl ʿImrān and recited it. He recited slowly: when he passed a verse containing glorification, he glorified [Allah]; when he passed a request, he asked; and when he passed a plea for refuge, he sought refuge. Then he bowed and began to say:
"Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty."
His bowing was about as long as his standing. Then he said:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him."
Then he stood for a long time, close to the length of his bowing. Then he prostrated and said:
"Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."
His prostration was close to the length of his standing.
He said: In the narration of Jarīr there is an addition, that he said:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, to You belongs all praise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you has finished the prayer in his mosque, let him set aside a share of his prayer for his house, for Allah will place good in his house through his prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not make your houses into graves. Indeed, Satan flees from the house in which Sūrat al-Baqarah is recited."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Would one of you like, when he returns to his family, to find three large, fat, pregnant she-camels there?" We said, "Yes." He said:
"Then three verses that one of you recites in his prayer are better for him than three large, fat, pregnant she-camels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out while we were in the Ṣuffah, and said:
"Which of you would like to go out every morning to Buṭḥān or to al-ʿAqīq and return from it with two large-humped she-camels, without any sin and without severing family ties?"
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, we would like that." He said:

"Then does not one of you go out in the morning to the mosque and learn, or recite, two verses from the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? That is better for him than two she-camels; three verses are better for him than three, and four are better for him than four, and than their number in camels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Qurʾān will come, together with its people who acted by it in this world, preceded by Sūrat al-Baqarah and Āl ʿImrān."
Nawwās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave three similes for them that I have not forgotten since. He said:
"They will come as though they were two clouds, or two black canopies with light between them, or as two flocks of birds in rows, pleading on behalf of their companion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While Jibrīl was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, he heard a creaking sound above him. He raised his head and said, "This is a door in heaven that has been opened today; it was never opened before today." Then an angel descended from it, and [Jibrīl] said, "This is an angel who has come down to earth; he never came down before today." He greeted [the Prophet ﷺ] with peace and said, "Receive glad tidings of two lights that have been given to you, which were not given to any prophet before you: the Opening of the Book and the last verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah. You will not recite a single letter of them except that you will be given it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Abū al-Mundhir, do you know which verse of the Book of Allah that you have is the greatest?"
I said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"O Abū al-Mundhir, do you know which verse of the Book of Allah that you have is the greatest?"
I said, "Allah—there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence."
He struck me on the chest and said:
"By Allah, may knowledge be easy for you, Abū al-Mundhir!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Gather together, for I will recite to you a third of the Qurʾān."

He said: Those who could gather did so. Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out and recited "Say: He is Allah, [who is] One," and then went back in. Some of us said to others, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'I will recite to you a third of the Qurʾān.'
I think this is news that came to him from heaven." Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out and said:
"I said I would recite to you a third of the Qurʾān. Indeed, it is equal to a third of the Qurʾān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Have you not seen the verses that were revealed tonight, the like of which has never been seen? 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was in the house when ʿUthmān looked down at them and said, "Bring me your two companions who incited you against me."
He said: They were brought, and they looked like two young camels, or like two donkeys.

He said: ʿUthmān looked down at them and said, "I ask you by Allah and by Islam, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah when there was no sweet water there except the well of Rūmah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever buys the well of Rūmah and puts his bucket alongside the buckets of the Muslims will have something better than it in Paradise.'
So I bought it from my own wealth, and today you prevent me from drinking from it, so that I would have to drink sea water."
They said, "O Allah, yes."
He said, "I ask you by Allah and by Islam, do you know that the mosque became too small for its people, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever buys the plot of land of the family of so-and-so and adds it to the mosque will have something better than it in Paradise.'
So I bought it from my own wealth, and today you prevent me from praying two rakʿahs in it."
They said, "O Allah, yes."
He said, "I ask you by Allah and by Islam, do you know that I equipped the army of hardship (Tabūk) from my own wealth?" They said, "O Allah, yes."

Then he said, "I ask you by Allah and by Islam, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on Thabīr in Makkah, and with him were Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and I, and the mountain shook until its stones fell down to the base? He kicked it with his foot and said:
'Be still, Thabīr, for upon you are only a prophet, a siddīq, and two martyrs.'"
They said, "O Allah, yes."
He said, "Allahu Akbar! By the Lord of the Kaʿbah, they have testified for me that I am a martyr," three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah commanded me to love four people and informed me that He loves them."
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, name them for us." He said:

"ʿAlī is among them"—he said that three times—"and Abū Dharr, al-Miqdād and Salmān. He commanded me to love them and informed me that He loves them." This hadith is ḥasan gharīb; we do not know it except from the narration of Sharīk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"ʿAlī is from me and I am from ʿAlī, and no one conveys on my behalf except myself or ʿAlī."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The most merciful of my nation toward my nation is Abū Bakr; the strongest of them in the matter of Allah is ʿUmar; the most truthful of them in modesty is ʿUthmān; the most knowledgeable of them about the lawful and the unlawful is Muʿādh ibn Jabal; the best versed of them in inheritance law is Zayd ibn Thābit; and the best reciter among them is Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. Every nation has a trustworthy one, and the trustworthy one of this nation is Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb; we do not know it from the narration of Qatādah except through this route.
It was also narrated by Abū Qilābah from Anas from the Prophet ﷺ similarly, and the well-known one is the narration of Abū Qilābah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmmār came asking permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Let him in. Welcome to the good one, the one made good."
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If I were to appoint anyone as leader without consulting them, I would appoint Ibn Umm ʿAbd over them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn:
"I am at war with whoever you fight, and at peace with whoever you make peace with."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of you is the best to his family, and I am the best of you to my family. And when your companion dies, leave him alone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf informed him that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Ḥamrāʾ said to him: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing on his mount at al-Ḥazwarah, saying:
"By Allah, you are the best of Allah's earth and the most beloved land of Allah to me. By Allah, had I not been driven out from you, I would not have left."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ relieved himself, then cleaned himself with water from a small vessel, then rubbed his hand on the ground.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The announcer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us and said: Indeed Allah and His Messenger forbid you from the meat of donkeys, for it is impure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar
performed ablution washing each part three times, attributing that to the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ...Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
Then he mentioned a hadith similar to the hadith of Dāwūd, with some additions and omissions. Among the additions in it was:
"Indeed, Allah does not look at your bodies or at your forms, but He looks at your hearts."
And he pointed with his fingers to his chest.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some young men of Quraysh entered upon ʿĀʾishah while she was at Minā, and they were laughing. She said, "What makes you laugh?" They said, "So-and-so tripped over the rope of a tent and almost broke his neck or lost his eye."
She said, "Do not laugh, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'No Muslim is pricked by a thorn or anything more than that, except that a degree is recorded for him because of it and a sin is erased from him because of it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:
"Whoever points a piece of iron at his brother, the angels curse him, even if he is his brother by his father and mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Transition to another chain) And Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us,
He said: I read to Mālik, from Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a man says, 'The people are ruined,' he is the one who has ruined them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ...may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited him, or that Abū Dharr visited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said, "May my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah! Which speech is most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" He said:
"That which Allah chose for His angels: 'Glory be to my Lord and praise be to Him, glory be to my Lord and praise be to Him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, the people of Paradise will eat and drink in it, but they will not spit, urinate, defecate, or blow their noses."
They said, "Then what happens to the food?" He said:
"A belch and sweat that is like the fragrance of musk. They will be inspired to glorify Allah and praise Him just as they are inspired to breathe."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard a sound from a grave and said:
"When did this person die?"
They said, "He died in the time of ignorance."
He was pleased by that and said:
"Were it not that you would stop burying one another, I would have asked Allah to let you hear the punishment of the grave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas said: I was with ʿUmar. (Transition to another chain) And Shaybān ibn Farrūkh narrated to us,
– and the wording is his – Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah narrated to us, from Thābit,
from Anas ibn Mālik,

He said: We were with ʿUmar between Makkah and Madinah, and we tried to sight the new moon. I was a man of sharp eyesight, so I saw it, and no one claimed to have seen it except me. He said: I began saying to ʿUmar, "Do you not see it?" But he could not see it. He said: ʿUmar said, "I will see it, while I am lying on my bed."
Then he began to tell us about the people of Badr. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to show us the places where the people of Badr would fall, the day before, saying:
"This is where so-and-so will fall tomorrow, if Allah wills."

He said: ʿUmar said, "By the One who sent him with the truth, they did not miss the spots that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had marked." He said: They were thrown into a well, one on top of another. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went until he reached them and said:
"O so-and-so son of so-and-so, and O so-and-so son of so-and-so, have you found what Allah and His Messenger promised you to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true."
ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, how can you speak to bodies that have no souls in them?" He said:
"You do not hear what I say any better than they do, except that they are unable to reply to me with anything."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a military expedition. He said: A group of people came to the Prophet ﷺ from the west, wearing woolen garments, and met him near a small hill. They were standing while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting. He said: My soul told me, "Go to them and stand between them and him, so that they do not attack him by surprise." He said: Then I thought, "Perhaps he is in private conversation with them."
So I went to them and stood between them and him. He said: I memorized four statements from him, which I count on my hand. He said:

"You will fight the Arabian Peninsula and Allah will give you victory over it; then Persia, and Allah will give you victory over it; then you will fight the Romans, and Allah will give you victory over them; then you will fight the Dajjāl, and Allah will give you victory over him."
He said: Nāfiʿ said, "O Jābir, we do not think the Dajjāl will emerge until the Romans have been conquered."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do you have any difficulty in seeing the moon on the night of the full moon?"
They said, "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Do you have any difficulty in seeing the sun when there is no cloud beneath it?"
They said, "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Then you will see Him in the same way. Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection and say: Whoever used to worship something, let him follow it.

So those who used to worship the sun will follow the sun, those who used to worship the moon will follow the moon, and those who used to worship the false deities will follow the false deities. And this nation will remain, with its hypocrites among it. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will come to them in a form other than the one they recognize, and say: I am your Lord.
They will say: We seek refuge in Allah from you. This is our place until our Lord comes to us; when our Lord comes, we will recognize Him.
Then Allah, Exalted, will come to them in the form they recognize, and say: I am your Lord.
They will say: You are our Lord.

So they will follow Him, and the bridge will be set up over the middle of Hell. I and my nation will be the first to cross, and none will speak on that day except the Messengers, and the supplication of the Messengers on that day will be: O Allah, grant safety, grant safety.
In Hell there are hooks like the thorns of the saʿdān. Have you seen the saʿdān?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said,

"They are like the thorns of the saʿdān, except that none knows how great they are save Allah. They will snatch the people according to their deeds. Among them will be the believer, who will remain safe because of his deeds, and among them will be the one who is repaid [for his deeds] until he is delivered. Then when Allah has finished judging between the servants and wishes, by His mercy, to bring out of the Fire whomever He wills, He will command the angels to bring out of the Fire those who did not associate anything with Allah, of those whom Allah, Exalted, wishes to show mercy, those who say: There is no god but Allah.

The angels will recognize them in the Fire; they will recognize them by the mark of prostration. The Fire consumes every part of the son of Adam except the mark of prostration; Allah has forbidden the Fire to consume the mark of prostration.

So they will come out of the Fire, already burnt, and the water of life will be poured over them, and they will sprout from it as a seed sprouts in the silt carried by a flood. Then Allah, Exalted, will finish judging between the servants, and a man will remain facing the Fire; he will be the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise. He will say: My Lord, turn my face away from the Fire, for its wind has poisoned me and its blaze has burned me. He will call upon Allah as long as Allah wills that he call upon Him. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say: If I do that for you, might you ask for something else?
He will say: I will not ask You for anything else.

And he will give his Lord whatever covenants and pledges Allah wills. So Allah will turn his face away from the Fire. Then when he faces Paradise and sees it, he will be silent for as long as Allah wills, and then he will say: My Lord, bring me forward to the gate of Paradise.
Allah will say to him: Have you not given your covenants and pledges that you would not ask Me for anything other than what I gave you? Woe to you, son of Adam, how treacherous you are!
He will say: My Lord! And he will call upon Allah until He says to him: If I give you that, might you ask for something else?
He will say: No, by Your might.

So he will give his Lord whatever covenants and pledges Allah wills, and He will bring him forward to the gate of Paradise. When he stands at the gate of Paradise, Paradise will open wide for him and he will see the good and joy within it. He will be silent for as long as Allah wills, and then he will say: My Lord, admit me into Paradise.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say to him: Have you not given your covenants and pledges that you would not ask for anything other than what you were given? Woe to you, son of Adam, how treacherous you are!
He will say: My Lord, let me not be the most wretched of Your creation.
He will keep calling upon Allah until Allah, Blessed and Exalted, laughs at him. When Allah laughs at him, He will say: Enter Paradise.
When he enters it, Allah will say to him: Wish.
So he will ask his Lord and wish, until Allah Himself will remind him of this and that, until, when his wishes are exhausted, Allah, Exalted, will say: That is yours, and the like of it with it."
ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd said: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī was with Abū Hurayrah and did not reject anything of his narration,
until Abū Hurayrah narrated that Allah said to that man, "and the like of it with it."
Abū Saʿīd said, "And ten times the like of it with it, O Abū Hurayrah."
Abū Hurayrah said, "I only memorized his saying: That is yours, and the like of it with it."
Abū Saʿīd said, "I bear witness that I memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ his saying: That is yours, and ten times the like of it."
Abū Hurayrah said, "And that man is the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Ḥaḍramawt and a man from Kindah came to the Prophet ﷺ. The Ḥaḍramī said, "O Messenger of Allah, this man has overpowered me and taken land of mine that belonged to my father."
The Kindī said, "It is my land, in my possession; I cultivate it, and he has no right to it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Ḥaḍramī, "Do you have proof?" He said, "No." He said, "Then you have his oath."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, the man is a wrongdoer who does not care what he swears to, and he holds back from nothing." He said,
"You have nothing from him except that."
So he went off to swear, and as he turned away the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"As for him, if he swears an oath over his property in order to consume it unjustly, he will meet Allah while He is turning away from him."
label: machine translation
