segments_en: When the House was burned in the time of Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, when the people of Syria attacked it and what happened happened, Ibn al-Zubayr left it as it was until the people came for the pilgrimage season, wishing to embolden them—or to incite them—against the people of Syria. When the people were departing, he said, "O people, advise me about the Kaʿbah: should I tear it down and then rebuild it, or repair what has become worn?" Ibn ʿAbbās said, "I have formed an opinion about it: I think you should repair what has become worn, and leave the House that people accepted Islam while it stood, and the stones that people accepted Islam while they were there, and upon which the Prophet ﷺ was sent."

Ibn al-Zubayr said, "If the house of one of you were burned, he would not be content until he restored it, so how about the House of your Lord? I will seek guidance from my Lord for three days, and then I will resolve upon my course." When the three days had passed, he resolved to tear it down. The people shrank from it, fearing that a command from the sky would strike the first person to climb up on it, until a man climbed it and threw down some stones from it. When the people saw that nothing had befallen him, they followed one after another and tore it down until they brought it down to the ground. Ibn al-Zubayr then set up pillars and hung curtains over them until its structure rose.
Ibn al-Zubayr said, "I heard ʿĀʾishah say that the Prophet ﷺ said:

'Were it not that your people are still close to the time of disbelief, and I do not have enough funds to afford rebuilding it, I would have included in it five cubits from al-Ḥijr, and I would have made for it a door for people to enter by and a door for them to leave by.'"

He said, "Today I have the means to spend, and I do not fear the people." He said: So he added five cubits from al-Ḥijr until he uncovered a foundation which the people saw, and he built the structure upon it. The height of the Kaʿbah had been eighteen cubits, but when he enlarged it he thought it too short, so he added ten cubits to its height, and he made two doors for it, one to enter by and the other to leave by.

When Ibn al-Zubayr was killed, al-Ḥajjāj wrote to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān informing him of that, and informing him that Ibn al-Zubayr had laid the building on a foundation which the trustworthy men of Makkah had seen.

ʿAbd al-Malik wrote back to him, "We have nothing to do with the blemishing done by Ibn al-Zubayr. As for what he added to its height, leave it as it is; as for what he added from al-Ḥijr, return it to its former structure, and close up the door that he opened."
So he tore it down and restored it to its former structure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I declare sacred what lies between the two lava tracts of Madinah: that its thorny trees not be cut down or its game be killed." And he said, "Madinah is better for them, if only they knew. No one leaves it out of aversion to it except that Allah replaces him in it with someone better than him, and no one remains steadfast through its hardship and difficulty except that I will be an intercessor or a witness for him on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Saʿd,
both said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, bless the people of Madinah in their mudd."
And he narrated the hadith, and in it:
"Whoever intends evil for its people, Allah will make him dissolve as salt dissolves in water."

segments_en: In this hadith—al-Walīd ibn Abī Hishām said—from Zayd ibn Zāʾid,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let none of my Companions pass on to me anything about anyone, for I love to come out to you with a sound heart."

segments_en: And he was
one of the companions of Ibn Masʿūd, from ʿĀʾishah, who said:
I imitated a man for the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:

She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, Ṣafiyyah is a woman—" and she gestured with her hand like this, as if she meant that she was short. He said:

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Envy devours good deeds as the Fire devours firewood; charity (ṣadaqah) extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire; prayer is the light of the believer; and fasting is a shield from the Fire."

segments_en: A man
cursed the wind—and Muslim said: A man's cloak was blown from him by the wind in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, so he cursed it—and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not curse it, for it is under command. Whoever curses something that does not deserve it, the curse returns upon him."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shall I not tell you of something better in rank than fasting, prayer, and charity (ṣadaqah)?" They said, "Yes." He said:
"Reconciling people to one another, for corruption in relations between people is the shaver [of religion]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permit any falsehood except in three cases. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:

"I do not consider him a liar: a man who reconciles between people, saying something only with the intention of making peace; a man who speaks in war; a man who speaks to his wife; and a woman who speaks to her husband."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever plays backgammon has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man following a pigeon, and he said:
"A devil following a devil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUthmān,
the two sons of Abū Shaybah—the meaning is the same—said: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us,
ʿUthmān said: and Jarīr al-Rāzī; (another chain:) and Wāṣil ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash,
from Abū Ṣāliḥ,
—and Wāṣil said: It was narrated to me from Abū Ṣāliḥ—
then they agreed—from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"Whoever relieves a believer of one of the distresses of this world, Allah will relieve him of one of the distresses of the Day of Resurrection; whoever eases the hardship of one in difficulty, Allah will ease things for him in this world and the Hereafter; and whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allah will conceal his faults in this world and the Hereafter. Allah is in the aid of the servant so long as the servant is in the aid of his brother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hāniʾ [said] that when he came as part of a delegation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, [the Prophet] heard them calling Hāniʾ Abū al-Ḥakam, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and said to him:
"Allah is the Judge (al-Ḥakam), and judgment belongs to Him. Why are you called Abū al-Ḥakam?"
He said, "When my people differ over something, they come to me and I judge between them, and both parties are satisfied." He said:
"How excellent this is! Do you have any children?"
He said: I have Shurayḥ, ʿAbdullāh, and Muslim. He said, "Which of them is the eldest?" I said, "Shurayḥ." He said:
"Then you are Abū Shurayḥ."
And he prayed for him and for his son.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said, "Who are you?" I said, "Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, if a son is born to me after you, may I name him with your name and give him your kunyah?" He said, "Yes."
Abū Bakr did not say "I said"; [rather] ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said to the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Woe to the one who tells a story to make people laugh, and lies in it. Woe to him, woe to him!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a man makes a promise to his brother, intending to fulfil it, and then does not fulfil it and does not come at the appointed time, there is no sin on him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When one of you stands to pray, he is screened if there is in front of him something like the back of a saddle. If there is not in front of him something like the back of a saddle, then a donkey, a woman, and a black dog will cut off his prayer."
I said, "O Abū Dharr, what is it about the black dog as opposed to the red dog or the yellow dog?" He said, "O my nephew, I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ just as you have asked me, and he said:
'The black dog is a devil.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prostrated at {When the sky is split apart}.
Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah said: This hadith is from the narration of Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd; I have not heard anyone mention it other than him.

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times and say:
"O Allah, You are Peace and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor."
Al-Walīd said: I asked al-Awzāʿī, "How is the seeking of forgiveness done?" He said, "You say: I seek forgiveness from Allah, I seek forgiveness from Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ finished the prayer with the salam, he would sit only for as long as it took to say:
"O Allah, You are Peace and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor."
And in the narration of Ibn Numayr:
"O Possessor of Majesty and Honor."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn Saʿīd,
both from al-Azraq,
Zuhayr said: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf al-Azraq narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us,
from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad,
from Sulaymān ibn Buraydah, from his father,
from the Prophet ﷺ, that a man asked him about the time of prayer, and he said to him:
"Pray with us these two [days]."

meaning two days. When the sun passed its zenith, he ordered Bilāl, who gave the call to prayer; then he ordered him and he gave the iqāmah for Ẓuhr; then he ordered him and he gave the iqāmah for ʿAṣr while the sun was high, white, and clear; then he ordered him and he gave the iqāmah for Maghrib when the sun had set; then he ordered him and he gave the iqāmah for ʿIshāʾ when the twilight had disappeared; then he ordered him and he gave the iqāmah for Fajr when dawn broke. On the second day, he ordered him to delay Ẓuhr until it cooled, and he delayed it, delaying it well until it cooled. He prayed ʿAṣr while the sun was still high, delaying it more than he had the day before. He prayed Maghrib before the twilight disappeared, prayed ʿIshāʾ after a third of the night had passed, and prayed Fajr when it was bright. Then he said:
"Where is the one who asked about the time of prayer?"
The man said, "I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"The time of your prayer is between what you have seen."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"How will you be when you have rulers who delay the prayer beyond its time, or let the prayer die away from its time?"
I said, "What do you command me [to do]?" He said:
"Pray the prayer at its time; then if you catch it with them, pray [again], for it will be a voluntary prayer for you."
And Khalaf did not mention "beyond its time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting in the mosque with Abū Hurayrah when the muʾadhdhin gave the call to prayer. A man got up from the mosque and walked away, and Abū Hurayrah followed him with his gaze until he left the mosque. Then Abū Hurayrah said, "As for this man, he has disobeyed Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, its expiation is to pray it when he remembers it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: {There is no blame upon you for shortening
the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may put you to trial}, yet people are now safe.
ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "I wondered at what you wonder at, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said:
'It is a charity (ṣadaqah) that Allah has given to you, so accept His charity.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"When the iqāmah for the prayer is called, there is no prayer except the obligatory one."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about the prayer of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at night. She said, "He would pray for a long part of the night standing and a long part of the night sitting. When he recited standing, he would bow standing, and when he recited sitting, he would bow sitting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, "With what did the Prophet ﷺ begin his prayer when he stood at night?" She said, "When he stood at night, he would begin his prayer by saying:

'O Allah, Lord of Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl, and Isrāfīl, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differed. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth in that over which there is disagreement. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.'"
He said: This is a good (ḥasan), gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Qilābah said to me, "Why don't you meet him and ask him?"
He said: So I met him and asked him, and he said, "We were at a watering place on the road where people passed,

and riders would pass by us, and we would ask them, 'What is the matter with the people? What is the matter with the people? Who is this man?' They would say, 'He claims that Allah has sent him and that revelation has come to him,
or that Allah has revealed such and such.'
I used to memorize those words,
and it was as though they were being fixed in my chest.
The Arabs were waiting for the conquest [of Mecca] before accepting Islam,
and they would say, 'Leave him and his people alone,
for if he prevails over them, then he is a truthful prophet.'
When the conquest took place, every people hastened to accept Islam,
and my father hastened to bring my people into Islam.
When he returned, he said, 'By Allah, I have come to you from the Prophet ﷺ in truth, and he said:
"Pray such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time,
and pray such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time,
and when the time for prayer comes, let one of you call the adhān,
and let the one among you who knows the most Qur'an lead you in prayer."'
So they looked, and no one knew more Qur'an than I did,
because of what I used to learn from the riders.
So they put me forward in front of them,
while I was six or seven
years old, and I was wearing a cloak,
which, whenever I prostrated, would draw up and leave me exposed.
A woman of the tribe said, 'Won't you cover the backside of your reciter from us?'
So they bought cloth and cut a shirt for me,
and I never rejoiced over anything as I rejoiced over that shirt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays entered upon ʿAbdullāh while he was eating his morning meal, and said, "Abū Muḥammad, come closer to the meal."

He said, "Is today not the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ?" He replied, "Do you know what the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ is?" He said, "What is it?" He said, "It is only a day that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast before the month of Ramadan was revealed; when the month of Ramadan was revealed, he abandoned it."
And Abū Kurayb said, "He abandoned it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I spent a night in the house of Maymūnah, while the Prophet ﷺ was with her, so that I could observe how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed at night.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ talked with his family for a while, then went to sleep.

When it was the last third of the night, or part of it, he sat up, looked toward the sky, and recited: {Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth} up to His saying {for those of understanding}. Then he got up, performed ablution, and cleaned his teeth with the siwāk,
then prayed eleven rakʿahs.
Then Bilāl called the adhān for the prayer, and he prayed two rakʿahs,
then went out and led the people in the dawn prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: peace be upon him, that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray two rakʿahs before the ʿAṣr prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade prayer after the ʿAṣr prayer, unless the sun is still white, clear, and high.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar saw me praying,
after the break of dawn, and said: "O Yasār, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were praying this prayer, and he said:
'Let those of you who are present convey this to those who are absent: do not pray after dawn except two prostrations.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'O son of Adam, do not fail me in four rakʿahs at the beginning of your day, and I will suffice you for the end of it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of the conquest [of Makkah], the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the voluntary Ḍuḥā prayer of eight rakʿahs, concluding with the salām after every two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hurayrah, both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a man wakes his wife at night and they pray, or [each] prays, two rakʿahs together, they are recorded among the men and women who remember Allah often."
Ibn Kathīr did not attribute it to the Prophet, nor did he mention Abū Hurayrah; he made it the saying of Abū Saʿīd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: with him, may Allah be pleased [with her], that ʿĀʾishah,
the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no person who has a night prayer that sleep overcomes him from performing, except that the reward of his prayer is recorded for him, and his sleep is a charity (ṣadaqah) for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the delegation of Thaqīf. He said: The Aḥlāf stayed with al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lodged Banū Mālik in a tent of his.
Musaddad said: He was among the delegation of Thaqīf who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Every night he would come to us after the ʿIshāʾ prayer and talk with us.

Abū Saʿīd said: [He would talk] standing on his feet, shifting from one foot to the other because of the length of his standing. Most of what he told us was about what he had met from his people, the Quraysh. Then he would say: "They are not the same. We were weak and humiliated" — Musaddad said: in Makkah — "and when we went out to Madinah, the war between us and them went back and forth: we prevailed over them and they prevailed over us." Then one night he was late beyond the time when he used to come to us, so we said: "You were late tonight."
He said: "A portion of my [nightly share] of the Qurʾān came upon me, and I disliked to come until I had completed it."

Aws said: I asked the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ how they divided the Qurʾān into portions. They said: three, five, seven, nine, eleven, thirteen, and the portion of al-Mufaṣṣal on its own.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught him that there are fifteen prostrations in the Qurʾān, three of them in al-Mufaṣṣal and two in Sūrat al-Ḥajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, was Sūrat al-Ḥajj favoured by having two prostrations in it?" He said:
"Yes. Whoever does not perform them should not recite them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Witr, then said:
"O people of the Qurʾān, pray the Witr, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Witr [One] and loves the Witr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He was] among those who prayed the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when he said:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him,"
in the second rakʿah, he stood for a short while.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked which deeds are best. He said:
"Faith about which there is no doubt, jihād in which there is no misappropriation of spoils, and an accepted Hajj."
It was said: "Which prayer is best?" He said: "The long standing [in prayer]."
It was said: "Which charity (ṣadaqah) is best?" He said: "The effort of one who has little."
It was said: "Which emigration is best?" He said:
"The one who abandons what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden."
It was said: "Which jihād is best?" He said:
"The one who strives against the polytheists with his wealth and his life."
It was said: "Which kind of death is most honourable?" He said:
"The one whose blood is spilled and whose horse is hamstrung."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given the seven long ones of the Mathānī, and Mūsā, peace be upon him, was given six. When he threw down the Tablets, two were taken up and four remained.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar
passed by Ḥassān while he was reciting poetry in the mosque, and he glanced at him. [Ḥassān] said, "I used to recite poetry in it when there was someone in it better than you."
Then he turned to Abū Hurayrah and said, "I ask you by Allah, did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Respond on my behalf. O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit'?"
He said, "O Allah, yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Zirr about the saying of the Exalted, {And he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer. Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed.} He said: ʿAbdullāh informed us that Muhammad ﷺ saw Jibrīl, who had six hundred wings.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a man calls his wife to his bed and she refuses and does not come to him, and he spends the night angry with her, the angels curse her until morning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muhammad ﷺ said:
"I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its inhabitants were the poor, and I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its inhabitants were women."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"While I was asleep, I saw myself in Paradise, and there was a woman performing ablution beside a palace. I said, 'For whom is this?' They said, 'For ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.'
Then I remembered ʿUmar's sense of jealousy, so I turned away and left."

Abū Hurayrah said: ʿUmar wept, while we were all in that gathering with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then ʿUmar said, "May my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah! Would I be jealous of you?" ʿAmr al-Nāqid and Ḥasan al-Ḥulwānī narrated it to me,
and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd,
they said: Yaʿqūb ibn
Ibrāhīm narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ,
from Ibn Shihāb,
with this chain of narration, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon,
and those who follow them will be like the most brightly shining star.
Their hearts will be as the heart of one man,
with no disagreement among them and no mutual hatred.
Each of them will have two wives,
and the marrow of the shins of each of them will be visible through the flesh because of her beauty.
They will glorify Allah morning and evening.
They will not fall ill, nor blow their noses, nor spit.
Their vessels will be of gold and silver, and their combs of gold,
and the fuel of their censers will be aloeswood—Abū al-Yamān said: meaning ʿūd—and their sweat will be musk."
Mujāhid said: al-Ibkār means the beginning of dawn,
and al-ʿashiyy is from the declining of the sun until it sets.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They either boasted or discussed whether there would be more men or more women in Paradise. Abū Hurayrah said, "Did Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ not say:

'The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon, and the group following them will be like the most brilliant shining star in the sky. Each of them will have two wives, the marrow of whose shins can be seen through the flesh, and there will be no unmarried person in Paradise'?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Paradise will see those in the upper chambers above them just as you see the distant shining star on the horizon, in the east or the west,
because of the difference in rank among them."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah,
those are the abodes of the prophets; no one else will reach them." He said:
"Yes, by the One in whose hand is my soul,
they are men who believed in Allah and affirmed the truth of the Messengers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"This fire of yours, which the son of Adam kindles, is one part of seventy parts of the heat of Hell."
They said, "By Allah, it would have been enough, O Messenger of Allah!" He said:
"It has been exceeded by sixty-nine parts, each of them like its heat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be concerned about this—and Ibn ʿUbayd said: they will be inspired to do this—and they will say: 'If only we sought intercession with our Lord so that He would relieve us from this place of ours.' So they will go to Adam ﷺ and say: 'You are Adam, the father of mankind. Allah created you with His Hand, breathed into you of His spirit, and commanded the angels, who prostrated to you. Intercede for us with your Lord so that He relieves us from this place of ours.'

He will say: 'I am not in a position for that'—and he will mention the mistake he committed and feel shame before his Lord because of it—'but go to Noah, the first messenger Allah sent.' So they will go to Noah ﷺ, and he will say: 'I am not in a position for that'—and he will mention the mistake he committed and feel shame before his Lord because of it—'but go to Abraham ﷺ, whom Allah took as a close friend.'

So they will go to Abraham ﷺ, and he will say: 'I am not in a position for that'—and he will mention the mistake he committed and feel shame before his Lord because of it—'but go to Moses ﷺ, to whom Allah spoke and whom He gave the Torah.'

He said: So they will go to Moses, peace be upon him, and he will say: 'I am not in a position for that'—and he will mention the mistake he committed and feel shame before his Lord because of it—'but go to Jesus, the spirit of Allah and His word.'
So they will go to Jesus, the spirit of Allah and His word, and he will say: 'I am not in a position for that.
But go to Muhammad ﷺ, a servant whose past and future sins have been forgiven.'"
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"So they will come to me, and I will ask permission to come before my Lord, and permission will be given to me. When I see Him, I will fall down in prostration, and He will leave me as long as Allah wills. Then it will be said: 'O Muhammad, raise your head. Speak, you will be heard; ask, you will be given; intercede, your intercession will be accepted.'

So I will raise my head and praise my Lord with a praise that He teaches me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will bring them out of the Fire and admit them into Paradise. Then I will return and fall down in prostration, and He will leave me as long as Allah wills. Then it will be said: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad. Speak, you will be heard; ask, you will be given; intercede, your intercession will be accepted.'

So I will raise my head and praise my Lord with a praise that He teaches me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will bring them out of the Fire and admit them into Paradise." He said: I do not know whether it was the third or the fourth time that he said: "Then I will say: 'O Lord, no one remains in the Fire except those whom the Qurʾān has confined,' meaning those for whom eternity [in the Fire] has become obligatory."
Ibn ʿUbayd said in his narration: Qatādah said: that is, those for whom eternity has become obligatory.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "I will be your forerunner at the Basin.
Whoever comes to it will drink from it,
and whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty afterward.
Some people will come to me whom I know and who know me,
then a barrier will be placed between me and them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The distance between the two sides of my Basin is like the distance between Ṣanʿāʾ and Medina," or "like the distance between Medina and ʿAmmān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard his statement about his Basin, that it is [as wide as] the distance between Ṣanʿāʾ and Medina.
Al-Mustawrid said to him: "Did you not hear him mention the vessels?" He said: "No."
Al-Mustawrid said: "You will see in it vessels like the stars."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I will be at the Basin until I see who among you comes to me,
and some people will be taken away from me, and I will say: 'My Lord, they are from me and from my Ummah.'
It will be said: 'Do you know what they did after you? By Allah, they kept turning back on their heels.'"
Ibn Abī Mulaykah used to say: "O Allah, we seek refuge in You from turning back on our heels or being tried away from our religion."
{You turned back on your heels} means: you turned back on your heels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah has not sent any prophet, nor appointed any successor,
except that he had two inner circles of advisers:
one circle that commands him to do good and urges him to it,
and another circle that commands him to do evil and urges him to it,
and the protected one is the one whom Allah, the Exalted, protects."
Sulaymān said, from Yaḥyā: Ibn Shihāb informed me of this,
and from Ibn Abī ʿAtīq and Mūsā, from Ibn Shihāb, similarly.
Shuʿayb said, from az-Zuhrī: Abū Salamah narrated to me from Abū Saʿīd, as his own statement.
Al-Awzāʿī and Muʿāwiyah ibn Sallām said: az-Zuhrī narrated to me: Abū Salamah narrated to me from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
Ibn Abī Ḥusayn and Saʿīd ibn Ziyād said, from Abū Salamah, from Abū Saʿīd, as his own statement.
ʿUbaydullāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar said: Ṣafwān narrated to me from Abū Salamah, from Abū Ayyūb, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We are the last, and we will be the foremost on the Day of Resurrection." [Narrated] similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They used to perform Hajj without taking provisions. Abū Masʿūd said: The people of Yemen, or some of the people of Yemen, used to perform Hajj without taking provisions, and they would say, "We are those who rely [on Allah]." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: {And take provisions, for indeed the best provision is piety} — the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaʿlā used to say to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him: "I wish I could see the Prophet of Allah ﷺ when revelation comes down to him."

So when the Prophet ﷺ was at al-Jiʿrānah, with a garment over the Prophet ﷺ that was being used to shade him, and some of his Companions with him, among them ʿUmar, a man came to him wearing a woollen cloak and smeared with perfume. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who has entered ihrām for ʿUmrah wearing a cloak, after having smeared himself with perfume?" The Prophet ﷺ looked at him for a while, then fell silent. Then revelation came to him, and ʿUmar motioned with his hand to Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah: "Come."
So Yaʿlā came and put his head in, and there was the Prophet ﷺ, his face red, breathing heavily for a while. Then it passed from him, and he said:
"Where is the one who asked me about ʿUmrah a moment ago?"
So the man was sought out and brought, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"As for the perfume on you, wash it off three times; and as for the cloak, take it off; then do in your ʿUmrah what you do in your Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr prayer in Medina four rakʿahs,
and the ʿAṣr prayer at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah two rakʿahs.
And from Ayyūb, from a man, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: Then he spent the night until morning and prayed the Fajr prayer,
then he mounted his riding animal, until when it stood upright with him on al-Baydāʾ, he declared the intention for ʿUmrah and Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr prayer in Medina four rakʿahs,
and the ʿAṣr prayer at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah two rakʿahs,
and I heard them calling out loudly for both of them together.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr prayer in Medina, with us accompanying him, four rakʿahs,
and the ʿAṣr prayer at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah two rakʿahs,
then he spent the night there until morning,
then he mounted until his animal stood upright with him on al-Baydāʾ,
he praised Allah, glorified Him, and pronounced His greatness,
then he declared the intention for Hajj and ʿUmrah,
and the people declared the intention for both,
and when we arrived, he ordered the people and they came out of ihrām,
until the Day of Tarwiyah, when they declared the intention for Hajj. He said: And the Prophet ﷺ sacrificed several camels with his own hand, standing,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered two white-and-black speckled rams in Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Ibn ʿAbbās when they mentioned the Dajjāl, and he said: "Between his eyes is written 'disbeliever.'"
He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I did not hear that."
He said: "That is so, but he said:

'As for Ibrāhīm, look at your companion. As for Mūsā, he was a man of brown complexion with curly hair, on a red camel whose halter was made of palm fibre. It is as if I can see him when he descends into the valley, saying the talbiyah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out declaring the intention for Hajj, in the months of Hajj and the sacred period of Hajj, and we stopped at Sarif.
The Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions:
"Whoever does not have a sacrificial animal with him,
and would like to make it an ʿUmrah,
let him do so; and whoever has a sacrificial animal with him, let him not."
The Prophet ﷺ and some of his Companions who were men of strength had sacrificial animals with them,
so they had no ʿUmrah.
The Prophet ﷺ came in to me while I was weeping, and said: "What makes you weep?"
I said: "I heard you say to your Companions what you said, and so I am prevented from ʿUmrah." He said: "What is the matter with you?"
I said: "I am not praying." He said:
"It does not harm you. You are one of the daughters of Ādam;
what has been decreed for them has been decreed for you.
So continue in your Hajj; perhaps Allah will grant it to you."
She said: So I remained so until we departed from Minā,
and we stopped at al-Muḥaṣṣab. He called ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and said:
"Take your sister out of the sacred precinct, and let her declare the intention for ʿUmrah,
then finish your circumambulation,
and I will wait for you both here."
So we came in the depth of the night. He said: "Have you finished?" I said: "Yes."
Then he called out the departure among his Companions, and the people set out,
including whoever had circumambulated the House
before the Fajr prayer,
then he left, heading towards Medina.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī and ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with them both, met at ʿUsfān. ʿUthmān used to forbid the tamattuʿ or the ʿUmrah. ʿAlī said: "What do you want with a matter the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did, that you forbid it?" ʿUthmān said: "Leave us alone."
He said: "I cannot leave you alone." So when ʿAlī saw that, he declared the intention for both together.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade steeping dates and raisins together, and he forbade steeping unripe dates and ripe dates together.
Al-Layth ibn Saʿd said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ al-Makkī narrated to me,
from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh,
from the Prophet ﷺ, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Zayd ibn Arqam was asked, "Narrate to us what you heard from
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," he would say: "I will narrate to you only what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us, and he used to command us to say:

'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, old age, and the punishment of the grave. O Allah, grant my soul its piety and purify it, for You are the best to purify it; You are its Guardian and Protector. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a soul that is never satisfied, from a heart that has no humility, from knowledge that does not benefit, and from a supplication that is not answered.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We returned with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Mecca to Medina, and when we reached a place with water on the road, some people hurried at the time of ʿAṣr and performed ablution in haste. When we reached them, their heels were gleaming, untouched by water. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perfect the ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Qatādah about spitting
in the mosque, and he said: I heard Anas ibn Mālik
say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Spitting in the mosque is a sin, and its expiation is to bury it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
they said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transition) He said: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ziyād also narrated to me: Ibrāhīm informed us,
meaning Ibn Saʿd, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd and Abū
Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Transition) He said: Ḥarmalah ibn Yaḥyā also narrated to me,
and the wording is his: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
who said: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me
that Abū Hurayrah
said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"When the prayer is called [for the iqāmah], do not come to it running; come walking, with calmness upon you. Pray what you catch, and complete what you miss."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
used to say these words aloud: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god but You."

And from Qatādah, that he wrote to him informing him about Anas ibn Mālik, who narrated to him, saying: I prayed behind the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, and they would begin with "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds," not mentioning "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" at the beginning of the recitation or at its end.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
they said: Sufyān narrated to us,
from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Were it not that it would be a hardship upon the believers (and in the narration of Zuhayr: upon my Ummah), I would have commanded them to use the siwāk at every prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two women
were sewing leather in a house (or in a room), and one of them came out with an awl having pierced her palm.
She made a claim against the other,
and the matter was brought to Ibn ʿAbbās,
and Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If people were given according to their claims, the blood and wealth of [other] people would be lost."
[He said:] "Remind her of Allah, and recite to her: 'Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah...'" So they reminded her, and she confessed.
Then Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The oath is upon the defendant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I was listening,
from Ibn Wahb,
who said: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me,
from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj,
from Busr ibn Saʿīd,
from Zayd ibn Khālid,
from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
"Whoever equips a fighter in the cause of Allah has fought, and whoever looks after the fighter's family well in his absence has fought."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by us while we were among a group of women, and he greeted us with salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When one of you comes to a gathering, let him give the greeting of salām. If it occurs to him to sit, let him sit. Then when he gets up, let him give the greeting of salām, for the first is no more deserving than the last."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw anyone more similar in bearing, manner, and conduct to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in her standing and sitting, than Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

She said: When she entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, he would rise to her, kiss her, and seat her in his place; and when the Prophet ﷺ entered upon her, she would rise from her seat, kiss him, and seat him in her place. When the Prophet ﷺ fell ill, Fāṭimah came in and bent over him and kissed him, then raised her head and wept; then she bent over him again, then raised her head and laughed. I said: I used to think that she was the most intelligent of our women, but she is just like the other women. Then when the Prophet ﷺ had died, I said to her: Tell me, when you bent over the Prophet ﷺ and raised your head you wept, then you bent over him and raised your head you laughed; what made you do that? She said: Then I would have been foolish. He told me that he would die of this illness of his, so I wept; then he told me that I would be the first of his family to join him, and that was when I laughed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that snakes be killed, and he said:
"Whoever fears their vengeance is not one of us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the killing of four creatures: the ant, the bee, the hoopoe, and the shrike.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Tell your husbands to clean themselves with water, for I am shy to tell them myself. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution: he washed his face three times, his hands twice, and his feet twice, and he wiped his head twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"Ablution has a devil called al-Walahān, so beware of the whispering [of doubt] about water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by two fresh graves and said:

"They are both being punished, and they are not being punished for something major. As for one of them, he did not protect himself from his urine; and as for the other, he used to go about spreading slander."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no ablution [required] except for a sound or a smell [of passing wind]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Ablution is required after eating what fire has touched, even if it is a piece of cheese."

He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to him, "O Abū Hurayrah, should we perform ablution because of oil? Should we perform ablution because of hot water?" Abū Hurayrah said: "O son of my brother, when you hear a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, do not make analogies to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about performing ablution after eating camel meat, and he said: "Perform ablution after it."
He was asked about performing ablution after eating mutton, and he said:
"Do not perform ablution after it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever touches his private part should not pray until he performs ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: When the two circumcised parts meet, ghusl becomes obligatory. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I did that, and we performed ghusl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Prophet ﷺ about prostatic fluid (madhy), and he said:
"From madhy, ablution is required; and from semen, ghusl is required."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A guest stayed with ʿĀʾishah, and she ordered a yellow sheet for him. He slept in it and had a wet dream. He was too shy to send it back with the traces of the wet dream on it, so he dipped it in water and then sent it back. ʿĀʾishah said: Why did he ruin our garment? It would have been enough for him to rub it with his fingers. Sometimes I would rub it with my fingers from the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"A menstruating woman and a person in a state of major impurity should not recite anything of the Qurʾān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about eating with a menstruating woman, and he said: "Eat with her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Were it not that it would be a hardship on my Ummah, I would have commanded them to delay the ʿIshāʾ prayer until a third of the night or half of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said: On the day of the Trench, the polytheists kept the Messenger of Allah ﷺ occupied from four prayers, until as much of the night had passed as Allah willed. He ordered Bilāl, who called the adhān, then the iqāmah, and he prayed Ẓuhr; then he called the iqāmah and prayed ʿAṣr; then he called the iqāmah and prayed Maghrib; then he called the iqāmah and prayed ʿIshāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Jabr ibn ʿAtīk,
that ʿAtīk ibn al-Ḥārith

(who was the grandfather of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbdullāh, the father of his mother) informed him that Jabr ibn ʿAtīk told him that the Prophet ﷺ came to visit ʿAbdullāh ibn Thābit when he was ill, and found that he had been overcome [by his illness]. He called out to him but he did not answer. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Indeed to Allah we belong and to Him we shall return," and said:
"We have been overcome concerning you, Abū ar-Rabīʿ."
The women cried out and wept, and Ibn ʿAtīk began to quiet them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Leave them. When the obligation occurs, let no weeping woman weep."
They said, "What is the obligation, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Death."
His daughter said, "I had hoped that you would be a martyr, for you had completed your preparations [for battle]."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has already settled his reward according to his intention. And what do you consider martyrdom to be?"
They said, "Being killed in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Martyrdom is of seven kinds besides being killed in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: the one who dies of plague is a martyr, the one who dies of a stomach illness is a martyr, the one who drowns is a martyr, the one killed by a collapsing building is a martyr, the one who dies of pleurisy is a martyr, the one who dies by burning is a martyr, and the woman who dies in childbirth is a martyr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Recite Yā Sīn over your dead."
This is the wording of Ibn al-ʿAlāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We buried someone who had died with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When we had finished, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned back and we turned back with him. When he was level with his door he stopped, and there was a woman coming towards us (he said: I think he recognized her). When she went away, it was Fāṭimah, peace be upon her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"What brought you out of your house, Fāṭimah?"
She said, "I came, O Messenger of Allah, to the people of this house, and I expressed my compassion for their deceased, or I offered them condolences for him."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"Perhaps you went with them as far as the kudā?"
She said, "I seek refuge in Allah! I have heard you mention about it what you mentioned." He said:
"If you had gone with them as far as the kudā..."
Then he mentioned a severe warning about that. I asked Rabīʿah about the kudā, and he said, "The graves, I think."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that the iron and leather [equipment] be removed from those killed at Uḥud, and that they be buried in their blood and their clothes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Ḥamzah on the day of Uḥud and stood over him, and saw that he had been mutilated. He said:
"If it were not that Ṣafiyyah would feel grief in her heart, I would leave him until the scavengers ate him and he was resurrected on the Day of Resurrection from their bellies."
He said: Then he called for a striped cloak and shrouded him in it. When it was pulled over his head, his feet showed, and when it was pulled over his feet, his head showed.
He said: The slain became many and the cloths few.
He said: So one man, two men, or three men would be shrouded in a single cloth and then buried in one grave. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would ask about them:
"Which of them knew more of the Qur'an?"
And he would put him forward towards the qiblah.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ buried them and did not pray over them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to me:
"Do not expose your thigh, and do not look at the thigh of anyone, living or dead."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shrouded in three garments of Najrān: a ḥullah consisting of two garments, and the shirt in which he died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We had carried the slain on the day of Uḥud in order to bury them, and the herald of the Prophet ﷺ came and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commands you to bury the slain where they fell." So we returned them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever prays the funeral prayer in the mosque, there is nothing [due] upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When you pray over the dead, make your supplication for him sincere."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer over a man of the Muslims, and I heard him say:
"O Allah, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, is in Your protection, so protect him from the trial of the grave."
ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān said:

"He is in Your protection and the bond of Your safeguard, so protect him from the trial of the grave and the punishment of the Fire. You are the One true to Your promise, and to You is praise. O Allah, forgive him and have mercy on him; indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful."
ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān said, from Marwān ibn Janāḥ [with this chain].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Breaking the bone of a dead person is like breaking the bone of a living person in sin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he saw
the grave of the Prophet ﷺ raised like a hump.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the wall collapsed upon them during the time of al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, they began rebuilding it,
and a foot appeared to them, and they were alarmed,

thinking that it was the foot of the Prophet ﷺ. They could find no one who knew about it until ʿUrwah said to them, "No, by Allah, it is not the foot of the Prophet ﷺ. It is only the foot of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: to ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr: "Bury me with my companions, and do not bury me with the Prophet ﷺ in the house,
for I dislike being held up as pure." And from Hishām, from his father: ʿUmar
sent word to ʿĀʾishah: "Permit me to be buried with my two companions." She said, "Yes, by Allah."
He said: Whenever any of the Companions sent a request to her, she would say, "No, by Allah, I will never prefer them over anyone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Lahab, may Allah's curse be upon him, said to the Prophet ﷺ, "May you perish for the rest of the day!"
Then was revealed: {Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I passed by al-Rabadhah and there was Abū
Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him. I said to him, "What brought you to this place of yours?" He said, "I was in Syria,
and Muʿāwiyah and I differed about those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the cause of Allah.
Muʿāwiyah said, 'It was revealed about the People of the Book.'
I said, 'It was revealed about us and them.'
So there was a dispute between him and me over that,
and he wrote to ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, complaining about me,
and ʿUthmān wrote to me to come to Medina.
I came to it, and people crowded around me as though they had never seen me before.
I mentioned that to ʿUthmān, and he said to me, 'If you wish, you may withdraw and stay nearby.'
That is what brought me to this place,
and even if they appointed an Abyssinian over me, I would listen and obey."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when two men came to him, one complaining of poverty,
and the other complaining of highway robbery.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"As for highway robbery, only a little time will pass before a caravan goes out to Mecca without a guard.
As for poverty, the Hour will not come until one of you goes around with his charity, finding no one to accept it from him.
Then each of you will stand before Allah, with no veil between him and Allah and no interpreter to translate for him,
and He will say to him, 'Did I not give you wealth?' He will say, 'Yes.'
Then He will say, 'Did I not send a messenger to you?' He will say, 'Yes.'
Then he will look to his right and see only the Fire,
then he will look to his left and see only the Fire.
So let each of you guard against the Fire, even with half a date,
and if he cannot find that, then with a good word."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Ask me."
But they were too awestruck to ask him.
Then a man came and sat down at his knees.
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is Islam?" He said,
"That you do not associate anything with Allah, that you establish prayer, give zakāh, and fast Ramaḍān." The man said, "You have spoken truly."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is faith?" He said,

"That you believe in Allah, His angels, His Book, the meeting with Him, and His messengers, and that you believe in the Resurrection and believe in the decree, all of it." The man said, "You have spoken truly."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is excellence (iḥsān)?" He said,
"That you fear Allah as though you see Him, for even if you do not see Him, He sees you." The man said, "You have spoken truly."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, when will the Hour come?" He said,

"The one being asked about it knows no more than the one asking. But I will tell you about its signs: when you see a woman give birth to her mistress, that is one of its signs; when you see the barefoot, the naked, the deaf and the dumb as the kings of the earth, that is one of its signs; and when you see the shepherds of sheep competing in constructing tall buildings, that is one of its signs. [It is] among five things of the unseen that none knows except Allah."

Then he recited: {Indeed, with Allah is the knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.} The narrator said: Then the man got up [and left], and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Bring him back to me."
They searched for him but did not find him. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"That was Jibrīl. He wanted you to learn, since you did not ask."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said this] on the pulpit, and he pointed with his two fingers to his ears: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,

"The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever guards against the doubtful matters has safeguarded his religion and his honor, and whoever falls into the doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd who grazes around a protected pasture, about to graze in it. Truly, every king has a protected pasture, and truly, the protected pasture of Allah is what He has forbidden. Truly, in the body there is a piece of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said,
"Tell me about a tree that resembles, or is like, a Muslim man: its leaves do not fall, and not, and not, and not,
and it yields its fruit at every season."
Ibn ʿUmar said: It came to my mind that it was the date palm,
but I saw Abū Bakr and ʿUmar not speaking,
so I disliked to speak.
When they said nothing, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "It is the date palm."
When we got up, I said to ʿUmar, "Dear father, by Allah, it had come to my mind that it was the date palm." He said, "What prevented you from speaking?" He said, "I did not see you speaking,
so I disliked to speak or say anything."
ʿUmar said, "For you to have said it would have been dearer to me than such and such."
label: machine translation

segments_en: […] ﷺ, while he was sitting in the mosque with the people around him, three men came forward. Two approached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and one went away.

He said: The two stood before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. One of them saw a gap in the circle and sat in it, while the other sat behind them, and the third turned away and left. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished, he said,

"Shall I not tell you about the three men? As for one of them, he took refuge with Allah, so Allah gave him refuge. As for the other, he felt shy, so Allah felt shy before him. And as for the other, he turned away, so Allah turned away from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew me close to him and said,
"O Allah, teach him wisdom."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came on a donkey. [Isnād switch:] And al-Qaʿnabī narrated to us, from Mālik,
from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: I came riding a she-donkey, and at that time I

had nearly reached puberty, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was leading the people in prayer at Minā. I passed in front of part of the row, then dismounted and let the donkey graze, and I entered the row, and no one objected to that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he claimed,
Maḥmūd, that he remembered the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said that he remembered a mouthful of water that he spat from a bucket that was in their house.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was asleep, I saw a cup brought to me with milk in it. I drank from it until I saw the satisfaction flowing in my fingernails. Then I gave the rest of mine to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb."
They said, "How did you interpret that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Knowledge."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to accept gifts and reward [the giver] for them.
Wakīʿ and Muḥāḍir did not mention [it] from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū az-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"My heirs shall not divide up a single dinar. Whatever I leave, after the maintenance of my wives and the wages of my worker, is charity (ṣadaqah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, establishes prayer, and fasts Ramadan,
it is a right upon Allah that He admit him to Paradise, whether he strives in the cause of Allah
or stays in the land in which he was born."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, should we not give the people this good news?" He said:
"In Paradise there are one hundred levels which Allah has prepared for those who strive in the cause of Allah.
The distance between any two levels is like the distance between the heavens and the earth.
So when you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws,
for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise.
I think that above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful,
and from it spring forth the rivers of Paradise."
Muḥammad ibn Fulayḥ said, from his father:
"And above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he came, he and Abū Ṭalḥah, with the Prophet ﷺ, and with the Prophet ﷺ was Ṣafiyyah, riding behind him on his mount.
When they were part of the way along the road, the she-camel stumbled,
and the Prophet ﷺ and the woman were thrown down.
Abū Ṭalḥah—I think he said—leapt down from his camel and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, may Allah make me your ransom,
has anything hurt you?" He said, "No,
but see to the woman."
So Abū Ṭalḥah threw his garment over his face,
and went straight to her and threw his garment over her, and the woman stood up.
Then he fastened the saddles on their mount for the two of them, and they mounted,
and they traveled on until, when they were at the outskirts of Madinah—or he said, when they overlooked Madinah—the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Returning, repenting, worshipping, praising our Lord."
And he kept saying it until he entered Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said— And [in another chain] ʿAmr an-Nāqid and Ḥasan al-Ḥulwānī narrated to us,
and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd,
ʿAbd said: He informed me; and the other two said:
Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, from al-Aʿraj,
who said: Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, Ghifār, Aslam, Muzaynah, and those of Juhaynah—or he said, Juhaynah and those of Muzaynah—are better with Allah on the Day of Resurrection than Asad, Ṭayyiʾ, and Ghaṭafān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Mahdī,
in his narration: Ibn Jurayj, from az-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah,
that the Prophet ﷺ died when he was sixty-three years old.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Prophet ﷺ gave him a dinar to buy a sheep with it,
and with it he bought two sheep for him.
He sold one of them for a dinar and came to him with a dinar and a sheep,
so [the Prophet ﷺ] prayed for blessing for him in his trading,
and [it was such that] had he bought dust, he would have made a profit in it.
Sufyān said: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmārah came to us with this ḥadīth from him,
he said: Shabīb heard it from ʿUrwah.
So I came to him, and Shabīb said, "I did not hear it from ʿUrwah,
I heard the tribe informing about him.
But I heard him say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection.'"
He said: And I saw in his house seventy horses.
Sufyān said: He was to buy a sheep for him, as if it were for sacrifice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: He informed us; and the others said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
who is Ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār,
that he heard Ibn ʿUmar
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is going to swear an oath, let him swear only by Allah."
Quraysh used to swear by their fathers, so he said:
"Do not swear by your fathers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Quraysh denied me, I stood up in the Ḥijr,
and Allah made Bayt al-Maqdis clear to me, so I began to inform them about its signs while I was looking at it."
Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm added: The son of my brother, Ibn Shihāb, narrated to us from his uncle:
"When Quraysh denied me when I was taken on the Night Journey to Bayt al-Maqdis," similar to it.
"Qāṣif" is a wind that shatters everything.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hilāl ibn Umayyah
accused his wife, in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, of [committing adultery] with Sharīk ibn Saḥmāʾ. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Bring proof, or [you will receive] the prescribed punishment on your back."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, if one of us saw a man with his wife, would he go off to look for proof?" But the Prophet ﷺ kept saying:
"Proof, or the prescribed punishment on your back."
Then he mentioned the hadith of the invocation of curses (liʿān).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ offered an oath to a group of people, and they hastened to take it,
so he ordered that lots be drawn among them as to which of them would swear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ mentioned from ʿAbdullāh, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever is going to swear an oath, let him swear by Allah or else remain silent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] to him: "I asked you what he commands you, and you claimed that he commands you to pray, to be truthful, to be chaste, to fulfil covenants, and to return trusts."
He said, "This is the description of a prophet."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jew from the people of al-Ḥīrah asked me, "Which of the two terms did Moses fulfil?" I said, "I do not know until I go to the great scholar of the Arabs and ask him." So I went,
and I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said, "He fulfilled the longer and the better of the two,
for when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said [he would do] something, he did it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O assembly of Muslims, how can you ask the People of the Book about anything, when your Book, which Allah revealed to your Prophet ﷺ, is the most recent of the reports from Allah, pure and unadulterated? Allah has told you that the People of the Book altered what Allah had written and changed it, and wrote the book with their own hands,
saying, 'This is from Allah,'
in order to sell it for a small price.
Does the knowledge that has come to you not forbid you from asking them?
No, by Allah, we have never seen any of them ask you about what was revealed to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was informed of that, and he said:
"Go with us so that we may make peace between them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ performed ʿUmrah in Dhū al-Qaʿdah,
the people of Makkah refused to let him enter Makkah,
until he made an agreement with them that he would stay there three days.
When they wrote the document, they wrote:
"This is what Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to."
They said, "We do not accept this.
If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not prevent you from anything,
but you are Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh." He said:
"I am the Messenger of Allah,
and I am Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh."
Then he said to ʿAlī:
"Erase 'the Messenger of Allah.'"
ʿAlī said, "No, by Allah, I will never erase you."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the document,
though he did not write well,
and wrote: "This is what Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh has agreed to: no weapons will be brought into Makkah,
except swords in their sheaths,
and none of its people will be taken out with him,
even if he wishes to follow him,
and he will not prevent any of his Companions
who wishes to remain there."
When he entered it and the term had passed, they came to ʿAlī and said, "Tell your companion to leave us,
for the term has passed."
So the Prophet ﷺ left, and the daughter of Ḥamzah followed him, calling, "O uncle! O uncle!" ʿAlī took her,
took her by the hand, and said to Fāṭimah, peace be upon her, "Take your cousin."
She carried her. Then ʿAlī, Zayd and Jaʿfar disputed over her.
ʿAlī said, "I took her, and she is my cousin."
Jaʿfar said, "She is my cousin, and her maternal aunt is my wife."
Zayd said, "She is my brother's daughter."
The Prophet ﷺ ruled that she go to her maternal aunt, and said:
"The maternal aunt has the status of the mother." And he said to ʿAlī:
"You are from me and I am from you." And he said to Jaʿfar:
"You resemble me in my physical form and my character." And he said to Zayd:
"You are our brother and our freed man."
ʿAlī said, "Will you not marry the daughter of Ḥamzah?" He said:
"She is the daughter of my brother by nursing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah, the Prophet ﷺ made peace with the polytheists on three conditions: that whoever came to him from the polytheists he would return to them,
and whoever came to them from the Muslims they would not return,
and that he would enter [Makkah] the following year and stay there three days,
and would not enter it except with the sheathed weapons, the sword, the bow and the like.
Then Abū Jandal came hobbling in his shackles, and he returned him to them.
He said: Muʾammal did not mention Abū Jandal from Sufyān, and said, "except with the sheathed weapons."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out intending ʿUmrah,
but the disbelievers of Quraysh stood between him and the House. So he slaughtered his sacrificial animal
and shaved his head at al-Ḥudaybiyah,
and he agreed with them that he would perform ʿUmrah the following year,
and would not carry weapons against them except swords,
and would not stay there except for as long as they wished.
So he performed ʿUmrah the following year,
and entered it as he had agreed with them.
When he had stayed there three days, they ordered him to leave, and he left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever attends a funeral until he prays over the deceased will have one qīrāṭ, and whoever attends until the burial will have two qīrāṭs."
It was asked, "What are the two qīrāṭs?" He said:
"Like two great mountains."

The report of Abū al-Ṭāhir ends here, and the other two added: Ibn Shihāb said that Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: Ibn ʿUmar used to pray over the deceased and then leave. When the hadith of Abū Hurayrah reached him, he said, "We have lost many qīrāṭs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
stood up in the mosque and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
from where do you command us to enter the state of iḥrām?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people of Madinah enter iḥrām from Dhū al-Ḥulayfah,
the people of Syria from al-Juḥfah,
and the people of Najd from Qarn."
Ibn ʿUmar said: They claim that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"And the people of Yemen enter iḥrām from Yalamlam."
Ibn ʿUmar used to say, "I did not learn this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the lavatory—Ḥammād reported that he said:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You."
And ʿAbd al-Wārith reported that he said:
"I seek refuge in Allah from the male and female evil beings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ liked to begin with the right side as much as he could, in his purification, in putting on his sandals, and in combing his hair.
And in Wāsiṭ, before this, he said: in all his affairs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about game caught by a trained dog. He said:
"If you send your trained dog and mention the name of Allah, eat what it catches for you. But if it eats [from it], do not eat, for it caught it only for itself."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what if our dogs mix with other dogs?" He said:
"You mentioned the name of Allah only over your dog, and did not mention it over the other."
Sufyān said: I dislike for him to eat it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"If one of you feels drowsy during prayer, let him sleep until the sleepiness leaves him, for if one of you prays while drowsy, perhaps he will intend to seek forgiveness but instead curse himself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a young son of hers who had not yet reached the age of eating food. ʿUbayd Allāh said: She told me that her son urinated in the lap of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for water and sprinkled it over his garment, and did not wash it thoroughly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAbdah,
and Abū Muʿāwiyah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: Fāṭimah bint Abī Ḥubaysh came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am a woman who has prolonged bleeding and I do not become pure. Should I give up prayer?" He said:
"No. That is only a vein, and it is not menstruation. When your menstruation comes, leave the prayer, and when it ends, wash the blood off yourself and pray."
Abū Muʿāwiyah said in his narration that he also said:
"Perform ablution for every prayer until that time comes [again]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet
ﷺ and I used to bathe from one vessel after sexual impurity.
And from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to go around to his wives in a single hour of the night or day,
and they were eleven.
[Qatādah] said: I asked Anas, "Was he able to do that?" He said, "We used to say that he was given the strength of thirty."
And Saʿīd reported from Qatādah that Anas told them [they were] nine wives.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And al-Awzāʿī,
and Abū Maʿīd—who is Ḥafṣ ibn Ghaylān—from al-Zuhrī,
who said: ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me,
and ʿAmrah bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah,

who said: Umm Ḥabībah bint Jaḥsh, the wife of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and the sister of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, experienced prolonged bleeding. She asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"This is not menstruation, but a vein. When the menstruation ends, bathe and pray, and when it comes, leave prayer during it."

ʿĀʾishah said: So she would bathe for every prayer and pray. Sometimes she would bathe in a large basin in the room of her sister Zaynab, who was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until the redness of the blood rose above the water. Then she would go out and pray with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that did not stop her from praying.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, concerning the expedition of Tabūk, and he said in it: "Then a messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me and said, 'Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ...'" And Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd informed me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Yūnus, who said: Ibn Shihāb said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik said: I heard Kaʿb ibn Mālik narrating his account of when he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the expedition of Tabūk, and he related his story, and he said: "Then a messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said, 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commands you to keep away from your wife.'
I said, 'Should I divorce her, or what?' He said, 'No, rather keep away from her and do not approach her.'
So I said to my wife, 'Go to your family and stay with them until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decides this matter.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:

"Indeed Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, never lied except three times: two of them for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, namely his saying, 'Indeed I am sick,' and his saying, 'Rather, this biggest one of them did it.' And while he was travelling in the land of one of the tyrants, he stopped at a place, and the tyrant was told, 'A man has stopped here with a woman who is the most beautiful of people.' He sent for him and asked him about her, and he said, 'She is my sister.'

Then when he returned to her, he said, 'This man asked me about you, and I told him that you are my sister, and today there is no believer on earth other than me and you, and you are my sister in the Book of Allah, so do not contradict me before him.'" And he related the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came as a Muslim in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and then his wife came as a Muslim, and he said, "O Messenger of Allah, she accepted Islam with me, so return her to me." So he returned her to him.
This is a sound hadith.
I heard ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd
say: I heard Yazīd ibn Hārūn
mention, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq,
this hadith and the hadith of al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather,
that the Prophet ﷺ returned his daughter Zaynab to Abū al-ʿĀṣ with a new dowry and a new marriage.
Yazīd ibn Hārūn said: The hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās has the better chain of narration.
And the practice is according to the hadith of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Salmā, a freed slave from the people of Madinah and a truthful man, said: While I was sitting with Abū Hurayrah, a Persian woman came to him with a son of hers, and they both claimed him, her husband having divorced her. She said, "O Abū Hurayrah," and she spoke to him in Persian, "my husband wants to take my son away." Abū Hurayrah said, "Draw lots over him," and he spoke to her in Persian to that effect. Then her husband came and said, "Who disputes with me over my son?" Abū Hurayrah said, "O Allah, I say this only because I heard a woman come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while I was sitting with him, and she said, 'O Messenger of Allah, my husband wants to take my son away, though he gives me water to drink from the well of Abū ʿInabah and he benefits me.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Draw lots over him."
Her husband said, "Who disputes with me over my son?" The Prophet ﷺ said,
"This is your father and this is your mother, so take the hand of whichever of them you wish."
So he took his mother's hand, and she went away with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning His saying, {Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it}, and He said, {And when We substitute one verse in place of another, and Allah knows best what He sends down}, the verse; and He said, {Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book}. The first thing abrogated of the Qurʾān was the direction of prayer. And He said, {Divorced women shall wait by themselves for three monthly periods}, and He said, {And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you doubt, their waiting period is three months}. Part of that was abrogated; the Exalted said, {If you divorce them before you have touched them}, {then you have no waiting period to count against them}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Marwān and said to him, "A woman of your family was divorced, and I passed by her while she was moving out. She said, 'Fāṭimah bint Qays commanded us, and informed us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded her to move out.'"
Marwān said, "She is the one who commanded them to do that."
ʿUrwah said: I said, "By Allah, ʿĀʾishah disapproved of that and said, 'Fāṭimah was in a desolate dwelling and was feared for, and for that reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave her a concession.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulating the Kaʿbah and saying:

"How pleasant you are, and how pleasant is your fragrance! How great you are, and how great is your sanctity! By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the sanctity of the believer is greater in the sight of Allah than your sanctity: his property and his blood, and that we think of him nothing but good."
