Then it will be said, 'O Muhammad, admit into Paradise those of your Ummah who have no reckoning against them, through the right-hand gate of the gates of Paradise. And they share with the other people in the rest of the gates. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between the two leaves of a gate of Paradise is like the distance between Makkah and Hajar,' or, 'like the distance between Makkah and Buṣrā.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw a man ask al-Aswad ibn Yazīd, while he was teaching the Qur'an in the mosque, "How do you recite this verse: 'fa-hal min muddakir'—with a dāl or a dhāl?" He said, "With a dāl. I heard ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, 'muddakir'" with a dāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"O Allah, Abraham was Your close friend and Your prophet, and You made Makkah sacred on the tongue of Abraham. O Allah, I am Your servant and Your prophet, and I declare sacred what lies between its two lābahs."
Abū Marwān said: "Its two lābahs" means the two lava fields of Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first day I witnessed [with the Prophet ﷺ] was the Day of the Trench.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went in to see Ḥafṣah, while her braided hair was dripping,
and I said, "You see what has happened among the people,
and no part of the matter has been given to me."
She said, "Go to them, for they are waiting for you,
and I fear that your staying away from them may cause a split."
She did not leave him alone until he went.
When the people dispersed, Muʿāwiyah gave a sermon and said, "Whoever wishes to speak about this matter, let him show us his horn,
for we are more deserving of it than he and his father."

Ḥabīb ibn Maslamah said, "Why did you not answer him?" ʿAbdullāh said, "I loosened my wrap and was about to say, 'The one more deserving of this matter than you is the one who fought you and your father over Islam.'
But I feared that I would say a word that would divide the community and shed blood,
and that something other than what I meant would be attributed to me,
so I remembered what Allah has prepared in the gardens of Paradise."
Ḥabīb said, "You were protected and guarded."
Maḥmūd, from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, said: "and her braids."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the confederates had withdrawn from him, [he said:]
"Now we will raid them and they will not raid us;
we will march against them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ led his Companions in the prayer of fear in the seventh campaign, the campaign of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ prayed the prayer of fear at Dhū Qarad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ﷺ prayed with them on the day of Muḥārib and Thaʿlabah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went out to Dhāt al-Riqāʿ from Nakhl and met a group of Ghaṭafān,
but there was no fighting,
and the people were afraid of one another, so the Prophet ﷺ prayed the two rakʿahs of fear.
Yazīd said, from Salamah: I fought with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of al-Qarad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ at Nakhl.
Then he mentioned the prayer of fear.
Mālik said: That is the best of what I have heard about the prayer of fear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ at Nakhl, and he prayed the prayer of fear.
Abū Hurayrah said: I prayed the prayer of fear with the Prophet ﷺ during the campaign of Najd.
Abū Hurayrah only came to the Prophet ﷺ in the days of Khaybar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hishām ibn Yūsuf dictated to me from memory: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī,
who said: Al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said to me, "Has it reached you that ʿAlī
was among those who slandered ʿĀʾishah?" I said, "No.

But two men of your people, Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, informed me that ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, told them that ʿAlī was submissive [to her innocence] in her affair."
They questioned him again, but he did not retract and said, "Submissive, without doubt," and so it was in the original old copy.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-walaq means lying.
Ibn Abī Mulaykah said: She knew more about that than others, because [revelation] was sent down about her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [I said] to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, "It has reached me that Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh
used to say that they were fourteen hundred."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was one of the people of the Tree. [The Prophet ﷺ said:] "The righteous will be taken one after another,
and there will remain dregs like the dregs of dates and barley,
to whom Allah pays no regard at all."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, to the market,
and a young woman met ʿUmar and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, my husband has died and left small children,
and by Allah, they cannot even cook a trotter,
and they have no crops and no livestock,
and I fear that the hyena will eat them,
and I am the daughter of Khufāf ibn Īmāʾ al-Ghifārī,
and my father witnessed al-Ḥudaybiyah with the Prophet ﷺ."
ʿUmar stopped with her and did not go on,
then he said, "Welcome to a close kinship."
Then he turned to a strong camel that was tied up in the house,
and loaded onto it two large sacks filled with food,
and placed between them money and clothing,
then handed her its halter and said, "Lead it away, for it will not run out before Allah brings you good."
A man said, "O Commander of the Faithful, you have given her too much."
ʿUmar said, "May your mother lose you!
By Allah, I can see that this woman's father and brother besieged a fortress for a long time and then conquered it,
and then we found ourselves seeking their share of it as spoils."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Tree was mentioned in the presence of Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, and he laughed and said, "My father informed me, and he had witnessed it,
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said, "Blessed are you! You accompanied the Prophet ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him under the Tree."
He said, "O son of my brother, you do not know what we did after him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḥudaybiyah.

His Companions said, "Congratulations, may it be wholesome! But what is there for us?" So Allah revealed: {That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens...} Shuʿbah said: I came to Kufa and narrated all of this from Qatādah, then I returned and mentioned it to him, and he said, "As for {Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory}, it is from Anas,
and as for 'Congratulations, may it be wholesome,' it is from ʿIkrimah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you is afflicted with fever, for fever is a piece of the Fire, let him extinguish it with water. Let him go down into a flowing river, facing the direction of the current, and say: 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, heal Your servant and confirm the truth of Your Messenger,' after the dawn prayer and before sunrise. Let him immerse himself in it three times for three days. If he is not cured in three, then five; if not cured in five, then seven; if not cured in seven, then nine, for it hardly ever lasts beyond nine days, by the permission of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The likeness of the sick person when he recovers and becomes healthy is only that of a hailstone falling from the sky in its purity and its color."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Learn the Qur'an and the laws of inheritance, and teach them to the people, for I am going to be taken away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the grandmother together with her son: she was the first grandmother to whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a sixth together with her son, while her son was still alive.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The maternal uncle is the heir of one who has no heir."
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith, and some of them transmitted it as mursal without mentioning ʿĀʾishah in it.

The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ differed about this. Some of them gave inheritance to the maternal uncle, the maternal aunt, and the paternal aunt, and most of the people of knowledge hold to this hadith regarding inheritance for blood relatives. As for Zayd ibn Thābit, he did not give them inheritance and placed the estate in the public treasury.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A freed slave
of the Prophet ﷺ fell from the branch of a date palm and died. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Look whether he has any heir." They said, "No." He said:
"Then give it to one of the people of the village."
This is a ḥasan hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The killer does not inherit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever inherits wealth inherits the right of walāʾ (patronage)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his sermon in the year of the Farewell Hajj say:

"Allah has given every rightful person his due, so there is no bequest for an heir. The child belongs to the marriage bed, and for the adulterer is the stone, and their reckoning is with Allah. Whoever claims to be the son of someone other than his father, or attributes himself to other than his masters, upon him is the curse of Allah, continuing until the Day of Resurrection. A woman must not spend from her husband's house except with her husband's permission."
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, not even food?" He said:
"That is the best of our wealth." Then he said:
"A loan must be returned, a gifted animal must be returned, a debt must be paid, and the guarantor is liable."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ruled that the debt is paid before the bequest, whereas you recite the bequest before the debt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were disputing about the divine decree. He became angry until his face turned red, as if pomegranate seeds had been split open on his cheeks, and he said:
"Were you commanded to do this, or was I sent to you for this? Those before you were destroyed only when they disputed about this matter. I adjure you not to dispute about it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of what we do: is it something newly begun, or is it something already decided?" He said:

"It is something already decided, O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, and everyone is facilitated. As for one who is of the people of happiness, he works for happiness; and as for one who is of the people of misery, he works for misery."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us with two books in his hand and said:
"Do you know what these two books are?"
We said, "No, O Messenger of Allah, unless you tell us."
He said about the one in his right hand:

"This is a book from the Lord of the worlds. In it are the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and their tribes. Then it was totaled up at the end of them, so nothing will ever be added to them or taken away from them."
Then he said about the one in his left hand:

"This is a book from the Lord of the worlds. In it are the names of the people of the Fire, the names of their fathers and their tribes. Then it was totaled up at the end of them, so nothing will ever be added to them or taken away from them."
His Companions said, "Then what is the point of acting, O Messenger of Allah, if the matter has already been decided?" He said:

"Aim straight and stay close, for the one destined for Paradise will have his life sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, whatever deeds he may have done, and the one destined for the Fire will have his life sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire, whatever deeds he may have done."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a gesture with his hands and cast the two books aside, and then he said:
"Your Lord has finished with the servants: one group in Paradise and one group in the Blaze."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that
ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit was visited while he was staying on the coast of Ḥimṣ,
in a building of his, and Umm Ḥarām was with him.
ʿUmayr said: Umm Ḥarām told us that she heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "
The first army of my Ummah to campaign by sea will have earned [Paradise]."
Umm Ḥarām said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, am I among them?" He said, "You are among them."
Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "
The first army of my Ummah to attack the city of Caesar will be forgiven."
I said, "Am I among them, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "No."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to Caesar, and said: "
But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the Arīsiyyīn [the peasants]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to Caesar, calling him to Islam,
and sent his letter to him with Diḥyah al-Kalbī,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to hand it to the governor of Buṣrā so that he would pass it to Caesar.
When Allah had driven the armies of Persia away from him, Caesar had walked from Ḥimṣ to Īliyā (Jerusalem),
in thanks for what Allah had bestowed upon him.
So when the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached Caesar, he said when he read it: "Look for me someone here from his people, so that I may ask them about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never intended an expedition without concealing it by referring to another.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rarely intended an expedition without concealing it by referring to another,
until the expedition of Tabūk,
which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ undertook in intense heat,
facing a long journey and desert,
and facing a numerous enemy.
So he made the matter clear to the Muslims,
so that they could prepare for their enemy,
and he informed them of the direction he intended.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: We returned the following year, and not even two of us agreed on the tree under which we had pledged allegiance;
it was a mercy from Allah.
I asked Nāfiʿ: For what did he take their pledge? For death? He said: No,
he took their pledge for steadfastness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh, may Allah be pleased with him, said: A man came to me today and asked me about a matter I did not know how to answer.
He said: Tell me about a man who is dutiful and energetic,
who goes out with our commanders on military expeditions,
and they impose on us things we cannot count.
I said to him: By Allah, I do not know what to say to you, except that we were with the Prophet ﷺ, and perhaps he would impose a matter on us only once until we did it.
And one of you will continue to be well as long as he fears Allah,
and if any doubt arises in himself, he asks a man, who cures him of it,
and it is likely that you will not find such a man.
By the One besides Whom there is no god, I do not see what remains of this world except like a pool of rainwater whose clear part has been drunk and whose murky part remains.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that Qays ibn Saʿd al-Anṣārī, may Allah be pleased with him, who was the bearer of the banner of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, wished to perform Hajj, so he combed [and oiled] his hair.

then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and when he finished reading the letter, there was much clamor in his presence, voices rose, and we were taken out.
I said to my companions when we were taken out: The affair of Ibn Abī Kabshah has become great,
for the king of the Banū al-Aṣfar fears him.

segments_en: I prepared the provisions bag of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the house of Abū Bakr when he intended to emigrate to Medina.
She said: We found nothing with which to tie the provisions bag or the water skin,
so I said to Abū Bakr: By Allah, I find nothing to tie with except my waist-belt.
He said: Then split it in two,
and tie the water skin with one and the provisions bag with the other. So I did,
and for that reason I was called Dhāt an-Niṭāqayn (She of the Two Waist-belts).
label: machine translation

and they were crying out with both together: Hajj and ʿUmrah.

on a packsaddle covered with a Fadakī woolen cloak,
and he seated Usāmah behind him.

segments_en: When we went up, we would say "Allāhu akbar,"
and when we went down, we would say "Subḥān Allāh."

segments_en: I was sitting in a circle in the mosque of Madinah. Among them was an elder of fine appearance, ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām. He began to narrate to them a fine account. When he got up, the people said, "Whoever would like to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man."
I said, "By Allah, I will follow him and find out where his house is."

So I followed him, and he walked until he was almost out of Madinah, then entered his house. I asked permission to enter and he let me in. He said, "What do you need, my nephew?" I said to him, "I heard the people say about you, when you got up, 'Whoever would like to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man.'
I would like to be with you." He said, "Allah knows best who the people of Paradise are. But I will tell you why they said that. While I was sleeping, a man came to me and said to me, 'Get up.'

He took me by the hand and I went with him. Suddenly I was before paths on my left. I went to take one of them, but he said to me, 'Do not take them, for those are the paths of the people of the left.' Then there was a clear, broad road on my right, and he said to me, 'Take this one.'

He brought me to a mountain and said to me, 'Climb.' Whenever I tried to climb, I fell on my backside. I did that many times. Then he went on with me until he brought me to a pillar whose top was in the sky and whose base was on the earth, and at its top was a ring. He said to me,
'Climb up above this.'

I said, 'How can I climb this when its top is in the sky?' So he took me by the hand and heaved me up, and suddenly I was hanging on to the ring. Then he struck the pillar and it fell, and I remained hanging on to the ring until morning. I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about it, and he said:

'As for the paths you saw on your left, they are the paths of the people of the left. As for the paths you saw on your right, they are the paths of the people of the right. As for the mountain, it is the abode of the martyrs, and you will not reach it. As for the pillar, it is the pillar of Islam. And as for the ring, it is the ring of Islam. You will remain holding fast to it until you die.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "Does Abū Hurayrah not amaze you? He came and sat beside my room, narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while making me hear it, and I was engaged in voluntary prayer. He got up before I finished my prayer. "You have lied. He will not enter it, for he took part in Badr and Ḥudaybiyah."

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I hope, Allah willing, that no one who took part in Badr and Ḥudaybiyah will enter the Fire."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of my Ummah is the generation in which I was sent, then those who follow them."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"May the nose of a man be rubbed in dust in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me; may the nose of a man be rubbed in dust who lives through Ramadan and it passes before he is forgiven; and may the nose of a man be rubbed in dust whose parents reach old age with him and they do not cause him to enter Paradise."

segments_en: I stayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah for a year. Nothing kept me from emigrating except [my wish to ask] questions: when one of us emigrated, he would not ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about anything. I asked him about righteousness and sin, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"O people, keep to calmness, for righteousness does not lie in rushing the horses and camels."
He said: I did not see her raise her forelegs, running, until he reached Jamʿ.
Wahb added: Then he had al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās ride behind him, and he said:
"O people, righteousness does not lie in rushing the horses and camels, so keep to calmness."

He said: "There was no part of the month in which you would want to see him fasting but that you would see him [fasting], nor [a part in which you would want to see him] not fasting but that you would see him [so];
nor [would you want to see him] standing in prayer at night but that you would see him [so];
nor sleeping but that you would see him [so].

segments_en: I went out with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) one night in Ramadan to the mosque,
and the people were scattered in separate groups; a man would pray by himself,
and a man would pray and a group would pray following his prayer. ʿUmar said: "I think that if I gather these people behind one reciter, it would be better."
Then he resolved to do so and gathered them behind Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
Then I went out with him another night,
and the people were praying behind their reciter. ʿUmar said:
"What an excellent innovation this is!
But the [part of the night] in which they sleep is better than the one in which they stand in prayer."
He meant the last part of the night,
while the people used to pray at the beginning of it.

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Tonight I saw two men who came to me
and took me out to a sacred land.
We set off until we came to a river of blood in which a man was standing,
and in the middle of the river was a man with stones in front of him.
The man in the river came forward, and whenever he wanted to get out, the other man would throw a stone into his mouth and send him back to where he had been.
Every time he came to get out, [the man] would throw a stone into his mouth,
and he would return as he was.
I said: 'What is this?' He said: 'The one you saw in the river is the one who consumed ribā (usury).'"

segments_en: I sat among a group of the poor Emigrants, some of whom were hiding behind others because of their lack of clothing, while a reciter was reciting to us. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and stood over us. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood there, the reciter fell silent. He greeted us with salām and then said:
"What were you doing?"
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, we had a reciter who was reciting to us, and we were listening to the Book of Allah."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said:
"Praise be to Allah, Who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient."

He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat down in the middle of us, so as to be level with us, and then he gestured with his hand like this, and they formed a circle, and their faces turned toward him. He said: I did not see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recognize any of them but me.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Rejoice, O company of the poor Emigrants, in the perfect light on the Day of Resurrection! You will enter Paradise before the wealthy people by half a day, and that is five hundred years."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying during Ramaḍān. I came and stood beside him, and another man came and stood too, until we were a small group. When the Prophet ﷺ sensed that we were behind him, he began to shorten the prayer. Then he went into his tent and prayed a prayer that he did not pray with us.
He said: When morning came, we said to him: Did you notice us last night? He said:
"Yes, that is what made me do what I did."

He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to fast continuously without breaking the fast at night, and that was at the end of the month. Some of his Companions began to do the same, so the Prophet ﷺ said:

"What is the matter with men who fast continuously? You are not like me. By Allah, if the month were extended for me, I would fast continuously in such a way that those who go to extremes would abandon their extremism."

segments_en: That Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq
wrote for him: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

This is the obligation of charity (ṣadaqah) which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made obligatory upon the Muslims, and which Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to impose. Regarding the ages of camels within the obligations for livestock: whoever owes, from his camels, the charity of a jadhaʿah but does not have a jadhaʿah and has a ḥiqqah, the ḥiqqah is to be accepted from him, and he is to add in its place two sheep, if they are easily available, or twenty dirhams. Whoever owes the charity of a ḥiqqah but has only a bint labūn, the bint labūn is to be accepted from him, and he gives along with it two sheep or twenty dirhams. Whoever owes a bint labūn but does not have one and has a ḥiqqah, the ḥiqqah is to be accepted from him, and the collector gives him twenty dirhams or two sheep. Whoever owes a bint labūn but does not have one and has a bint makhāḍ, the bint makhāḍ is to be accepted from him, and he gives along with it twenty dirhams or two sheep.

Whoever owes a bint makhāḍ but does not have one and has a bint labūn, the bint labūn is to be accepted from him, and the collector gives him twenty dirhams or two sheep. And whoever does not have a bint makhāḍ of the proper kind but has a male ibn labūn, it is to be accepted from him, and nothing further is due with it.

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the expedition of Tabūk, and we came to Wādī al-Qurā at a garden belonging to a woman. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Estimate its yield."
So we estimated it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ estimated it at ten wasqs. He said to her:
"Keep count of it until we return to you, Allah willing."
We set out until we reached Tabūk, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Tonight a violent wind will blow upon you, so none of you should stand up in it, and whoever has a camel should tie its hobble tightly."

A violent wind blew, and a man stood up and the wind carried him until it threw him onto the two mountains of Ṭayyiʾ. The envoy of Ibn al-ʿUlamāʾ, the ruler of Aylah, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a letter and presented him with a white mule, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to him and presented him with a cloak. Then we came back until we reached Wādī al-Qurā, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked the woman about her garden:
"How much did its fruit reach?"
She said: "Ten wasqs."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I am going to hurry on, so whoever of you wishes may hurry with me, and whoever wishes may stay."
So we set out until we overlooked Madīnah, and he said:
"This is Ṭābah, and this is Uḥud, a mountain that loves us and that we love." Then he said:

"The best of the houses of the Anṣār is the house of Banū an-Najjār, then the house of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, then the house of Banū ʿAbd al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, then the house of Banū Sāʿidah; and in all the houses of the Anṣār there is good."
Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah caught up with us, and Abū Usayd said: "Have you not seen that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ranked the houses of the Anṣār and placed us last?"
Saʿd caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you ranked the houses of the Anṣār and placed us last." He said:
"Is it not enough for you to be among the best?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Dates used to be brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the time of the date harvest; this one would come with his dates and that one with his dates, until they became a heap of dates in his presence.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, began playing with those dates,
and one of them took a date
and put it in his mouth.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at him and took it out of his mouth, and said:
"Do you not know that the family of Muhammad ﷺ do not eat charity?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, should we not go out and fight in jihad with you? For I do not see any deed in the Qur'an better than jihad." He said:
"No, but the best and most beautiful jihad is Hajj to the House, an accepted Hajj."

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate during prayer:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the False Messiah, the Dajjāl,
and I seek refuge in You from the trial of life and the trial of death.
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sin and from debt."
Someone said to him, "How often you seek refuge from debt!" He said:
"When a man falls into debt, he speaks and lies, and he promises and breaks his promise." And from az-Zuhrī, who said:
ʿUrwah informed me
that ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking refuge in his prayer from the trial of the Dajjāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The scribe of al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah said: Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah dictated to me, in a letter to Muʿāwiyah, that the Prophet ﷺ used to say at the end of every obligatory prayer:
"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise,
and He has power over all things.
O Allah, none can withhold what You give,
and none can give what You withhold,
and the fortune of the fortunate cannot benefit him against You."
Shuʿbah said, from ʿAbd al-Malik, the same,
and from al-Ḥakam, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Warrād, the same.
Al-Ḥasan said: al-jadd means wealth.

from Ibn ʿUmar, that ʿUmar

ibn al-Khaṭṭāb saw a silk-striped garment at the door of the mosque and said, "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would buy this and wear it for the people on Friday and for the delegations when they come to you."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Only one who has no share in the Hereafter wears this."

Then some garments of this kind came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave one of them to ʿUmar. ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have clothed me with it, though you said about the garment of ʿUṭārid what you said?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

So ʿUmar gave it to a brother of his in Makkah who was a polytheist.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on the pulpit and we sat around him, and he said:
"Among the things I fear for you after me is what will be opened up to you of the blossom of this world and its adornment."

A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, can good bring about evil?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent. It was said to the man, "What is the matter with you? You speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he does not speak to you." We saw that revelation was coming down upon him. Then he recovered, wiping the sweat from himself, and said:

"Where is the questioner?" And it was as if he approved of him. Then he said: "Good does not bring about evil. Indeed, among what the spring rain makes grow is what kills or nearly kills, except for the animal that eats the green plants: it eats until, when its flanks are full, it faces the sun, passes dung and urine, then goes back to graze. This wealth is green and sweet, and an excellent companion is it for the Muslim, if he gives from it to the poor, the orphan, and the wayfarer" or as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "but whoever takes it without its right is like one who eats and is never satisfied, and it will be a witness against him on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Abū Ṭālib was approaching death, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and found with him Abū Jahl and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Umayyah ibn al-Mughīrah. He said:
"Uncle, say: 'There is no god but Allah,'
a word with which I will plead for you before Allah."
Abū Jahl and ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Umayyah said, "Do you turn away from the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept presenting it to him,
and the two kept repeating that statement to him, until the last thing Abū Ṭālib said to them was that he was on the religion of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib,
and he refused to say, "There is no god but Allah."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By Allah, I will surely ask forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden to do so."
Then Allah revealed: {It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists}, and Allah revealed concerning Abū Ṭālib,
and He said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: {Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.}
Ibn ʿAbbās said: {Those of strength}: a group of men could not lift it. {Would weigh down}: would burden.
{Empty}: except for the remembrance of Moses. {The exultant}: the boastful.
{Follow him}: follow his trail,
and it can also mean relating a account, as in {We relate to you}.
{From a distance}: from afar; ʿan junub and ʿan janābah are the same,
and also ʿan ijtināb. Yabṭishu and yabṭushu [are both used]. {They are conspiring}: they are consulting one another.
ʿUdwān, ʿadāʾ, and taʿaddī are the same. {I perceived}: I saw.
Al-jadhwah is a thick piece of wood
that has no flame,
whereas a shihāb has a flame.
The snakes are of the kinds of jinn: vipers and black snakes. {A helper}: an aid.
Ibn ʿAbbās read {confirm me}. Another said: {We will strengthen}: we will support you; whenever you strengthen something, you have made an arm for it. Maqbūḥīn: destroyed.
{We have connected}: We made it clear and completed it.
{Is brought}: is carried. {Became insolent}: became arrogant.
{In its mother, a messenger}: the Mother of the Towns is Makkah and what surrounds it. {Conceal}: hide.
Aknantu al-shayʾ means I hid it,
and kanantuhu means I hid it and [also] I made it apparent.
{Wayka-nna Allah} is like "Do you not see that Allah {extends provision to whom He wills and restricts}": He gives abundance to him and narrows it for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"A man will keep asking people until he comes on the Day of Resurrection with not a piece of flesh on his face."
And he said: "On the Day of Resurrection the sun will come near until sweat reaches half of the ear,
and while they are in that state, they will seek help from Adam, then from Moses, then from Muhammad ﷺ."
ʿAbdullāh added: Al-Layth narrated to me, Ibn Abī Jaʿfar narrated to me:
"He will intercede so that judgment is passed among the creation,
and he will walk until he takes hold of the ring of the door,
and on that day Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station,
all the people of the gathering will praise him."

segments_en: ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, came to the Prophet ﷺ from Yemen, and he said, "For what did you declare your intention?"

Muḥammad ibn Bakr added, from Ibn Jurayj, that the Prophet ﷺ said to him:

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said:

"Whoever has a need from Allah or from any of His creation, let him perform ablution, pray two units, and then say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the things that make Your mercy certain, and the resolute means of Your forgiveness, and a share of every good deed, and safety from every sin. I ask You not to leave any sin of mine except that You forgive it, nor any distress except that You relieve it, nor any need with which You are pleased except that You fulfil it for me.' Then let him ask Allah for whatever he wishes of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, for He is able to do it."

from Ibn ʿAbbās,

who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I saw myself last night while I was asleep, as if I were praying behind a tree. I prostrated, and the tree prostrated at my prostration, and I heard it say: O Allah, record for me a reward with You because of it, remove from me a burden because of it, make it a stored treasure for me with You, and accept it from me as You accepted it from Your servant Dāwūd.'
Al-Ḥasan said: Ibn Jurayj said to me: Your grandfather said to me: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ recited a verse of prostration and then prostrated.
He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: I heard him saying the same as what the man had reported from the tree's words."

segments_en: He stopped at Tabūk while on Hajj, and there was a man who was crippled. He asked him about his condition, and the man said to him: I will tell you a hadith, but do not narrate it as long as you hear that I am alive. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at Tabūk by a palm tree and said, "This is our qiblah."
Then he prayed toward it. I came running, being a boy, until I passed between him and it. He said:
"He has cut off our prayer; may Allah cut off his trace."
I have not been able to stand on them [my feet] to this day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We descended with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the pass of Adhākhir, and the time for prayer came. He prayed facing a wall, taking it as his qiblah, while we were behind him. A lamb came and tried to pass in front of him, and he kept blocking it until his belly was pressed against the wall, and it passed behind him.
Or as Musaddad said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was praying, and a kid went to pass in front of him, so he kept guarding against it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to be between the Prophet ﷺ and the qiblah—Shuʿbah said: I think she said—while I was menstruating.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to sleep with my legs in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying at night. When he wanted to prostrate, he would tap my legs, so I drew them in, and he prostrated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The soul of the believer comes out as a trickle [of sweat], and I do not like a death like the death of a donkey."
It was asked, "What is the death of a donkey?" He said, "Sudden death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are no two recording angels who raise to Allah what they recorded of the night or the day, and Allah finds good at the beginning of the record and at the end of the record, except that Allah the Exalted says: 'Bear witness that I have forgiven My servant whatever lies between the two ends of the record.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Beware of announcing death in the manner of the pre-Islamic era, for that is from the practice of the Jāhiliyyah."
ʿAbdullāh said: "Naʿy is announcing the death of the deceased."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ʿĪsā said: This is more authentic than the hadith of ʿAnbasah from Abū Ḥamzah.
Abū Ḥamzah is Maymūn al-Aʿwar, and he is not considered strong by the scholars of hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of perfumes is musk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ shrouded Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib in a single striped garment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Four things in my Ummah are from the affairs of the Jāhiliyyah which people will not abandon: wailing over the dead, slandering lineages, contagion—[as in:] a camel gets mange, then a hundred camels get mange, so who gave mange to the first camel?—and attributing rain to the stars, saying: 'We were given rain by such-and-such a star.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no deceased person who dies and then the one weeping over him stands up and says, 'O my mountain! O my master!' or the like, except that two angels are assigned to him, striking him in the chest, [saying], 'Was this how you were?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ took ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf by the hand and went with him to his son Ibrāhīm, and found him breathing his last. The Prophet ﷺ took him and placed him in his lap, and he wept. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to him, "Do you weep? Were you not forbidden from weeping?" He said:
"No, but I was forbidden from two foolish, sinful sounds: a sound at a calamity, [accompanied by] scratching faces and tearing garments, and the cry of Satan."
There is more to this hadith than this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [the narrator is] the imam of Banū Taymillāh, from Abū Mājid,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd,
who said: We asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about walking behind the funeral procession, and he said:

"[Walk] at a pace less than a trot. If the deceased was good, you are hastening him to it; and if he was evil, then only the people of the Fire are kept far away. The funeral is followed and does not follow, and whoever goes ahead of it is not of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away, they differed about his burial. Abū Bakr said, "I heard something from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that I have not forgotten. He said:
'Allah does not take the soul of a prophet except in the place where he loves to be buried.'
Bury him in the place of his bed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I buried my son Sinān while Abū Ṭalḥah al-Khawlānī was sitting at the edge of the grave. When I wanted to leave, he took me by the hand and said, "Shall I not give you glad tidings, O Abū Sinān?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A child is not prayed over, does not inherit, and is not inherited from, until it cries out [at birth]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Saʿd
died while the Prophet ﷺ was absent. When he arrived, he prayed over her, and a month had passed since then.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I accompanied Abū Hurayrah for ten years, and I heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Whoever follows a funeral and carries it three times has fulfilled what is due from him regarding its right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The one who dug the niche in the grave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Abū Ṭalḥah, and the one who placed the velvet cloak beneath him was Shuqrān, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade that graves be plastered, that anything be written on them, that anything be built over them, or that they be trodden upon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by the graves of Madinah, turned his face toward them, and said:
"Peace be upon you, O people of the graves. May Allah forgive us and you. You are our predecessors, and we follow in your footsteps."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I had forbidden you from visiting graves, but Muhammad has been given permission to visit the grave of his mother. So visit them, for they remind [one] of the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr died at Ḥubshī.

He was carried to Makkah and buried there. When ʿĀʾishah came, she went to the grave of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr and said: "We were like the two boon companions of Jadhīmah for a long period of time, until it was said they would never part. Then when we were separated, it was as if I and Mālik, after such long companionship, had not spent even a single night together." Then she said, "By Allah, had I been present with you, I would not have buried you except where you died, and had I witnessed your death, I would not have visited you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He had met the Prophet ﷺ.
His mother, Zaynab bint Ḥumayd, took him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, take his pledge of allegiance." The Prophet ﷺ said, "He is [too] young."
So he wiped his head and made supplication for him.
And he used to sacrifice a single sheep on behalf of all his family.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"After me there will be twelve leaders."
He said: Then he said something that I did not understand, so I asked the person next to me, and he said that he said:
"All of them will be from Quraysh."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer, so ʿUmar went out and said, "The prayer, O Messenger of Allah!
The women and children have fallen asleep."
So he came out with his head dripping water, saying:
"Were it not that it would be hard on my Ummah, or on the people,
and Sufyān also said:
on my Ummah, I would have commanded them to pray this prayer at this hour."
Ibn Jurayj reported from ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās: The Prophet ﷺ delayed this prayer, so ʿUmar came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the women and children have fallen asleep."
So he came out, wiping the water from one side of his head, and said, "It is indeed the proper time for it,
were it not that it would be hard on my Ummah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted continuously, without breaking the fast, at the beginning of the month of Ramadan, and some of the Muslims did likewise. When this reached him, he said:

"If the month were extended for us, I would continue fasting in such a way that those who go to extremes would give up their extremism. You are not like me," or he said, "I am not like you. I spend the night [in such a state that] my Lord feeds me and gives me drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ash-Shaʿbī said to me: What do you think of the hadith of al-Ḥasan from the Prophet ﷺ? I sat with Ibn ʿUmar for nearly two years, or a year and a half, and I never heard him narrate anything from the Prophet ﷺ other than this. He said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, among them Saʿd, went to eat some meat,
and a woman from among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ called out to them that it was the meat of a dabb (spiny-tailed lizard), so they held back.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Eat, or feed [others], for it is lawful," or he said, "there is no harm in it."
[The narrator doubted which.] "But it is not among my food."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Your Ummah will keep on saying, 'What is this? What is that?' until they say, 'This is Allah, who created creation, so who created Allah?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Abū Hurayrah, and he was wearing two linen garments dyed with red ochre. He blew his nose into one of them, then said, "Well, well! Abū Hurayrah blows his nose into linen! I have seen myself fall down, collapsed from hunger, between the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the room of ʿĀʾishah, and someone would come and place his foot on my neck, thinking I was mad. But I was not mad; it was nothing but hunger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ established a pact of brotherhood between the Anṣār and Quraysh in my house in Madinah.
And he recited the Qunūt for a month, invoking [Allah] against some clans of Banū Sulaym.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Dajjāl was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Indeed, Allah is not hidden from you.
Indeed, Allah is not one-eyed," and he pointed with his hand to his eye, "while the Messiah, the Dajjāl, is blind in the right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The verse of the ḥijāb was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and on that day bread and meat were served at her wedding feast. She used to boast over the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and would say, "Allah married me [to him] from above the heavens."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A servant committed a sin," and he may have said, "[a servant] sinned, and said, 'My Lord, I have sinned,'" and he may have said, "'I have committed [a sin], so forgive me.' His Lord said, 'Does My servant know that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes to account for them? I have forgiven My servant.'
Then he remained [for a time] as long as Allah willed,
then he committed a sin, or sinned,
and said, 'My Lord, I have sinned,' or 'committed,' 'another sin, so forgive it.'
He said, 'Does My servant know that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes to account for them? I have forgiven My servant.'
Then he remained as long as Allah willed, then he sinned," and he may have said, "committed a sin," he said, "he said, 'My Lord, I have committed,' or 'sinned,' 'another sin, so forgive it for me.'
He said, 'Does My servant know that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes to account for them? I have forgiven My servant,'" three times, ""so let him do as he wishes.""
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting on the pulpit: {And they will call, "O Mālik, let your Lord put an end to us."} Qatādah said: [This is] an example for later generations, an admonition for those who come after them.

Another said: {muqrinīn} means those who are able to control; it is said, "So-and-so is muqrin for so-and-so," meaning he is in control of him. And the akwāb are the pitchers that have no spouts. {The first of the worshippers}, that is: if there were [a son], then I would be the first of those who refuse; the two forms are both dialects, ʿābid and ʿabid, and ʿAbd Allāh recited {and the Messenger said, "O my Lord"}. It is also said: {the first of the worshippers} means the first of those who deny, from ʿabada, yaʿbadu.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb, and Ibn
Numayr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ayyūb,
from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn,
who said: I heard Abū Hurayrah
say: Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:
"Name yourselves with my name, but do not take my kunyah as yours."
ʿAmr said, from Abū Hurayrah, and he did not say, "I heard."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west.
When it rises and the people see it, they will all believe,
and that is when belief will not benefit a soul
that had not believed before,
or earned some good through its belief.
The Hour will certainly come while two men have spread out their cloth between them, and they will neither sell it nor fold it up.
The Hour will certainly come when a man has gone away with the milk of his she-camel, and he will not drink it.
The Hour will certainly come while a man is plastering his trough, and he will not water [his animals] from it.
The Hour will certainly come when a man has raised his morsel to his mouth, and he will not eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The husband of
Barīrah was a black slave called Mughīth. So he, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, gave her the choice, and commanded her to observe the waiting period (ʿiddah).
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm,
and Ibn Abī ʿUmar,
Isḥāq said: "He informed us," and the others said: "He narrated to us", Sufyān, from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn
ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When any of you eats food, let him not wipe his hand until he has licked it or has it licked."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb, and Ibn
Numayr and Abū Kurayb said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
who is Ibn ʿUlayyah, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb, from Anas,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to perfume himself with saffron.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and began to speak, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, some eloquence is like magic, and indeed, some poetry contains wisdom."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr, the wording being that of Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā. Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: "He informed us," and the others said: "He narrated to us", Ismāʿīl,
who is Ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār,
that he heard Ibn ʿUmar
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the Jews greet you, one of them says, 'as-sāmu ʿalaykum' [death be upon you], so say: 'And upon you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Abū Saʿīd al-Ashajj said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us,
and [in another chain] Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb narrated to me,
Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from his father,
both of them from ʿUmārah ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ,
from Abū Zurʿah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, make the provision of the family of Muḥammad just enough to sustain them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
all of them from al-Qāsim ibn Mālik,
ʿAmr said: Qāsim ibn Mālik al-Muzanī narrated to us,
Ayyūb ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Ṭāʾī narrated to us,
from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujāhid,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: Allah made the prayer obligatory through the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ as two rakʿahs for the traveller, four for the resident, and one rakʿah in [times of] fear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On this day we set out in the morning with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Minā to ʿArafah. Some of us were saying the takbīr and some were saying the talbiyah, and neither group criticized the other, nor did the other criticize them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man stayed late with the Prophet ﷺ, then returned to his family and found the children had fallen asleep. His family brought him his food, and he swore that he would not eat because of his children. Then it occurred to him [to do otherwise] and he ate. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him do that [better thing] and make expiation for his oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Madinah, and he would delay the ʿAṣr prayer as long as the sun remained white and clear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Ẓuhr at the height of the midday heat, and there was no prayer harder on the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than it. So it was revealed: {Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer}. And he said:
"Indeed, before it are two prayers and after it are two prayers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ʿAmr, meaning al-Awzāʿī, said: That is when you see
the sunlight on the ground turned yellow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray Maghrib at the moment the sun set, when its upper edge had disappeared.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Abū Ayyūb came to us as a fighter in the cause of Allah, ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir was at that time governing Egypt, and he delayed Maghrib. Abū Ayyūb stood up to him and said to him, "What is this prayer, ʿUqbah?" He said, "We were occupied."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We waited for the Prophet ﷺ for the ʿIshāʾ prayer, and he delayed until someone thought he was not coming out, and one of us said, "He has prayed." While we were in that state, the Prophet ﷺ came out. They said to him what they had said, and he said to them:
"Delay this prayer until the dark of night, for you have been favored by it over all other nations, and no nation before you has prayed it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me, and among what he taught me was:
"Guard the five prayers."
I said, "These are hours in which I have occupations, so command me with something comprehensive which, if I do it, will suffice for me." He said:
"Guard the two ʿAṣrs."
It was not part of our dialect, so I said, "What are the two ʿAṣrs?" He said:
"The prayer before sunrise and the prayer before sunset."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are five things; whoever comes with them together with faith will enter Paradise: whoever guards the five prayers, with their ablution, their bowing, their prostration, and their times, and fasts Ramadan, and performs Hajj to the House if he is able to find a way to it, and gives zakāh willingly from himself, and fulfills the trust."
They said, "Abū ad-Dardāʾ, what is fulfilling the trust?" He said, "The bath after sexual impurity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿādh ibn Jabal came to us in Yemen as the envoy of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to us. He said: I heard his takbīr at dawn, a man with a hoarse voice. He said: Love for him fell upon my heart, and I did not part from him until I buried him, dead, in Syria. Then I looked for the most knowledgeable of people after him, so I came to Ibn Masʿūd and stayed with him until he died. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"How will you fare when rulers come to you who pray the prayer at other than its time?"
I said, "What do you command me to do, Messenger of Allah, if that reaches me?" He said:
"Pray the prayer at its time, and make your prayer with them a voluntary prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"After me there will be rulers over you whom things will keep from praying on time until its time has passed. So pray the prayer at its time."
A man said, "Messenger of Allah, shall I pray with them?" He said:
"Yes, if you wish."
And Sufyān said: "If I reach it with them, shall I pray with them?" He said:
"Yes, if you wish."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"After me there will be rulers over you who delay the prayer. It is for you and against them, so pray with them as long as they pray facing the qiblah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this report he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Move from your place in which heedlessness overtook you."
He said: Then he commanded Bilāl, who called the adhān, gave the iqāmah, and he prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was on a journey, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned aside, and I turned aside with him. He said, "Look."
I said, "This is a rider; these are two riders; these are three," until we were seven. He said:
"Watch over our prayer for us."

meaning the dawn prayer. Then sleep was cast over their ears, and nothing woke them except the heat of the sun. They got up and traveled a little, then dismounted and performed ablution, and Bilāl called the adhān. They prayed the two units of Fajr, then prayed the Fajr prayer and mounted. Some of them said to others, "We have been negligent in our prayer." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no negligence in sleep; negligence is only in wakefulness. So if one of you forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it, and the next day at its [proper] time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Banū Zurayq, from Abū Qatādah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly, adding:
"Then let him sit afterward if he wishes, or go off to his need."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever comes to the mosque for something, that is his share."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When what was said about me had been said, of which I knew nothing, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up to address the people. He recited the testimony of faith, praised Allah and extolled Him as He deserves, and then said:

"To proceed: advise me regarding people who have slandered my family. By Allah, I have never known any evil in my family; and they have slandered a man about whom, by Allah, I have never known any evil, and he never entered my house except when I was present, and he never travelled without being with me." Then Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up and said, "Permit me, O Messenger of Allah, to strike their necks."

Then a man from the Khazraj stood up, and Hassān ibn Thābit's mother was from that man's clan. He said, "You lie! By Allah, if they were from the Aws you would not wish to have their necks struck." It nearly led to evil between the Aws and the Khazraj in the mosque, and I knew nothing of it. When evening came that day, I went out for some need of mine, and Umm Misṭaḥ was with me. She stumbled and said, "May Misṭaḥ perish!" I said to her, "O mother, are you cursing your son?" She was silent. Then she stumbled a second time and said, "May Misṭaḥ perish!" I said to her, "O mother, are you cursing your son?" She was silent. Then she stumbled a third time and said, "May Misṭaḥ perish!" I rebuked her and said, "O mother, are you cursing your son?" She said, "By Allah, I only curse him because of you."
I said, "Concerning what?" She said, and she brought the whole account to me. I said, "Has this really happened?" She said, "Yes."

By Allah, I returned to my house, and it was as though what I had gone out for had not been done at all; I found no relief from it, little or much. I became feverish, and I said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Send me to my father's house." So he sent the servant boy with me. I entered the house and found Umm Rūmān downstairs and Abū Bakr upstairs reciting. My mother said, "What brings you, my daughter?" I told her and related the account to her, but it had not affected her as it had affected me. She said, "My daughter, take the matter lightly, for by Allah, rarely is there a beautiful woman with a husband who loves her, and who has co-wives, but they envy her and speak against her." It had not affected her as it had affected me. I said, "And does my father know of it?" She said, "Yes."
I said, "And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said, "Yes."

I burst into tears and wept. Abū Bakr heard my voice while he was upstairs reciting, and he came down and said to my mother, "What is the matter with her?" She said, "What was said about her has reached her."
His eyes overflowed with tears, and he said, "I adjure you, my daughter, to return to your house."

So I returned. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had come to my house and asked my maidservant about me. She said, "No, by Allah, I know of no fault in her except that she would sleep until the sheep came in and ate her dough or her kneaded dough." Some of his Companions rebuked her and said, "Tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the truth," until they spoke harshly to her about it. She said, "Glory be to Allah! By Allah, I know of her only what a goldsmith knows of pure red gold." The matter then reached the man about whom it was said, and he said, "Glory be to Allah! By Allah, I have never uncovered the garment of any woman." ʿĀʾishah said: He was later killed as a martyr in the cause of Allah. She said: In the morning my parents were with me, and they stayed with me until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me, having prayed the ʿAṣr prayer. Then he entered while my parents were on either side of me, on my right and on my left. The Prophet ﷺ recited the testimony of faith, praised Allah and extolled Him as He deserves, and then said:
"To proceed: O ʿĀʾishah, if you have committed an evil or wronged yourself, then repent to Allah, for Allah accepts repentance from His servants."
She said: A woman of the Anṣār had come and was sitting at the door. I said, "Are you not ashamed before this woman, that you should mention anything?"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then gave his exhortation. I turned to my father and said, "Answer him."
He said, "And what should I say?" Then I turned to my mother and said, "Answer him."

She said, "What should I say?" She said: When they did not answer, I recited the testimony of faith, praised Allah and extolled Him as He deserves, and then said, "By Allah, if I tell you that I did not do it, and Allah bears witness that I am truthful, that will not benefit me with you, for you have spoken of it and it has sunk into your hearts. And if I say that I did it, and Allah knows that I did not do it, you will say, 'She has admitted it against herself.' And by Allah, I find no likeness for me and you except that of the father of Yūsuf when he said:

'So patience is most fitting; and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.'" She said: I tried to recall the name of Yaʿqūb but could not, and said only 'the father of Yūsuf.' She said: Then revelation came upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at that very moment, and we fell silent. Then it was lifted from him, and I could see the joy on his face as he wiped his brow and said:
"Good news, O ʿĀʾishah! Allah has revealed your innocence."
She said: I was at my most angry, and my parents said to me, "Get up and go to him."

I said, "No, by Allah, I will not get up to him, nor will I praise him, nor will I praise either of you; rather, I will praise Allah, who revealed my innocence. You heard it and did not deny it, nor did you change it." ʿĀʾishah used to say: As for Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, Allah protected her through her religion, so she said nothing but good. As for her sister Ḥamnah, she perished among those who perished. Those who spoke about it were Misṭaḥ, Ḥassān ibn Thābit, and the hypocrite ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl, who was the one who managed it and gathered them; he and Ḥamnah were the ones who took the greater part in it. She said: Abū Bakr swore that he would never again benefit Misṭaḥ in any way. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse:
'And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give...' to the end of the verse, meaning Abū Bakr:
'...to the relatives, the needy, and the emigrants in the cause of Allah,' meaning Misṭaḥ, up to His saying:

'Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.' Abū Bakr said, "Yes, by Allah, our Lord, we love that You forgive us." And he restored to him what he used to give.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There are only two things: speech and guidance. The best speech is the Speech of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad. Beware of newly invented matters, for the worst of matters are those newly invented, every newly invented matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance. Do not let the span of time grow long for you, lest your hearts become hardened. Indeed, what is coming is near, and what is far is only that which will not come. Indeed, the wretched one is the one who was wretched in his mother's womb, and the fortunate one is the one who takes admonition from others. Indeed, fighting a believer is disbelief, and insulting him is wickedness, and it is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three days. Beware of lying, for lying is not fitting either in earnest or in jest, and a man should not promise his child something and then not fulfil it for him. Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire; truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. It is said to the truthful one: 'He has spoken the truth and been righteous.'
And it is said to the liar: 'He has lied and been wicked.'
Indeed, a servant keeps on lying until he is recorded with Allah as a great liar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: {It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are clear, they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are ambiguous} up to His words {and none remember except those of understanding}. Then he said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, when you see those who dispute about it, they are the ones Allah meant, so beware of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah does not accept from an innovator fasting, prayer, charity (ṣadaqah), Hajj, ʿUmrah, jihad, or any obligatory or voluntary act. He departs from Islam as a hair is drawn out of dough."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah refuses to accept the deeds of an innovator until he abandons his innovation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever gives a legal opinion without certainty, the sin of it falls upon the one who gave him the opinion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen, he said:
"Do not judge or decide except by what you know. If a matter is unclear to you, stop until you have clarified it, or write to me about it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The affair of the Children of Israel remained upright until there arose among them the muwallads, the children of the captives of the nations. They spoke by personal opinion, so they went astray and led others astray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ while we were strong, sturdy youths, and we learned faith before we learned the Qurʾān. Then we learned the Qurʾān, and it increased us in faith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Faith is knowledge in the heart, speech with the tongue, and action with the limbs."
Abū aṣ-Ṣalt said: If this chain of transmission were recited over a madman, he would be cured.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever departs from this world in sincerity to Allah alone, worshipping Him without partner, and establishing prayer and giving zakāh, dies with Allah pleased with him."

Anas said: This is the religion of Allah with which the messengers came and which they conveyed from their Lord, before the confusion of narrations and the divergence of desires. Its confirmation is in the Book of Allah, in the last of what was revealed. Allah says: {But if they repent} — he said: they cast off the idols and their worship — {and establish prayer and give zakāh}. And in another verse He says: {But if they repent, establish prayer and give zakāh, then they are your brothers in religion.} Abū Ḥātim narrated to us,
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā al-ʿAbsī narrated to us,
Abū Jaʿfar ar-Rāzī narrated to us,
from ar-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ...ʿAbbās, both said: Faith increases and decreases.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Faith increases and decreases.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He entered upon ʿĀʾishah and mentioned something about divine decree (qadar) to her. She said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Whoever speaks about anything of the divine decree will be asked about it on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever does not speak about it will not be asked about it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to his Companions while they were disputing about the divine decree, and his face was as red as if pomegranate seeds had been split open on it from anger. He said:
"Were you commanded with this, or were you created for this? You strike parts of the Qurʾān against other parts.
It was by this that the nations before you were destroyed."
He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: I never envied myself for any gathering from which I was absent from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as I envied myself for that gathering and my absence from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim came to Kufa, we went to him with a group of the jurists of the people of Kufa.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to meet a group of Quraysh while they were talking, and they would break off their conversation. We mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:

"What is the matter with people who are talking, and when they see a man from my family they break off their conversation? By Allah, faith will not enter a man's heart until he loves them for the sake of Allah and for their kinship to me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah has taken me as a close friend (khalīl) just as He took Ibrāhīm as a close friend. So my place and the place of Ibrāhīm will be in Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, facing one another, and al-ʿAbbās will be between us, a believer between two close friends."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever loves al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn has loved me, and whoever hates them has hated me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whenever two matters were presented to ʿAmmār, he would choose the more rightly guided of the two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first to make their Islam public were seven: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿAmmār and his mother Sumayyah, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, and al-Miqdād. As for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah protected him through his uncle Abū Ṭālib. As for Abū Bakr, Allah protected him through his people. As for the rest, the polytheists seized them, put iron coats of mail on them, and left them to bake in the sun. There was none of them who did not give them what they wanted, except Bilāl, for he considered himself of little worth for the sake of Allah, and his people also held him cheap. So they seized him and gave him to the boys, who kept leading him around the mountain paths of Makkah while he said, "One, One!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A poet
praised Bilāl ibn ʿAbdillāh, saying: "Bilāl ibn ʿAbdillāh is the best Bilāl."
Ibn ʿUmar said: "You have lied! Rather, Bilāl, the Messenger of Allah's [Bilāl], is the best Bilāl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khabbāb came to ʿUmar, who said: "Come closer, for no one has more right to this seat than you, except ʿAmmār."
So Khabbāb began to show him the marks on his back from the torture the polytheists had inflicted on him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar used to say: "Do not revile the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, for the standing of one of them for a single hour is better than the deeds of any of you for his entire life."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"May Allah have mercy on the Anṣār, the sons of the Anṣār, and the grandsons of the Anṣār."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Khawārij are the dogs of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A generation will arise who recite the Qur'an but it does not go beyond their collarbones. Every time a generation emerges, it is cut off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"A people will emerge at the end of time," or "in this Ummah," "who recite the Qur'an but it does not go beyond their collarbones," or "their throats. Their sign is shaving the head. When you see them," or "when you meet them, kill them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Our Lord laughs at the despair of His servants, while His relief is near."
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, does the Lord laugh?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "We will never lack good from a Lord who laughs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"While the people of Paradise are in their bliss, a light shines upon them. They raise their heads, and behold, the Lord is looking down upon them from above, and He says: 'Peace be upon you, O people of Paradise.'

He said: And that is the saying of Allah: {"Peace," a word from a Merciful Lord.} He said: "Then He looks at them and they look at Him, and they do not turn to any of the bliss as long as they are looking at Him, until He veils Himself from them, and His light and blessing remain upon them in their dwellings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no heart except that it is between two of the fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills, He sets it straight, and if He wills, He lets it deviate."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"O Turner of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion." He said:
"And the Scale is in the hand of the Most Merciful; He raises some people and lowers others until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah laughs at three: the row in prayer, the man who prays in the depths of the night, and the man who fights," I think he said, "behind the battalion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ concerning the saying of the Exalted: {Every day He is engaged in some matter.} He said:
"Part of His matter is that He forgives a sin, relieves distress, raises some people, and lowers others."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made an appointment with Jibrīl (peace be upon him) for a certain hour to come to him. That hour came and he did not come. In his hand was a staff, and he threw it from his hand and said:
"Allah does not break His promise, nor do His messengers."
Then he turned and saw a puppy under his bed, and said:
"ʿĀʾishah, when did this dog come in here?"
She said, "By Allah, I did not know."
So he ordered that it be taken out, and it was taken out. Then Jibrīl came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You made an appointment with me and I sat waiting for you, but you did not come."
He said, "The dog that was in your house prevented me. We do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who maintains family ties is not the one who merely reciprocates, but the one who maintains them when his ties of kinship have been cut off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some of the Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Do you kiss your children?" They said, "Yes."
They said, "But we, by Allah, do not kiss [ours]."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Can I do anything for you if Allah has removed mercy from you?"
And Ibn Numayr said:
"[...] has removed mercy from your heart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up for prayer and we stood with him. A Bedouin said while in prayer, "O Allah, have mercy on me and Muhammad, and do not have mercy on anyone else along with us."
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had given the salām, he said to the Bedouin:
"You have restricted something that is vast."
He meant the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah does not show mercy to the one who does not show mercy to people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the Fire, and he turned away and averted his face, then said, "Beware of the Fire."
Then he turned away and averted his face until we thought that he was as if looking at it. Then he said:
"Beware of the Fire, even with half a date; and whoever does not find that, then with a good word."
Abū Kurayb did not mention "as if," and he said: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibrīl and says, 'I love so-and-so, so love him.' Then Jibrīl loves him, and then calls out in the heavens, saying, 'Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.'
The inhabitants of the heavens love him, and then acceptance is placed for him on earth.

And when He hates a servant, He calls Jibrīl and says, 'I hate so-and-so, so hate him.' Then Jibrīl hates him, and then calls out to the inhabitants of the heavens, 'Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him.' They hate him, and then hatred is placed for him on earth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh said to me about istabraq. He said: I said, "It is the thick and coarse kind of brocade."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If a man says to his brother, 'O disbeliever,' then one of them has surely earned it."
And ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār said, from Yaḥyā,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd,
that he heard Abū Salamah,
