that he heard Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn among a group of us, and among us was Bashīr ibn Kaʿb. ʿImrān narrated to us,
that day, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Modesty is all good."
Or he said:
"Modesty is entirely good."
Bashīr ibn Kaʿb said, "We find in some books or in wisdom that from it comes tranquility and dignity before Allah, and from it comes weakness."
He said: ʿImrān became angry until his eyes turned red, and said, "Do I narrate to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and you oppose it?"
He said: ʿImrān repeated the hadith, and Bashīr repeated [his remark], and ʿImrān became angry. He said: We kept saying, "He is one of us, Abū Nujayd; there is no harm in him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she used to play with dolls in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: My friends used to come to me, and they would hide from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would send them to me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who loves a people but has not joined them?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A person is with those whom he loves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from his father,
who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite Sūrat al-Ṭūr in the Maghrib prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Ibn ʿAbbās, "Sūrat at-Tawbah?" He said, "At-Tawbah? Rather, it is the Exposer. It kept being revealed, saying 'and among them... and among them...'
until they thought that none of us would be left without being mentioned in it."
I said, "Sūrat al-Anfāl?" He said, "That is the sūrah of Badr."
I said, "And al-Ḥashr?" He said, "It was revealed concerning Banū al-Naḍīr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said: I was absent from Badr, the first

battle the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought against the polytheists. [I said,] "If Allah lets me witness a battle against the polytheists, Allah will surely see what I do." Then on the day of Uḥud, the Muslims were routed, and he said, "O Allah, I declare to You my innocence from what these have brought,
meaning the polytheists, and I apologize to You for what these are doing,
meaning his own companions." Then he advanced and Saʿd met him and said, "My brother, what have you done?" He said, "I am with you, yet I could not do what he did."
Then they found on him eighty-some wounds from sword strikes, spear thrusts and arrow shots. We used to say that this verse was revealed about him and his companions:
"Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is he who still waits."
Yazīd said: meaning this verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was revealed about us: "When two groups among you were about to lose heart, while Allah was their ally." He said: We are the two groups, Banū Ḥārithah and Banū Salimah,
and we would not wish—and Sufyān once said: it would not please me—that it had not been revealed, because of Allah's words: "while Allah was their ally."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Uḥud I saw, on the right of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and on his left, two men wearing white clothes, fighting on his behalf with the fiercest fighting. I had not seen them before nor did I see them after.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Drowsiness overcame us while we were in our battle lines on the day of Uḥud. He related that he was among those overcome by drowsiness that day. He said: My sword kept falling from my hand and I would pick it up, and it would fall from my hand and I would pick it up. As for the other group, the hypocrites, they had no concern except for themselves—the most cowardly of people, the most fearful, and the most unwilling to support the truth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he raised his head from bowing in the last rakʿah of the Fajr prayer, say:
"O Allah, curse so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so,"
after he said:
"Allah hears whoever praises Him; our Lord, to You belongs all praise."
So Allah revealed: "You have no say in the matter" up to His words "for they are wrongdoers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The anger of Allah is intense against a people who did this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,"
while at that moment he was pointing to his front tooth. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The anger of Allah is intense against a man whom the Messenger of Allah kills in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made qunūt for a month after bowing, supplicating against some tribes of the Arabs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes grew wild and the hearts reached the throats," she said: That was on the day of the Trench.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:
"There is no god but Allah alone; He gave might to His army, gave victory to His servant, and defeated the confederates alone, so there is nothing after Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ on a military expedition, six of us with one camel that we took turns riding.
Our feet became worn and sore, my feet became worn, and my toenails fell off,
and we used to wrap rags around our feet.
So it was named the expedition of Dhāt al-Riqāʿ,
because of the rags we bound around our feet.
Abū Mūsā related this,
then he disliked that.
He said, "What good was it for me to mention it?"
It was as though he disliked that any of his deeds should be disclosed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was sitting beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when tranquillity overcame him, and the thigh of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to rest on my thigh,
and I never felt anything heavier than the thigh of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then it passed from him, and he said, "Write."
So I wrote on a shoulder bone:
"Not equal are those of the believers who sit [at home]
and those who strive in the cause of Allah"
up to the end of the verse. Then Ibn Umm Maktūm, who was a blind man, stood up when he heard the merit of those who strive, and said:

"O Messenger of Allah, what about those believers who are unable to strive?" When he finished speaking, tranquillity overcame the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and his thigh came to rest on my thigh, and I felt its weight a second time just as I had felt it the first time. Then it passed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, "
Recite, Zayd."
So I recited: "Not equal are those of the believers who sit [at home]", and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "except those with a disability," the whole verse. Zayd said:
"So Allah revealed it on its own, and I added it.
By the One in whose hand is my soul, it is as though I can see the place where it was joined, at a crack in the shoulder bone."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from the expedition of Tabūk and drew near to Madinah, he said, "
In Madinah there are people who were with you on every journey you made and every valley you crossed."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, while they were in Madinah?" He said, "
Yes, they were in Madinah; an excuse kept them back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] from Banū Sulaym, on the authority of ʿUtbah ibn ʿAbd as-Sulamī,
and this is his wording, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
Do not cut the forelocks of horses, nor their manes, nor their tails,
for their tails are their fly-whisks, their manes are their warmth,
and their forelocks have goodness tied up in them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ill omen was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "
If there is ill omen in anything, it is in the house, the woman, and the horse."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ combined his father and mother for him [in a saying] on the day of Uhud.
He said: There was a man among the polytheists who had been burning the Muslims, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him, "
Shoot! May my father and mother be your ransom."
He said: So I drew an arrow for him that had no head, and it struck his side, and he fell and his private parts were exposed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until I saw his back teeth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while his coat of mail was pledged with a Jew for thirty ṣāʿ of barley for his family.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said, "
Among the signs of the Hour is that you will fight a people who wear shoes made of hair,
and among the signs of the Hour is that you will fight a people with broad faces,
as though their faces were hammered shields."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Hour will not come until you fight a people whose shoes are made of hair,
and the Hour will not come until you fight a people whose faces are like hammered shields."
Sufyān said: Abū az-Zinād added to it, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah, in his narration: "small-eyed, flat-nosed,
as though their faces were hammered shields."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the Confederates, "
O Allah, Revealer of the Book, swift in reckoning,
defeat the Confederates and shake them."
Al-Ḥumaydī added: Sufyān narrated to us,
Ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us,
I heard ʿAbdullāh [say]: I heard the Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: I pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, then I moved aside to the shade of a tree.
When the people had thinned out, he said, "
O Ibn al-Akwaʿ, will you not pledge allegiance?"
I said, "I have already pledged allegiance, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Again." So I pledged allegiance to him a second time.
I said to him, "O Abū Muslim,
on what were you pledging allegiance that day?" He said, "To death."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us out, and we were three hundred men carrying our provisions on our shoulders. Our provisions ran out until each man among us had only one date a day.

It was said to him, "O Abū ʿAbdillāh, what could one date do for a man?" He said, "We felt its loss when it was gone. Then we came to the sea, and there was a huge fish that the sea had cast up, and we ate from it for eighteen days as much as we wished."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Hunger will be cast upon the people of the Fire, and it will equal all the punishment they are already in. So they will cry out for help, and they will be given food of bitter thorny plants, which neither nourishes nor relieves hunger. Then they will cry out for food, and they will be given food that chokes. They will remember that in the world they used to get rid of choking by drinking, so they will cry out for drink, and boiling water will be raised to them with iron hooks. When it comes near their faces, it will scorch their faces, and when it enters their bellies, it will cut up whatever is in their bellies. They will say: 'Call the keepers of Hell.' They will say: 'Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?' They will say: 'Yes.'
They will say: 'Then call out yourselves.' But the calling of the disbelievers is only in error.
He said: Then they will say: 'Call Mālik.' So they will say:
'O Mālik, let your Lord put an end to us.' He said: He will answer them: 'You will remain.'"
Al-Aʿmash said: It has been conveyed to me that between their calling and Mālik's answer to them is a thousand years. He said: "
They will say: 'Call your Lord, for there is none better than your Lord.' So they will say:
'Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it; and if we return, then we will be wrongdoers.' He said: He will answer them:
'Remain despised in it and do not speak to Me.' He said: At that point they will despair of every good, and at that point they will begin wailing, grief, and cries of woe."
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: The people do not trace this hadith back to the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "...while they therein will have their lips drawn back." He said: "
The Fire will scorch them, so the upper lip will shrivel until it reaches the middle of the head, and the lower lip will hang down until it strikes the navel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

If a lead weight like this—and he pointed to something like a skull—were sent down from the heaven to the earth, a distance of five hundred years' journey, it would reach the earth before night. But if it were sent down from the head of the chain, it would take forty autumns, night and day, before it reached its base or bottom."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah says: 'Bring out of the Fire whoever remembered Me one day or feared Me in a [certain] standing.'"
He said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Some of the people of monotheism will be punished in the Fire until they become like charcoal in it. Then mercy will reach them, and they will be brought out and thrown at the gates of Paradise.
He said: The people of Paradise will sprinkle water over them, and they will sprout as debris sprouts in the silt carried by a flood. Then they will enter Paradise."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ, and it has been narrated from Jābir through more than one route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men among those who entered the Fire cried out loudly, so the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Bring them out.'
When they were brought out, He said to them: 'Why did you cry out so loudly?' They said: 'We did that so that You would have mercy on us.'
He said: 'My mercy upon you is that you go and throw yourselves back where you were in the Fire.'

So they went, and one of them threw himself in, and He made it cool and safe for him. The other stood and did not throw himself in. The Lord, Mighty and Majestic, said to him: 'What prevented you from throwing yourself in as your companion did?' He said: 'My Lord, I hope that You will not return me to it after You have brought me out of it.'
The Lord said to him: 'You have what you hoped for.'
So both of them entered Paradise by the mercy of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I have never seen the like of the Fire, whose one who flees from it sleeps, nor the like of Paradise, whose seeker sleeps."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ did not consider the abandonment of any deed to be disbelief except prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Indeed, the religion will retreat to the Hijaz as a snake retreats to its hole, and the religion will take refuge in the Hijaz as a mountain goat takes refuge at the top of a mountain. Indeed, the religion began as a stranger and will return as a stranger, so glad tidings to the strangers, who set right what people corrupt of my Sunnah after me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

There will certainly come upon my Ummah what came upon the Children of Israel, step by step, such that if one of them openly approached his mother, there would be someone in my Ummah who does that. The Children of Israel split into seventy-two sects, and my Ummah will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect." They said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Those who follow what I and my Companions are upon."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created His creation in darkness, then cast some of His light upon them. Whoever was touched by that light was guided, and whoever it missed went astray. For that reason I say: the pen has dried according to the knowledge of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever goes out in pursuit of knowledge is in the cause of Allah until he returns."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn Wahb, from Yūnus,
from Ibn Shihāb,
that ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī

informed him that Ḥumrān, the freed slave of ʿUthmān, informed him that ʿUthmān called for water for ablution and performed ablution: he washed his palms three times, then rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose, then washed his face three times, then washed his right arm up to the elbow three times, then washed his left arm likewise, then wiped his head, then washed his right foot up to the ankles three times, then washed his left foot likewise. Then he said, "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution like this ablution of mine." Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then stands and prays two rakʿahs, not letting his mind wander in them, will have his previous sins forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Numayr,
all of them from Ibn ʿUyaynah,
Qutaybah said: Sufyān narrated to us,
from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"When one of you uses stones to clean himself, let him use an odd number; and when one of you performs ablution, let him put water in his nose and then blow it out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we washed the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, he said to us while we were washing her:
"Begin with her right side and the parts of ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ sought water for ablution, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Does anyone among you have water?"
Then he put his hand into the water and said:
"Perform ablution, in the name of Allah."
I saw water flowing from between his fingers until all of them had performed ablution, down to the last of them.
Thābit said: I asked Anas, "How many do you think they were?" He said, "About seventy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey,
and [the Prophet ﷺ] went off to relieve himself,
and al-Mughīrah began pouring water over him while he performed ablution,
and he washed his face and his arms, wiped his head, and wiped over his leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā al-Māzinī, from his father,

that he said to ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿĀṣim, who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and the grandfather of ʿAmr ibn Yaḥyā: "Can you show me how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ablution?" ʿAbdullāh ibn Zayd said, "Yes."

So he called for water for ablution and poured it over his hands and washed his hands twice each, then rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose three times, then washed his face three times, then washed his arms twice each up to the elbows, then wiped his head with his hands, moving them forward and back: he began at the front of his head, then took them to the back of his neck, then returned them until he came back to the place where he had begun. Then he washed his feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Men and women used to perform ablution in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Musaddad said, from one vessel, all together.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ate a bone with meat on it, or meat, then prayed without performing ablution and without touching water.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cutting [meat] from a shoulder of lamb in his hand,
and he was called to prayer, so he put it down along with the knife with which he had been cutting,
then stood and prayed, and did not perform ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by one of the walled gardens of Mecca or Medina and heard the voices of two people being punished in their graves. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"They are being punished, and not for something major." Then he said:
"Rather, one of them did not clean himself properly of his urine, and the other used to go about spreading slander."
Then he called for a palm branch, broke it into two pieces, and placed one piece on each grave. It was said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, why did you do this?" He said:
"Perhaps their punishment will be lightened as long as these do not dry out," or "until they dry out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ met Ibn Ṣāʾid on one of the roads of Madinah and detained him. He was a Jewish boy with a forelock, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar were with the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of Allah?"
He said, "Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of Allah?" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "What do you see?"
He said, "I see a throne above the water." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"You see the throne of Iblīs above the sea." Then he said, "What else do you see?"
He said, "I see two truthful ones and one liar," or "two liars and one truthful." The Prophet ﷺ said, "He has been confused."
So he left him. [The narrator] said: On this topic there are also narrations from ʿUmar, Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, Ibn ʿUmar, Abū Dharr, Ibn Masʿūd, Jābir and Ḥafṣah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Ṣāʾid accompanied me, either on Hajj or on ʿUmrah. The people went ahead and he and I were left behind. When I was alone with him, I shuddered from him and felt uneasy about him because of what people said about him. When I stopped, I said to him, "Put your belongings down there, by that tree."
He said: He saw some sheep, so he took a cup, went and milked, then brought me milk and said to me, "Abū Saʿīd, drink."
I disliked drinking anything from his hand because of what people said about him, so I said to him, "Today is a hot day and I dislike milk in this heat."

He said to me, "Abū Saʿīd, I was about to take a rope, tie it to a tree and then hang myself because of what people say about me and concerning me. Do you see anyone to whom my affair is hidden? It will not be hidden from you. Are you not the most knowledgeable of people about the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? O company of the Anṣār, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not say that he is a disbeliever, while I am a Muslim? Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not say that he is barren and has no children, while I have left my children in Madinah? Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not say that he will not enter, or that Makkah and Madinah are not lawful for him? Am I not from the people of Madinah? And here I am going with you to Makkah."

By Allah, he kept coming up with such things until I said, "Perhaps it was falsely said about him." Then he said, "Abū Saʿīd, by Allah, I will tell you something true. By Allah, I know him, I know his father, and I know where he is on earth right now."
I said, "May you perish for the rest of the day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Dajjāl is blind in the left eye, with bushy hair. He has with him a paradise and a fire; his fire is a paradise and his paradise is a fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people will flee from the Dajjāl until they join the mountains."
Umm Sharīk said, "O Messenger of Allah, where will the Arabs be on that day?" He said, "They will be few."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Hasten to do good deeds before six things: the sun rising from the west, the smoke, the Dajjāl, the Beast, the death of one of you, or the general affair [of the Hour]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"When the treasures of Persia and Rome are opened to you, what kind of people will you be?"
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said, "We will say what Allah has commanded us."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Or something other than that: you will compete with one another, then envy one another, then turn your backs on one another, then hate one another," or words like that. "Then you will go to the poor among the Emigrants and place some of them over the necks of others."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The family of Muḥammad ﷺ never ate their fill of barley bread for two consecutive days until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: I am the most self-sufficient of partners, needing no partner. Whoever does a deed in which he associates anyone else with Me, I am free of him, and it belongs to the one he associated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you yawns, let him hold his hand over his mouth, for Satan enters."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman used to circumambulate the House while naked, saying, "Who will lend me a cloth for circumambulation that I may put over my private parts?" and she would say, "Today some of it or all of it will show, and what shows of it I do not make lawful." Then this verse was revealed: {Take your adornment at every place of prayer.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ made supplication (qunūt) for a month after rising from the bowing position in prayer, when he said:
"Allah hears the one who praises Him."
He would say in his qunūt:

"O Allah, rescue al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd. O Allah, rescue Salamah ibn Hishām. O Allah, rescue ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah. O Allah, rescue the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, press down Your tread upon Muḍar. O Allah, make it upon them years like the years of Yūsuf."

Abū Hurayrah said: Then I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ abandon the supplication afterward, so I said, "I see that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has stopped supplicating for them." He said: It was said, "Do you not see that they have come?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We made camp for the night with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and did not wake until the sun had risen. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Let every man take hold of the head of his mount, for this is a place in which the devil was present with us."
He said: So we did that. Then he called for water and performed ablution, then prostrated twice. Yaʿqūb said: then he prayed two units. Then the prayer was called, and he led the morning prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
asked Ibn ʿAbbās: I miss the prayer in congregation while I am in al-Baṭḥāʾ.
What do you think I should pray?
He said: Two units, the Sunnah of Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas ibn Mālik about shortening the prayer,
and Anas said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out on a journey of three miles or three farsakhs—Shuʿbah was unsure—he would pray two units.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with Shuraḥbīl ibn as-Simṭ to a village seventeen or eighteen miles away, and he prayed two units.
I asked him about it, and he said: I saw ʿUmar pray two units at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah. I asked him about it, and he said: I am only doing as I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Madinah to Makkah, and he prayed two units, two units, until he returned.
I asked: How long did he stay in Makkah? He said: Ten days.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on his mount while returning from Makkah to Madinah, in whatever direction it faced. He said: And it was concerning this that it was revealed: {Wherever you turn, there is the face of Allah.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: when he was hurried in travel, he would delay the Ẓuhr prayer until the time of ʿAṣr and combine the two, and he would delay the Maghrib prayer until he combined it with ʿIshāʾ when the twilight had disappeared.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas ibn Mālik: How should I turn away when I have prayed, to my right
or to my left?
He said: As for me, most often
I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turn away to his right.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray Ḍuḥā. She said: No, except when he came back from an absence.
I asked: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ join two sūrahs together [in one unit]? She said: From the Mufaṣṣal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That she asked ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her: How many units did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray in the Ḍuḥā prayer? She said: Four units, and he would add as much as he wished.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That his father, ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal,

said: I asked, and I was eager to find someone who would tell me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed the voluntary Ḍuḥā prayer, but I found no one to tell me that, except that Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came after the day had risen on the day of the Conquest, and a garment was brought and held up as a screen for him. He bathed, then stood and prayed eight units. I do not know whether his standing in them was longer, or his bowing, or his prostration; all of it was close to equal. She said: I never saw him pray it before or after.
Al-Murādī said, from Yūnus:
and he did not say, "He told me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Every morning, charity is due on every joint of the children of Ādam: his greeting of whomever he meets is charity, his enjoining what is right is charity, his forbidding what is wrong is charity, his removing harm from the road is charity, and his intimacy with his wife is charity."
They said: O Messenger of Allah, he fulfills his desire and that is charity for him? He said:
"Do you not see that if he put it in an unlawful place, would he not bear sin?" He said:
"And two units of Ḍuḥā suffice in place of all of that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray the two units of Fajr and make them so light that I would say, "Did he recite the Opening of the Qurʾān in them?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and when we reached him he asked about the people,
until he came to me. I said, "I am Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn."

He reached his hand toward my head and undid my upper button, then undid my lower button, then placed his palm between my breasts—and I was a young boy at the time—and said, "Welcome, ask whatever you wish."

So I asked him, and he was blind. The time of prayer came, so he stood up wrapped in a small woven cloth; whenever he placed it on his shoulders its ends fell back to him because of its smallness, while his cloak was beside him on the clothes rack. He led us in prayer. I said, "Tell us about the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

He gestured with his hand and held up nine fingers, and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed nine years without performing Hajj. Then in the tenth year he announced to the people that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was going to perform Hajj. So a great number of people came to Madinah, all of them wishing to follow the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to do as he did. He set out and we set out with him. We came to Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, where Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr. She sent word to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'What should I do?' He said:
'Bathe, bind [yourself] with a cloth, and enter the state of iḥrām.'
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in the mosque, then mounted al-Qaṣwāʾ,

until his she-camel stood upright with him on the open plain of al-Baydāʾ." Jābir said, "I looked as far as my sight reached in front of him, riders and walkers, and the same on his right, the same on his left, and the same behind him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among us, and the Qurʾān was being revealed to him, and he knew its interpretation; whatever he did, we did. So he proclaimed the oneness of Allah [in the talbiyah]:
'Labbayka Allāhumma labbayk, labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk. Inna al-ḥamda wa al-niʿmata laka wa al-mulk, lā sharīka lak.'
The people also called out the talbiyah which they usually called out, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not reject any of it from them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept to his own talbiyah.

Jābir said, "We intended only Hajj; we did not know ʿUmrah [as part of it]. Then when we came to the House with him, he touched the Corner, walked briskly three times and walked [normally] four. Then he went to the Station of Ibrāhīm and recited:
'And take the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer.'

He placed the Station between himself and the House." My father used to say—and I know only that he related it from the Prophet ﷺ—that he used to recite in the two rakʿahs, 'Say: O disbelievers' and 'Say: He is Allah, [who is] One.'
Then he returned to the House and touched the Corner, then went out by the gate to aṣ-Ṣafā. When he drew near to aṣ-Ṣafā he recited:
'Indeed, aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.'
'We begin with what Allah began with.' So he began with aṣ-Ṣafā.
He climbed it until he saw the House, then he declared Allah's greatness, declared His oneness, praised Him, and said:

'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things. There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and defeated the confederates alone.'

Then he made supplication between these, saying the like of this three times. Then he descended toward al-Marwah and walked until his feet came down into the valley bed, [where] he ran in the middle of the valley; when they ascended—meaning his feet—he walked until he reached al-Marwah. He did on al-Marwah as he had done on aṣ-Ṣafā. When it was the last circuit of his walking on al-Marwah, he said:

'If I had known beforehand what I know now, I would not have brought the sacrificial animals, and I would have made it an ʿUmrah. So whoever among you has no sacrificial animal with him, let him come out of iḥrām and make it an ʿUmrah.'

So all the people came out of iḥrām and shortened their hair, except the Prophet ﷺ and those who had sacrificial animals with them. Then Surāqah ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, is this for our year only, or for ever?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ interlaced his fingers one into the other and said:
'ʿUmrah has entered into Hajj, like this'—twice—'No, rather for ever and ever.'
He said: ʿAlī came from Yemen with sacrificial camels for the Prophet ﷺ.
He found that Fāṭimah was among those who had come out of iḥrām; she had put on dyed garments and applied kohl, and ʿAlī disapproved of that in her. She said, "My father ordered me to do this."

ʿAlī used to say in Iraq: "So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to incite him against Fāṭimah for what she had done, and to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what she had said on his behalf, as I had disapproved of it in her." He said:
'She spoke the truth, she spoke the truth. What did you say when you undertook the Hajj?'
He said: I said, "O Allah, I am entering iḥrām for that for which Your Messenger ﷺ has entered iḥrām." He said:
'Then I have the sacrificial animals with me, so do not come out of iḥrām.'

He said: The total of the sacrificial animals which ʿAlī brought from Yemen and which the Prophet ﷺ brought from Madinah was one hundred. Then all the people came out of iḥrām and shortened their hair, except the Prophet ﷺ and those who had sacrificial animals with them. When it was the Day of Tarwiyah and they headed toward Minā, they entered iḥrām for Hajj.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rode and prayed at Minā the Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib, ʿIshāʾ and Fajr prayers. Then he waited a little until the sun rose, and ordered that a tent of hair be pitched for him at Namirah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out, and the Quraysh had no doubt that he would stop at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, or Muzdalifah, as the Quraysh used to do in the Jāhiliyyah. But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed on until he came to ʿArafah, and found the tent pitched for him at Namirah. He dismounted there, and when the sun had passed its zenith he ordered al-Qaṣwāʾ to be saddled for him. He rode until he came to the middle of the valley, and addressed the people, saying:

'Indeed your blood and your wealth are sacred to you, like the sacredness of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours. Indeed, everything of the affair of the Jāhiliyyah is placed under these two feet of mine; the bloodshed of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished. The first blood I abolish is the blood of Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith—he was being nursed among Banū Saʿd and Hudhayl killed him. The usury of the Jāhiliyyah is abolished; the first usury I abolish is our usury, the usury of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, for it is abolished entirely. So fear Allah regarding women, for you have taken them by the trust of Allah, and made their private parts lawful to you by the word of Allah. You have the right over them that they not allow anyone whom you dislike to tread on your bedding. If they do that, strike them in a manner that is not severe. They have the right over you to their provision and clothing in a fair manner. I have left among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah. And you will be asked about me, so what will you say?'
They said, "We bear witness that you have conveyed [the message], fulfilled [your trust], and given sincere advice."
Then he raised his forefinger to the sky and pointed it down toward the people, saying:
'O Allah, bear witness! O Allah, bear witness!'

Three times. Then Bilāl gave the call to prayer, then the iqāmah, and he prayed Ẓuhr; then he gave the iqāmah and prayed ʿAṣr, and he prayed nothing between them. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rode until he came to the place of standing; he made the belly of his she-camel face the rocks, placed the path of those on foot in front of him, and faced the qiblah. He remained standing until the sun set and the yellow light faded a little, until the disc disappeared. He seated Usāmah ibn Zayd behind him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ moved on, drawing al-Qaṣwāʾ's reins so tightly that her head nearly touched the front of his saddle, and he said with his right hand:
'O people, calm, calm!'

Whenever he came to a mound, he loosened the reins a little for her until she climbed. Then he came to Muzdalifah and prayed Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ there with one call to prayer and two iqāmahs, and he prayed nothing between them. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lay down until dawn rose, and he prayed Fajr when the morning became clear to him, with a call to prayer and an iqāmah. Then he rode al-Qaṣwāʾ until he came to al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, climbed it, praised Allah, declared His greatness and His oneness, and remained standing until it became very bright. Then he moved on before the sun rose, seating al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās behind him—a man with beautiful hair, fair-skinned and handsome. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ moved on, a group of women riding in howdahs passed by, and al-Faḍl began to look at them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his hand on the other side [of his face], and al-Faḍl turned his face to the other side to look. [He went on] until he came to Muḥassir, where he urged [his mount] on a little. Then he took the middle road which leads out to the greatest Jamrah, until he came to the Jamrah near the tree. He threw seven pebbles, declaring 'Allāhu akbar' with each pebble, [each] like the pebbles used for flicking, and he threw from the middle of the valley. Then he went to the place of sacrifice and sacrificed sixty-three camels with his own hand. Then he gave ʿAlī [the knife] and he sacrificed the remainder, and he made him a partner in his sacrificial animals. Then he ordered that a piece of each camel be taken, and they were put in a pot and cooked, and the two of them ate of its meat and drank of its broth. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the House, and prayed Ẓuhr at Makkah. He came to Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, who were drawing water from Zamzam, and said:
'Draw water, O Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib! Were it not that people would overpower you in [taking over] your watering duty, I would draw with you.'
So they handed him a bucket, and he drank from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out to us on the day he returned from the Confederates:
"None of you should pray Ẓuhr except at Banū Qurayẓah."
Some people feared that the time would pass, so they prayed before reaching Banū Qurayẓah.
Others said, "We will not pray except where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us, even if the time passes us by." He said: Yet he did not rebuke either of the two groups.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered while two girls were with me singing the songs of Buʿāth. He lay down on the bed and turned his face away. Then Abū Bakr entered and scolded me, saying, "The instrument of Satan in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to him and said, "Leave them."

When he was no longer paying attention, I signalled to them and they left. It was a day of Eid, when the Sudanese would play with shields and spears. Either I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or he said, "Would you like to watch?"
I said, "Yes." So he stood me behind him, my cheek against his cheek, and he was saying:
"Carry on, O Banū Arfidah!"
until I grew tired. He said, "Is that enough for you?" I said, "Yes." He said, "Then go."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to go out to the place of prayer on the day of Eid with a short spear carried before him. When he reached the place of prayer, it was planted in front of him and he prayed facing it. This was because the place of prayer was an open space with nothing in it to serve as a screen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stood on the day of Fiṭr and prayed, beginning with the prayer before the sermon, and then addressed the people. When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ had finished, he came down and went to the women and admonished them, leaning on the hand of Bilāl while Bilāl spread out his garment, and the women were throwing charity [into it].
I said to ʿAṭāʾ, "Was it the zakāh of the day of Fiṭr?" He said, "No, rather it was charity that they gave then; a woman would throw her ring, and they kept throwing."

I said to ʿAṭāʾ, "Is it now a duty upon the imam to come to the women when he has finished and admonish them?" He said, "Yes, by my life, it is indeed a duty upon them. What is wrong with them that they do not do it?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I attended the prayer on the day of Fiṭr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān. All of them would pray it before the sermon and then deliver the sermon afterwards.
Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came down, and it is as though I can see him now, motioning with his hand for the men to sit down,

then he made his way through them until he came to the women with Bilāl. He recited: {O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor kill their children, nor bring forth a slander they invent between their hands and feet} until he had finished the whole verse. Then, when he had finished, he said:
"Do you hold to that?"
One woman, and none other answered him, said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah,"
(al-Ḥasan did not know who she was). He said, "Then give charity."
And Bilāl spread out his garment, and they began throwing rings and finger rings into Bilāl's garment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, entered upon her while two girls were with her during the days of Minā, playing tambourines and beating them,
while the Prophet ﷺ was covered with his garment.
Abū Bakr scolded them, so the Prophet ﷺ uncovered his face and said:
"Leave them, O Abū Bakr, for these are days of Eid."
And those days were the days of Minā.
ʿĀʾishah said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ shielding me
while I was watching the Abyssinians playing in the mosque.
ʿUmar rebuked them, so the Prophet ﷺ said, "Leave them.
Safe conduct, O Banū Arfidah!"
meaning, [it comes] from security.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, about the qunūt.
He said, "It was before bowing."
I said, "So-and-so claims that you said it was after bowing." He said, "He lied."

Then he narrated to us from the Prophet ﷺ that he recited the qunūt for a month after bowing, invoking against some clans of Banū Sulaym. He said: He had sent forty or seventy (the narrator was unsure) of the Qurʾān reciters to some of the polytheists,
but these [clans] confronted them and killed them,
though there had been a treaty between them and the Prophet ﷺ.
I never saw him grieve over anyone as he grieved over them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sometimes the Prophet ﷺ would say to me: "
O you with the two ears!"
Abū Usāmah said: meaning, he was joking with him.
This is a ḥasan gharīb ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ḥumaydah or ʿUbaydah bint ʿUbayd ibn Rifāʿah az-Zuraqī, from her father,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "
You say a blessing for one who sneezes three times; then if you wish to say it for him, do so, and if you wish, refrain."
label: machine translation

segments_en: …may Allah be pleased with him, that he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me something to say when I go to my bed." He said: "Recite:
'Say: O disbelievers' for it is a declaration of freedom from polytheism."
Shuʿbah said: Sometimes he would say it once, and sometimes he would not say it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Clean earth is the purifier of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years. Then when he finds water, let him touch his skin with it, for that is better."
And Maḥmūd said in his narration: "
Clean earth is the ablution of the Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "
O ʿAlī, three things you should not delay: the prayer when its time comes, the funeral when it is present, and the unmarried woman when you find a suitable match for her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is ʿAbthar ibn al-Qāsim, from Ashʿath, from al-Ḥasan,
from ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ,
who said: Among the last things the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrusted to me was that I appoint a muʾadhdhin who does not take payment for his call to prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "
O ʿAlī, I love for you what I love for myself, and I dislike for you what I dislike for myself. Do not sit in iqʿāʾ between the two prostrations."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would give one salutation to end the prayer, facing straight ahead, inclining slightly toward the right side.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madinah and said, "O Allah, grant me a righteous companion."

He said: Then I sat with Abū Hurayrah and said, "I asked Allah to provide me with a righteous companion, so narrate to me a ḥadīth you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that perhaps Allah may benefit me through it." He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "

The first of his deeds for which a servant will be held to account on the Day of Resurrection is his prayer. If it is sound, he has succeeded and prospered; and if it is defective, he has failed and lost. If something is lacking from his obligatory prayers, the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'See whether My servant has any voluntary prayers with which the shortfall in the obligatory prayers can be made up.' Then the rest of his deeds will be treated in the same way."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Ḥujayrah al-Miṣrī, from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Prophet ﷺ said: "
When you have paid the zakāh of your wealth, you have fulfilled what was due from you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about zakāh, and he said: "
Indeed, in wealth there is a right besides zakāh."
Then he recited this verse from Sūrat al-Baqarah: "It is not righteousness that you turn your faces..." the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, you fast until you hardly break your fast, and you break your fast until you hardly fast, except for two days: if they fall within your fasting, [you fast], and if not, you fast them." He said, "Which two days?"
I said, "Monday and Thursday." He said: "
Those are two days on which deeds are presented to the Lord of the Worlds, and I love for my deeds to be presented while I am fasting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to observe iʿtikāf, he would pray the dawn prayer and then enter the place where he wished to stay in iʿtikāf. He wished to observe iʿtikāf during the last ten days of Ramadan, so he gave an order and a tent was pitched for him. Ḥafṣah gave an order and a tent was pitched for her. When Zaynab saw her tent, she gave an order and a tent was pitched for her. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw that, he said: "Is it righteousness that you desire?"
So he did not observe iʿtikāf in Ramadan, and he observed it for ten days of Shawwāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The Black Stone came down from Paradise, and it was whiter than milk, but the sins of the children of Ādam made it black."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"May Allah have mercy on a man who gets up at night and prays, then wakes his wife and she prays; and if she refuses, he sprinkles water on her face. And may Allah have mercy on a woman who gets up at night and prays, then wakes her husband and he prays; and if he refuses, she sprinkles water on his face."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The one who recites the Qur'an aloud is like the one who gives charity openly,
and the one who recites the Qur'an quietly is like the one who gives charity secretly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the Witr prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

She said: "We used to prepare his tooth-stick and his water for ablution, and Allah would wake him whenever He willed during the night. He would use the tooth-stick, perform ablution, and then pray nine rakʿahs, sitting only at the eighth. He would supplicate to his Lord, remember Allah, praise Him, and call upon Him, then rise without giving the salutation. Then he would stand and pray the ninth, then sit, remember Allah, praise Him, supplicate to his Lord, and send blessings upon his Prophet, then give a salutation that we could hear. Then, after giving the salutation, he would pray two rakʿahs while sitting. That made eleven rakʿahs. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ grew older and heavier, he would pray Witr with seven, and pray two rakʿahs after giving the salutation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, there is a sūrah of the Qur'an of thirty verses that interceded for a man until he was forgiven. It is Sūrah Tabārak alladhī bi-yadihi al-mulk."
This hadith is ḥasan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say in the prostration of recitation at night, repeating it in the prostration:
"My face has prostrated to the One who created it and split open its hearing and sight, by His might and His power."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said:
"Indeed, Allah has granted you an additional prayer that is better for you than red camels: the Witr. Allah has made its time for you between the ʿIshāʾ prayer and the rising of dawn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Witr is a duty upon every Muslim. So whoever wishes to pray Witr with five, let him do so; whoever wishes to pray Witr with three, let him do so; and whoever wishes to pray Witr with one, let him do so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever sleeps through the Witr or forgets it, let him pray it when he remembers and when he wakes up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My beloved friend ﷺ advised me with three things that I never leave, whether traveling or at home: the two rakʿahs of Ḍuḥā, fasting three days of every month, and not sleeping except after praying Witr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and about his prayer. She said, "What do you have to do with his prayer? He would pray, then sleep for as long as he had prayed, then pray for as long as he had slept, then sleep for as long as he had prayed, until morning."
Then she described his recitation to him, and she was describing a recitation that was clearly explained, letter by letter.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, your Lord is Ever-Living and Generous. He is shy before His servant when he raises his hands to Him, to return them empty"—or he said, "disappointed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard a man supplicating, saying: "O Allah, I ask You, for I bear witness that You are Allah, there is no god but You, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who has not begotten and was not begotten, and there is none comparable to Him." He said, so he ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, he has asked Allah by His Greatest Name, which when He is called upon by it He answers, and when He is asked by it He gives."
Zayd said: I mentioned it to Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiyah some years later, and he said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to me from Mālik ibn Mighwal.
Zayd said: Then I mentioned it to Sufyān al-Thawrī, and he narrated to me from Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Shahr ibn Ḥawshab,
from Asmāʾ bint Yazīd,
that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"The Greatest Name of Allah is in these two verses:

'And your God is one God; there is no god but Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate,' and the opening of Āl ʿImrān: 'Alif Lām Mīm. Allah—there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while I was supplicating with my fingers, and he said, "One, One," and he pointed with the index finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ counting the tasbīḥ—Ibn Qudāmah said—with his right hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to my father:
"Ḥuṣayn, how many gods do you worship today?"
My father said, "Seven: six on earth and one in heaven." He said:
"Which of them do you rely on for your hope and your fear?"
He said, "The one in heaven." He said:
"Ḥuṣayn, if you were to accept Islam, I would teach you two phrases that would benefit you."
He said: When Ḥuṣayn accepted Islam, he said, "Messenger of Allah, teach me the two phrases you promised me." He said:
"Say: O Allah, inspire me with my right guidance and protect me from the evil of my own self."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
This hadith has also been narrated from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn through another route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ counting the glorification (tasbīḥ) on his fingers.
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith by this route, from the hadith of al-Aʿmash from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib.
Shuʿbah and al-Thawrī narrated this hadith from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib in full.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding His saying:
"Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter" he said: In this world it is knowledge and worship, and in the Hereafter it is Paradise.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among the supplications of Dāwūd was: O Allah, I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and the deed that will bring me to Your love. O Allah, make Your love dearer to me than myself, my family, and cold water."
He said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned Dāwūd and spoke about him, he would say:
"He was the most devout of people."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he used to say in his supplication:

"O Allah, grant me Your love and the love of those whose love benefits me with You. O Allah, whatever You have given me of what I love, make it a strength for me in what You love. O Allah, and whatever You have kept from me of what I love, make it a freedom for me for what You love."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was asked, "Messenger of Allah, which supplication is most likely to be heard?" He said:
"The latter part of the night, and after the obligatory prayers."
He said: This is a ḥasan hadith.
It has also been narrated from Abū Dharr and Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
"The latter part of the night: supplication then is better, or more likely to be answered."
Or words to that effect.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Messenger of Allah, I heard your supplication last night, and what reached me of it was that you said:
'O Allah, forgive my sin, make my provision ample for me, and bless me in what You have provided me.'" He said:
"Do you think they have left anything out?"
He said: This is a gharīb hadith.
Abū al-Salīl's name is Ḍurayb ibn Nufayr, and it is also said Ibn Nuqayr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rarely rose from a gathering without making these words of supplication for his Companions:

"O Allah, apportion to us such fear of You as will stand between us and disobeying You, and such obedience to You as will bring us to Your Paradise, and such certainty as will make the calamities of this world easy for us. Let us enjoy our hearing, our sight, and our strength as long as You keep us alive, and make it our inheritor. Make our vengeance fall upon those who wronged us, and help us against those who are hostile to us. Do not let our calamity be in our religion, do not make this world our greatest concern or the limit of our knowledge, and do not set over us those who will not show us mercy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father heard me
as I was saying, "O Allah,
I seek refuge in You from worry, laziness, and the punishment of the grave."
He said, "My son, from whom did you hear this?" I said, "I heard you saying them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Shall I not teach you words which, if you say them, Allah will forgive you, even if you have already been forgiven?" He said:
"Say: There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne."
ʿAlī ibn Khashram said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid also informed us, from his father,
with the same, except that he said at the end of it:
"Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith that we know only by this route, from the hadith of Abū Isḥāq from al-Ḥārith from ʿAlī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The supplication of Dhū al-Nūn when he called out while in the belly of the whale: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers.'
No Muslim man ever supplicates with it about anything except that Allah answers him."
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf said once, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Maslamah ibn Mukhallad, and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ was with him. ʿAbdullāh said, "The Hour will not come except upon the worst of people. They are worse than the people of the Jāhiliyyah. They do not call upon Allah for anything except that He rejects it for them."
While they were in that state, ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir arrived. Maslamah said to him, "ʿUqbah, listen to what ʿAbdullāh is saying."
ʿUqbah said, "He knows best. As for me, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'A group of my Ummah will not cease fighting for the command of Allah, overpowering their enemy. Those who oppose them will not harm them, until the Hour comes upon them while they are in that state.'"
Then ʿAbdullāh said, "Yes.

Then Allah will send a wind like the scent of musk, its touch like the touch of silk, and it will leave no soul with even the weight of a grain of faith in its heart except that it will take it. Then the worst of people will remain, and upon them the Hour will come."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people of the West will continue to prevail upon the truth until the Hour comes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, the like of that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, his hadith about hunting. Then Ibn Ḥātim said: Ibn Mahdī narrated to us from Muʿāwiyah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr and Abū al-Zāhiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī,
like the hadith of al-ʿAlāʾ, except that he did not mention its rotting, and he said about the dog:
"Eat it after three days, unless it rots, in which case leave it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [I heard] Jābir say, about the army of al-Khabaṭ, that a man slaughtered three camels, then three, then three, and then Abū ʿUbaydah forbade him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent us out, and we were three hundred men, carrying our provisions on our shoulders.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a detachment of three hundred and appointed Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ as their commander. Their provisions ran out, so Abū ʿUbaydah gathered their provisions in a bag, and he would give us our sustenance from it, until each day we received only one date.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a detachment, and I was among them, to the seashore.
They all narrated the rest of the hadith like the hadith of ʿAmr ibn Dīnār and Abū al-Zubayr, except that in the hadith of Wahb ibn Kaysān: "The army ate from it for eighteen nights."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out an expedition to the land of Juhaynah and appointed a man over them. And he narrated the hadith like their hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was on the pulpit, about eating the lizard (ḍabb), and he said:
"I do not eat it, and I do not forbid it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought the meat of a lizard (ḍabb) while he was in the house of Maymūnah, and Khālid ibn al-Walīd was with him.
Then he mentioned it with the meaning of the hadith of al-Zuhrī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Aṣamm said: A bridegroom invited us in Madinah, and he served us thirteen lizards. Some ate and some did not. I met Ibn ʿAbbās the next day and told him. The people around him spoke a great deal about it, until some of them said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'I do not eat it, nor do I forbid it, nor do I prohibit it.'"

Ibn ʿAbbās said, "What you have said is evil. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ was sent only to make things lawful and unlawful. While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with Maymūnah, and with him were al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and another woman, a table was brought to them with meat on it. When the Prophet ﷺ wanted to eat, Maymūnah said to him, 'It is lizard meat.'
So he held back his hand and said:
'This is meat I have never eaten.' And he said to them, 'Eat.'
So al-Faḍl, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and the woman ate from it.
And Maymūnah said, 'I will not eat anything except what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eats from.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said, "Messenger of Allah, I am in a land full of lizards. What do you command us, or what is your ruling for us?" He said:
"It was mentioned to me that a nation of the Children of Israel was transformed."
So he neither commanded nor forbade it.

Abū Saʿīd said: Later on, ʿUmar said, "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, benefits more than one person by it, and it is the food of most of these herdsmen. If I had it, I would eat it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ merely found it distasteful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: ʿUtbah ibn Abī Waqqāṣ made a request to his brother Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ to take into his custody the son of the slave woman of Zamʿah.
ʿUtbah said: "He is my son."
So when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came [to Makkah] at the time of the Conquest, Saʿd took the son of the slave woman of Zamʿah,
and he came with him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and ʿAbd ibn Zamʿah came along with him.
Saʿd said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is my brother's son; he charged me with the matter, saying that he is his son."
But ʿAbd ibn Zamʿah said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is my brother, the son of the slave woman of Zamʿah,
born on his bed."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at the son of the slave woman of Zamʿah,
and he was indeed the most similar of people to [ʿUtbah],
so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He is yours, O ʿAbd ibn Zamʿah,"
because he was born on the bed of his father.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Observe veiling from him, O Sawdah daughter of Zamʿah,"
because of what he saw of his resemblance to ʿUtbah.
And Sawdah was the wife of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The two parties to a sale have the option [to cancel] as long as they have not separated."
Hammām said: I found in my book: "he has the choice" three times. "If they are truthful and make things clear, their transaction will be blessed for them,
but if they lie and conceal, they may make a profit,
but the blessing of their transaction will be wiped out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade going out to meet the caravans, and forbade a city dweller from selling for a desert dweller.
[The narrator] said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās: "What is meant by 'a city dweller selling for a desert dweller'?" He said: "That he should not act as a broker for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hind bint ʿUtbah, the wife of Abū Sufyān, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Abū Sufyān is a miserly man; he does not give me enough maintenance for me and my children, except what I take from his wealth without his knowledge.
Is there any blame on me in that?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Take from his wealth in a reasonable manner what is sufficient for you and your children."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, and they were paying in advance for fruits for two and three years. So he said:
"Pay in advance for fruits for a known measure and a known term."
ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Walīd said: Sufyān narrated to us,
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to us, and he said:
"for a known measure and a known weight."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man who had died owing a debt would be brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would say:
"Has he left anything to pay off his debt?"
If he was told that he had left enough to settle it, he would pray over him; otherwise he would say to the Muslims:
"Pray over your companion."
Then when Allah granted him conquests, he stood and said:
"I am closer to the believers than their own selves. So whoever of the Muslims dies leaving a debt, its payment is my responsibility, and whoever leaves wealth, it belongs to his heirs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ made an arrangement with [the people of] Khaybar for half of what came out of it, whether fruit or crops.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd
Allāh ibn Numayr, the wording being Zuhayr's, said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Anas,

who said: The Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah when I was ten years old, and he died when I was twenty. My mothers used to urge me to serve him. He came into our house, and we milked for him from a domestic sheep, and water from the well in the house was mixed with it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank, while ʿUmar and Abū Bakr were on his left. ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of Allah, give it to Abū Bakr."
But he gave it to a Bedouin on his right, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one on the right, then the one on the right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Allah commanded Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā with five statements, that he act upon them and command the Children of Israel to act upon them. He was about to delay in doing so, so ʿĪsā said: 'Allah has commanded you with five statements that you act upon them and command the Children of Israel to act upon them. Either you command them, or I will command them.'

Yaḥyā said: 'I fear that if you get ahead of me in it, I will be swallowed by the earth or be punished.' So he gathered the people in Bayt al-Maqdis, and the mosque filled up and they sat on the balconies. Then he said: 'Allah has commanded me with five statements to act upon them, and He commands you to act upon them. The first is that you worship Allah and associate nothing with Him. The example of one who associates others with Allah is that of a man who bought a slave with his own pure money, with gold or silver, and said: "This is my house and this is my work, so work and pay [your earnings] to me." The slave would work and pay to someone other than his master. Which of you would be pleased for his slave to be like that? And Allah has commanded you to pray, so when you pray, do not turn around, for Allah sets His Face toward the face of His servant in his prayer as long as he does not turn away. And He has commanded you to fast, and the example of that is a man in a group who has with him a pouch containing musk, and all of them admire its scent. The scent of the fasting person is better with Allah than the scent of musk. And He has commanded you to give charity, and the example of that is a man whom the enemy captured, tied his hands to his neck, and brought him forward to strike his neck. He said: "I will ransom myself from you with little and with much."

So he ransomed himself from them. And He has commanded you to remember Allah, and the example of that is a man whom the enemy pursued swiftly until he reached a strong fortress and secured himself from them. In the same way, the servant cannot protect himself from Satan except by the remembrance of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ said:

"And I command you with five things that Allah has commanded me: listening, obedience, jihad, Hijrah, and the community. For whoever departs from the community by a handspan has cast off the yoke of Islam from his neck unless he returns. And whoever calls with the call of the Jāhiliyyah, he is among the crouching [bodies] of Hell."
A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, even if he prays and fasts?" He said:
"Even if he prays and fasts. So call yourselves by the call of Allah, who named you the Muslims, the believers, the servants of Allah."
This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb.
Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl said: Al-Ḥārith al-Ashʿarī had companionship [with the Prophet ﷺ], and he has other ḥadīth besides this one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah, the Emigrants came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have never seen a people more generous with much, nor better in giving support from little, than the people among whom we have settled. They spared us the burden and shared the pleasant gains with us, until we feared they would take all the reward." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"No, as long as you pray to Allah for them and praise them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim, or from Abū al-Haytham,
from Abū Saʿīd,
that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Do not keep company except with a believer, and let no one eat your food except a God-fearing person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit and called out in a loud voice, saying:

"O group of those who have submitted with their tongues while faith has not reached their hearts: do not harm the Muslims, do not shame them, and do not pursue their faults. For whoever pursues the fault of his Muslim brother, Allah will pursue his fault, and whoever Allah pursues his fault, He will expose him even in the depths of his home."
He said: One day Ibn ʿUmar looked at the House, or at the Kaaba, and said: "How great you are and how great is your sanctity! But the believer has greater sanctity with Allah than you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mercy is not removed except from one who is wretched."

He said: The name of Abū ʿUthmān, who narrated from Abū Hurayrah, is not known. It is said that he is the father of Mūsā ibn Abī ʿUthmān, from whom Abū al-Zinād narrated. Abū al-Zinād narrated from Mūsā ibn Abī ʿUthmān, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, more than one ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: An elderly man came wishing to see the Prophet ﷺ, but the people were slow to make room for him. So the Prophet ﷺ said:
"He is not one of us who does not show mercy to our young and respect our elders."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Having a good opinion of Allah is part of the excellence of worshipping Allah."
This ḥadīth is gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up on the day of the conquest of Makkah and said:

"A woman inherits from her husband's blood-money and his property, and he inherits from her blood-money and her property, so long as one of them has not killed the other. If one of them kills the other intentionally, he does not inherit anything from the victim's blood-money or property. If one of them kills the other by mistake, he inherits from the victim's property but does not inherit from the blood-money."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"It is disbelief for a person to claim a lineage that he does not know, or to deny his lineage, even if it is something small."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A child does not inherit until he cries out loudly at birth."
He said: Its crying out means that he weeps and screams, or sneezes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever equips a warrior in the cause of Allah until he is ready to set out will have a reward like his, until he dies or returns."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever equips a warrior in the cause of Allah will have a reward like his, without anything being reduced from the warrior's reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah, Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh and ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn all narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said:

"Whoever sends money for the cause of Allah while staying at home will have, for every dirham, seven hundred dirhams. And whoever fights himself in the cause of Allah and spends on that, will have, for every dirham, seven hundred thousand dirhams."
Then he recited this verse: {And Allah multiplies [it] for whom He wills.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān addressed the people and said: O people, I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that nothing prevented me from telling you except my being protective of you and of your companionship. So let each person choose for himself, or leave it. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Whoever keeps watch for one night in the cause of Allah, glorified is He, it is like a thousand nights of fasting by day and standing in prayer by night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever dies while keeping watch in the cause of Allah, the reward of the righteous deed he used to do will continue to be granted to him, his provision will continue to be granted to him, he will be safe from the trial [of the grave], and Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection safe from the great terror."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"One day of keeping watch in the cause of Allah, guarding the vulnerable frontier of the Muslims, seeking reward from Allah, outside the month of Ramadan, is greater in reward than a hundred years of worship, fasting by day and standing in prayer by night. And one day of keeping watch in the cause of Allah, guarding the vulnerable frontier of the Muslims, seeking reward from Allah, in the month of Ramadan, is better with Allah and greater in reward — I think he said — than a thousand years of worship, fasting by day and standing in prayer by night. If Allah returns him safely to his family, no sin will be recorded against him for a thousand years, good deeds will be recorded for him, and the reward of keeping watch will continue for him until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"May Allah have mercy on the one who stands guard."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Standing guard for a night in the cause of Allah is better than a man fasting and standing in prayer among his family for a thousand years, the year being three hundred and sixty days, and the day being like a thousand years."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When you are called to go out [for battle], then go out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever goes out for a journey in the cause of Allah, for the dust that touches him he will have the like of musk on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A battle at sea is like ten battles on land, and the one who becomes dizzy at sea is like one who is wallowing in his blood in the cause of Allah, glorified is He."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The martyr of the sea is like two martyrs of the land, and the one who is seasick at sea is like one wallowing in his blood on land. The one between the two waves is like one who traverses the world in obedience to Allah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has appointed the Angel of Death to seize the souls, except the martyr of the sea, for He Himself takes charge of seizing their souls. The martyr of the land is forgiven all sins except debt, while the martyr of the sea is forgiven sins and debt."
label: machine translation
