segments_en: Ruwaym [reported] that Ibn al-Daylamī rode off seeking ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ. Ibn al-Daylamī said: I went in to him and said, "O ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, have you heard
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention anything about the matter of khamr?" He said, "Yes, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'No man from my nation drinks khamr and has Allah accept a prayer from him for forty days.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I accompanied Ibn ʿUmar to al-Ḥumā. When the sun set, I hesitated to say to him, "Prayer." He kept travelling until the whiteness of the horizon and the blackness of the early night had gone. Then he dismounted and prayed Maghrib, three rakʿahs, and then prayed two rakʿahs right after it. Then he said, "This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled until he came to ʿArafah, and found the tent had been pitched for him at Namirah. He stayed there until, when the sun had passed its zenith, he ordered al-Qaṣwāʾ to be saddled for him. When he reached the middle of the valley, he addressed the people. Then Bilāl called the adhān and then the iqāmah, and he prayed Ẓuhr; then he called the iqāmah again and prayed ʿAṣr, and he did not pray anything between them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿUmar when he left ʿArafāt. When he came to Jamʿ [Muzdalifah], he combined Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ. When he had finished, he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did the same as this in this place."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was in the mosque of ʿAmr ibn Sharḥabīl when the prayer was called. They began to wait for him, and he said, "I was praying Witr."

He said: ʿAbdullāh was asked, "Is there Witr after the adhān?" He said, "Yes, and after the iqāmah." And he narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he slept through the prayer until the sun rose, and then prayed. The wording is Yaḥyā's.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When they slept through the prayer until the sun rose, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let one of you pray it the next day at its proper time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey and travelled by night. When it was near dawn, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted and slept, and the people slept, and we did not wake until the sun had risen upon us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the muʾadhdhin, who called the adhān. Then he prayed the two rakʿahs before Fajr. Then he ordered him, and he called the iqāmah, and he led the people in prayer. Then he told us of what will happen until the Hour is established.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we were kept from the prayers of Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ. That was hard on me, and I said to myself, "We are with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and in the cause of Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered Bilāl, who called the iqāmah, and he led us in Ẓuhr; then he called the iqāmah and he led us in ʿAṣr; then he called the iqāmah and he led us in Maghrib; then he called the iqāmah and he led us in ʿIshāʾ. Then he went around among us and said:
"There is no group on the earth remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, other than you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled by night, then stopped to rest at the end of the night. He did not wake until the sun, or part of it, had risen. He did not pray until the sun had risen high, and then he prayed. And it is the middle prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Ḥunayn, I went out as one of ten men from the people of Makkah in search of them. We heard them calling the adhān for prayer, so we got up and called the adhān, mocking them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have heard among these the adhān of a person with a beautiful voice."
He sent for us, and we called the adhān one man after another, and I was the last of them. When I called the adhān, he said, "Come."
He seated me in front of him, passed his hand over my forelock, and blessed me three times. Then he said:
"Go and call the adhān at the Sacred House."
I said, "How, O Messenger of Allah?" He taught me, as you call it now:

"Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Come to prayer, come to prayer. Come to success, come to success. Prayer is better than sleep, prayer is better than sleep."
[This is] in the first [adhān] of the morning. He said: And he taught me the iqāmah, two times each:

"Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Come to prayer, come to prayer. Come to success, come to success. The prayer has begun, the prayer has begun. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said on the following day, the Day of Sacrifice, while he was at Minā: "
Tomorrow we will camp at Khayf Banī Kinānah, where they pledged themselves to disbelief."
He meant by that al-Muḥaṣṣab,
and that was because Quraysh and Kinānah had made a pact against Banū Hāshim and Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib,
or Banū al-Muṭṭalib, that they would not marry them
nor trade with them until they handed over the Prophet ﷺ to them.
Salāmah related from ʿUqayl, and Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk from al-Awzāʿī: Ibn Shihāb informed me; and both said "Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions came to Makkah, and the fever of Yathrib had weakened them.
The polytheists said, "Tomorrow a people will come to you whom the fever has weakened, and they have suffered severely from it."

So they sat on the side near the Ḥijr, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded them to walk briskly for three circuits and to walk normally between the two corners, so that the polytheists would see their strength. The polytheists said, "These are the ones you claimed the fever had weakened? They are stronger than such and such!"
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Nothing prevented him from commanding them to walk briskly in all the circuits except his concern for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ṭawāf in Hajj and ʿUmrah, on first arriving he would walk briskly for three circuits around the House, then walk for four, then pray two prostrations [units of prayer], then perform the circuits between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib
asked permission from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to stay in Makkah during the nights of Minā because of his duty of providing water to the pilgrims, and he gave him permission.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Tamattuʿ in the Farewell Hajj, combining ʿUmrah with Hajj. He offered a sacrificial animal and brought it with him from Dhū al-Ḥulayfah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began by declaring the intention for ʿUmrah, then for Hajj, and the people performed Tamattuʿ with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, combining ʿUmrah with Hajj. Among the people were those who offered a sacrificial animal and brought it along, and among them were those who did not. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Makkah, he said to the people: "

Whoever among you has brought a sacrificial animal, nothing that was forbidden to him becomes lawful until he completes his Hajj. And whoever among you has not brought a sacrificial animal, let him perform ṭawāf around the House and between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, cut his hair short, and come out of iḥrām, then declare the intention for Hajj and offer a sacrificial animal. Whoever cannot find an animal, let him fast three days during the Hajj and seven when he returns to his family."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ṭawāf when he arrived in Makkah. He first touched the corner, then walked briskly for three of the seven circuits and walked the remaining four. Then, when he finished his ṭawāf around the House, he prayed two units at the Station [of Ibrāhīm], then gave the salām and left. He went to aṣ-Ṣafā and performed seven circuits between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. Then he did not come out of iḥrām from anything that was forbidden to him until he completed his Hajj, slaughtered his sacrificial animal on the Day of Sacrifice, and poured forth and performed ṭawāf around the House. Then everything that had been forbidden to him became lawful. And the people who had offered a sacrificial animal and brought it along did just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Bakr, from ʿAmrah

bint ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, that she informed him that Ibn Ziyād wrote to ʿĀʾishah: "ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās said that whoever sends a sacrificial animal, what is forbidden to the pilgrim becomes forbidden to him until the animal is slaughtered. I have sent my sacrificial animal, so write to me with your instruction."

ʿAmrah said: ʿĀʾishah said, "It is not as Ibn ʿAbbās said. I twisted the garlands of the sacrificial animals of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with my own hands; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ garlanded them with his own hand, then sent them with my father. Nothing that Allah had made lawful for him became forbidden to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until the animal was slaughtered."

label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to twist the garlands of the sacrificial animals of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with my own hands; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would garland them with his own hand, then send them with my father. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not leave anything that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had made lawful for him until the animal was slaughtered.

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to be asked on the day of Minā, and he would say: "
No harm, no harm."
A man came to him and said, "I shaved my head before I slaughtered." He said, "No harm."
He said, "I threw the pebbles after evening had come." He said, "No harm."

and if she confesses, stone her."

and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered those who were in the house to beat him. [The narrator] said: I was among those who beat him,

"This does not enter the house of any people except that Allah makes humiliation enter it."

So they said: "[Then] you spare us the labor, and we will share the fruit with you."

segments_en: I knew during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that land was rented out.
Then ʿAbdullāh feared that the Prophet ﷺ might have introduced something new regarding that which he did not know about,
so he gave up renting out land.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They used to rent out land during the time of the Prophet ﷺ for what grew by the water channels, or for something the owner of the land set aside for himself, so the Prophet ﷺ forbade that. I said to Rāfiʿ: "What about [renting] it for dinars and dirhams?" Rāfiʿ said: "There is no harm in [renting] it for dinars and dirhams."
Al-Layth said: What was forbidden in that was something which, if people of understanding of the lawful and the unlawful were to examine it, they would not permit it,
because of the uncertainty and risk it involves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was speaking one day, and with him was a man from the desert-dwelling Arabs: "
A man from the people of Paradise asked his Lord for permission to farm. [Allah] said: 'Are you not already in what you wish?'
He said: 'Yes, but I love to farm.'

So he hurried and sowed, and in the blink of an eye his plants sprouted, matured, and were harvested, [piled up] like mountains. Then Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Take it, O son of Adam, for nothing satisfies you.'"
The Bedouin said: "O Messenger of Allah, you will only find this man to be a Qurashī or an Anṣārī, for they are people of farming,
whereas we are not people of farming."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed the eclipse prayer, and he said: "
The Fire was brought close to me until I said: 'O my Lord,
[will] I be with them?' And there was a woman—I think he said—being scratched by a cat. He said: 'What is the matter with this one?' They said: 'She confined it until it died of hunger.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Indeed, Allah has angels who go about the roads,
seeking the people of remembrance [of Allah].
So when they find a people remembering Allah, they call out to one another, 'Come to what you need.'
He said: So they surround them with their wings up to the lowest heaven.
He said: Then their Lord asks them, though He knows best about them, 'What are My servants saying?' They say: 'They are glorifying You, declaring Your greatness, praising You, and exalting You.'
He said: He says, 'Have they seen Me?' He said: They say, 'No, by Allah, they have not seen You.'
He said: He says, 'And how would it be if they had seen Me?' He said: They say, 'If they had seen You, they would be more intense in worship of You,
more intense in exalting You,
and more frequent in glorifying You.'
He said: He says, 'What are they asking of Me?' He said: They say, 'They ask You for Paradise.'
He said: He says, 'Have they seen it?' He said: They say, 'No, by Allah, O Lord, they have not seen it.'
He said: He says, 'And how would it be if they had seen it?' He said: They say, 'If they had seen it, they would be more eager for it,
more earnest in seeking it,
and greater in their desire for it.'
He said: 'And from what do they seek refuge?' He said: They say, 'From the Fire.'
He said: He says, 'Have they seen it?' He said: They say, 'No, by Allah, they have not seen it.'
He said: He says, 'And how would it be if they had seen it?' He said: They say, 'If they had seen it, they would flee from it more intensely,
and fear it more.'
He said: So He says, 'I call you to witness that I have forgiven them.'
He said: One of the angels says, 'Among them is so-and-so, who is not one of them; he only came for some need.'
He said: 'They are the companions in whose company no one who sits with them is left wretched.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
There are two blessings in which many people are cheated: health and free time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah and Umm Salamah were asked which deed was most beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They both said: "The one that is done continuously, even if it is little."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
None of you will be saved by his deeds."
They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "
Not even I, unless Allah envelops me in forgiveness and mercy."
And Ibn ʿAwn gestured with his hand like this and pointed to his head: "
Not even I, unless Allah envelops me in forgiveness and mercy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed, Allah created mercy, on the day He created it, in one hundred parts,
and He kept ninety-nine parts of mercy with Him,
and sent down one part of mercy among all His creation.
If the disbeliever knew all the mercy that is with Allah, he would not despair of Paradise,
and if the believer knew all the punishment that is with Allah, he would not feel safe from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

My likeness is that of a man who kindled a fire, and when it lit up what was around it, moths and these insects that fall into fire began to fall into it, and he began to hold them back, but they overpowered him and plunged into it. He said: That is my likeness and yours: I am taking hold of your waists to keep you from the Fire, [saying,] 'Come away from the Fire! Come away from the Fire!' but you overpower me and plunge into it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said—and I did not hear anyone say 'The Prophet ﷺ said' other than him, so I drew near to him and heard him say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Whoever does a deed to be heard, Allah will make it known [to people] about him,
and whoever does it to be seen, Allah will expose him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to narrate that a funeral procession passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "One at rest, and one from whom others are at rest."
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is the one at rest and the one from whom others are at rest?" He said: "
The believing servant is at rest from the toil of this world and its harm, [going] to the mercy of Allah,
while the wicked servant, people, lands, trees, and animals are at rest from him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three groups: those hoping and fearing; two on one camel, three on one camel, four on one camel, and ten on one camel. And the rest of them the Fire will gather: it will rest with them where they rest at midday, stay with them where they spend the night, be with them in the morning wherever they are in the morning, and be with them in the evening wherever they are in the evening."
label: machine translation

segments_en: You will meet Allah barefoot, naked, walking, and uncircumcised."
Sufyān said: This is among what we count as [hadith] that Ibn ʿAbbās heard from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Indeed, Allah will say to the people of Paradise, 'O people of Paradise.'
They will say, 'At Your service, our Lord, and at Your pleasure, and all good is in Your hands.'
He will say, 'Are you content?' They will say, 'Why should we not be content, O Lord, when You have given us what You have not given to any of Your creation?'
He will say, 'Shall I not give you something better than that?'
They will say, 'O Lord, what could be better than that?' He will say, 'I will bestow My good pleasure upon you, and I will never be displeased with you after it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿAmr ibn Abī Sufyān], an ally of Banū Zuhrah, who was among the companions of Abū Hurayrah, reported from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ten men as a reconnaissance party,
and appointed ʿĀṣim ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī over them,
the grandfather of ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
When they reached al-Hadah, between ʿUsfān and Makkah, they were mentioned to a clan of Hudhayl called Banū Liḥyān,
so about a hundred archers set out after them.
They followed their tracks until they found the remains of the dates they had eaten at a place where they had camped, and they said: These are the dates of Yathrib. So they pursued their tracks.
When ʿĀṣim and his companions sensed them, they took refuge in a high place,
and the people surrounded them,
and said to them: Come down and surrender, and you have our covenant and pledge that we will not kill any of you.
ʿĀṣim ibn Thābit said: O people,
as for me, I will not come down under the protection of a disbeliever.
Then he said: O Allah, inform Your Prophet ﷺ about us. They shot them with arrows and killed ʿĀṣim,
and three of them came down to them under the covenant and pledge,
among them Khubayb, Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah, and another man.
When the enemy had overpowered them, they loosened the strings of their bows and bound them with them.
The third man said: This is the first betrayal.
By Allah, I will not accompany you.
I have an example in these men, meaning the slain. They dragged him and struggled with him,
but he refused to go with them.
So Khubayb and Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah were taken away, and they sold them after the Battle of Badr.
The sons of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir ibn Nawfal bought Khubayb,
for Khubayb was the one who had killed al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir on the day of Badr.
Khubayb remained with them as a prisoner until they resolved to kill him.
He borrowed a razor from one of the daughters of al-Ḥārith to shave with, and she lent it to him.
A little son of hers wandered over to him while she was not paying attention, until he reached him,

and she found him sitting him on his thigh with the razor in his hand. She said: I was seized by a fright that Khubayb noticed, and he said: Are you afraid that I will kill him? I would never do that. She said: By Allah, I never saw a prisoner better than Khubayb.
By Allah, I found him one day eating from a bunch of grapes in his hand,
while he was bound in iron chains,
and there was no fruit in Makkah at that time. She used to say: It was provision that Allah gave to Khubayb.
When they took him out of the Sanctuary to kill him in the unsanctified area, Khubayb said to them: Let me pray two rakʿahs.
They left him, and he prayed two rakʿahs,
then he said: By Allah, were it not that you would think I am anxious, I would have prayed more.
Then he said: O Allah, count them one by one, kill them scattered,
and do not leave any of them.

Then he began to recite: I do not care, as I am killed a Muslim, on which side my death falls for Allah. That is for the sake of God, and if He wills, He will bless the severed parts of a torn body. Then Abū Sirwaʿah ʿUqbah ibn al-Ḥārith stood up to him
and killed him. Khubayb was the one who established the prayer as a practice for every Muslim who is killed in captivity.
He [the Prophet ﷺ] informed his companions of their news on the day they were struck.
Some people of Quraysh sent word, when they heard that ʿĀṣim ibn Thābit had been killed, that something of him be brought that could be recognized,
for he had killed one of their great men.
So Allah sent for ʿĀṣim something like a cloud of bees,
which protected him from their messengers,
and they were unable to cut anything from him.
Kaʿb ibn Mālik said: They mentioned Murārah ibn al-Rabīʿ al-ʿAmrī and Hilāl ibn Umayyah al-Wāqifī,
two righteous men who had witnessed Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas brought out to us two sandals without hair, each with two straps.
Then Thābit al-Bunānī later told me from Anas that they were the sandals of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The news of the Prophet's ﷺ emergence reached us while we were in Yemen, so we set out as emigrants to him,
I and two brothers of mine, I being the youngest of them,
one of them Abū Burdah and the other Abū Ruhm,
either he said: in some,
or he said: in fifty-three or fifty-two men of my people. We boarded a ship,
and our ship cast us ashore at the Negus in Abyssinia,
where we met Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and his companions with him. Jaʿfar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us here,
and commanded us to stay, so stay with us. So we stayed with him,
until we all came back together,
and we met the Prophet ﷺ when he had conquered Khaybar, and he gave us a share.
Or he said: he gave us some of it.
He did not apportion anything of it to anyone who was absent from the conquest of Khaybar,
except to those who had witnessed it with him,
except for the people of our ship who came with Jaʿfar and his companions;
he apportioned to them along with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "It is not right for a Muslim who has something to bequeath to let three nights pass without having his will written down with him."
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: "Not a single night has passed since I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that, except that I have my will with me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Saʿd said:] The Prophet ﷺ came to him while he was ill, and he said: "I have no child except one daughter. Shall I bequeath all my wealth?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "No."
He said: "Then shall I bequeath half of it?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "No."
He said: "Then shall I bequeath a third of it?" He said:
"A third—and a third is a lot."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Thaqīf were allies of Banū ʿUqayl. Thaqīf captured two men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ captured a man from Banū ʿUqayl and took al-ʿAḍbāʾ along with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by him while he was in bonds, and he said: "O Muḥammad!" He came to him and said: "What is the matter with you?"
He said: "Why did you seize me, and why did you seize the one who outstrips the pilgrims?" He said, stressing the gravity of it:
"I seized you for the offence of your allies, Thaqīf."
Then he turned away from him, and the man called out to him: "O Muḥammad! O Muḥammad!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was merciful and gentle, so he returned to him and said: "What is the matter with you?"
He said: "I am a Muslim." He said:
"Had you said it while you were in control of your affair, you would have been completely successful."
Then he turned away, and the man called out to him: "O Muḥammad! O Muḥammad!" He came to him and said: "What is the matter with you?"
He said: "I am hungry, so feed me, and I am thirsty, so give me drink." He said: "That is what you need."

Then he was exchanged for the two men. He said: A woman of the Anṣār was captured, and al-ʿAḍbāʾ was taken. The woman was kept in bonds, and the people used to rest their camels in front of their houses. One night she slipped free of the bonds and went to the camels. Whenever she approached a camel it groaned, so she left it, until she reached al-ʿAḍbāʾ, who did not groan. He said: She was a docile, well-trained camel. She sat on its back, urged it on, and it set off. The people noticed and sought her, but she outpaced them. He said: She vowed to Allah that if Allah saved her on it, she would sacrifice it. When she arrived in Madinah, the people saw her.
They said: "Al-ʿAḍbāʾ, the camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!"
She said that she had vowed that if Allah saved her on it, she would sacrifice it.
They went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. He said:

"Glory be to Allah! What an evil repayment she gave it! She vowed to Allah that if Allah saved her on it, she would sacrifice it. There is no fulfilling of a vow in disobedience, nor in what a person does not own."
And in the narration of Ibn Ḥujr:
"There is no vow in disobedience to Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came upon an old man walking between his two sons, leaning on them, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"What is the matter with this man?"
His two sons said: "O Messenger of Allah, he had made a vow." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Ride, old man, for Allah is independent of you and of your vow."
The wording is that of Qutaybah and Ibn Ḥujr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The expiation for a vow is the expiation for an oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"An oath is according to the intention of the one who requires the oath."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar
called for a slave boy of his and saw a mark on his back. He said to him: "Did I hurt you?" He said: "No."
He said: "Then you are free."
Then he picked up something from the ground and said: "I have no reward in this that equals the weight of this. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever strikes his slave for a punishment he did not commit, or slaps him, his expiation is to set him free.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī said: I was beating a slave of mine with a whip when I heard a voice behind me:
"Know, Abū Masʿūd!"
I did not understand the voice because of my anger. He said: When he came near me, it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was saying:
"Know, Abū Masʿūd! Know, Abū Masʿūd!"
He said: I threw the whip from my hand, and he said:
"Know, Abū Masʿūd, that Allah has more power over you than you have over this slave."
He said: I said: "I will never beat a slave after this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out an army and appointed ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib over them. He went on with the expedition and took a slave girl, and they disapproved of that. Four of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a pact and said, "When we meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we will tell him what ʿAlī did." When the Muslims returned from a journey, they would begin with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, greet him, and then go to their homes. So when the expedition arrived, they greeted the Prophet ﷺ, and one of the four stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, have you not seen that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib did such and such?"

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him. Then the second stood up and said the same as he had said, and he turned away from him. Then the third stood up and said the same, and he turned away from him. Then the fourth stood up and said the same as they had said, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to him, with anger visible on his face, and said:
"What do you want from ʿAlī? What do you want from ʿAlī? What do you want from ʿAlī? Indeed ʿAlī is from me and I am from him, and he is the guardian of every believer after me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever I am his master, then ʿAlī is his master."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"May Allah have mercy on Abū Bakr: he married his daughter to me, carried me to the abode of emigration, and freed Bilāl from his own wealth. May Allah have mercy on ʿUmar: he speaks the truth even if it is bitter; the truth has left him without a friend. May Allah have mercy on ʿUthmān: the angels feel shy before him. May Allah have mercy on ʿAlī. O Allah, turn the truth with him wherever he turns."
label: machine translation

segments_en: At al-Raḥbah he said: When it was the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah, some of the polytheists came out to us, among them Suhayl ibn ʿAmr and some of the leaders of the polytheists. They said, "O Messenger of Allah, some of our sons, brothers, and slaves have come out to you, and they have no understanding of the religion. They only came out to flee from our wealth and our estates, so send them back to us."
"If they have no understanding of the religion, we will teach them." Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"O company of Quraysh, you must stop, or Allah will send against you someone who will strike your necks with the sword over the religion, one whose heart Allah has tested for faith."
They said, "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" Abū Bakr said to him, "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" and ʿUmar said, "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"He is the one who is mending the sandal."
He had given ʿAlī his sandal to mend. Then ʿAlī turned to us and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib:
"You are from me and I am from you."
There is a story in the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ established brotherhood between his Companions. Then ʿAlī came with tears in his eyes and said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have made brothers of your Companions but you have not made a brother of me with anyone."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"You are my brother in this world and the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a bird with him and said:
"O Allah, bring me the most beloved of Your creation to You, to eat this bird with me."
Then ʿAlī came and ate with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said, "When I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would give me, and when I was silent, he would begin by giving me." This hadith is ḥasan gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I am the house of wisdom, and ʿAlī is its door."
This hadith is gharīb munkar.
Some of them narrated this hadith from Sharīk without mentioning in it al-Ṣunābiḥī, and we do not know this hadith from any of the trustworthy narrators other than Sharīk.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called ʿAlī on the day of al-Ṭāʾif and spoke with him privately. The people said, "His private conversation with his cousin has been long."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I did not speak with him privately; rather, Allah spoke with him privately."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAlī:
"O ʿAlī, it is not lawful for anyone to be in a state of major impurity in this mosque except me and you."
ʿAlī ibn al-Mundhir said: I said to Ḍirār ibn Ṣurad, "What is the meaning of this hadith?" He said, "It is not lawful for anyone to pass through it in a state of major impurity except me and you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was sent [with the message] on Monday, and ʿAlī prayed on Tuesday.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he said:

There were only four years between their embracing Islam and the revelation of this verse by which Allah rebuked them: {And let them not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term became long for them, so their hearts hardened; and many of them are defiantly disobedient.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at a funeral. He sat at the edge of the grave and wept until the soil was wet. Then he said:
"O my brothers, prepare for the like of this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no believing servant from whose eyes tears come out, even if like the head of a fly, out of fear of Allah, and then they touch something of the heat of his face, except that Allah forbids him from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Deeds are only like a container: if its bottom is good, its top is good, and if its bottom is corrupt, its top is corrupt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a servant prays well in public and prays well in private, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'This is truly My servant.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were discussing the False Messiah, and he said:
"Shall I not tell you of what I fear for you more than the False Messiah?"
He said: We said, "Yes." He said:
"Hidden shirk: that a man stands to pray and beautifies his prayer because he sees another man looking at him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"What I fear most for my nation is associating partners with Allah. I do not say that they will worship the sun, the moon, or an idol, but [they will do] deeds for other than Allah, and [have] a hidden desire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The good whose reward comes quickest is righteousness and maintaining family ties, and the evil whose punishment comes quickest is oppression and severing family ties."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, "Which people are best?" He said:
"Everyone with a purified heart and truthful tongue."
They said, "We know the truthful tongue, but what is a purified heart?" He said:
"It is the God-fearing, pure one, in whom there is no sin, no transgression, no rancor, and no envy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no intellect like forethought, no piety like restraint, and no lineage like good character."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I know a phrase—and ʿUthmān said, a verse—that if all people adopted it, it would suffice them."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, which verse, which verse?" He said:
"And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us at al-Nabāʾ or al-Nabāwah—he said: al-Nabāwah is by Ṭāʾif—and he said:
"You will soon be able to tell the people of Paradise from the people of the Fire."
They said, "By what, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"By good praise and bad praise. You are the witnesses of Allah over one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, how can I know whether I have done well when I have done well, and whether I have done wrong when I have done wrong?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When your neighbors say that you have done well, then you have done well, and when they say that you have done wrong, then you have done wrong."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people of Paradise are those whose ears Allah fills with the good praise of people while he hears it,
and the people of the Fire are those whose ears are filled with the bad talk of people while he hears it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The example of this nation is like four men:
a man whom Allah has given wealth and knowledge, so he acts on his knowledge with his wealth, spending it rightfully; and a man whom Allah has given knowledge but not wealth, so he says:
'If I had the like of this, I would do with it what he does.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The two are equal in reward. And a man whom Allah has given wealth but not knowledge, so he squanders his wealth, spending it wrongfully; and a man whom Allah has given neither knowledge nor wealth, so he says:
'If I had the like of this man's wealth, I would do with it what he does.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The two are equal in sin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, and they had two days on which they would play. He said:
"What are these two days?"
They said, "We used to play on them in the days of ignorance."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, Allah has replaced them for you with something better than them: the Day of Sacrifice and the Day of Fitr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Busr, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, went out with the people on the day of ʿĪd, either al-Fiṭr or al-Aḍḥā, and he objected to the imam's delay. He said, "We would have already finished at this hour of ours," and that was at the time of the voluntary prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Rain fell on the people on the day of ʿĪd during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he led them in prayer in the mosque.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on an extremely hot day. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed with his Companions and made the standing so long that they began to fall down. Then he bowed and made it long, then he rose and made it long, then he bowed and made it long, then he rose and made it long, then he prostrated twice. Then he stood and did the like of that. He would move forward, then move back. So it was four bowings and four prostrations. They used to say that the sun and the moon are eclipsed only for the death of one of their great men, but they are two signs among the signs of Allah which He shows you. So when an eclipse occurs, pray until it clears.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a man of the people of Basra, who attended a sermon one day by Samurah ibn Jundub. In his sermon he mentioned a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Samurah ibn Jundub said: One day, while I and a boy from the Anṣār were shooting at two targets of ours during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when the sun was, in the eye of the observer, about two or three spear-lengths above the horizon, it turned black. One of us said to his companion, "Let us go to the mosque, for by Allah, this sun will surely bring about something new for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning his nation." He said: We hurried to the mosque, and we met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he came out to the people. He said: He went forward and prayed, and he stood for the longest standing he had ever made with us in any prayer, and we heard no sound from him. Then he bowed with us for the longest bowing he had ever made with us in any prayer, and we heard no sound from him. Then he prostrated with us for the longest prostration he had ever made with us in any prayer, and we heard no sound from him. Then he did the same in the second rakʿah. He said: The clearing of the sun coincided with his sitting in the second rakʿah. He gave the salām, then praised Allah and extolled Him, and testified that there is no god but Allah and that he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger. (Abridged.)
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited a long recitation and recited it aloud, meaning in the eclipse prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to Ibn ʿAbbās after the dawn prayer, "So-and-so has died," referring to one of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. He prostrated. It was said to him, "Do you prostrate at this hour?" He said, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not say:
'When you see a sign, prostrate'?
And what sign is greater than the passing away of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Your Lord is amazed at a shepherd of sheep on the peak of a mountain crag who calls the adhān for prayer and prays. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Look at this servant of Mine, who calls the adhān and establishes the prayer, fearing Me. I have forgiven My servant and admitted him into Paradise.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at a place, he would not set out until he had prayed Ẓuhr. A man said to him, "Even if it is midday?" He said, "Even if it is midday."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is ʿĀmir ibn Wāthilah, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal:

that during the expedition of Tabūk, when the Prophet ﷺ set out before the sun passed its zenith, he would delay Ẓuhr until he combined it with ʿAṣr and prayed them together. And when he set out after the sun passed its zenith, he would hasten ʿAṣr to Ẓuhr and pray Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr together, then travel on. And when he set out before Maghrib, he would delay Maghrib until he prayed it with ʿIshāʾ, and when he set out after Maghrib, he would hasten ʿIshāʾ and pray it with Maghrib.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray four rakʿahs before Ẓuhr when the sun passed its zenith, not separating between them with a salām. He said:
"Indeed, the gates of heaven are opened when the sun passes its zenith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"May Allah have mercy on a person who prays four rakʿahs before ʿAṣr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a military expedition, and he saw people gathered around something. So he sent a man and said:
"Go and see why these people have gathered."
The man came back and said, "They are gathered around a woman who has been killed." He ﷺ said:
"She was not one who would have fought."
He said: Khālid ibn al-Walīd was in command of the vanguard, so he sent a man and said:
"Tell Khālid not to kill any woman or any hired laborer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Of their women—she means Banū Qurayẓah—none was killed except one woman. She was sitting with me, talking and laughing heartily, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was killing their men with the swords, when a caller called out her name: "Where is so-and-so?" She said, "I am here."
I said, "What is the matter with you?" She said, "A new matter I introduced."
She said: So she was taken away and her neck was struck. I will never forget how astonishing she was, laughing heartily although she knew she would be killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and he went off to relieve himself. We saw a hummarah [a small bird] with two chicks, so we took its two chicks. The bird came and began to beat its wings in distress. Then the Prophet ﷺ came and said:
"Who has distressed this bird by taking its young? Return its young to it."
And he saw an anthill that we had burned, and he said:
"Who burned this?" We said, "We did." He said:
"It is not fitting for anyone to punish with fire except the Lord of the fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for [the expedition of] Tabūk, so I went to my family and came back, and the first of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had already set out. I began calling out in Madīnah: "Is there anyone who will carry a man, for which he will have a share [of the spoils]?" An old man of the Anṣār called out: "We will give him his share on condition that we carry him in turns and his food is with us." I said, "Yes."
He said, "Then proceed, with the blessing of Allah, the Exalted."

He said: So I set out with the best of companions, until Allah granted us spoils. I received some young she-camels, and I drove them until I came to him. He came out and sat on a saddle-bag of his camel's saddle-bags, then said, "Drive them away from me."
Then he said, "Drive them toward me."
Then he said, "I see that your she-camels are only noble ones." He said, "They are only your spoils, which was the condition I made with you."
He said, "Take your she-camels, nephew, for it was not your share that we intended."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAbdullāh ibn Ghālib al-Laythī on a military expedition, and I was among them. He commanded them to launch a raid on Banū al-Mulawwaḥ at al-Kadīd. So we set out, and when we reached al-Kadīd, we met al-Ḥārith ibn al-Barṣāʾ al-Laythī and seized him. He said, "I only came wanting Islam, and I only came out to go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." We said, "If you are a Muslim, our keeping you bound for a day and a night will not harm you, and if you are otherwise, we will secure you." So we bound him tightly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The captives were brought when they were brought, while Sawdah bint Zamʿah was at the house of the family of ʿAfrāʾ, in their resting place, with ʿAwf and Muʿawwidh, the two sons of ʿAfrāʾ. He said: That was before the hijāb was imposed upon them. Sawdah said: By Allah, I was with them when I came and it was said, "These are the captives, who have been brought."
So I returned to my house, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in it, and there was Abū Yazīd Suhayl ibn ʿAmr in a corner of the room, with his hands tied to his neck with a rope.
Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman whose children did not survive would vow that if a child of hers lived, she would make him Jewish. When Banū al-Naḍīr were expelled, among them were some sons of the Anṣār. They said, "We will not abandon our sons." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {There is no compulsion in religion; truly the right path has become distinct from error.} Abū Dāwūd said: The miqlāt is the woman whose children do not survive.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the conquest of Makkah:
"There are four people I will not grant safety, whether in the sanctuary or outside it." And he named them.
He said: And two singing-girls belonging to Miqyas; one of them was killed and the other escaped and later accepted Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays wanted to appoint

Masrūq to office. ʿUmārah ibn ʿUqbah said to him, "Will you appoint a man who is one of the remnants of the killers of ʿUthmān?" Masrūq said to him, "ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated to us—and he was, in our view, trustworthy in narration—that when the Prophet ﷺ wanted to kill your father, he said, 'Who will care for the children?' He ﷺ said, 'The Fire.'
I am satisfied for you with what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was satisfied with for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We fought alongside ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and four non-Arab men of the enemy were brought to him. He ordered that they be killed, and they were killed while bound.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no prayer for one who does not recite the Opening of the Book (al-Fātiḥah) and something more."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to lead us in the first two rakʿahs of the Ẓuhr prayer, and he would sometimes let us hear a verse. He would lengthen the first and shorten the second. He would do the same in the Fajr prayer, lengthening the first and shortening the second. And in the first two rakʿahs of the ʿAṣr prayer he would recite with us, lengthening the first and shortening the second.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer, meaning the ʿAtamah, behind Abū Hurayrah. He recited the sūrah {When the sky is split open}, and prostrated in it. When he had finished, I said, "O Abū Hurayrah, what is this prostration? We did not use to prostrate in it."
He said, "Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ prostrated in it while I was behind him, so I will keep prostrating in it until I meet Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When

the imam says {not of those who incur wrath, nor of those who go astray}, then say 'Āmīn', for the angels say 'Āmīn', and the imam says 'Āmīn'. Whoever's saying of 'Āmīn' coincides with the angels' saying of 'Āmīn' will have his previous sins forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn and I prayed

behind ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. Whenever he prostrated he said the takbīr, whenever he raised his head he said the takbīr, and whenever he rose after the two rakʿahs he said the takbīr. When we finished the prayer, ʿImrān took me by the hand and said, "This man has led us in the prayer of Muḥammad ﷺ."
Or he said, "This man has reminded me of the prayer of Muḥammad ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for prayer, he would say the takbīr as he stood, then say the takbīr as he bowed, then he would say:
"Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him)
as he raised his back from bowing. Then, while standing, he would say:
"Rabbanā wa laka al-ḥamd" (Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise).

Then he would say the takbīr as he went down to prostrate, then say the takbīr as he raised his head, then say the takbīr as he prostrated, then say the takbīr as he raised his head. Then he would do the same throughout the whole prayer until he completed it, and he would say the takbīr as he stood up after sitting at the end of the two rakʿahs. Then Abū Hurayrah would say, "Indeed, I am the one among you whose prayer most resembles that of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed beside my father, and when I bowed I interlaced my fingers and placed them between my knees. He struck my hand. When he finished the prayer he said, "We used to do this, then we were commanded to place our hands on the knees."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "I will certainly show you how close I can bring you to the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said: Abū Hurayrah used to recite the qunūt in the last rakʿah of the Ẓuhr prayer,
and of the late ʿIshāʾ prayer, and of the Fajr prayer, after saying "Sami ʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah"; he would pray for the believers and curse the disbelievers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah
used to say the takbīr in every prayer, obligatory and otherwise, in Ramadan and at other times.
He would say the takbīr when he stood,
then say the takbīr when he bowed,
then say, "Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah."
Then he would say, "Rabbanā wa laka al-ḥamd,"
before he prostrated.
Then he would say, "Allāhu akbar"
as he went down to prostrate,
then say the takbīr as he raised his head from prostration,
then say the takbīr as he prostrated,
then say the takbīr as he raised his head from prostration,
then say the takbīr as he stood up from sitting after the two rakʿahs,
and he would do that in every rakʿah until he finished the prayer.

Then, when he turned away from the prayer, he would say, "By the One in whose hand is my soul, I am the closest of you in resemblance to the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This was his prayer until he departed from this world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to prostrate on seven parts, and he forbade gathering up the hair and clothing: on the hands, the knees, and the tips of the toes.
Sufyān said: Ibn Ṭāwus told us that he placed his hands on his forehead and passed them over his nose.
He said, "This counts as one." The wording is that of Muḥammad.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Prophet ﷺ praying, and when he was at an odd-numbered rakʿah of his prayer, he would not rise until he was sitting upright.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jābir prayed wearing a waist-wrapper that he had tied at the back of his neck,
while his clothes were placed on the clothes-rack. Someone said to him, "Do you pray in a single wrapper?" He replied, "I only did that so that a fool like you would see me.
Which of us had two garments in the time of the Prophet ﷺ?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh about prayer
in a single garment. He said: I went out with the Prophet ﷺ on one of his journeys,
and one night I came to him for some matter of mine,
and I found him praying, wearing a single garment.
So I wrapped myself in it and prayed beside him.
When he finished, he said,
"What brought you out at night, Jābir?" So I told him of my need.
When I had finished, he said,
"What is this wrapping that I saw?"
I said, "It was a garment," meaning it was narrow. He said,
"If it is wide, then wrap it around yourself,
and if it is narrow, then use it as a waist-wrapper."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr sent me during that Hajj among the announcers
whom he sent on the Day of Sacrifice to announce at Minā that after this year no polytheist may perform Hajj,
and that no naked person may circumambulate the House.
Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib after him,
and commanded him to announce the declaration of immunity (Barāʾah).
Abū Hurayrah said: So ʿAlī announced with us on the Day of Sacrifice to the people of Minā the declaration of immunity,
and that after this year no polytheist may perform Hajj,
and that no naked person may circumambulate the House.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah had a thin patterned curtain with which she covered one side of her house. The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Take this curtain of yours away from us,
for its images keep appearing before me in my prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw a man who was not completing his bowing or his prostration.
When he finished his prayer, Ḥudhayfah said to him, "You have not prayed." He said—and I think he said—"If you died, you would die on other than the way of Muḥammad ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We asked Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, about a man
who circumambulated the House during ʿUmrah
but did not walk between Ṣafā and Marwah:
may he go to his wife? He said: The Prophet ﷺ arrived and circumambulated the House seven times,
prayed two units behind the Station [of Ibrāhīm],
and walked between Ṣafā and Marwah seven times,
and "in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example."
He said: And we asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh, may Allah be pleased with them both, and he said: He must not approach her until he has walked between Ṣafā and Marwah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar said: I agreed with Allah in three things—or: my Lord agreed with me in three things. I said, "O Messenger of Allah,
if only you took the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer." And I said, "O Messenger of Allah, both the righteous and the wicked enter upon you,
so if only you commanded the Mothers of the Believers to observe the veil." Then Allah revealed the verse of the veil. He said: And news reached me of the Prophet ﷺ rebuking some of his wives,
so I went in to them and said, "Either you stop, or Allah will replace His Messenger ﷺ with better wives than you,"
until I came to one of his wives,
and she said, "O ʿUmar,

does the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not have what he needs to admonish his wives, that you admonish them?" Then Allah revealed: {Perhaps, if he divorces you, his Lord will replace you with wives better than you, Muslim women...} the verse.
Ibn Abī Maryam said: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed us: Ḥumayd narrated to me: I heard Anas, from ʿUmar,
label: machine translation

segments_en: with this [narration].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw phlegm on the wall in the direction of prayer,
and that was hard on him, until it was seen on his face.
He got up and scraped it off with his hand and said,
"When any of you stands in his prayer,
he is conversing with his Lord—or his Lord is between him and the direction of prayer—so none of you should spit in front of him,
but rather to his left,
or beneath his feet."
Then he took the edge of his cloak and spat in it,
then folded one part over the other, and said,
"Or do it like this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered, together with Masrūq,

upon ʿĀʾishah, and we said, "O Mother of the Believers, there are two men among the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ: one of them hastens to break the fast and hastens the prayer, and the other delays breaking the fast and delays the prayer."
She said, "Which of them is the one who hastens to break the fast and hastens the prayer?" He said, we said, "ʿAbdullāh," meaning Ibn Masʿūd.
She said, "This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do it."
Abū Kurayb added: "and the other was Abū Mūsā."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to kiss [his wives] during the month of fasting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And al-Ḥakam,
and Salamah ibn Kuhayl,
from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my sister has died, and she owed two consecutive months of fasting." He said,
"Tell me, if your sister had owed a debt, would you have paid it?" She said, "Yes." He said,
"Then the right of Allah is more deserving [of being paid]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Fasting is a shield from the Fire. So whoever wakes up fasting, let him not behave ignorantly that day, and if a person acts ignorantly toward him, let him not curse him or revile him, but let him say, 'I am fasting.' By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the breath from the mouth of a fasting person is better with Allah than the fragrance of musk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She, al-ʿAdawiyyah, asked ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fast three days of every month?" She said, "Yes."
I said to her, "Which days of the month did he fast?" She said, "He did not mind which days of the month he fasted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Prophet ﷺ [narrated] from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:
"Whoever fasts Ramadan and then follows it with six days of Shawwāl, it is as though he had fasted for a lifetime."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasting during the [first] ten days [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions did not perform more than a single circuit between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.
In the narration of Muḥammad ibn Bakr, [it adds]: "his first circuit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"I have sacrificed here, and all of Minā is a place of sacrifice."
And he stood at ʿArafah and said:
"I have stood here, and all of ʿArafah is a place of standing."
And he stood at al-Muzdalifah and said:
"I have stood here, and all of al-Muzdalifah is a place of standing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Saʿīd ibn Jubayr at Jamʿ: he made the iqāmah and prayed the Maghrib prayer, three rakʿahs, then made the iqāmah again and prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer, two rakʿahs. Then he mentioned that Ibn ʿUmar did the same with them in that place, and he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did the same in that place.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We joined together with the Prophet ﷺ in Hajj and ʿUmrah, seven people sharing in each camel. A man said to Jābir, "Can one share in a badanah as one shares in a jazūr?" He said, "It is nothing but one of the badanah animals."
And Jābir was present at al-Ḥudaybiyah. He said: "That day we sacrificed seventy camels, with seven of us sharing in each camel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is as though I am looking at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the pulpit, wearing a black turban with both ends let down between his shoulders.
Abū Bakr did not say "on the pulpit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbaydillāh ibn Maʿmar
wanted to arrange the marriage of
his son Ṭalḥah to the daughter of Shaybah ibn Jubayr during the Hajj, while Abān ibn ʿUthmān was at that time the leader of the pilgrims. So he sent word to Abān: "I wish to marry
Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUmar, and I would like you to attend that."
Abān said to him, "I see you are an uncouth Iraqi! I heard ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'A person in iḥrām may not marry.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married me in Shawwāl and consummated the marriage with me in Shawwāl. So which of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more favored by him than I?
He [the narrator] said: ʿĀʾishah used to like to have her women [relatives] brought to their husbands in Shawwāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ [narrated] that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"What is forbidden through breastfeeding is what is forbidden through birth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: to her:
"Do not observe hijāb from him, for what is forbidden through breastfeeding is what is forbidden through lineage."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
brought a black slave girl to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
"Messenger of Allah, I owe the freeing of a believing slave." He ﷺ said to her: "Where is Allah?"
She pointed to the sky with her finger. He ﷺ said to her: "And who am I?"
She pointed to the Prophet ﷺ and then to the sky,
meaning: You are the Messenger of Allah. He ﷺ said:
"Free her, for she is a believer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "By Allah,
I will certainly fight Quraysh." Then he ﷺ said: "
If Allah wills." Then he ﷺ said: "
By Allah, I will certainly fight Quraysh, if Allah wills." Then he ﷺ said: "
By Allah, I will certainly fight Quraysh."
Then he fell silent, then said: "
If Allah wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
stood up on the day of the Conquest and said:
"Messenger of Allah, I vowed to Allah that if He granted you the conquest of Makkah, I would pray two rakʿahs in Bayt al-Maqdis." He ﷺ said: "
Pray here."
Then the man repeated it to him, and he ﷺ said: "
Pray here."
Then he repeated it to him again, and he ﷺ said: "Then it is up to you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbbās:
Ibn Ḥannah; both reported from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, from some men
of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, with this report.
He added that the Prophet ﷺ said: "
By the One who sent Muhammad with the truth, if you had prayed here, it would have sufficed you in place of prayer in Bayt al-Maqdis."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
"Messenger of Allah, I vowed to beat the tambourine over your head." He ﷺ said: "Fulfil your vow." She said:
"I also vowed to sacrifice at such and such a place,
a place where the people of the Jāhiliyyah used to sacrifice." He ﷺ said: "For an idol?" She said: "No." He said: "For a statue?" She said: "No." He said: "Fulfil your vow."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, vowed to slaughter camels at Buwānah,
so he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
"I vowed to slaughter camels at Buwānah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Was there any idol of the idols of the Jāhiliyyah worshipped there?" They said: "No." He said: "
Was there any festival of theirs held there?" They said: "No."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Fulfil your vow,
for there is no fulfilling of a vow that involves disobedience to Allah, nor in what the son of Adam does not own."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with my father on the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and heard the people saying:
"The Messenger of Allah ﷺ," so I kept fixing my gaze on him,
and my father drew near to him, while he was on a she-camel of his, carrying a whip like the whip of a schoolteacher.
I heard the Bedouins and the people saying: "The aṭ-Ṭabṭabiyyah! The aṭ-Ṭabṭabiyyah!"
My father drew near to him and took hold of his foot. She said:
He allowed him, and stopped and listened to him, and my father said:
"Messenger of Allah, I vowed that if a male child were born to me, I would slaughter a number of sheep at the top of Buwānah, on a mountain pass." He said:
I only know that she said fifty.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Is there anything of the idols there?" He said: "No." He ﷺ said: "
Then fulfil what you vowed to Allah." She said:
So he gathered them and began to slaughter them, and one sheep escaped from him, so he went after it, saying:
"O Allah, fulfil my vow for me." Then he caught it and slaughtered it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: to the Prophet ﷺ, or Abū Lubābah, or whomever Allah willed:
"Part of my repentance is that I leave the home of my people, in which I committed the sin,
and that I give up all my wealth as charity." He ﷺ said: "
A third will suffice for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Lubābah was,
and he mentioned its meaning, and the story is about Abū Lubābah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A woman was punished because of a cat that she had confined
until it died of hunger,
and because of it she entered the Fire. [It was said, and Allah knows best:] 'You did not feed it or give it water when you confined it,
and you did not release it so that it could eat from the vermin of the earth.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had a she-camel from my share of the war booty on the day of Badr, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had also given me another she-camel from the fifth on that day. When I wanted to consummate my marriage with Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I arranged with a goldsmith of Banū Qaynuqāʿ to travel with me and bring back idhkhir grass, which I wanted to sell to the goldsmiths and so use the money toward my wedding feast. While I was gathering for my two she-camels their equipment, saddle frames, sacks and ropes, my two she-camels were kneeling beside the room of a man of the Anṣār. When I had finished gathering what I gathered, I found that my two she-camels had had their humps cut off, their flanks slit open, and some of their livers taken. I could not hold back my tears when I saw them in that state. I said, "Who did this?" They said, "Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib did it. He is in this house with a group of the Anṣār drinking; a singing girl and his companions were entertaining him, and she sang in her song: 'O Ḥamzah, [rise] to the fat young she-camels!'" So Ḥamzah stood up with his sword, cut off their humps, slit open their flanks and took some of their livers. ʿAlī said: I went until I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah was with him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw in my face what I had suffered.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "What is the matter with you?"

I said, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have never seen the like of today! Ḥamzah attacked my two she-camels, cut off their humps and slit open their flanks, and there he is in a house with a group of drinkers." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for his cloak and put it on, then set off walking, and I and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah followed him until he came to the door of the house where Ḥamzah was. He asked permission to enter and they permitted him, and there they were, drinking. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to rebuke Ḥamzah for what he had done, but Ḥamzah's eyes were red. Ḥamzah looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then raised his gaze to his knees, then raised his gaze and looked at his navel, then raised his gaze and looked at his face. Then Ḥamzah said, "Are you anything but slaves of my father?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ realized that he was intoxicated, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stepped back on his heels and left, and we left with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If I had gold equal to Uḥud,
it would not please me for three nights to pass while I still had any of it with me,
except something that I would set aside to pay a debt."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:
"A man died and entered Paradise. It was said to him, 'What used to be your deeds?' He said, [either he remembered or he was reminded.]
He said, 'I used to deal with people in business, and I would give time to the one in difficulty and be lenient in [accepting] coins or in payment.' So he was forgiven."
Abū Masʿūd said: And I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs,
and whoever leaves behind dependents, they are our responsibility."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men insulted each other, a man from the Muslims and a man from the Jews.
The Muslim said, "By the One who chose Muḥammad above all the worlds!"
The Jew said, "By the One who chose Moses above all the worlds!"
Thereupon the Muslim raised his hand and slapped the Jew's face.
The Jew went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about what had happened between him and the Muslim.
The Prophet ﷺ called the Muslim and asked him about it,
and he told him. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do not give me preference over Moses,
for the people will be struck unconscious on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be struck unconscious with them,
and I will be the first to recover.
Then I will find Moses holding on to a side of the Throne,
and I do not know whether he was among those who were struck unconscious and recovered before me,
or was among those whom Allah exempted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Jewish man
crushed the head of a girl between two stones.
It was said to her, "Who did this to you? Was it so-and-so? So-and-so?" until the Jewish man was named, and she signaled with her head.
The Jewish man was brought and he confessed,
so the Prophet ﷺ ordered that his head be crushed with stones.
Hammām said: [It was] between two stones.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a date on the road and said:
"If I were not afraid that it might be from charity, I would have eaten it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), while in Yemen, sent a small piece of gold in its raw earth to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided it among four men: al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis al-Ḥanẓalī, ʿUyaynah ibn Badr al-Fazārī, ʿAlqamah ibn ʿUlāthah al-ʿĀmirī, then one of the Banū Kilāb, and Zayd al-Khayr aṭ-Ṭāʾī, then one of the Banū Nabhān. He said: Quraysh became angry and said, "Does he give the chiefs of Najd and leave us out?" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I only did that to win their hearts."
Then a man with a thick beard, prominent cheekbones, sunken eyes, a protruding forehead, and a shaved head came and said, "Fear Allah, Muhammad!"
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who would obey Allah if I disobeyed Him? Does He trust me over the people of the earth, and you do not trust me?"
He said: Then the man turned away, and a man from the people asked permission to kill him; they thought it was Khālid ibn al-Walīd. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"From the offspring of this man will come a people who recite the Qur'an but it does not go beyond their throats. They kill the people of Islam and leave the idol worshippers. They pass through Islam as an arrow passes through its game. If I were to reach them, I would kill them as ʿĀd was killed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out one day alarmed, his face red, saying:
"There is no god but Allah. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today an opening has been made in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this."
And he made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it.
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us?" He said:
"Yes, when wickedness becomes abundant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to recite the Qur'an to my father in the covered porch, and when I recited a verse of prostration he would prostrate. I said to him, "Father, do you prostrate on the road?" He said: I heard Abū Dharr say: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the first mosque set up on earth. He said: "The Sacred Mosque."
I said, "Then which?" He said: "The Farthest Mosque."
I said, "How long was between them?" He said:
"Forty years. Then the earth is a place of prayer for you, so wherever the prayer finds you, pray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And al-Ajlaḥ,
and Mālik ibn Mighwal,
from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah,
from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā,
from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah,
who said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is the greeting of peace upon you, which we have learned; so how do we send blessings upon you?" He said:

"Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrāhīm; You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrāhīm; You are Praiseworthy and Glorious."
Maḥmūd said: Abū Usāmah said: Zāʾidah added for me, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā: And we say, "and upon us with them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, saying:
"I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every poisonous creature, and from every evil eye." He said:
"And our father Ibrāhīm used to seek refuge with them for Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq." Or he said: "Ismāʿīl and Yaʿqūb."
And this is the version of Wakīʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Many men have reached perfection,
but among women none has reached perfection except Āsiyah, the wife of Pharaoh,
and Maryam, the daughter of ʿImrān,
and the superiority of ʿĀʾishah over other women is like the superiority of tharīd over all other foods."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"ʿĪsā, son of Maryam, saw a man stealing and said to him, 'Did you steal?' He said, 'Never, by the One besides whom there is no god.'
So ʿĪsā said, 'I believe in Allah, and I doubt my own eyes.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was of medium height,
broad between the shoulders,
with hair reaching the lobe of his ear,
I saw him in a red garment,
and I never saw anything more beautiful than him.
Yūsuf ibn Abī Isḥāq said, from his father: to his shoulders.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: I accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for three years; at no time in my life was I more eager to retain hadith than during those years. I heard him say, gesturing like this with his hand:
"Before the Hour, you will fight a people whose sandals are made of hair,
and they are these people who are prominent."
And Sufyān said once: "and they are the people of al-Bāzar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that Heraclius sent for him [Abū Sufyān] among a party of Quraysh who were merchants in Syria, during the period in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made a truce with Abū Sufyān and the disbelievers of Quraysh.
They came to him while they were in Īliyā' (Jerusalem), and he summoned them to his court,

with the nobles of the Romans around him. Then he called them and called for his interpreter, and said, "Which of you is closest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet?" Abū Sufyān said, "I said: I am the closest of them in lineage."
He said, "Bring him close to me, and bring his companions near,
and place them behind his back."
Then he said to his interpreter, "Tell them that I am going to ask this man about that man [the Prophet],
and if he lies to me, then call him a liar."
Abū Sufyān said: By Allah, had it not been for shame that they would report a lie against me, I would have lied about him.
Then the first thing he asked me about him was, "How is his lineage among you?" I said, "He is of noble lineage among us."
He said, "Has anyone among you ever said this before him?" I said, "No."
He said, "Was any of his forefathers a king?" I said, "No."
He said, "Do the nobles of the people follow him, or their weak?" I said, "Rather, their weak."
He said, "Are they increasing or decreasing?" I said, "Rather, they are increasing."
He said, "Does anyone among them apostatize out of resentment of his religion after having entered it?" I said, "No."
He said, "Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he said?" I said, "No."
He said, "Does he betray?" I said, "No,
and we are in a period [of truce] with him in which we do not know what he will do."
He said: And no word allowed me to insert anything [against him] other than this word.
He said, "Have you fought him?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "How was your fighting with him?" I said, "The war between us and him goes back and forth,
he gets the better of us and we get the better of him."
He said, "What does he command you?" I said, "He says: Worship Allah alone,
and do not associate anything with Him,
and abandon what your forefathers say,
and he commands us to pray, to be truthful, to be chaste, and to maintain family ties."
Then he said to the interpreter, "Tell him: I asked you about his lineage,
and you mentioned that he is of noble lineage among you,
and likewise the messengers are sent from the lineage of their people.
I asked you whether anyone among you had said this before, and you mentioned that no one had,
so I said: if anyone had said this before him, I would have said he is a man imitating a statement made before him.
I asked you whether any of his forefathers was a king, and you mentioned that none was,
I said: if any of his forefathers had been a king, I would have said he is a man seeking his father's kingdom.
I asked you whether you accused him of lying before he said what he said, and you mentioned that you did not,
so I know that he would not leave off lying about people and then lie about Allah.
I asked you whether the nobles of the people followed him or their weak, and you mentioned that their weak followed him,
