and they are the followers of the messengers.
I asked you whether they are increasing or decreasing, and you mentioned that they are increasing,
and so it is with the matter of faith until it is complete.
I asked you whether anyone apostatizes out of resentment of his religion after entering it, and you mentioned that no one does,
and so it is with faith when its joy mixes with the hearts.
I asked you whether he betrays, and you mentioned that he does not,
and so the messengers do not betray.
I asked you what he commands you,
and you mentioned that he commands you to worship Allah,
and not to associate anything with Him,
and he forbids you from worshipping idols,
and commands you to pray, to be truthful, and to be chaste.
If what you say is true, he will soon possess the place of these two feet of mine,
and I knew that he was going to appear,
but I did not think that he would be from among you.
If I knew that I could reach him, I would undertake the hardship of meeting him,
and if I were with him, I would wash his feet."
Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which Dihyah had delivered to the governor of Buṣrā,
and he handed it to Heraclius, who read it, and in it was: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
From Muḥammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, ruler of the Romans.
Peace be upon whoever follows guidance.
To proceed: I invite you with the call of Islam. Accept Islam and you will be safe,
and Allah will give you your reward twice.

But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the Arisiyyīn (your subjects). And: {O People of the Book, come to a common word between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and associate nothing with Him, and that none of us take others as lords besides Allah. But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims.} Abū Sufyān said: When he had said what he said,
and finished reading the letter, there was a great clamor around him,
and voices were raised, and we were taken out.
I said to my companions when we were taken out: The affair of Ibn Abī Kabshah has become great,
for even the king of the Banū al-Aṣfar (the Romans) fears him.
I remained certain that he would prevail until Allah brought Islam into my heart.
Ibn al-Nāṭūr was the governor of Īliyā' and [a friend of] Heraclius, a bishop over the Christians of Syria,
and he used to relate that when Heraclius came to Īliyā', one morning he was troubled in spirit,
and some of his patricians said, "We find your appearance unfamiliar."
Ibn al-Nāṭūr said: Heraclius was a soothsayer who looked at the stars.
He said to them when they asked him: "Tonight, when I looked at the stars, I saw that the king of those who are circumcised has appeared.
Who among this nation are circumcised?" They said, "Only the Jews are circumcised, so do not be concerned about them. Write to the cities of your kingdom,
and let them kill the Jews who are in them."
While they were engaged in this matter, a man was brought to Heraclius, sent by the king of Ghassān,
to report about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When Heraclius questioned him, he said, "Go and see whether he is circumcised or not." They looked at him,
and told him that he was circumcised,
and he asked him about the Arabs, and he said, "They are circumcised."
Heraclius said, "This is the king of this nation; he has appeared."
Then Heraclius wrote to a friend of his in Rome,
who was his equal in knowledge,
and Heraclius set out for Ḥimṣ,
and he had not left Ḥimṣ when a letter came to him from his friend agreeing with Heraclius's view regarding the emergence of the Prophet ﷺ and that he was a prophet.
Heraclius then gave permission to the Roman nobles to enter a palace of his in Ḥimṣ, then ordered its doors, and they were locked.
Then he looked out and said, "O assembly of the Romans,
do you desire success and right guidance, and that your kingdom remain firm? Then pledge allegiance to this Prophet."
They bolted like wild donkeys toward the doors,
but found them locked.
When Heraclius saw their aversion,
and despaired of their faith, he said, "Bring them back to me."
He said, "I said what I said just now only to test how firm you are in your religion, and I have seen it."
So they prostrated to him and were pleased with him,
and that was the last of the affair of Heraclius.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was on a journey when he heard someone cursing, and he said, "What is this?"
They said, "This is so-and-so, who cursed her riding camel." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Take your things off her, for she is cursed." So they took their things off her.
ʿImrān said, "It is as though I can see her now, a dusky-colored she-camel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from a journey, we would be brought out to meet him. Whichever of us was met first, he would place in front of him. So I was met first, and he carried me in front of him. Then one of the two, Ḥasan or Ḥusayn, was brought, and he placed him behind him. And we entered Madinah in that manner.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"There are camels for the devils and houses for the devils. As for the camels of the devils, I have seen them: one of you goes out with several fine camels that he has fattened, yet he mounts none of them, and he passes by his brother who has been left stranded, and does not carry him. As for the houses of the devils, I have not seen them."
Saʿīd used to say, "I think they are only these cages which people cover with brocade."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, similar to this, saying after his words "its due":
"And do not go beyond the [designated] stopping places."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Travel by night, for the earth is folded up [i.e., distances are shortened] during the night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dāwūd said: He is Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād. My father, who

nursed me, and who was one of the Banū Murrah ibn ʿAwf, narrated to me, and he was present in that battle, the battle of Mu'tah. He said: By Allah, it is as though I can see Jaʿfar when he leapt down from his chestnut horse and hamstrung it, then fought the enemy until he was killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to condition horses by slimming them down for racing, and he would race them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ held a race between horses and gave preference in the finish to the mature horses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her: she was with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey. She said: I raced him and beat him on foot. Later, when I had put on weight, I raced him and he beat me. He said,
"This is for that earlier victory."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of transmission of ʿAbbād and with its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade cutting a strap between two fingers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among them, he said: I saw the banner of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it was yellow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The watchword of the Emigrants was ʿAbdullāh, and the watchword of the Helpers was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, as our commander, and we raided some of the polytheists. We attacked them by night and killed them. Our watchword that night was "Amit, amit [Kill, kill]."
Salamah said: That night I killed with my own hand seven households of the polytheists.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ travelled and night fell, he would say,

"O earth, my Lord and your Lord is Allah. I seek refuge in Allah from your evil, and the evil of what is in you, and the evil of what was created in you, and from the evil of what crawls upon you. And I seek refuge in Allah from lions and black serpents, from snakes and scorpions, from the inhabitant of the land, and from the begetter and what he begot."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"When three people are on a journey, let them appoint one of them as leader."
Nāfiʿ said: So we said to Abū Salamah, "You are our commander."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbaydullāh ibn Mūsā,
from Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ,
from Khālid ibn al-Fizr,
who said: Anas ibn Mālik narrated to me
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Set out in the name of Allah, by Allah, and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah. Do not kill a very old man, nor a child, nor a little one, nor a woman. Do not steal from the war booty, but gather your spoils, and set things right and do good: {Indeed, Allah loves those who do good.}"
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said to him, "Build [it]."
He said, "We know better; it is, my son, Palestine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, sent Basbasah as a scout to see what the caravan of Abū Sufyān had done.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From his clan, he said: The Prophet ﷺ sent out a detachment, and I equipped one of their men with a sword. When he returned, he said, "If only you had seen how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rebuked us." He said,
"Are you unable, when I send a man among you and he does not carry out my order, to put in his place someone who will carry out my order?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Among my nation are those who will intercede for a large group, among them those who will intercede for a tribe, among them those who will intercede for a band, and among them those who will intercede for a single man, until they all enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Every prophet has a basin, and they vie with one another over whose will have the most visitors. I hope that mine will have the most visitors."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"What an evil servant is the servant who is conceited and arrogant and forgets the Great, the Most High. What an evil servant is the servant who is tyrannical and transgresses and forgets the Compeller, the Most High. What an evil servant is the servant who is heedless and distracted and forgets the graves and decay. What an evil servant is the servant who is rebellious and overstepping and forgets the beginning and the end. What an evil servant is the servant who seeks the world through religion. What an evil servant is the servant who undermines religion through doubtful matters. What an evil servant is the servant whose greed leads him. What an evil servant is the servant whose desire misleads him. What an evil servant is the servant whose craving humiliates him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever fears [the enemy] travels at night, and whoever travels at night reaches the destination. Indeed, the merchandise of Allah is precious. Indeed, the merchandise of Allah is Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you were always as you are when you are with me, the angels would shade you with their wings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"Everything has a peak of eagerness, and every peak of eagerness has a lull. If its possessor is steady and moderate, then have hope for him; but if he is pointed out with fingers, do not count on him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When two thirds of the night had passed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would get up and say:
"O people, remember Allah! Remember Allah! The first blast has come, followed by the second blast. Death has come with what it brings! Death has come with what it brings!"
Ubayy said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I send many blessings upon you, so how much of my prayer should I devote to you?" He said, "As much as you wish."
I said, "A quarter?" He said,
"As you wish, but if you add more, it is better for you." I said, "Half?" He said,
"As you wish, but if you add more, it is better for you."
I said, "Then two thirds?" He said,
"As you wish, but if you add more, it is better for you."
I said, "Shall I devote all of my prayer to you?" He said,
"Then your concerns will be taken care of and your sin will be forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Have true modesty before Allah."
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are modest, and praise be to Allah." He said,

"That is not it. True modesty before Allah is that you guard the head and what it contains, guard the stomach and what it holds, and remember death and decay. Whoever desires the Hereafter abandons the adornment of this world. Whoever does that has truly been modest before Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he was reclining on a woven mat, and I saw its mark on his side.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were tested with hardship alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we were patient. Then after him we were tested with ease, and we were not patient.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while we had a little barley on our shelf. We ate from it for as long as Allah willed, then I told the servant girl to measure it, and she measured it, and it was soon used up.
She said: Had we left it unmeasured, we would have eaten from it for longer than that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We had a curtain with images on it at my door, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw it and said:
"Take it down, for it reminds me of the world."
She said: We also had a worn velvet cloth with a silk border, which we used to wear.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They slaughtered a sheep, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"What is left of it?"
She said, "Nothing is left of it except the shoulder." He said,
"All of it is left, except the shoulder."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out on a cold day from the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, having taken a soaked hide, cut a hole in its middle, and put my neck through it, and I tied my waist with palm leaves. I was extremely hungry, and had there been any food in the house of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would have eaten some of it. So I went out seeking something. I passed by a Jewish man in his orchard, who was drawing water with a pulley. I looked at him through a gap in the wall, and he said, "What is the matter, Bedouin? Would you like a date for every bucket?" I said, "Yes, so open the gate so I can come in." He opened it and I entered, and he gave me his bucket. Each time I drew a bucket, he gave me a date, until my hand was full. Then I let go of his bucket and said, "That is enough for me." I ate the dates, then drank some water, and then came to the mosque and found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb copied it out for me: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what the servant of Allah, ʿUmar, wrote concerning Thamgh. He then related its account similar to the hadith of Nāfiʿ, saying: "...not accumulating wealth from it. Whatever is left over of its fruit is for the beggar and the deprived." He went on to relate the story, and said: "And if the guardian of Thamgh wishes, he may buy slaves with some of its fruit to work it." Muʿayqīb wrote it, and ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Arqam witnessed it. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what the servant of Allah, ʿUmar, the Commander of the Faithful, bequeathed, should anything happen to him: that Thamgh, and Ṣirmah ibn al-Akwaʿ, and the slave in it, and the hundred shares at Khaybar, and its slave in it, and the hundred that Muhammad ﷺ granted him in the valley, shall be managed by Ḥafṣah as long as she lives, and then by a person of sound judgment from her family; that it is not to be sold or bought, and he is to spend it wherever he sees fit, on the beggar, the deprived, and the relatives. There is no blame on whoever manages it if he eats from it or feeds [others], or buys a slave from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil
made a bequest that

a hundred slaves be freed on his behalf. His son Hishām freed fifty slaves, and his son ʿAmr wished to free the remaining fifty on his behalf, but he said, "Not until I ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Messenger of Allah, my father bequeathed the freeing of a hundred slaves, and Hishām has freed fifty on his behalf, and fifty remain. Shall I free them on his behalf?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If he had been a Muslim and you had freed slaves on his behalf, or given charity on his behalf, or performed Hajj on his behalf, that would have reached him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fell ill, and I had seven sisters. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me and blew on my face, and I recovered. I said, "Messenger of Allah, shall I not bequeath a third to my sisters?" He said, "Do good."
I said, "Half?" He said, "Do good."
Then he went out and left me, and he said:
"Jābir, I do not see you dying from this illness of yours. Allah has revealed [a ruling] and made clear what is for your sisters: He has assigned them two-thirds."
He said: Jābir used to say that this verse was revealed concerning me: {They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning one who leaves no parent or child.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: And others,
from the people of knowledge, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl,
from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh: that the wife of
Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ said, "Messenger of Allah, Saʿd has died and left two daughters."
And he related it similarly. Abū Dāwūd said: This is the correct version.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿādh ibn Jabal
gave inheritance to a sister and a daughter, assigning half to each of them, while he was in Yemen and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was alive at that time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ assigned the grandmother a sixth when there was no mother nearer than her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿUmar said:] "Which of you knows what share the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the grandfather?" Maʿqil ibn Yasār said, "I do. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him a sixth."
He said, "Together with whom?" He said, "I do not know."
He said, "May you not know! Then what use are you?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"I am the heir of one who has no heir: I free his captive and inherit his property. And the maternal uncle is the heir of one who has no heir: he frees his captive and inherits his property."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "I have the inheritance of a man from al-Azd, and I cannot find any Azdī to give it to." He said:
"Go and look for an Azdī for a year."
He said: He came to him after the year and said, "Messenger of Allah, I did not find an Azdī to give it to." He said:
"Go and look for the first person from Khuzāʿah you meet, and give it to him."
When he turned to leave, he said, "Bring the man back to me."
When he came, he said:
"Look for the eldest of Khuzāʿah and give it to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of Khuzāʿah died, and his inheritance was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. He said:
"Look for an heir or a blood relative for him."
They found no heir and no blood relative for him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Give it to the eldest of Khuzāʿah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ assigned the inheritance of the son of a woman who had been through li'ān to his mother and to her heirs after her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two brothers,

a Jew and a Muslim, brought a dispute to Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, and he gave the inheritance to the Muslim among them. He said: Abū al-Aswad told me that a man told him that Muʿādh told him, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Islam increases and does not decrease." So he gave the inheritance to the Muslim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Anas ibn Mālik,
who said: "We would pray the ʿAṣr prayer, and then someone would go to Qubā' and reach them while the sun was still high."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Buraydah on an expedition on a cloudy day, and he said: "Pray the ʿAṣr prayer early, for the Prophet ﷺ said:
'Whoever abandons the ʿAṣr prayer, his deeds have become void.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Abū az-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Angels of the night and angels of the day succeed one another among you, and they gather together at the Fajr prayer and the ʿAṣr prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend, and their Lord asks them, though He knows best about them: 'How did you leave My servants?' They say: 'We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah,

the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "One night the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer, which is the one called al-ʿAtamah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not come out until ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, 'The women and children have fallen asleep.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out and said to the people of the mosque when he came out to them:
'No one among the people of the earth is waiting for it except you.'"
That was before Islam had spread among the people.
Ḥarmalah added in his narration: Ibn Shihāb said: It was mentioned to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It was not right for you to pester the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the prayer."
And that was when ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb called out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was occupied one night and could not pray it,
so he delayed it until we had fallen asleep in the mosque,
then we woke up, then slept, then woke up again,
then the Prophet ﷺ came out to us and said:
"None of the people of the earth is waiting for the prayer except you."
Ibn ʿUmar did not mind whether he prayed it early or delayed it, as long as he did not fear that sleep would overcome him and make him miss its time,
and he would sleep before it.
Ibn Jurayj said: I said to ʿAṭāʾ, and he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer one night until the people had slept and woken up, and slept and woken up,
then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb stood up and said: "The prayer!"
ʿAṭāʾ said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came out, as though I am looking at him now,
with water dripping from his head,
placing his hand on his head, and he said:
"Were it not that I would be placing a hardship on my Ummah, I would have commanded them to pray it like this."
ʿAṭāʾ made sure how the Prophet ﷺ had placed his hand on his head, as Ibn ʿAbbās had informed him,
so ʿAṭāʾ spread his fingers apart for me somewhat,
then placed the tips of his fingers on the side of the head and then brought them together,
passing them over the head like that until his thumb touched the edge of the ear nearest the face, by the temple and the side of the beard,
neither shortening nor hurrying except like that, and he said:
"Were it not that I would be placing a hardship on my Ummah, I would have commanded them to pray like this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: "O son of my sister, the Prophet ﷺ never left the two prostrations [two rakʿahs] after ʿAṣr while he was with me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: "There are two prayers that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never left in my house, neither in secret nor in public: two rakʿahs before Fajr and two rakʿahs after ʿAṣr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when some of the people said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would make camp for us to rest." He said:
"I fear that you will sleep through the prayer."
Bilāl said: "I will keep watch over you."
So they lay down and slept, and Bilāl leaned his back against his mount. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up when the edge of the sun had already risen, and he said:
"O Bilāl, where is what you said?"
He said: "I have never been overcome by sleep like this before."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, took your souls when He willed and returned them when He willed. Get up, O Bilāl, and call the people to prayer."
So Bilāl got up and called the adhān, and they performed ablution, meaning when the sun had risen, then he stood and led them in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it;
there is no expiation for it other than that."
{And establish prayer for My remembrance.} Mūsā said: Hammām said: I heard him say after that, {And establish prayer for My remembrance.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he slaughtered his sacrificial animal before the prayer and mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Repeat your sacrifice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered his sacrificial animal with his own hand, with a large knife, at the end of the alley on the road of Banū Zurayq.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that a piece be taken from every camel, and they were put in a pot. Then they ate of the meat and sipped of the broth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only forbade [keeping] the meat of sacrificial animals because of the hardship of the people; then he permitted it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The ʿaqīqah is to be offered for the boy, and his head is not to be touched with blood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a man who was dragging a sheep by its ear, and he said:
"Leave its ear and take it by the nape of its neck."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that knives be sharpened and that they be hidden from the animals, and he said:
"When one of you slaughters, let him finish it quickly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to a man of the Anṣār, who took a knife to slaughter for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Beware of the milch animal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him and to ʿUmar:
"Come with us to al-Wāqifī."
He said: So we set off by moonlight until we came to the orchard, and he said, "Welcome!"
Then he took the knife and went about among the sheep, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of the milch animal," or he said, "the one that gives milk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey when a camel bolted, and a man shot it with an arrow. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"These animals have wild traits—I think he said—like the wildness of wild animals. So whatever of them overpowers you, do this to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade mutilating animals.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ declared certain things forbidden, until he mentioned domestic donkeys.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Their dog and their bird—meaning the Magians.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are a people who shoot." He said:
"When you shoot and the arrow pierces, eat what it has pierced."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the mirʿāḍ [a headless arrow], and he said:
"Do not eat [the game] unless it pierces."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"In the last times there will be a people who cut off the humps of camels and cut off the tails of sheep. Beware! Whatever is cut from a living animal is dead meat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two kinds of dead meat and two kinds of blood have been made lawful for us. As for the two dead meats, they are fish and locusts; and as for the two bloods, they are the liver and the spleen."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ used to give one another locusts as gifts on platters.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade killing the shrike, the frog, the ant, and the hoopoe.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded her to kill geckos.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the gecko "the little wrongdoer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She entered upon ʿĀʾishah and saw a spear placed in her house. She said: "O Mother of the Believers, what do you do with this?" She said: "We kill these geckos with it. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ informed us that when Ibrāhīm was thrown into the Fire, there was no creature on earth that did not try to put out the fire, except the gecko, which used to blow on it. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that it be killed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have come to ask you about the vermin of the earth. What do you say about the fox?" He said:
"And who eats the fox?"
I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the wolf?" He said:
"And does anyone in whom there is good eat the wolf?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the People of the Ṣuffah called out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he finished the prayer and said: "O Messenger of Allah, our land is a land full of lizards. What is your view on lizards?" He said:
"It has reached me that they are a nation that was transformed."
But he neither commanded it nor forbade it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I do not declare it forbidden"—meaning the lizard.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, came to us after he had prayed and called for water for ablution. We said, "What will he do with water for ablution when he has already prayed? He only wants to teach us." So a vessel containing water and a basin were brought. He poured from the vessel over his right hand and washed his hands three times. Then he rinsed his mouth and cleaned his nose three times, rinsing and blowing out with the same hand from which he took the water. Then he washed his face three times, then washed his right hand three times and his left hand three times. Then he put his hand in the vessel and wiped his head once. Then he washed his right foot three times and his left foot three times. Then he said, "Whoever would like to know the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: a chair was brought to him and he sat on it. Then he called for a pot containing water and poured it over his hands three times. Then he rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose with one handful, three times, and washed his face three times, and washed his forearms three times each. He took some water and wiped his head—and Shuʿbah indicated once, from the front of his head to the back of it—then he said, "I do not know whether he brought them back or not." And he washed his feet three times each. Then he said, "Whoever would like to see the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is his ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned that he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he described his ablution and said: He wiped his head with water other than what was left over on his hands, and he washed his feet until he had cleaned them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped his head with his hands, moving them forward and backward. He began with the front of his head, then took them to the back of his neck, then brought them back until he returned to the place where he had started. Then he washed his feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performing ablution. She said: He wiped his head, wiping the front of it and the back of it, and his temples and his ears, once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed ablution and put his two fingers into the openings of his ears.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Blow out water from your nose thoroughly, twice or three times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performing ablution while wearing a Qatari turban. He put his hand under the turban and wiped the front of his head, and he did not undo the turban.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, may I wipe over the leather socks?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "For a day?" He said, "A day."
He said, "And two days?" He said, "And two days."
He said, "And three?" He said,
"Yes, and as much as you wish."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam and we mentioned what requires ablution. Marwān said, "Ablution is required after touching the private part."
ʿUrwah said, "I did not know that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a boy who was skinning a sheep, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,
"Step aside so that I may show you."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put his hand between the skin and the flesh and pushed it in until it disappeared up to the armpit, and he said,
"O boy, skin like this."
Then he went on and led the people in prayer, and he did not perform ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ate a shoulder of meat, then wiped his hands on a mat that was beneath him, then got up to pray and prayed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last of the two matters from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was leaving ablution after eating what fire has touched.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The eyes are the cord that ties the anus, so whoever sleeps, let him perform ablution."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a man who often emitted prostatic fluid, so I kept bathing until my back cracked. I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ—or it was mentioned to him—and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not do that. When you see prostatic fluid, wash your private part and perform ablution as your ablution for prayer, and when you emit semen in spurts, bathe."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went around to his wives one day, bathing at this one's and at that one's.
He said: I said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, will you not make it a single bath?" He said,
"This is purer, better and cleaner."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever leaves the place of a single hair unwashed after sexual impurity, such and such will be done to him from the Fire."
ʿAlī said: So from that time I have been hostile to my head, from that time I have been hostile to my head," three times.
And he used to cut his hair short.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command any of us, when she was menstruating, to wrap an izār around herself, and then her husband would lie beside her. And once he said: he would have contact with her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I own a riding animal that I look after; I travel on it and I hire it out. Sometimes this month, meaning Ramadan, comes upon me while I am strong and young, and I find that fasting, O Messenger of Allah, is easier for me than delaying it so that it becomes a debt. Should I fast, O Messenger of Allah, which is greater for my reward, or should I break my fast?" He said:
"Whichever you wish, O Ḥamzah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has a means of transport that carries him to a state of satisfaction, let him fast Ramadan wherever it finds him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is overtaken by Ramadan while travelling..." Then he mentioned a similar meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Abū Baṣrah al-Ghifārī, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, on a ship from al-Fusṭāṭ in Ramadan. It was set sail, then his midday meal was brought near. Jaʿfar said in his narration: He had not yet passed beyond the houses when he called for the dining cloth and said, "Come near."
I said, "Do you not see the houses?" Abū Baṣrah said, "Do you turn away from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" Jaʿfar said in his narration: Then he ate.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Diḥyah ibn Khalīfah

once went out from a village near Damascus to a distance about the same as the village of ʿAqabah from al-Fusṭāṭ, which is three miles, in Ramadan. Then he broke his fast, and some people broke their fast with him, while others disliked to break it. When he returned to his village he said, "By Allah, today I saw something I never thought I would see: people turning away from the guidance of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions."
He said that about those who had fasted. Then at that moment he said, "O Allah, take me to You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar
used to go out to al-Ghābah, and he would neither break his fast nor shorten the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He entered with ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr upon his father ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who brought food near to them and said, "Eat."
He said, "I am fasting."
ʿAmr said, "Eat, for these are the days on which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us to break the fast and forbade us from fasting them."
Mālik said: They are the days of Tashrīq.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When it was mentioned to him that [the Prophet ﷺ] had forbidden fasting on Saturday, Ibn Shihāb would say, "This is a Ḥimṣī ḥadīth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I kept it hidden until I saw that it had spread.
He meant this ḥadīth of ʿAbdullāh ibn Busr about fasting on Saturday.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then left, and came to him again a year later, his condition and appearance having changed. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you not recognize me?" He said, "And who are you?"
He said, "I am al-Bāhilī who came to you the previous year." He said:
"What has changed you, when you had a good appearance?"
He said, "I have not eaten any food except at night since I left you."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Why did you torment yourself?" Then he said:
"Fast the month of patience and one day of every month."
He said, "Give me more, for I have strength." He said, "Fast two days." He said, "Give me more." He said:
"Fast three days." He said, "Give me more." He said:
"Fast from the sacred months and leave off; fast from the sacred months and leave off; fast from the sacred months and leave off."
And he indicated with his three fingers, joining them together and then releasing them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He set out with Usāmah to Wādī al-Qurā in search of some property of his, and he used to fast on Monday and Thursday. His freed slave said to him, "Why do you fast on Monday and Thursday when you are an old man?" He said, "The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to fast on Monday and Thursday, and when he was asked about that, he said:
'The deeds of the servants are presented on Monday and Thursday.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Aslam
came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Have you fasted this day of yours?" They said, "No." He said:
"Then complete the rest of your day and make it up [later]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Umm Salamah and asked her about fasting. She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command me to fast three days of every month, the first of them being Monday and Thursday."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of the Conquest, the conquest of Makkah, Fāṭimah came and sat on the left of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Umm Hāniʾ was on his right. She said: A young female servant came with a vessel containing a drink and handed it to him, and he drank from it. Then he handed it to Umm Hāniʾ, and she drank from it. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have broken my fast, and I was fasting." He said to her:
"Were you making up something?" She said, "No." He said:
"Then it does not harm you, if it was voluntary."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A insane woman who had committed adultery was brought to ʿUmar. He consulted some people about her, and ʿUmar ordered that she be stoned. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by her and said, "What is the matter with this woman?" They said, "She is an insane woman from the family of so-and-so who committed adultery, and ʿUmar has ordered that she be stoned."

He said: So he said, "Take her back." Then he went to ʿUmar and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, do you not know that the pen has been lifted from three: from the insane person until he recovers, from the sleeper until he wakes, and from the child until he reaches understanding?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "Then what is the matter with this woman being stoned?" He said, "Nothing." He said, "Then release her." He said, "Release her."
He said: And he began to say "Allāhu akbar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Janbī said: A woman who had committed fornication was brought to ʿUmar, and he ordered that she be stoned. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by, took hold of her and let her go. ʿUmar was told, and he said, "Call ʿAlī for me."
So ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, came and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, you surely know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'The pen has been lifted from three: from the child until he reaches puberty, from the sleeper until he wakes, and from the mentally impaired until he recovers.'
And this woman is a mentally impaired woman from the family of so-and-so. Perhaps the one who came to her came to her while she was in her affliction."
He said: ʿUmar said, "I do not know."
And ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said, "And I do not know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: This is the limit between the young and the adult.
label: machine translation

segments_en: {And those of your women who commit immorality, call four of you to testify against them. If they testify, then confine them in the houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way.} Then he mentioned the man after the woman and then combined them, saying: {And the two among you who commit it, punish them both. But if they repent and reform, then leave them alone.} That was abrogated by the verse of flogging, as He said: {The woman who commits unlawful sexual intercourse and the man who does so, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: "The way" is the prescribed punishment. Sufyān said: {Punish them both} refers to the unmarried ones; {confine them in the houses} refers to the previously married women.
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of Yaḥyā and its meaning, they both said:
"A hundred lashes and stoning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Māʿiz ibn Mālik was an orphan under the guardianship of my father.

He had relations with a slave girl of the neighbourhood. My father said to him, "Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tell him what you did, perhaps he will ask forgiveness for you." He only intended by that the hope that he might find a way out. So he came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed adultery, so carry out the Book of Allah on me."
He turned away from him. He returned and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed adultery, so carry out the Book of Allah on me."
He said it four times. The Prophet ﷺ said:

"You have said it four times. With whom?" He said, "With so-and-so." He said, "Did you lie with her?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Did you have physical contact with her?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Did you have intercourse with her?" He said, "Yes."
He said: So he ordered that he be stoned, and he was taken out to the Ḥarrah.

When he was stoned and felt the touch of the stones, he panicked and ran off. ʿAbdullāh ibn Unays met him, his companions having been unable to catch him. He took the shank bone of a camel, threw it at him and killed him. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said:
"Why did you not leave him? Perhaps he would repent and Allah would accept his repentance."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I mentioned the story of Māʿiz ibn Mālik to ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatādah, and he said to me: Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated to me,
He said: He narrated that to me,
from the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Why did you not leave him?"
[He said:] "Ask any of the men of Aslam you wish, those whom I do not suspect."

He said: I did not know this hadith. He said: So I came to Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh and said, "Some men of Aslam narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them, when they mentioned to him Māʿiz's panic at the stones when they struck him, 'Why did you not leave him?' And I do not know this hadith."

He said, "O son of my brother, I am the most knowledgeable of people about this hadith. I was among those who stoned the man. When we took him out and stoned him and he felt the touch of the stones, he cried out to us, 'O people, return me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for my people have killed me and deceived me about myself, and they told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not kill me.' We did not stop until we killed him. When we returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, he said:
'Why did you not leave him and bring him to me?'
so that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ might verify the matter with him, but not in order to abandon a prescribed punishment." He said: So I understood the meaning of the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were on a military expedition—Sufyān once said: in an army—and a man from the Muhājirūn kicked a man from the Anṣār on the buttocks. The Anṣārī said, "O Anṣār!"
And the Muhājirī said, "O Muhājirūn!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard that and said,
"What is the matter with this call of the days of ignorance?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, a man from the Muhājirūn kicked a man from the Anṣār." He said,
"Leave it, for it is foul."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy heard of that and said, "Have they done it?
By Allah, if we return to Madīnah, the mightier will surely drive out the weaker from it."
This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿUmar stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite." The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Leave him, lest people say that Muhammad kills his Companions."
The Anṣār were more numerous than the Muhājirūn when they first came to Madīnah,
but afterwards the Muhājirūn became more numerous.
Sufyān said: I memorized it from ʿAmr. ʿAmr said: I heard Jābir [say], "We were with the Prophet ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"I have several names: I am Muhammad, and I am Aḥmad, and I am al-Māḥī (the Eraser), through whom Allah erases disbelief, and I am al-Ḥāshir (the Gatherer), at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-ʿĀqib (the Last), after whom there is no one."
And Allah has named him Compassionate and Merciful.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The likeness of me and the prophets is that of a man who built a house and completed it and perfected it, except for the place of one brick. People began to enter it and marvel at it, saying, 'If only not for the place of this brick.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I am the place of that brick. I came and sealed the prophets."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
from Anas ibn Mālik,

that he heard him say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not very tall nor short; he was not pure chalk-white nor dark brown; his hair was neither tightly curled nor lank. Allah sent him at the beginning of his fortieth year, and he stayed in Makkah ten years and in Madīnah ten years. Allah took him at the beginning of his sixtieth year, and there were not twenty white hairs in his head and beard.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaḥyā said: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah,

the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never given a choice between two matters except that he took the easier of them, so long as it was not a sin; if it was a sin, he was the furthest of people from it. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never took revenge for himself, unless the sanctity of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, was violated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas—Abū ʿAbdullāh said: his name is ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī ʿUtbah—[said], I heard Abū Saʿīd
say: The Prophet ﷺ was more modest than a virgin in her private chamber.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah sat down beside the room of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, while she was praying, and he began to say, "Listen, O mistress of the room!"—twice.
When she finished her prayer, she said, "Are you not amazed at this man and his talk? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would relate a narration such that if one who counted wished to count it, he could."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to stand at the base of a tree—or he said, by a palm trunk—then he made a pulpit.
He said: The trunk wailed—Jābir said—until the people of the mosque heard it, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to it and stroked it, and it quieted.
Some of them said, "Had he not come to it, it would have wailed until the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"After me there will be favoritism and matters that you disapprove of."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you command those of us who live to see that?" He said,
"Fulfill the right that is upon you, and ask Allah for what is yours."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Hour will not come until two groups fight one another,
and there will be a great slaughter between them, though their claim is one;
and the Hour will not come until nearly thirty deceitful impostors are raised up,
each of whom claims that he is the Messenger of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "My brother has loose bowels." He said, "Give him honey to drink."
He gave it to him, then came back and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I gave him honey to drink, but it only made his looseness worse."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Give him honey to drink."
He gave it to him, then came to him again and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I gave him honey to drink, but it only made his looseness worse."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's belly has lied. Give him honey to drink."
So he gave him honey to drink, and he was cured.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asked about the earnings of the cupper,
and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was cupped; Abū Ṭaybah cupped him,
and he gave him two ṣāʿs of food,
and he spoke to his masters, and they reduced what was due from him. And he said,
"The best of what you use for treatment is cupping and sea costus." And he said,
"Do not torture your children by pressing on the throat to treat the uvula; rather, use costus."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me, or it was commanded, that ruqyah be sought for the evil eye.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered, together with Thābit al-Bunānī,
upon Anas ibn Mālik, and Thābit said, "O Abū Ḥamzah, I am ill."
Anas said, "Shall I not perform ruqyah for you with the ruqyah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"O Allah, Lord of the people, remover of harm, heal, for You are the Healer; there is no healer but You; a healing that leaves no illness behind."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Sālim,
the two sons of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"There is no contagion and no bad omen; ill omen is only in three things: the woman, the horse, and the house."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah in the year of the Conquest with a helmet on his head.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"When one of you puts on sandals, let him begin with the right, and when he takes them off, let him begin with the left,
so that the right is the first of the two to be put on and the last of the two to be taken off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a gold ring made,
and when he wore it, he placed its bezel on the inner side of his palm.
Then the people had gold rings made, so he ascended the pulpit,
praised Allah and extolled Him, and said,
"I had had it made,
and I will not wear it."
Then he threw it away, and the people threw theirs away.
Juwayriyah said: I think he said that it was on his right hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a ring and had an inscription engraved on it. He said,
"We have made a ring and had an inscription engraved on it, so let no one engrave the like of its inscription."
Then Anas said: It is as though I can see its gleam on his hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ cursed effeminate men,
and women who imitate men, and he said,
"Remove them from your houses."
He said: So the Prophet ﷺ expelled so-and-so,
and ʿUmar expelled so-and-so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik was asked, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dye his hair?" He said, "He was seen to have only about seventeen or twenty white hairs at the front of his beard."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw anyone more handsome in a red garment than the Prophet ﷺ.
Some of my companions said, from Mālik: His hair used to reach down close to his shoulders.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The hair of the Prophet ﷺ used to reach his shoulders.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid qazaʿ.
ʿUbaydullāh said: I asked, "What is qazaʿ?" ʿUbaydullāh gestured to us and said, "When a boy's head is shaved and a tuft of hair is left here, and here, and here."
ʿUbaydullāh gestured to us toward his forelock and the two sides of his head.
ʿUbaydullāh was asked, "What about a girl and a boy?" He said, "I do not know; that is how he said it: the boy."
ʿUbaydullāh said: I asked him again, and he said, "As for the forelock and the nape for a boy, there is no harm in them. But qazaʿ is that hair is left on his forelock,
and there is no other hair on his head,
and likewise when one side of his head is shaved and the other side."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ — and Hannād said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ — when he wanted to enter the state of iḥrām, would apply oil with the finest perfume he could find, until I could see its gleam on his head and beard.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Men go out to fight, but women do not go out to fight, and we receive only half of the inheritance." So Allah revealed:
"And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others."
Mujāhid said: Then He revealed concerning it:
"Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women..." And Umm Salamah was the first woman traveling in a howdah to arrive in Madinah as an emigrant.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From a son of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah,
who said: "O Messenger of Allah, I do not hear Allah mention women in connection with emigration."
So Allah, the Exalted, revealed:
"Indeed, I do not let the deed of any doer among you go to waste, whether male or female; you are of one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Not equal are those believers who sit [at home], other than those with a valid excuse," [that is, who stayed behind] from Badr, and those who went out to Badr. When the expedition of Badr was revealed, ʿAbdullāh ibn Jahsh and Ibn Umm Maktūm said: "We are both blind, O Messenger of Allah; is there a concession for us?" So this was revealed:
"Not equal are those believers who sit [at home], other than those with a valid excuse," and:
"Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit by a degree." So these are the ones who sit, other than those with a valid excuse:
"And Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit with a great reward," [that is,] degrees from Him over the believers who sit, other than those with a valid excuse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said to Ibn ʿAbbās, "Why is it that the people of this house give nabīdh to drink, while their cousins give milk, honey, and sawīq to drink? Is it stinginess on their part, or need?" Ibn ʿAbbās said, "It is neither stinginess nor need on our part. Rather, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came on his mount with Usāmah ibn Zayd behind him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked for a drink, and nabīdh was brought to him. He drank from it and passed the remainder to Usāmah ibn Zayd, who drank from it. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You have done well and you have done beautifully. Do likewise."
So this is how we are; we do not want to change what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do when he entered the Kaʿbah?" He said, "He prayed two rakʿahs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ left her house happy, then returned to me sorrowful, and said:
"I entered the Kaʿbah, but had I known beforehand what I came to know afterwards, I would not have entered it. I fear that I have made things difficult for my Ummah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿUthmān, "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to you when he called you?" He said:
"I forgot to tell you to cover the two horns, for it is not proper that there be anything in the house that distracts the one who is praying."
Ibn al-Sarḥ said: My maternal uncle, Musāfiʿ ibn Shaybah, [said this].
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we came back with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Liyyah, and reached the lote tree, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at the edge of the black hill opposite it. He faced Nakhb with his gaze, and once he said, "its valley," and he stood until all the people had gathered. Then he said:
"The game of Wajj and its thorny trees are sacred, made sacred for Allah."
That was before his going down to Ṭāʾif and his siege of Thaqīf.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a protected area on every side of Madinah, one barīd by one barīd: its trees were not to be beaten down for fodder, nor cut down, except what is needed to drive a camel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ seize a man who was hunting in the sacred territory of Madinah, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made sacred, and he stripped him of his clothes. His masters came and spoke to him about it, and he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made this territory sacred and said:
'Whoever finds anyone hunting in it, let him strip him of his clothes.'
So I will not return to you a provision that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me as food. But if you wish, I will pay you its price."
label: machine translation

segments_en: To Saʿd: Indeed Saʿd

found some slaves of the slaves of Madinah cutting from the trees of Madinah, so he took their belongings and said to their masters, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid cutting anything from the trees of Madinah, and he said:
'Whoever cuts anything from it, then whoever catches him may have his belongings.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Its trees are not to be beaten down for fodder, nor cut down; the protected area of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [is protected]. But [leaves] may be knocked down gently."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no one who greets me with salām but Allah returns my soul to me so that I may return his greeting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb informed me,
from Saʿīd al-Maqburī,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not make your houses graves, and do not make my grave a place of festivity. And send blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me wherever you are."
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ any hadith ever, except one hadith.

He said: I said, "What is it?" He said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who intended the graves of the martyrs, until we looked out over the lava field of Wāqim. When we went down from it, there were graves in a bend of the valley. We said, "O Messenger of Allah, are these the graves of our brothers?" He said, "They are the graves of our Companions."
Then when we came to the graves of the martyrs, he said:
"These are the graves of our brothers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mālik said: It is not appropriate for anyone to pass by al-Muʿarras when returning to Madinah without praying there as much as he wishes, because it has reached me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a night halt there.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"A fornicator who has been flogged may marry only one like him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no [legal] suckling except that which strengthens the bone and grows the flesh.
Abū Mūsā said, "Do not ask us while this great scholar is among you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke one morning silent and distressed, so Maymūnah said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have found your appearance strange since today."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Jibrīl had promised to meet me tonight, but he did not meet me. By Allah, he has never broken a promise to me."

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in that state throughout that day. Then it occurred to him that there was a puppy under a tent of ours, so he ordered that it be removed. It was taken out, then he took some water in his hand and sprinkled the place. When evening came, Jibrīl met him, and he said to him,
"You had promised to meet me last night."
He replied, "Yes, but we do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image."
So that morning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the killing of dogs, to the point that he would order the killing of the dog of a small garden, while leaving the dog of a large garden.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to sit with Ibn ʿAbbās in Makkah, and a fever seized me.
He said, "Cool it down with Zamzam water,
for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Fever is from the heat of Hell, so cool it with water.'" Or he said, "with Zamzam water." Hammām was unsure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men insulted each other in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and one of them became angry, his face turning red. The Prophet ﷺ looked at him and said,
"I know a phrase which, if he said it, this [anger] would leave him: 'I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan.'"
So one of the men who had heard the Prophet ﷺ went to that man and said, "Do you know what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ just said?" He said,
"I know a phrase which, if he said it, this [anger] would leave him: 'I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan.'"
The man said to him, "Do you think I am mad?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"If a fly falls into the drink of one of you, let him dip it in completely, for in one of its wings is disease and in the other is cure, and it shields itself with the wing that has the disease. So let him immerse all of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was walking
with the Prophet ﷺ in one of the fields of Madinah, and he was leaning on a palm-stalk he had with him,
we passed by a group of the Jews, and some of them said to others, "Ask him about the soul."
Some of them said, "Do not ask him, lest he bring something concerning it that you dislike."
Others said, "We will certainly ask him."

So a man from among them stood up to him and said, "O Abū al-Qāsim, what is the soul?" The Prophet ﷺ remained silent toward him, and I knew that revelation was coming to him. Then he said: {They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is of the affair of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.}
Al-Aʿmash said: "This is how it is in our recitation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn al-Zubayr said to me, "ʿĀʾishah used to confide in you often. What did she tell you about the Kaʿbah?" I said, "She told me that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'O ʿĀʾishah,

were it not that your people are close to the time of [Ibn al-Zubayr said: disbelief], I would have demolished the Kaʿbah and made two doors for it: a door for people to enter and a door for them to leave.'"
And Ibn al-Zubayr did that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said: I was a man who often emitted prostatic fluid, and the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ was my wife, and I was too shy to ask him. So I said to a man sitting beside me, "Ask him." He asked him, and he said, "Wuḍūʾ is required for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from Kurayb,
the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Usāmah ibn Zayd,

that he heard him say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed from ʿArafah, and when he reached the mountain pass, he dismounted and urinated, then performed wuḍūʾ without making the wuḍūʾ complete. I said to him, "The prayer?" He said, "The prayer is ahead of you."

Then he mounted, and when he came to Muzdalifah he dismounted and performed wuḍūʾ, making it complete. Then the prayer was called, and he prayed the Maghrib. Then each person made his camel kneel at his place. Then the ʿIshāʾ prayer was called, and he prayed it, and he did not pray anything between the two.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to say that some people say: when you sit to relieve yourself,
do not face the qiblah or Bayt al-Maqdis.
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: "I once climbed onto the roof of a house of ours,
and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on two bricks, facing Bayt al-Maqdis, relieving himself."
And he said, "Perhaps you are one of those who pray pressing down on their hips."
I said, "By Allah, I do not know."
Mālik said: He means the one who prays without rising off the ground,
who prostrates while clinging to the ground.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I climbed onto the roof of Ḥafṣah's house for some need of mine,
and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ relieving himself with his back to the qiblah, facing Syria.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day I went up onto the roof of our house,
and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sitting on two bricks, facing Bayt al-Maqdis.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went out to relieve himself, a boy and I would follow him, with us a staff, or a stick, or a short spear, and with us a water container.
When he finished his need, we handed him the water container.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"While a man was walking along a road, he became extremely thirsty. He found a well, so he went down into it and drank, then came out, and there was a dog panting, eating moist earth out of thirst. The man said, 'This dog has reached the same thirst that had reached me.'
So he went down into the well, filled his leather sock with water, then held it in his mouth until he climbed up, and gave the dog a drink. Allah appreciated his deed and forgave him."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, is there really a reward for us in these animals?" He said:
"In every living creature with a moist liver there is a reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said: I was a man who often emitted prostatic fluid,
and I was too shy to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I instructed al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad, and he asked him. He said, "Wuḍūʾ is required for it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man of the Anṣār and sent for him. He came out with his head dripping, and he said, "Perhaps we have made you hurry."
He said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"If you are rushed or do not ejaculate, then ghusl is not required of you, but wuḍūʾ is required."
Ibn Bashshār said:
"If you are rushed or do not ejaculate."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ moved on from ʿArafah, he turned aside to the mountain pass and relieved himself.
Usāmah ibn Zayd said: I began pouring water for him while he performed wuḍūʾ, and I said, "O Messenger of Allah, will you pray?" He said, "The place of prayer is ahead of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning this verse: "Not equal are those believers who sit [at home] and those who strive in the cause of Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed Zayd, who came with a shoulder blade to write it down. Then Ibn Umm Maktūm complained to him about his blindness, and [the words] were revealed: "...other than those who have a disability." Shuʿbah said: Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm also informed me, from a man, from Zayd ibn Thābit, concerning this verse, "Not equal are those believers who sit [at home]...", similar to the hadith of al-Barāʾ. Ibn Bashshār said in his narration: Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from a man, from Zayd ibn Thābit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Khaybar: "
Tomorrow I will give this banner to a man
at whose hands Allah will grant victory,
who loves Allah and His Messenger,
and whom Allah and His Messenger love."
He said: The people spent the night debating which of them would be given it. When morning came, the people went early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
each of them hoping to be given it. He said: "
Where is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib?"
It was said: "He is suffering from his eyes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Send for him."
He was brought, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spat in his eyes and made supplication for him,
and he was healed as though he had never had any pain. Then he gave him the banner.
ʿAlī said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I fight them until they become like us?" He said: "
Proceed calmly until you reach their territory,
then invite them to Islam,
and inform them of what is required of them regarding the right of Allah in it.
For by Allah, if Allah guides one single man through you, that is better for you than red camels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Read to him while I was listening,]
from Ibn Wahb,
who said: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
who said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me
that Abū Hurayrah
informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, 'There is no god but Allah.' Whoever says, 'There is no god but Allah,' his property and his life are protected from me, except by its right, and his reckoning is with Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was wearing a Najrānī cloak with a thick border.
A Bedouin caught up with him and pulled him violently by his cloak,
so that I looked at the side of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ neck and saw that the border of the cloak had left a mark on it from the force of his pulling.
Then he said: "O Muhammad, order that I be given some of the wealth of Allah that you have."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to him, then laughed, then ordered that he be given a gift.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, sent me among those who were to announce on the Day of Sacrifice at Minā: "No polytheist may perform Hajj after this year,
and no one may circumambulate the House naked."
The Day of the Greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.
It was only called "the Greater" because of the people's saying "the Lesser Hajj."
So Abū Bakr renounced [the treaties] with the people in that year,
and in the year of the Farewell Hajj, when the Prophet ﷺ performed Hajj, no polytheist performed Hajj.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanding that dogs be killed, saying: "
Kill snakes and dogs, and kill the one with two stripes and the tailless one, for they take away eyesight and cause pregnant women to miscarry."
Al-Zuhrī said: We think that is due to their poison, and Allah knows best.

Sālim said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: I continued not to leave any snake I saw without killing it. One day, while I was chasing a snake of the kind found in houses, Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb or Abū Lubābah passed by me as I was chasing it, and said: "Wait, O ʿAbdullāh."
I said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that they be killed."
He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ later forbade [killing] those found in houses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: People are [like] mines, like the mines of silver and gold. The best of them in the time of ignorance are the best of them in Islam, if they gain understanding. And souls are conscripted armies: those that recognize one another become close, and those that do not recognize one another differ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

It was said to the Children of Israel: 'Enter the gate prostrating and say: Ḥiṭṭah [Forgiveness], and We will forgive you your sins.' But they changed it, and entered the gate dragging themselves on their backsides, and said: 'A grain in a hair.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best of its women is Maryam daughter of ʿImrān, and the best of its women is Khadījah daughter of Khuwaylid."
Abū Kurayb said: Wakīʿ pointed to the sky and the earth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever says, 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things,'

ten times after the Maghrib prayer, Allah will send for him guards who will protect him from Satan until morning, Allah will record for him ten decisive good deeds on account of it, wipe away from him ten ruinous sins, and it will be for him equal to freeing ten believing slaves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah said: 'O son of Adam, as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for whatever you have done, and I do not mind. O son of Adam, if your sins reach the clouds of the sky and then you seek My forgiveness, I will forgive you, and I do not mind. O son of Adam, if you came to Me with an earth-load of sins and then met Me without associating anything with Me, I would come to you with an earth-load of forgiveness.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The miser is the one in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Hold fast to the night prayer, for it was the practice of the righteous before you; the night prayer is a means of drawing near to Allah, a deterrent from sin, an expiation for evil deeds, and a repeller of illness from the body."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever invokes against the one who wronged him has indeed taken his due retribution."
He said: This is a gharīb ḥadīth; we only know it from the narration of Abū Ḥamzah.
Some of the people of knowledge have criticized Abū Ḥamzah on account of his memory; he is Maymūn al-Aʿwar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever says ten times: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things,'
it will be for him equal to freeing four slaves from the descendants of Ismāʿīl."
He said: This ḥadīth has also been narrated from Abū Ayyūb as a mawqūf report.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while I had four thousand date stones in front of me, with which I was glorifying Allah. I said, "I have glorified Allah with these." He said:
"Shall I not teach you something greater than what you have glorified with?"
I said, "Yes, teach me." He said:
"Say: Glory be to Allah as many times as the number of His creation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq stood on the pulpit and then wept, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood on the pulpit in the first year and then wept, and said:
"Ask Allah for pardon and well-being, for no one has been given after certainty anything better than well-being."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth by this route from Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent a expedition toward Najd, and they took a great deal of spoils and returned quickly. A man who had not gone out said, "We have never seen an expedition that returned faster or had better spoils than this one." So the Prophet ﷺ said:

"Shall I not tell you of a people who have better spoils and return faster? They are a people who attended the dawn prayer, then sat remembering Allah until the sun rose upon them. Those are the ones who return faster and have better spoils."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, that a mukātab
came to him and said, "I am unable to pay my contract of emancipation, so help me."
He said, "Shall I not teach you words that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me? Even if you owed a debt as large as a mountain, Allah would settle it for you." He said:
"Say: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and make me independent through Your bounty of all besides You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was ill, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while I was saying: "O Allah, if my appointed time has come, then give me relief; and if it is delayed, then ease my life; and if it is a trial, then grant me patience."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "What did you say?"
He said: So he repeated to him what he had said. He said: Then he struck him with his foot and said:
"O Allah, grant him well-being," or "heal him." Shuʿbah was the one in doubt.
He said: After that I never again complained of my pain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Khuṭmī, the freed slave of az-Zubayr, from az-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām,
said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no morning on which the servants wake except that a caller calls out: 'Glorify the King, the Most Holy.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Khālid ibn Sufyān al-Hudhalī, who was near ʿUranah and ʿArafāt, and said, "Go and kill him."

He said: I saw him, and the time of the ʿAṣr prayer had come. I said, "I fear that something may come between him and me that would make me delay the prayer."
