So I set out walking, praying while gesturing with nods in his direction. When I drew near him, he said to me, "Who are you?" I said, "A man of the Arabs. It has reached me that you are gathering people against this man, so I have come to you for that."
He said, "Indeed, I am engaged in that." So I walked with him for a while, until, when I had the opportunity, I struck him with my sword until he was still.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh ibn Ziyād al-Kindī, from Bilāl,
that he related to him that he

came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to inform him of the morning prayer. ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, occupied Bilāl with a matter she was asking him about until the dawn light exposed him and it became very bright. He said: Bilāl stood and called the prayer for him and kept repeating his call, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not come out. When he came out, he led the people in prayer, and [Bilāl] told him that ʿĀʾishah had occupied him with a matter she was asking him about until it became very bright, and that he had been delayed in coming out. He said,
"I had prayed the two rakʿahs of Fajr."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, it has become very bright." He said,
"Even if it had become brighter than it did, I would still have prayed them, and done so well and beautifully."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do not abandon the two, even if the cavalry drives you out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was heard reciting in the two rakʿahs of Fajr, in the first rakʿah, {Say: We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to us}, and in the other rakʿah this verse: {Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down and we follow the Messenger, so record us among the witnesses}, or {Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bearer of good news and a warner, and you will not be asked about the companions of the Blazing Fire}. Al-Darāwardī was unsure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer in the last part of the night, he would look; if I was awake, he would talk with me, and if I was asleep, he would wake me. He would pray the two rakʿahs, then lie down until the muʾadhdhin came to inform him of the dawn prayer. Then he would pray two brief rakʿahs and go out to the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with the Prophet ﷺ for the dawn prayer. He would not pass by a man without calling him to prayer or nudging him with his foot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray two rakʿahs after every obligatory prayer, except Fajr and ʿAṣr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray after ʿAṣr while forbidding it, and he used to fast continuously while forbidding continuous fasting.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar was asked about the two rakʿahs
before Maghrib. He said, "I never saw anyone in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray them."
And he permitted the two rakʿahs after ʿAṣr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Whoever remains seated in his place of prayer after finishing the dawn prayer until he prays the two rakʿahs of Ḍuḥā, saying nothing but good, his sins will be forgiven, even if they are more than the foam of the sea."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was a Companion; they consider that he was ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr. He said that the Prophet ﷺ said,
"Come to me tomorrow, and I will grant you, reward you, and give you."
Until I thought he would give me a gift. He said,
"When the day passes its zenith, stand and pray four rakʿahs."
Then he mentioned something similar, and said,

"When you raise your head, meaning from the second prostration, sit up straight and do not stand until you have said subḥānallāh ten times, alḥamdulillāh ten times, Allāhu akbar ten times, and lā ilāha illā Allāh ten times. Then do that in the four rakʿahs." He said,
"Even if you were the greatest of the people of the earth in sin, you would be forgiven by that."
I said, "What if I cannot pray them at that time?" He said,
"Pray them at night or by day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to lengthen the recitation in the two rakʿahs after Maghrib until the people of the mosque dispersed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [I asked about] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never prayed ʿIshāʾ and then entered my room without praying four rakʿahs or six rakʿahs. Once it rained on us at night, so we spread a leather mat for him, and it is as if I can see a hole in it from which water was welling up. And I never saw him shield himself from the ground with any of his garments.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever seeks knowledge, it will be an expiation for his past [sins]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he raised his gaze to the sky and then said:
"This is the time when knowledge will be snatched away from the people, until they have no power over any of it."
Ziyād ibn Labīd al-Anṣārī said, "How will it be snatched away from us when we have recited the Qur'an? By Allah, we will recite it, and we will teach it to our women and our children." He said:

"May your mother be bereaved of you, Ziyād! I used to count you among the jurists of the people of Madinah. Here are the Torah and the Gospel with the Jews and the Christians; what benefit are they to them?"

Jubayr said: I met ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit and said, "Do you not hear what your brother Abū al-Dardāʾ is saying?" and I told him what Abū al-Dardāʾ had said. He said, "Abū al-Dardāʾ spoke the truth. If you wish, I will tell you of the first knowledge to be taken away from the people: humble reverence (khushūʿ). It is likely that you will enter a congregational mosque and not see a single humble man in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to write, but he did not permit us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of the Anṣār used to sit with the Prophet ﷺ and hear hadith from the Prophet ﷺ; it would impress him, but he could not memorize it. He complained of that to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I hear hadith from you and it impresses me, but I cannot memorize it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Seek help with your right hand."
And he gestured with his hand to [indicate] writing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ asking for a mount, but he found nothing with him to mount him on, so he directed him to another man, who provided him with a mount.
He then came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him, and he said:
"The one who points to good is like the one who does it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"My son, if you are able to spend the morning and the evening with no ill will in your heart toward anyone, then do so."
Then he said to me:
"My son, that is part of my Sunnah, and whoever revives my Sunnah has loved me.
And whoever loves me will be with me in Paradise."
In the hadith there is a long story.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Leave me as I have left you. When I narrate to you, take it from me. Those before you were destroyed only by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A narration:
"It is likely that people will strike
the livers of camels [in travel], seeking knowledge, and will find no one more knowledgeable than the scholar of Madinah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yazīd ibn Salamah said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have heard from you
a great deal of hadith, and I fear that its end will make me forget
its beginning. So tell me a comprehensive word." He said:
"Fear Allah regarding what you know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Two traits do not come together in a hypocrite: good conduct and understanding of the religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men were mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, one a worshipper and the other a scholar. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over the lowest of you."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah, His angels, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, even the ant in its hole and even the fish, send blessings upon the one who teaches people good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The believer will never be satisfied with good that he hears until his final end is Paradise."
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Mūsā asked permission to enter upon ʿUmar. He said, "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" ʿUmar said, "One."
Then he was silent for a while and said, "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" ʿUmar said, "Two."
Then he was silent for a while and said, "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" ʿUmar said, "Three."
Then he turned back. ʿUmar said to the doorkeeper, "What did he do?" He said, "He went back."
He said, "Bring him to me."
When he came, [ʿUmar] said, "What is this that you did?" He said, "The Sunnah."
He said, "The Sunnah? By Allah, you will bring me proof or evidence for this, or I will certainly do something to you."

He said: Then he came to us, a group of the Anṣār, and said, "O assembly of the Anṣār, are you not the most knowledgeable of people about the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not say:
'Asking permission is three times; if you are permitted, [enter], and if not, then go back'?"
The people began to jest with him. Abū Saʿīd said: Then I raised my head to him and said, "Whatever punishment you receive for this, I will be your partner."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ three times, and he permitted me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, when two men meet, which of them should begin with the greeting of peace?" He said, "The one closer to Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to trim or clip his mustache, and Ibrāhīm, the Close Friend of the Most Merciful, used to do it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to say in the evening:
"We have reached the evening, and the dominion belongs to Allah at the evening. All praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner."
In the narration of Jarīr there is an addition, and as for Zubayd, he said that Ibrāhīm ibn Suwayd used to say:

"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what comes after it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what comes after it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and from the evil of old age, or disbelief. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave."
And when he reached the morning, he would also say it:
"We have reached the morning, and the dominion belongs to Allah in the morning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah is more delighted with the repentance of one of you than one of you is with his lost animal when he finds it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was one of the scribes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Abū Bakr met me and said, "How are you, Ḥanẓalah?" I said, "Ḥanẓalah has become a hypocrite." He said, "Glory be to Allah! What are you saying?" I said, "We are with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he reminds us of the Fire and Paradise until it is as if we see them with our own eyes. Then when we leave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we busy ourselves with our wives, children and livelihoods, and we forget much." Abū Bakr said, "By Allah, we experience the same."
So Abū Bakr and I set out until we entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I said, "Ḥanẓalah has become a hypocrite, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "What is that?"

I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are with you and you remind us of the Fire and Paradise until it is as if we see them with our own eyes. Then when we leave you, we busy ourselves with our wives, children and livelihoods, and we forget much."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you were to remain always as you are with me and in remembrance, the angels would shake hands with you on your beds and on your paths. But, Ḥanẓalah, there is a time for this and a time for that." He said it three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Az-Zuhrī said to me, "Shall I not tell you two amazing hadiths?" Az-Zuhrī said: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān informed me, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"A man wronged himself excessively, and when death approached him, he instructed his sons, saying: 'When I die, burn me, then grind me up, then scatter me in the wind over the sea. For by Allah, if my Lord gets hold of me, He will punish me with a punishment He has not inflicted on anyone else.'"
He said: "They did that to him. Then Allah said to the earth, 'Give back what you took.'"
"And there he was, standing. Allah said to him, 'What made you do what you did?' He said, 'Fear of You, my Lord,' or he said, 'Dread of You.'"
"So He forgave him because of that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I dealt with a woman on the outskirts of Madinah and I did with her everything short of touching her [in intercourse]. Here I am, so judge me as you wish."

ʿUmar said to him, "Allah had concealed your sin; if only you had concealed it yourself." He said: The Prophet ﷺ did not reply at all. The man got up and left, and the Prophet ﷺ sent a man after him to call him back, and recited to him this verse: {Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.} A man from the people said, "O Prophet of Allah, is this for him alone?" He said:
"No, rather for all people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah recited this verse:
{On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth}. She said, "O Messenger of Allah, where will the people be then?" He said, "On the Ṣirāṭ."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
It has also been narrated from another route from ʿĀʾishah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"When the servant is placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him..."
Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Shaybān from Qatādah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ three days before his death say:
"None of you should die except while thinking well of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Send blessings upon me in abundance on Friday, for it is a witnessed day, which the angels attend. No one sends blessings upon me but that his prayer is presented to me until he finishes it."
He said: I asked, "And after death?" He said: "
Even after death. Indeed, Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets."
So the Prophet of Allah is alive and provided for.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Indeed, Allah has people whom He frees [from the Fire] at every breaking of the fast, and that is every night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ramadan began.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

This month has come to you, and in it is a night better than a thousand months. Whoever is deprived of it has been deprived of all good, and none is deprived of its good except one who is truly deprived."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade hastening the fast of a day before the sighting of the moon.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] from the pulpit: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say from the pulpit before the month of Ramadan: "
Fasting is on such and such a day, and we are starting early. So whoever wishes to start early, let him do so, and whoever wishes to delay, let him delay."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
How much of the month has passed?" He said: We said:
"Twenty-two have passed and eight remain."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The month is like this, and the month is like this, and the month is like this."
Three times, and he held back one [finger].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted a concession to a pregnant woman who fears for herself to break her fast, and to a nursing woman who fears for her child.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came out to them on a day that he used to fast, and he asked for a vessel and drank. So we said:
"O Messenger of Allah, this is a day you used to fast." He said: "Yes, but I vomited."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Among the best qualities of the fasting person is the siwāk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The one who performs cupping and the one who has it done have broken their fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The one who performs cupping and the one who has it done have broken their fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A freed slave woman of the Prophet ﷺ said:
The Prophet ﷺ was asked about a man who kissed his wife while they were both fasting. He said: "They have both broken their fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Many a fasting person gains nothing from his fast except hunger.
And many a person who stands in night prayer gains nothing from his standing except sleeplessness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Seek help in the pre-dawn meal for fasting during the day, and in the midday nap for standing in prayer at night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to see me and said: "
Do you have anything?" We would say: "No." Then he would say: "Then I am fasting."
So he would continue his fast. Then something would be given to us as a gift and he would break his fast. She said:
And sometimes he fasted and then broke his fast. I said: "How is that?" She said:
"This is only like a man who goes out with charity, gives some of it away and keeps some back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah, I did not say: "
Whoever wakes up in a state of janābah, let him break his fast." Muhammad ﷺ said it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would spend the night in a state of janābah. Then Bilāl would come to him,
and let him know of the prayer, so he would get up and bathe.
I can still see the water running down from his head.
Then he would go out and I would hear his voice in the Fajr prayer. Muṭarrif said:
I asked ʿĀmir: "In Ramadan?"
He said: "Ramadan and other than it are the same."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said:
"O Messenger of Allah!
What about one who fasts two days and breaks his fast one day?" He said: "
Can anyone bear that?" He said:
"O Messenger of Allah!
What about one who fasts one day and breaks his fast one day?" He said: "
That is the fast of Dāwūd." He said:
"What about one who fasts one day and breaks his fast two days?" He said: "
I wish that I had been given the strength for that."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nūḥ fasted perpetually, except for the day of Fiṭr and the day of Aḍḥā."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "
Whoever fasts six days after Fiṭr, it completes the year: {Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof}."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever fasts the day of ʿArafah,
he will be forgiven the year before it and the year after it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), when asked about the fear prayer, would say: The imam advances along with a group of the people, and the imam leads them in one rakʿah.
Another group of them remains between them and the enemy, not having prayed.
When those with him have prayed one rakʿah, they withdraw to the place of those who have not prayed, without concluding the prayer with the salām.
Then those who have not prayed come forward and pray one rakʿah with him.
Then the imam departs, having prayed two rakʿahs.
Then each of the two groups stands and prays one rakʿah by themselves after the imam has departed,
so that each of the two groups has prayed two rakʿahs.
If the fear is more intense than that, they pray on foot,
standing upon their feet,
or riding, whether facing the qiblah or not facing it.
Mālik said: Nāfiʿ said: I do not think that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar mentioned that except from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last verse to be revealed was the verse on ribā, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken [in death] without having explained it to us, so abandon ribā and whatever raises doubt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rode a donkey with a Fadakī velvet cloth over it,
and he seated Usāmah ibn Zayd behind him,
going to visit Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah among the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, before the Battle of Badr. He said: He passed by a gathering in which was ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl,
and that was before ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy accepted Islam. In the gathering was a mixture of Muslims and polytheists who worshipped idols, and Jews, and Muslims,
and in the gathering was ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah.
When the dust of the animal covered the gathering, ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy covered his nose with his cloak,
then said: Do not raise dust over us.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ greeted them with salām, then stopped and dismounted, and invited them to Allah,
and recited the Qurʾān to them.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl said: O man,
there is nothing better than what you say,
if it is true,
so do not bother us with it in our gathering.
Go back to your mount,
and whoever comes to you, tell it to him.
ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah,
come to us with it in our gatherings,
for we love that.
Then the Muslims, the polytheists, and the Jews began to revile one another until they almost came to blows.
The Prophet ﷺ kept calming them until they quieted down.
Then the Prophet ﷺ mounted his animal and rode until he entered upon Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah,
and the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"O Saʿd, did you not hear what Abū Ḥubāb said?"
He meant ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy.
"He said such and such."
Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah said: O Messenger of Allah,
pardon him and overlook it,
for by the One who sent down the Book to you,
Allah has brought the truth that He sent down to you,
and the people of this town had agreed to crown him and wrap him with the turban [of leadership].
But when Allah refused that through the truth He gave you, he choked on it,
and that is what led him to do what you saw.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pardoned him. The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions used to pardon the polytheists and the People of the Book, as Allah had commanded them,

and to be patient with harm. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: {And you will surely hear from those who were given the Book before you and from those who associate others with Allah much abuse} — the verse.
And Allah said: {Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves} — to the end of the verse.
The Prophet ﷺ used to act upon pardon as Allah had commanded him,
until Allah gave permission regarding them.
Then when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought the Battle of Badr,
and Allah killed through him the leaders of the disbelievers of Quraysh, Ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl said,
and those with him of the polytheists
and idol-worshippers: This matter has now taken a [clear] direction.
So they pledged allegiance to the Messenger ﷺ upon Islam, and they accepted Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Khudrī [reported] that some men

from among the hypocrites in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever the Prophet ﷺ went out on a military expedition, would stay behind and rejoice at their staying behind contrary to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Prophet ﷺ returned, they would make excuses to him and swear oaths, and they loved to be praised for what they had not done. So it was revealed: {Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done — do not think them to be in safety from the punishment.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one day in his sermon: "

Indeed, my Lord has commanded me to teach you what you do not know, of what He taught me this day of mine: 'Every wealth I have granted to a servant is lawful. I created all My servants as ḥunafāʾ (upright in pure monotheism), but the devils came to them and led them away from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me partners for which I sent down no authority.' And indeed Allah looked at the people of the earth and despised them, Arab and non-Arab alike, except for remnants among the People of the Book. And He said: 'I have sent you only to test you and to test others through you. And I have sent down to you a Book that water does not wash away, which you recite while asleep and awake.' And indeed Allah commanded me to burn Quraysh. I said: 'My Lord, they would crush my head and turn it into a loaf of bread.' He said: 'Drive them out as they drove you out, fight them and We will support you in fighting them, spend and We will spend on you, send an army and We will send five times its like, and fight with those who obey you against those who disobey you.'

He said: The people of Paradise are three: a ruler who is just and charitable, granted success; a man who is merciful and tender-hearted toward every relative and every Muslim; and a chaste man who restrains himself from what is unlawful, and who has dependents. He said: And the people of the Fire are five: the weak man who has no restraint, those among you who are followers, who seek neither family nor wealth; the treacherous one whose greed is never hidden, even if it is for something small, but he betrays for it; and a man who, morning and evening, does nothing but deceive you concerning your family and your wealth."
And he mentioned miserliness or lying, "and the foul-mouthed, ill-natured one."
And Abū Ghassān did not mention in his narration: "
'Spend and We will spend on you.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon one day.
And he narrated the hadith, and at its end he said: Yaḥyā said: Shuʿbah said, from Qatādah, who said: I heard Muṭarrif in this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Saʿīd said: I did not witness it from the Prophet ﷺ, but Zayd ibn Thābit narrated it to me. He said: While the Prophet ﷺ was in an orchard belonging to Banū al-Najjār, riding a mule of his, and we were with him, the mule suddenly shied with him and almost threw him. And there were graves, six, or five, or four (al-Jurayrī used to say it thus). He said: "
Who knows the occupants of these graves?"
A man said: I do. He said: "
When did these people die?"
He said: They died in a state of polytheism. He said: "
This community is tested in its graves. Were it not that you would stop burying one another, I would have asked Allah to let you hear the punishment of the grave that I hear."
Then he turned his face to us and said: "
Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the Fire."
They said: We seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the Fire. He said: "
Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave."
They said: We seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave. He said: "
Seek refuge with Allah from trials, both what is apparent of them and what is hidden."
They said: We seek refuge with Allah from trials, both what is apparent of them and what is hidden. He said: "
Seek refuge with Allah from the trial of the Dajjāl."
They said: We seek refuge with Allah from the trial of the Dajjāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the soul of the believer departs, two angels receive it and ascend with it."
Ḥammād said: He mentioned how pleasant its scent is, and he mentioned musk. He said: "
The inhabitants of heaven say: 'A pure soul has come from the earth. May Allah bless you and the body you used to inhabit.'
Then it is taken to its Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, who then says: 'Take him to the final appointed time.'" He said: "
And as for the disbeliever, when his soul departs" (Ḥammād said: and he mentioned its stench and mentioned cursing) "the inhabitants of heaven say: 'A foul soul has come from the earth.'
He said: Then it is said: 'Take him to the final appointed time.'"
Abū Hurayrah said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pressed a thin cloth he was wearing over his nose, like this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Every servant will be resurrected in the state in which he died."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ woke from his sleep saying: "
There is no god but Allah. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today an opening has been made in the barrier of Yājūj and Mājūj like this."
And Sufyān made a ring with his hand, indicating ten.
I said: O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us? He said: "
Yes, when wickedness becomes abundant."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He wrote to Anas ibn Mālik to console him over those of his family and cousins who had been struck down on the Day of al-Ḥarrah. [Anas] wrote back to him: "I give you glad tidings from Allah: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'O Allah, forgive the Anṣār, the children of the Anṣār, and the children of their children.'"
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
Qatādah also narrated it from al-Naḍr ibn Anas,
from Zayd ibn Arqam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Convey greetings of peace to your people, for they are, as far as I know, people of chastity and patience."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever wants to humiliate Quraysh, Allah will humiliate him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, You made the first of Quraysh taste punishment, so let the last of them taste bounty."
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of the Anṣār are Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we reached Ḥarrat al-Suqyā, which belonged to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bring me water for ablution."
He performed ablution, then stood and faced the qiblah, then said:

"O Allah, Ibrāhīm was Your servant and Your close friend, and he prayed for the people of Makkah for blessing. I am Your servant and Your Messenger, and I pray to You for the people of Madīnah, that You bless them in their mudd and their ṣāʿ twice as much as You blessed the people of Makkah, with blessing upon blessing."
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: What is between my house and my minbar is a garden from the gardens of Paradise."
And with this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"One prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except al-Masjid al-Ḥarām." This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ, and it has also been narrated from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, through more than one route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is able to die in Madīnah, let him die there, for I will intercede for whoever dies there."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The last of the towns of Islam to fall into ruin will be Madīnah."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb. We do not know it except from the narration of Junādah, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah.
He said: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl was astonished by this hadith of Abū Hurayrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah revealed to me: whichever of these three you descend upon, that is the abode of your emigration: Madīnah, or Bahrain, or Qinnasrīn."
This hadith is gharīb. We do not know it except from the narration of al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā; Abū ʿĀmir was alone in narrating it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Makkah:
"How good a city you are, and how beloved to me! Had my people not driven me out of you, I would not have settled anywhere else."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"O Salmān, do not hate me, or you will depart from your religion."
I said: O Messenger of Allah, how could I hate you, when Allah guided us through you? He said:
"You hate the Arabs, and so you hate me."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb. We do not know it except from the narration of Abū Badr Shujāʿ ibn al-Walīd.
And I heard Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl say: Abū Ẓabyān did not meet Salmān; Salmān died before ʿAlī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever cheats the Arabs will not enter into my intercession, and my affection will not reach him."
This hadith is gharīb. We do not know it except from the narration of Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿUmar al-Aḥmasī, from Mukhāriq.
And Ḥuṣayn is not considered strong by the scholars of hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whenever one of the Arabs died, Umm al-Ḥarīr would be greatly distressed, so it was said to her: We see that when a man of the Arabs dies, you are greatly distressed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The non-Arabs were mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"I have more trust in them, or in some of them, than I have in you, or in some of you."
This hadith is gharīb. We do not know it except from the narration of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh.
And this Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ is called Ṣāliḥ ibn Mihrān, the freed slave of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ looked toward Yemen and said:
"O Allah, turn their hearts toward us, and bless us in our ṣāʿ and our mudd."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Sovereignty is in Quraysh, judgeship is among the Anṣār, the call to prayer is among the Abyssinians, and trustworthiness is among al-Azd," meaning Yemen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The lowest of the people of Paradise is the one who has eighty thousand servants and seventy-two wives, and a dome of pearl, peridot and ruby will be set up for him, as wide as the distance between al-Jābiyah and Ṣanʿāʾ."
And with this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Whoever among the people of Paradise dies, whether young or old, will be restored to the age of thirty in Paradise, and they will never exceed it, and the same applies to the people of the Fire."
And with this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"They will wear crowns, and the least of the pearls on them would light up what lies between the east and the west."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"In Paradise there is a gathering of the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr ʿīn) who raise their voices with a sound the like of which creation has never heard." He said: "They say: We are the everlasting, so we never perish; we are the blissful, so we never suffer hardship; we are the content, so we never become displeased. Glad tidings to those who belong to us and to whom we belong."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of the Almighty:
"So they will be in a garden, delighted" (30:15), he said: It is the listening (samāʿ).
And the meaning of samāʿ is as stated in the hadith, that the wide-eyed maidens raise their voices.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Three are loved by Allah: a man who stands in the night reciting the Book of Allah; a man who gives charity with his right hand and conceals it—I think he said: from his left; and a man who was in a military detachment and his companions were routed, so he faced the enemy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Paradise there is a sea of water, a sea of honey, a sea of milk, and a sea of wine, and then the rivers branch out from them afterward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"On the Day of Resurrection a neck will emerge from the Fire, with two eyes that see, two ears that hear, and a tongue that speaks. It will say: I have been put in charge of three: every obstinate tyrant, everyone who called upon another god alongside Allah, and the image-makers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwān said on this pulpit of ours, the pulpit of Basra, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"A huge rock would be thrown from the edge of Hell and would fall into it for seventy years without reaching its bottom."
He said: ʿUmar used to say: Remember the Fire often, for its heat is intense, its depth is far, and its maces are of iron.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Aṣ-Ṣaʿūd is a mountain of fire which the disbeliever will be made to climb for seventy autumns, then he will fall down with it, and so it will be for him forever."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith; we only know it as a raised narration from the hadith of Ibn Lahīʿah.
Something of this has been narrated from ʿAṭiyyah, from Abū Saʿīd, as his own statement (mawqūf).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The thickness of the skin of the disbeliever is forty-two cubits, his molar is like Uḥud, and his seat in Hell is like the distance between Makkah and Madinah."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith from the narration of al-Aʿmash.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The disbeliever will drag his tongue for a farsakh or two farsakhs, and people will trample on it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Like molten brass" (18:29): like the dregs of oil; when it is brought close to him, the skin of his face falls off into it."
And with this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"The enclosure of the Fire has four walls, the thickness of each wall being like a journey of forty years."
And with this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"If a bucket of ghassāq were poured out in the world, the people of the world would stink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Boiling water will be poured over their heads and will penetrate until it reaches his innards, dissolving what is inside him until it passes out through his feet, and that is ṣahr (melting). Then he will be restored as he was."
Saʿīd ibn Yazīd has the kunyah Abū Shujāʿ; he is Egyptian, and al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrated from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ concerning His saying:
"He will be given to drink of purulent water, which he will gulp down" (14:16-17), he said:

"It will be brought close to his mouth and he will loathe it. When it is brought nearer, it will scorch his face and the skin of his head will fall off. When he drinks it, it will cut his intestines until they come out of his rear. Allah says:
'And they will be given boiling water to drink, which will cut their intestines apart' (47:15), and He says:
'And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces. How wretched a drink!' (18:29)"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of you are those who are best to their wives."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ raced me, and I beat him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, newly married to Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy, the women of the Anṣār came and spoke about her.
She said: I disguised myself and veiled my face and went. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at my eyes and recognized me.
She said: I turned away and hurried my steps, but he caught up with me and embraced me, and said: "How did you see her?"
She said: I said: A Jewish woman among Jewish women!
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah said: I did not know anything until Zaynab entered upon me without permission, while she was angry.
Then she said: O Messenger of Allah, is it enough for you that the daughter of Abū Bakr should overturn her two small arms against you?
Then she turned to me, but I turned away from her, until the Prophet ﷺ said: "Go ahead and defend yourself."
So I turned to her until I saw that her saliva had dried in her mouth and she could not answer me with anything, and I saw the face of the Prophet ﷺ light up.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon, then mentioned women and advised the men about them, then said:
"Why does one of you beat his wife as a slave woman is beaten, when perhaps he will lie with her at the end of the day?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ married Umm Salamah in Shawwāl and consummated the marriage with her in Shawwāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded her that she should let a man go in to his wife before he had given her anything.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"There is no ill omen, but good fortune may be found in three things: in a woman, a horse, and a house."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the child belongs to the marriage bed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ with two small children of hers; she was carrying one of them and leading the other. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Women who carry [children], who bear children, who are merciful—were it not for what they do to their husbands, those among them who pray would enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"The unlawful does not make the lawful unlawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What is the matter with people who play with the limits of Allah, one of them saying: I have divorced you, I have taken you back, I have divorced you?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Fāṭimah bint Qays: Tell me about your divorce.
She said: My husband divorced me three times while he was leaving for Yemen, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ allowed that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He had Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqbah as his wife, and she said to him while she was pregnant: Put my heart at ease with a divorce.
So he divorced her with one divorce, then went out to prayer, and when he returned she had given birth.
He said: What is wrong with her? She deceived me—may Allah deceive her! Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"The Book has run its term. Propose to her as for herself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The two of them wrote to Subayʿah bint al-Ḥārith asking her about her case,

and she wrote back to them that she had given birth twenty-five days after her husband's death, and she adorned herself seeking a good marriage. Abū al-Sanābil ibn Baʿkak passed by her and said: You are in a hurry! Observe the longer of the two periods, four months and ten days.
So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmrah bint al-Jawn
sought refuge from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when she was brought in to him, and he said:
"You have sought refuge with One who gives refuge."
So he divorced her and commanded Usāmah or Anas to give her a gift of three Rāziqī garments.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]

"If a woman claims that her husband divorced her and brings one upright witness to that, the husband is made to swear an oath. If he swears, the witness's testimony is void; if he refuses to swear, his refusal stands in the place of a second witness, and his divorce takes effect."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed Allah has overlooked for my Ummah mistakes, forgetfulness, and what they are forced to do."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"There is no divorce before marriage, and no manumission before ownership."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"A woman who asks her husband for divorce without due cause will not smell the fragrance of Paradise,
though its fragrance can be found from a distance of forty years' travel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ swore that he would not go in to his wives for a month. He stayed away for twenty-nine days, and on the evening of the thirtieth he came in to me. I said: You swore that you would not come in to us for a month. He said: "The month is like this,"
and he let his fingers out, three times, "and like this,"
and he let out all his fingers but held back one finger on the third time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from the Ansar, called Abū Madhkūr, freed a slave of his, called Yaʿqūb, by a posthumous manumission, and he had no other property. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for him and said, "Who will buy him?"
Nuʿaym ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Naḥḥām bought him for eight hundred dirhams and handed the money over to him. Then he ﷺ said, "
When one of you is poor, let him begin with himself. If there is any surplus, then [let it go] to his dependents; and if there is any surplus, then to his relatives." Or he said, "
to those related to him. And if there is still a surplus, then [give] here and there."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My master ordered me to cut
meat into strips. A poor man came and I fed him some of it. My master found out about that and beat me. So I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he summoned him and said, "Why did you beat him?"
He said, "He feeds [people] from my food without my command," and on another occasion he said, "without my permission." He ﷺ said, "The reward is shared between the two of you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said while on the pulpit, mentioning charity and abstaining from begging, "
The upper hand is better than the lower hand. The upper hand is the one that spends, and the lower is the one that begs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mukhāriq al-Hilālī said: I took on a debt [to settle a dispute] and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to ask him for help with it. He said, "
Stay until charity (ṣadaqah) comes to us, and we will order that you be given some of it."
He said: Then he said, "

O Qabīṣah, begging is not permissible except for one of three: a man who has taken on a debt [for others], for whom begging is permissible until he obtains it, then he stops; a man struck by a calamity that destroyed his wealth, for whom begging is permissible until he obtains a means of subsistence—or he said, a sufficiency of livelihood; and a man struck by poverty, until three sensible people of his people say, 'Poverty has indeed struck so-and-so,' for whom begging is permissible until he obtains a means of subsistence—or he said, a sufficiency of livelihood. Anything other than these, O Qabīṣah, is unlawful gain, which the one who takes it eats as unlawful gain."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Mālikī said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, appointed me over the charity (ṣadaqah). When I had finished with it and handed it over to him, he ordered a payment for my work. I said, "I only worked for Allah, and my reward is with Allah."
He said, "Take what you are given, for I worked during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he gave me payment, and I said the same as you said. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me, "
When you are given something without having asked for it, then eat it and give in charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He mentioned the Khawārij and said: Among them is a man with a deformed hand—or a stunted hand, or a hand like a small breast. [He said:] If it were not that you would become arrogant, I would tell you what Allah promised those who fight them, on the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ. He [the narrator] said: I said, "Did you hear it from Muḥammad ﷺ?" He said, "Yes, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah, yes, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah, yes, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I am amazed at the one who starts the month early, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
When you see the new moon, fast; and when you see it, break the fast. If it is cloudy for you, then complete the count of thirty days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Marwān sent him to Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, to ask about a man who wakes up in a state of major ritual impurity: may he fast? She said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would wake up in a state of major impurity from intercourse, not from a wet dream, and then he would neither break his fast nor make it up."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for Makkah in the year of the Conquest and fasted until he reached Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm, and the people fasted with him. It was said to him, "The fasting has become hard on the people, and the people are watching what you do."

So he called for a cup of water after the ʿAṣr prayer and drank while the people were looking at him. Some of them broke their fast and some continued fasting. Then it reached him that some people had continued to fast, and he said, "Those are the disobedient."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Ibn ʿAbbās while he was resting with his cloak as a pillow by Zamzam, and I said, "Tell me about the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ: which day is it, that I may fast it?" He said, "When you see the new moon of Muḥarram, count, and then on the ninth morning be fasting."
He said: I said, "Is this how Muḥammad ﷺ used to fast it?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ and ordered that it be fasted, they said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is a day that the Jews and the Christians venerate."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Then next year, if Allah wills, we shall fast on the ninth day."
He said: The next year did not come before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I took this document from Thumāmah ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Anas ibn Mālik, from Anas ibn Mālik, that Abū Bakr wrote for them: "These are the obligations of charity (ṣadaqah) which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made obligatory upon the Muslims, and which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Messenger ﷺ [to enforce]. Whoever among the Muslims is asked for it according to its proper manner, let him give it; and whoever is asked for more than that, let him not give. For fewer than twenty-five camels, one sheep is due for every five camels. When they reach twenty-five, a bint makhāḍ (a one-year-old she-camel) is due, up to thirty-five. If there is no bint makhāḍ, then a male ibn labūn (a two-year-old male camel). When they reach thirty-six, a bint labūn (a two-year-old she-camel) is due, up to forty-five. When they reach forty-six, a ḥiqqah (a three-year-old she-camel fit to be covered by the stud camel) is due, up to sixty. When they reach sixty-one, a jadhaʿah (a four-year-old she-camel) is due, up to seventy-five. When they reach seventy-six, two bint labūn are due, up to ninety. When they reach ninety-one, two ḥiqqahs fit to be covered by the stud camel are due, up to one hundred and twenty. When they exceed one hundred and twenty, then for every forty a bint labūn, and for every fifty a ḥiqqah. If the ages of the camels differ in the obligatory charities: whoever owes a jadhaʿah as charity but does not have a jadhaʿah and has a ḥiqqah, the ḥiqqah is accepted from him and he adds with it two sheep if they are easily available to him, or twenty dirhams. Whoever owes a ḥiqqah but does not have a ḥiqqah and has a jadhaʿah, it is accepted from him and the collector gives him twenty dirhams or two sheep if they are easily available to him. Whoever owes a ḥiqqah but does not have one and has a bint labūn, it is accepted from him and he adds with it two sheep if they are easily available to him, or twenty dirhams. Whoever owes a bint labūn but has only a ḥiqqah, it is accepted from him and the collector gives him twenty dirhams or two sheep. Whoever owes a bint labūn but does not have a bint labūn and has a bint makhāḍ, it is accepted from him and he adds with it two sheep if they are easily available to him, or twenty dirhams. Whoever owes a bint makhāḍ but has only a male ibn labūn, it is accepted from him and nothing further is added. Whoever has only four camels, nothing is due on them unless their owner wishes. As for the charity on sheep that graze freely: when they reach forty, one sheep is due, up to one hundred and twenty. If there is one more, two sheep are due, up to two hundred. If there is one more, three sheep are due, up to three hundred. If they exceed that, one sheep for every hundred. No old animal, no defective animal, and no billy goat is to be taken as charity, unless the collector wishes. Animals that are separate are not to be combined, nor those that are combined to be separated, out of fear of the charity. Whatever belongs to two partners, they settle with one another equally. If a man's freely grazing sheep are short of forty by even one sheep, nothing is due on them unless their owner wishes. On silver, one-fortieth is due; if it is only one hundred and ninety dirhams, nothing is due on it unless its owner wishes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Muʿādh ibn Jabal when he sent him to Yemen:
"You will come to a people from the People of the Book.
When you come to them, invite them to testify that there is no god but Allah,
and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.
If they obey you in that, then inform them that Allah has made obligatory upon them five prayers every day and night.
If they obey you in that,
then inform them that Allah has made obligatory upon them charity (ṣadaqah),
taken from their wealthy
and given back to their poor.
If they obey you in that,
then beware of [taking] the best of their wealth,
and fear the supplication of the wronged, for there is no veil between it and Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"By Him in whose hand is my soul," or "By Him besides whom there is no god,"

or as he swore, "there is no man who has camels, cattle, or sheep and does not pay what is due on them, except that they will be brought on the Day of Resurrection at their largest and fattest, trampling him with their hooves and goring him with their horns.
Whenever the last of them has passed, the first of them is returned to him,
until judgment is passed between the people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is better for one of you to take his rope and gather firewood and carry it on his back than to go to a man whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given of His bounty and ask him, whether he gives him or refuses him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ take a piece of barley bread, place a date on it, and say:
"This is the relish for this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Laqīṭ ibn ʿĀmir
went out as a delegate to the Prophet ﷺ. Laqīṭ said:
We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned a hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ said: "By the life of your God."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He swore an oath to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Do not swear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah used to narrate that a man
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
Tonight I saw [in a dream]... and he mentioned a dream, which Abū Bakr interpreted. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"You were right in part and wrong in part." The man said:
I swear to you, O Messenger of Allah, by my father, you must tell me what I got wrong. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not swear."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some guests of ours stayed with us. He said:
Abū Bakr used to talk with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at night, and he said:
I will not return to you until you have finished entertaining these guests and serving them. So he brought them their meal, but they said:
We will not eat until Abū Bakr comes. Then he came and said:
What have your guests done? Have you finished serving them? They said: No. I said:
I brought them their meal, but they refused and said:
By Allah, we will not feed him until he comes. Then they said:
He is right; he brought it to us, but we refused until you came. He said:
What stopped you? They said: Your absence. He said:
By Allah, I will not eat it tonight. Then they said:
And by Allah, we will not eat it until you eat. He said:
I have never seen evil like tonight. He said: Bring your food. He said:
So their food was brought near, and he said:
In the name of Allah. He ate and they ate. Then I was told that he went in the morning to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what he had done and what they had done. He said:
"Rather, you are the most dutiful of them and the most truthful of them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two brothers
from the Anṣār had an inheritance between them, and one asked the other for its division. The other said:
If you ask me about dividing it again, then all my wealth is in the doorway of the Kaʿbah.
ʿUmar said to him:
The Kaʿbah has no need of your wealth.
Expiate your oath and speak to your brother. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"There is no oath binding on you,
and no vow in disobedience to the Lord, in severing family ties, or concerning what you do not own."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no vow or oath concerning what the son of Ādam does not own, nor in disobedience to Allah, nor in severing family ties.
Whoever swears an oath and then sees that something else is better than it, let him leave it and do what is better,
for leaving it is its expiation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men
brought a dispute to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ asked the claimant for proof,
but he had no proof. So he made the defendant swear, and he swore by Allah, besides whom there is no god.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Yes, you did do it,
but you have been forgiven because of your sincere saying of 'There is no god but Allah.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Anas ibn ʿIyāḍ: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥarmalah narrated to me,
from Umm Ḥabīb bint Dhuʾayb ibn Qays al-Muzaniyyah,
who was married to a man of them who had accepted Islam, and then was married to a nephew of Ṣafiyyah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Ḥarmalah said:
Umm Ḥabīb gave us a ṣāʿ as a gift. She narrated to us from Ṣafiyyah's nephew, from Ṣafiyyah, that it was the ṣāʿ of the Prophet ﷺ. Anas said: I tested it,
or he said: I estimated it, and found it to be two and a half mudds by the mudd of Hishām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We had a makkūk called the makkūk of Khālid, which was two kaylajahs by the kaylajah of Hārūn. Muḥammad said:
The ṣāʿ of Khālid is the ṣāʿ of Hishām, meaning Ibn ʿAbd al-Malik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Khālid al-Qasrī took charge, he doubled the ṣāʿ, so the ṣāʿ became sixteen raṭls.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said:
O Messenger of Allah, I have a slave girl whom I slapped.
That weighed heavily on the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I said: Should I not free her? He said: "Bring her to me." He said:
So I brought her. He said: "Where is Allah?" She said: In the heavens. He said: "Who am I?" She said:
You are the Messenger of Allah. He said:
"Free her, for she is a believer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Go, Rāfiʿ"—to his gatekeeper—"to Ibn ʿAbbās and say: 'If every one of us who rejoices in what he has done, and loves to be praised for what he has not done, is to be punished, then all of us will be punished.'"
Ibn ʿAbbās said: "What do you have to do with this verse? This verse was only revealed about the People of the Book."

Then Ibn ʿAbbās recited: {And [mention] when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it"}, this verse. And Ibn ʿAbbās recited: {Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done...}. And Ibn ʿAbbās said: "The Prophet ﷺ asked them about something, and they concealed it from him and told him something else. They went out having shown him that they had informed him of what he had asked them about, seeking his praise for that, and rejoicing in what they had done by concealing from him what he had asked them about."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "I fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit me while I was unconscious. When I came to, I said: 'How should I dispose of my wealth?' He was silent and did not answer me until the verse was revealed:
{Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, the equivalent of the share of two females}." Abū ʿĪsā said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
And more than one narrator has reported it from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A verse] about which the people of Kūfah disagreed,

so I traveled to Ibn ʿAbbās and asked him about it. He said: "This verse was revealed: {And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell}. It is the last thing that was revealed, and nothing has abrogated it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was reclining at ʿĀʾishah's, and she said: "O Abū ʿĀʾishah, there are three things; whoever says any one of them has forged an enormous lie against Allah."
I said: "What are they?" She said: "Whoever claims that Muḥammad ﷺ saw his Lord has forged an enormous lie against Allah."

He said: I had been reclining, so I sat up and said: "O Mother of the Believers, give me time and do not rush me. Did Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not say: {And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon}, {And he certainly saw him in another descent}?"
She said: "I was the first of this Ummah to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said:

'It was only Jibrīl. I did not see him in his true form, in which he was created, other than on these two occasions: I saw him descending from the sky, his great size filling what is between the sky and the earth.'"

Then she said: "Have you not heard that Allah says: {Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives all vision, and He is the Subtle, the Aware}? Have you not heard that Allah says: {It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a partition, or that He sends a messenger who then reveals by His permission whatever He wills; indeed, He is Most High and Wise}?" She said: "And whoever claims that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concealed anything of the Book of Allah has forged an enormous lie against Allah, while Allah says: {O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message}."

She said: "And whoever claims that he would tell what will happen tomorrow has forged an enormous lie against Allah, while Allah says: {Say: None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah}."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to him: "Did you hear it from ʿAbdullāh?" He said: "Yes."
And he attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:

"No one is more jealous [protective] than Allah, and for that reason He has forbidden indecencies, those of them that are apparent and those that are hidden. And no one loves praise more than Allah, and for that reason He praised Himself."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Kaʿb
—who was Kaʿb's guide among his sons when he went blind—from Kaʿb ibn Mālik, who said: I said:
"O Messenger of Allah, part of my repentance is that I divest myself of my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Keep some of your wealth, for that is better for you." I said:
"Then I will keep my share in Khaybar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"{All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds} is the Mother of the Qurʾān, the Mother of the Book, and the Seven Oft-Repeated verses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn al-Musayyab said that Abū Hurayrah said: On the night he was taken on the Night Journey, the Prophet ﷺ was brought two cups at Īliyāʾ, one of wine and one of milk. He looked at them and took the milk.
Jibrīl, peace be upon him, said to him: "Praise be to Allah, who guided you to the natural disposition (fiṭrah). Had you taken the wine, your Ummah would have gone astray."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the news of the Prophet's ﷺ mission in Mecca reached Abū Dharr, he said to his brother, "Ride to this valley and find out for me about this man who claims that news comes to him from the heaven. Listen to what he says, then come back to me."

So the other man set out until he reached Mecca, and he listened to what he said. Then he returned to Abū Dharr and said, "I saw him commanding noble character, and [speaking] words that are not poetry."
Abū Dharr said, "You have not satisfied me in what I wanted."

So he prepared provisions and carried a water skin of his containing water until he reached Mecca. He came to the mosque and looked for the Prophet ﷺ, but he did not know him, and he disliked asking about him. Then night overtook him and he lay down. ʿAlī saw him and realized that he was a stranger. When Abū Dharr saw him, he followed him, and neither of them asked the other about anything until morning. Then he took up his water skin and provisions to the mosque and spent that day without seeing the Prophet ﷺ, until evening came and he returned to his place of lying down. ʿAlī passed by him and said, "Is it not yet time for the man to know his lodging?" So he made him get up and took him along with him, and neither of them asked the other about anything. When the third day came, he did the same, and ʿAlī made him get up with him. Then he said to him, "Will you not tell me what brought you to this town?" He said, "If you give me a covenant and a pledge that you will guide me, I will do so."

ʿAlī did so, and Abū Dharr told him. ʿAlī said, "It is true, and he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When morning comes, follow me. If I see anything I fear for you, I will stop as though I am pouring out water. If I keep going, follow me until you enter where I enter."
He did so and went following him until he entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, and he entered with him. He listened to his words and accepted Islam on the spot. The Prophet ﷺ said to him,
"Return to your people and inform them, until my instruction comes to you."
He said, "By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will proclaim it loudly among them."
He went out until he came to the mosque and called out at the top of his voice, "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

The people rose up and beat him until they laid him down. Then al-ʿAbbās came and threw himself over him and said, "Woe to you! Do you not know that he is from Ghifār, and that the route of your caravans to Syria passes by them?"
So he rescued him from them. Then the next day he returned and did the same, and they rose up against him and beat him, and al-ʿAbbās threw himself over him and rescued him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, have you benefited Abū Ṭālib in any way?
For he used to protect you and become angry on your behalf." He said,
"Yes, he is in a shallow part of the Fire.
Were it not for me, he would be in the lowest depth of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard, when his uncle Abū Ṭālib was mentioned in his presence, and he said,
"Perhaps my intercession will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, so that he is placed in a shallow part of the Fire that reaches only his ankles,
from which his brain boils."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of Allah:

"And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people", he said: It was a vision of the eye that the Prophet ﷺ was shown on the night he was taken on the night journey to Bayt al-Maqdis. He said:
"and the accursed tree in the Qurʾān" is the tree of Zaqqūm.
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "I am one of the leaders who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said, "We pledged allegiance to him that we would not associate anything with Allah, nor commit fornication, nor steal, nor kill the soul that Allah has forbidden except by right, nor plunder, nor disobey. For [us] is Paradise if we do that. If we fall into any of that, its judgment is up to Allah."
Ibn Rumḥ said: "Its judgment was up to Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"I was shown you twice before I married you.
I saw the angel carrying you in a piece of silk, and I said to him, 'Uncover her.'
He uncovered, and it was you.
I said, 'If this is from Allah, He will bring it to pass.'
Then I was shown you again, carried in a piece of silk, and I said, 'Uncover her.'
He uncovered, and it was you. I said, 'If this is from Allah, He will bring it to pass.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was travelling from Mecca to Medina, Surāqah ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum followed him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicated against him, and his horse sank [into the ground]. He said, "Supplicate to Allah for me, and I will not harm you."
He said: So he supplicated to Allah. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became thirsty, and they passed by a shepherd of sheep.
Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq said: I took a cup and milked into it a small amount of milk for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I brought it to him, and he drank until I was pleased.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If a man
bought fruit before its good condition appeared,
and then a blight struck it,
what struck it would be the loss of its owner.
Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh informed me from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not sell fruit until its good condition appears,
and do not sell fresh fruit for dried dates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Abraham, peace be upon him, migrated with Sarah,
and entered a town in which there was a king among the kings,
or a tyrant among the tyrants.
It was said: Abraham has entered with a woman
who is among the most beautiful of women.
So he sent for him: O Abraham,
who is this woman with you? He said: My sister.
Then he returned to her
and said: Do not give the lie to my statement, for I told them that you are my sister,
and by Allah, there is no believer on the earth other than you and me.
So he sent her to him, and he got up to approach her,
and she got up to perform ablution and pray. She said: O Allah, if I have believed in You and in Your messenger, and have guarded my chastity
except from my husband, then do not give this disbeliever power over me.
So he was choked until he kicked the ground with his foot."
Al-Aʿraj said: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said that Abū Hurayrah said: She said: O Allah, if he dies, it will be said that she killed him.
So he released her, then got up to approach her again.
She got up to perform ablution and pray,
and she said: O Allah, if I have believed in You and in Your messenger, and have guarded my chastity
except from my husband,
then do not give this disbeliever power over me.
So he was choked until he kicked the ground with his foot.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Abū Salamah said: Abū Hurayrah said: She said: O Allah, if he dies, it will be said that she killed him.
So he released her the second time,
or the third,
and said: By Allah, you have sent me only a devil.
Return her to Abraham, and give her a gift.
So she returned to Abraham, peace be upon him, and said: Did you know that Allah has humbled the disbeliever and given a servant girl for service?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, when a man came to him and said: O Abū ʿAbbās, I am a man
whose livelihood is only from the work of my hands,
and I make these pictures.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: I will only tell you what I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say. I heard him say:
"Whoever makes a picture, Allah will punish him
until he breathes a soul into it,
and he will never be able to breathe into it."
The man gasped greatly and his face turned pale.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Woe to you! If you insist on doing it,
then stick to these trees,
everything that has no soul.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sold the mudabbar [a slave promised freedom after his master's death].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sold him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, about advance payment (salam)
for dates. He said: The sale of dates was forbidden until they are fit,
and the sale of silver on credit for cash.
And I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about advance payment for dates.
He said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of dates until some of it is eaten,
or can be eaten, and until it is weighed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: for dates. He said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of fruit until it is fit,
and he forbade silver for gold on credit for cash.
And I asked Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the sale of dates until it is eaten or can be eaten, and until it is weighed.
I said: What is meant by "weighed"? He said: A man who is with him, until it is estimated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib, ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad, and a man from the Banū Asad from the people of Qinnasrīn came as a delegation to Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān. Muʿāwiyah said to al-Miqdām, "Did you know that al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī has died?" Al-Miqdām said, "To Him we belong and to Him we return." A man said to him, "Do you consider it a calamity?" He said to him, "Why should I not consider it a calamity, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed him in his lap and said:
'This one is from me, and Ḥusayn is from ʿAlī.'"
The man from Banū Asad said, "[He was] a live coal that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has extinguished."
He said: Al-Miqdām said, "As for me, I will not leave today until I anger you and make you hear what you dislike."
Then he said, "O Muʿāwiyah, if I speak the truth, then confirm me, and if I lie, then call me a liar." He said, "I will."
He said, "I ask you by Allah, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing gold?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "I ask you by Allah, did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid wearing silk?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "I ask you by Allah, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing the skins of predatory animals and riding on them?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "By Allah, I have seen all of this in your house, O Muʿāwiyah."

Muʿāwiyah said, "I knew that I would not escape from you, O Miqdām." Khālid said: Then Muʿāwiyah ordered for him [a gift] that he did not order for his two companions, and he assigned for his son two hundred [in the stipend]. Al-Miqdām distributed it among his companions. He said: The man from Banū Asad did not give anyone anything of what he had taken. That reached Muʿāwiyah, and he said, "As for al-Miqdām, he is a generous man who spreads his hand open; as for the Asadī, he is a man who keeps a good hold of his belongings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Busr ibn Arṭāh at sea when a thief called Miṣdar was brought, who had stolen a Bactrian camel. [Busr] said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Hands are not to be cut off during travel.'
Were it not for that, I would have cut off his hand."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went with my father toward the Prophet ﷺ. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to my father, "Is this your son?"
He said, "Yes, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah." He said, "Truly?"
He said, "I bear witness to it."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled, laughing at how clearly I resembled my father and at my father's oath on my behalf. Then he said:
"Indeed, he will not be held liable for a crime you commit, nor will you be held liable for a crime he commits."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: {No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Jews split into seventy-one sects: one is in Paradise and seventy are in the Fire. The Christians split into seventy-two sects: seventy-one are in the Fire and one is in Paradise. By the One in whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, my Ummah will split into seventy-three sects: one in Paradise and seventy-two in the Fire."
It was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" He said, "The main body [al-jamāʿah]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"My intercession is for the people of major sins from my Ummah."
Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī said: Jābir said to me, "O Muḥammad, whoever is not from the people of major sins, what need has he of intercession?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr, whoever is killed defending his religion is a martyr, whoever is killed defending his life is a martyr, and whoever is killed defending his family is a martyr."
He said: This is a ḥasan ḥadīth.
Likewise, more than one narrator reported something like this from Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd.
Yaʿqūb is the son of Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf al-Zuhrī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zāriʿ, who was among the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays, said: When we came to Medina, we hurried from our mounts and kissed the hand and foot of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: Al-Mundhir al-Ashajj waited until he came to his bag, put on his two garments, and then came to the Prophet ﷺ. He said to him:
"There are two qualities in you that Allah loves: forbearance and deliberateness."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, did I acquire them myself, or did Allah create me with them?" He said:
"Rather, Allah created you with them."
He said, "Praise be to Allah, who created me with two qualities that Allah and His Messenger love."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Sāʿidī (Sahl ibn Saʿd) said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have come to offer myself to you."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at her, raising his gaze and lowering it as he examined her, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowered his head.
