and he would break his fast until we said, "He does not fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would strive hard in the last ten [nights of Ramadan] in a way that he did not strive in any other time.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was delivering a sermon, saying: "
Trousers are for the one who cannot find a waist-wrapper, and leather socks are for the one who cannot find sandals." He meant the one in iḥrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was at al-Jiʿrānah, and I was with the Prophet ﷺ. The man was wearing a garment of cut pieces—meaning a cloak—and was smeared with khalūq perfume. He said, "I have entered iḥrām for ʿUmrah, and I am in this [garment] and smeared with khalūq."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "
What would you have done in your Hajj?"
He said, "I would take off these clothes and wash this khalūq off me."
So the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "
Whatever you would have done in your Hajj, do it in your ʿUmrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zayd ibn Arqam arrived, and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās said to him, asking him to recall: "How did you tell me about the meat of game that was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in iḥrām?" He said: A portion of the meat of game was given to him, and he returned it. He said: "
We do not eat it, for we are in iḥrām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not know whether it was Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr or Suʿdā bint ʿAwf.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited Ḍubāʿah bint ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and said: "
What prevents you, O my aunt, from Hajj?"
She said, "I am a sickly woman, and I fear being detained." He said: "
Then enter iḥrām and make the condition that your place of release is wherever you are held back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoning the jamrah while he was on his camel, and he was saying: "
O people, take your rites [of Hajj] from me, for I do not know; perhaps I will not perform Hajj after this year of mine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I performed Hajj in the Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ, and I saw Bilāl leading his mount by the halter, and Usāmah ibn Zayd holding up his garment to shade him from the heat, while he was in iḥrām, until he stoned Jamrat al-ʿAqabah. Then he addressed the people, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said much.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and Ibn
ʿUmar used to stay at al-Abṭaḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to take charge of his sacrificial camel, to give its meat, hides, and covers as charity, and not to give the butcher anything of it. He said: "
We will give him from our own [wealth]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ we performed Hajj at-tamattuʿ, slaughtering a cow for seven people and a camel for seven, sharing in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ led his Companions in prayer during a state of fear. He placed them in two rows behind him, and he led the row nearest to him in one rakʿah. Then he stood and remained standing until those behind them had prayed a rakʿah. Then they moved forward and those who had been in front moved back, and the Prophet ﷺ led them in one rakʿah. Then he sat until those who had lagged behind had prayed a rakʿah, and then he gave the salām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he

prayed the prayer of fear with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led one of the two groups in two rakʿahs, then he led the other group in two rakʿahs. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed four rakʿahs, and he led each group in two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah led those before us astray from Friday. The Jews had Saturday and the Christians had Sunday. Then Allah brought us and guided us to Friday, and so He placed Friday, Saturday and Sunday [in that order]. Likewise they will follow us on the Day of Resurrection. We are the last of the people of this world and the first on the Day of Resurrection, those judged for before all creation."
In another narration, Wāṣil [said]: "those judged between them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to pray with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then we would return and rest our water-carrying camels.
Ḥasan said: I asked Jaʿfar, "At what hour was that?" He said, "When the sun passed its zenith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give two sermons, sitting between them, reciting the Qurʾān and admonishing the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He entered the mosque while ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Umm al-Ḥakam was delivering the sermon sitting down. He said, "Look at this wicked man delivering the sermon sitting down!" And Allah the Exalted said: {And when they see trade or amusement, they rush to it and leave you standing}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Rifāʿah said: I reached the Prophet ﷺ while he was delivering a sermon. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, a stranger has come asking about his religion; he does not know what his religion is." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to me and left his sermon until he reached me. A chair was brought, and I think its legs were of iron. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on it and began to teach me from what Allah had taught him. Then he returned to his sermon and completed the end of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr
sent him to al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, the nephew of Namir, to ask him about something

Muʿāwiyah had done in prayer. He said: I prayed the Friday prayer with him in the enclosure, and when I gave the salām I stood in my place and prayed. When he entered [his quarters], he sent for me and said, "Do not do again what you did. When you have prayed the Friday prayer, do not join it with another prayer until you speak or go out, for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ commanded that a prayer not be joined to another prayer until one has spoken or gone out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some Abyssinians came and were performing a dance in the mosque on a day of ʿĪd. The Prophet ﷺ called me, and I placed my head on his shoulder and began watching their play, until I was the one who turned away from watching them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas said: Rain fell on us while we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ uncovered his garment until the rain reached him. We said, "O Messenger of Allah, why did you do this?" He said, "Because it is newly come from its Lord, the Exalted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Kathīr ibn ʿAbbās used to narrate that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās

used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed during an eclipse of the sun, like the hadith of ʿUrwah from ʿĀʾishah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he prayed two rakʿahs, with two bowings in each rakʿah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Muʿāwiyah

made half a ṣāʿ of wheat equal to a ṣāʿ of dates, Abū Saʿīd objected to that and said, "I will give only what I used to give in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: a ṣāʿ of dates, or a ṣāʿ of raisins, or a ṣāʿ of barley, or a ṣāʿ of dried cheese."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
– and Ḥāmid and Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā said: the man –
used to set aside some palm trees from his land for the Prophet ﷺ,
until Qurayẓah and an-Naḍīr were conquered, after which he began to return to him what he had given.

Anas said: My family told me to go to the Prophet ﷺ and ask him for what they had given him, or part of it. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ had given it to Umm Ayman. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and he gave them back to me. Then Umm Ayman came, put the garment around my neck, and said: By Allah, we will not give them to you, for he has given them to me.
So the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"Umm Ayman, leave him, and you will have such and such."
But she kept saying: Never, by the One besides Whom there is no god!
So he kept saying such and such until he gave her ten times as much, or nearly ten times as much.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from the people of Egypt performed Hajj to the House and saw some people sitting. He said: Who are these? They said: Quraysh.
He said: And who is this old man? They said: Ibn ʿUmar.
So he went to him and said: I will ask you about something, so tell me. I adjure you by Allah, by the sanctity of this House: do you know that ʿUthmān fled on the day of Uḥud? He said: Yes.
He said: Do you know that he was absent from the Pledge of Riḍwān and did not witness it? He said: Yes.
He said: Do you know that he was absent on the day of Badr and did not witness it? He said: Yes.
He said: Allahu akbar!

Ibn ʿUmar said to him: Come, and I will explain to you what you asked about. As for his fleeing on the day of Uḥud, I testify that Allah pardoned him and forgave him. As for his absence on the day of Badr, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was his wife, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"You will have the reward of a man who witnessed Badr, and his share [of the spoils]."

And he told him to stay behind with her, as she was ill. As for his absence from the Pledge of Riḍwān, had there been anyone in the valley of Makkah more honored than ʿUthmān, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have sent him in ʿUthmān's place. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿUthmān to Makkah, and the Pledge of Riḍwān took place after ʿUthmān had gone to Makkah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, holding up his right hand:
"This is the hand of ʿUthmān."
And he struck it upon his other hand and said: "This is for ʿUthmān," may Allah be pleased with him.
[Ibn ʿUmar] then said to him: Go now with this answer with you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was standing
in the rank on the day of Badr, I looked to my right and to my left,
and there I was between
two young boys of the Anṣār, of tender age. I wished I were between stronger men than them. Then one of them nudged me

and said: Uncle, do you know Abū Jahl? I said: Yes, what do you want with him, nephew? He said: I was told that he insults the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By the One in Whose hand is my soul, if I see him, my body will not leave his body until the one of us fated to die first dies.

He said: I was amazed at that. Then the other nudged me and said the same. He said: It was not long before I saw Abū Jahl moving about among the people. I said: Do you not see? That is your man whom you were asking about. He said: They rushed at him, struck him with their swords until they killed him, then went back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him. He said: "Which of you killed him?"
Each of them said: I killed him. He said:
"Have you wiped your swords?" They said: No.
He looked at the two swords and said: "You both killed him."
And he judged that his spoils go to Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ. The two men were Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ and Muʿādh ibn ʿAfrāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Messenger of Allah, I had vowed to spend a day in iʿtikāf in the Jāhiliyyah.
So he ordered him to fulfill it.
He said: ʿUmar had taken two slave girls from the captives of Ḥunayn,
and placed them in one of the houses of Makkah. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then showed favor to the captives of Ḥunayn [by freeing them],
and they began to hurry through the streets. ʿUmar said: ʿAbdullāh,
see what this is. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has shown favor to the captives.
He said: Go and release the two girls.
Nāfiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not perform ʿUmrah from al-Jiʿrānah; had he done so, it would not have been hidden from ʿAbdullāh.
Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim added, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: from the fifth [khumus].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"There were two men among the Children of Israel who were brothers in faith. One of them would commit sins, while the other strove hard in worship. The one who strove hard would keep seeing the other committing a sin and would say, 'Stop.'

One day he found him committing a sin and said to him, 'Stop.' He replied, 'Leave me to my Lord. Were you sent as a watcher over me?' The other said, 'By Allah, Allah will not forgive you,' or, 'Allah will not admit you to Paradise.'

Then their souls were taken and the two met before the Lord of the worlds. He said to the one who had strived hard, 'Did you have knowledge of Me, or did you have power over what was in My hand?' And He said to the sinner, 'Go and enter Paradise by My mercy.' And He said of the other, 'Take him away to the Fire.'"
Abū Hurayrah said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, he spoke a word that destroyed both his worldly life and his Hereafter.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he

entered, together with his father, upon Anas ibn Mālik in Medina in the time of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, when he was governor of Medina. He was praying a light, brief prayer, as if it were the prayer of a traveler or close to it. When he finished the prayer, my father said, "May Allah have mercy on you. Was this the obligatory prayer, or is it something you were praying voluntarily?" He said, "It is the obligatory prayer, and it is the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I did not err in anything except something I forgot." Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say:

"Do not be harsh upon yourselves, lest it be made harsh upon you. For a people were harsh upon themselves, so Allah made it harsh upon them. Those are their remnants in the monasteries and the dwellings: 'Monasticism, which they invented; We did not prescribe it for them.'"

Then the next morning he said, "Will you not ride out so that you may look and take a lesson?" He said, "Yes." So they all rode out, and came upon dwellings whose people had perished, passed away and been destroyed, lying in ruins. He said:
"Do you recognize these dwellings?"

I said, "How well I know them and their people! These are the dwellings of a people whom injustice and envy destroyed. Envy extinguishes the light of good deeds, and injustice confirms that or denies it. The eye commits adultery, as do the hand, the foot, the body, the tongue, and the private part, and that is confirmed or denied."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When a servant curses something, the curse rises to the heaven, and the gates of heaven are closed against it. Then it descends to the earth, and its gates are closed against it. Then it turns right and left, and when it finds no way through, it returns to the one who was cursed if he deserves it; otherwise, it returns to the one who uttered it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"It is not lawful for a believer to forsake a believer for more than three days. If three days pass, let him meet him and greet him with salām. If he returns the greeting, both share in the reward; if he does not return it, he has incurred the sin." Aḥmad added:
"And the Muslim has come out of the forsaking."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not for a Muslim to forsake a Muslim for more than three days. If he meets him and greets him with salām three times, and each time he does not return it, then he has incurred his sin."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three days. Whoever forsakes him for more than three days and dies, will enter the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever forsakes his brother for a year, it is like shedding his blood."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The believer is the mirror of the believer, and the believer is the brother of the believer: he protects him from loss of his property and guards him in his absence."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, the Abyssinians played in celebration of his arrival, rejoicing at it; they played with their spears.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He heard] a reed pipe. He said: He put his two fingers in his ears and moved away from the road, and said to me, "Nāfiʿ, do you hear anything?" I said, "No."
He said: Then he removed his fingers from his ears and said, "I was with the Prophet ﷺ and he heard something like this, and he did the same."
Abū ʿAlī al-Luʾluʾī said: I heard Abū Dāwūd say, "This hadith is munkar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was present with Abū Wāʾil at a wedding feast, and they began to play and sing. Abū Wāʾil undid his wrap and said: I heard ʿAbdullāh say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Singing makes hypocrisy grow in the heart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A effeminate man was brought to the Prophet ﷺ who had dyed his hands and feet with henna. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"What is the matter with this one?"
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, he is imitating women."
So he ordered that he be banished to an-Naqīʿ. They said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not kill him?" He said:
"I have been forbidden to kill those who pray."
Abū Usāmah said: An-Naqīʿ is an area outside Medina; it is not al-Baqīʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a funeral bier was brought.
They said, "Pray over him." He said, "
Does he owe any debt?" They said, "No." He said, "
Did he leave anything behind?" They said, "No."
So he prayed over him. Then another bier was brought,
and they said, "O Messenger of Allah, pray over him." He said, "
Does he owe any debt?" It was said, "Yes." He said, "
Did he leave anything behind?"
They said, "Three dinars." So he prayed over him.
Then a third bier was brought,
and they said, "Pray over him." He said, "
Did he leave anything behind?" They said, "No." He said, "
Does he owe any debt?"
They said, "Three dinars." He said, "
Pray over your companion."
Abū Qatādah said, "Pray over him, O Messenger of Allah, and the debt is on me." So he prayed over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: By the One in whose hand is my soul,
were it not that I would be leaving the last of the people with nothing,
I would not conquer any town except that I would divide it [among the fighters], just as the Prophet ﷺ divided Khaybar,
but I leave it as a treasury for them, to divide among themselves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī,
and I said to him, "Tell me something you heard from

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: I traveled with him on one of his journeys. Abū ʿAqīl said: I do not know whether it was a military expedition or an ʿUmrah. When we were returning, the Prophet ﷺ said, "
Whoever wishes to hurry ahead to his family, let him hurry."
Jābir said: So we set off, and I was on a camel of mine, ashen in color, with no blemish, and the people were behind me.
While I was like that, it stopped under me,
and the Prophet ﷺ said to me, "
O Jābir, hold on tight."
Then he struck it once with his whip,
and the camel leapt forward from its place. He said, "Will you sell the camel?" I said, "Yes."
When we arrived in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ entered the mosque among groups of his Companions, and I went in to him,
after tying the camel at the side of the paved area.
I said to him, "This is your camel." He came out,
and began to walk around the camel, saying, "The camel is our camel."
Then the Prophet ﷺ sent some ounces of gold and said, "Give it to Jābir." Then he said, "Have you received the full price?" I said, "Yes." He said, "
The price and the camel are both yours."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
There are forty good deeds, the highest of which is lending a she-goat for its milk.
There is no one who does one of them hoping for its reward and believing in what has been promised for it, except that Allah will admit him to Paradise because of it."
Ḥassān said: We counted what is lesser than lending a she-goat, such as returning a greeting, saying "may Allah have mercy on you" to one who sneezes,
removing harm from the road, and the like,
and we were not able to reach fifteen deeds.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which he wrote for ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm when he sent him to Najrān—the letter was with Abū Bakr ibn Ḥazm—and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote:
"This is a declaration from Allah and His Messenger: {O you who believe, fulfill your contracts.}"
He wrote out the verses from it until he reached {Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning}. Then he wrote:
"This is the writing about wounds: for a life, one hundred camels." Similar to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The letter which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote for ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm concerning blood-money:

"For a life, one hundred camels; for the nose, when it is completely cut off, one hundred camels; for the head wound reaching the membrane of the brain (al-māmūmah), a third of the blood-money for a life, and for the wound penetrating the body cavity (al-jāʾifah) the same; for the hand, fifty; for the eye, fifty; for the foot, fifty; for each finger of those, ten camels; for a tooth, five; and for a wound exposing the bone (al-mūḍiḥah), five."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin

came to the door of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and put his eye to the gap in the door. The Prophet ﷺ saw him and went at him with an iron implement or a stick to poke out his eye. When the man realized, he drew back. The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Had you stood your ground, I would have poked out your eye."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, the thief does not steal while he is a believer, and the one who drinks wine does not drink it while he is a believer—and he mentioned a fourth, which I forgot. When he does that, he removes the tie of Islam from his neck; but if he repents, Allah accepts his repentance.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, I have forgiven him." He said:
"Why did you not do so before you brought him to me, Abū Wahb?"
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had his hand cut off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
stole a garment and was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who ordered his hand to be cut off. The man said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is his [i.e., I give it to him]." He said:
"Why not before now?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He circled the House and prayed, then folded a cloak of his made of striped cloth, put it under his head and slept. A thief came and pulled it out from under his head and took it. He was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and [Ṣafwān] said, "This man stole my cloak."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Did you steal this man's cloak?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"Take him away and cut off his hand."
Ṣafwān said, "I did not want his hand to be cut off for the sake of my cloak." He said to him:
"Then why not before this?"
Ashʿath ibn Sawwār differed from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafwān was sleeping in the mosque with his cloak under him, and it was stolen. He got up after the man had gone, caught up with him and seized him, and brought him to the Prophet ﷺ, who ordered his hand to be cut off. Ṣafwān said, "O Messenger of Allah, my cloak is not worth a man's hand being cut off for it." He said:
"Why was this not [done] before you brought him to us?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with them both: A woman
used to borrow jewelry from people and then keep it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let this woman repent to Allah and His Messenger and return what she takes from the people."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Get up, Bilāl, take her by the hand and cut it off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
used to borrow jewelry in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She borrowed some jewelry, gathered it and kept it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let this woman repent and hand over what she has."
[He said it] several times, but she did not do so, so he ordered it and her hand was cut off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
of Banū Makhzūm borrowed jewelry on the word of some people, then denied it. The Prophet ﷺ ordered it, and her hand was cut off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman of Makhzūm used to borrow goods and deny it. She was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was spoken to about her. He said:
"If it were Fāṭimah, her hand would be cut off."
Sufyān was asked, "Who reported it?" He said, "Ayyūb ibn Mūsā, from az-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah, Allah willing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A thief was brought to the Prophet ﷺ and he had his hand cut off. They said, "We did not want it to come to this for him." He said:
"If it were Fāṭimah, I would cut it off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off a hand for [the theft of] a shield.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man stole a shield in the time of Abū Bakr. It was valued at five dirhams, and his hand was cut off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, like the first.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey on a dark night, and we did not know where the qiblah was. So each man among us prayed in the direction he was facing. When morning came, we mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and [the following verse] was revealed:
"Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed three: a man who leads people in prayer while they dislike him; a woman who spends the night while her husband is angry with her; and a man who hears "Come to success" and then does not respond.
label: machine translation

segments_en: It used to be said that the people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are two: a woman who disobeys her husband, and the imam of a people who dislike him.

Hannād said: Jarīr said: Manṣūr said: We asked about the matter of the imam, and we were told: This only refers to unjust imams. As for one who upholds the Sunnah, the sin is upon whoever dislikes him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Three whose prayer does not rise beyond their ears: a runaway slave until he returns; a woman who spends the night while her husband is angry with her; and the imam of a people who dislike him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade letting the garment hang loose (sadl) during prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ saw a boy of ours called Aflaḥ, who blew [on the ground] when he prostrated, and he said:
"O Aflaḥ, let your face touch the dust."
Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ said: ʿAbbād ibn al-ʿAwwām disliked blowing during prayer, and said that if one blows, it does not invalidate his prayer.
Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ said: And we hold to this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed the two prostrations after the salutation [ending the prayer].
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you makes a mistake in his prayer and does not know whether he has prayed one [unit] or two, let him build on one. If he does not know whether he has prayed two or three, let him build on two. If he does not know whether he has prayed three or four, let him build on three. And let him perform two prostrations before he gives the salutation."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If one breaks wudūʾ—meaning a man—after he has sat at the end of his prayer, before giving the salutation, then his prayer is valid."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey and reached a narrow place, and the time for prayer came. The sky rained on them from above and there was mud beneath them. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while on his mount, gave the call to prayer and the iqāmah—or [someone] gave the iqāmah—and he moved forward on his mount and led them in prayer, gesturing, making the prostration lower than the bowing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ had prayed the two units of Fajr, if he had a need of me he would speak to me; otherwise he would go out to the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qays said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out and the prayer was called, so I prayed the Morning Prayer with him. Then the Prophet ﷺ turned away and found me praying, and he said:
"Easy, Qays! Two prayers together?"
I said: O Messenger of Allah, I had not prayed the two units of Fajr. He said: "Then there is no harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has not prayed the two units of Fajr, let him pray them after the sun has risen."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ten units that he used to pray by night and day: two units before Ẓuhr and two after it, two units after Maghrib, and two units after the late evening prayer (ʿIshāʾ).
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is al-ʿAqadī, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr. Sufyān narrated to us,
from Abū Isḥāq,
from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī,
who said: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray four units before ʿAṣr, separating between them with the salutation upon the angels brought near and those who follow them among the Muslims and the believers.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed two units after Maghrib with the Prophet ﷺ in his house.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about the prayer of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: He used to pray two units before Ẓuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib, two after ʿIshāʾ, and two before Fajr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū ʿĪsā said: The most that is reported from the Prophet ﷺ regarding the night prayer is thirteen units including the Witr, and the least that is described of his night prayer is nine units.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stood [in prayer] one night with a single verse of the Qurʾān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best of your prayers is that which is in your homes, except the obligatory prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray Witr with three units, reciting in them nine sūrahs from the Mufaṣṣal, reciting three sūrahs in each unit, the last of them being "Say: He is Allah, [who is] One."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Hasten to pray Witr before the morning comes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: "Tell me about the worst thing the polytheists did to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said: "While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying in the courtyard of the Kaʿbah,
ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ came forward,
seized the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by the shoulder, twisted his garment around his neck, and choked him severely.
Then Abū Bakr came and seized him by the shoulder,
and pushed him away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: 'Would you kill a man for saying, "My Lord is Allah," when he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord?'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"I saw myself entering Paradise,
and there was al-Rumayṣāʾ, the wife of Abū Ṭalḥah, and I heard a soft footstep.
I said, 'Who is this?' It was said, 'This is Bilāl.'
And I saw a palace with a young woman in its courtyard.
I said, 'For whom is this?' It was said, 'For ʿUmar.'
I wanted to enter it and look at it, but I remembered your sense of jealousy."
ʿUmar said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah! Would I be jealous of you?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: "We have been mighty ever since ʿUmar accepted Islam."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar asked me about some of
the affairs of ʿUmar, and I told him. Then he said:
"After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken, I never saw anyone more earnest and more generous, until he reached the end of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUmar was stabbed, he began to groan in pain.
Ibn ʿAbbās said to him, as though trying to ease his distress: "O Commander of the Faithful,
even if it is so, you accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and kept good company with him,
then you parted from him while he was pleased with you.
Then you accompanied Abū Bakr and kept good company with him,
then you parted from him while he was pleased with you.
Then you accompanied their companions and kept good company with them,
and if you part from them, you will part from them while they are pleased with you."
He said: "As for what you mention about accompanying the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his pleasure,
that is only a favor from Allah, the Exalted, which He bestowed upon me.
And as for what you mention about accompanying Abū Bakr and his pleasure,
that is only a favor from Allah, majestic is His mention, which He bestowed upon me.
And as for what you see of my distress,
it is on account of you and your companions.
By Allah, if I had enough gold to fill the earth, I would ransom myself with it from the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, before seeing it."
Ḥammād ibn Zayd said: Ayyūb narrated to us,
from Ibn Abī Mulaykah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
"I went in to see ʿUmar," and he related this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, who was holding the hand of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. ʿUmar said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, you are dearer to me than everything except myself." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"No, by the One in whose hand is my soul, not until I am dearer to you than yourself."
ʿUmar said to him, "Now, by Allah, you are dearer to me than myself." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Now, O ʿUmar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to collect charity (ṣadaqah), and Ibn Jamīl, Khālid ibn al-Walīd and al-ʿAbbās refused to give. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Ibn Jamīl takes offense only because he was poor and Allah enriched him. As for Khālid ibn al-Walīd, you are wronging Khālid, for he has devoted his armor and his equipment in the cause of Allah. As for al-ʿAbbās, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his [charity] is upon me, and the like of it along with it." Then he said:
"Do you not know that a man's paternal uncle is like his father's twin?" or [he said], "the twin of his father."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The poor person is not the one who goes around among the people, and is turned away with a morsel or two morsels, or a date or two dates."
They said, "Then who is the poor person, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"The one who does not find enough to meet his needs, and is not noticed so that charity might be given to him, and who does not ask the people for anything."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Barīrah had three rulings [connected with her case]: people used to give her charity and she would give us gifts, so I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"It is charity for her and a gift for you, so eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made obligatory the zakāh of al-Fiṭr, a ṣāʿ of dates
or a ṣāʿ of barley, upon the slave and the free person, the male and the female,
the young and the old among the Muslims,
and he commanded that it be paid before the people go out to the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Zayd ibn Aslam,
from ʿIyāḍ ibn
ʿAbdullāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ, that he heard Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī
say: We used to give the zakāh of al-Fiṭr as a ṣāʿ of food, or a ṣāʿ of barley, or a ṣāʿ of dates, or a ṣāʿ of dried yogurt (aqiṭ), or a ṣāʿ of raisins.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Nāfiʿ] informed [me] that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mount his riding animal at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, and then he would begin the talbiyah when it stood upright with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what clothing a muḥrim may wear, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not wear shirts, nor turbans, nor trousers, nor hooded cloaks, nor leather socks, except for someone who cannot find sandals; let him wear leather socks and cut them off below the ankles. And do not wear any clothing that has been touched by saffron or wars."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Bukayr, the two sons of Muḥammad ibn Zayd, [reported] that they heard Nāfiʿ
narrating from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar,
from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to say:

"Labbayk, Allāhumma labbayk; labbayk, lā sharīka laka labbayk. Inna al-ḥamda wa-n-niʿmata laka wa-l-mulk, lā sharīka lak." [Here I am, O Allah, here I am; here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Indeed all praise, favor and sovereignty belong to You; You have no partner.]
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] a reading to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah,
who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Farewell Hajj, and we declared the intention for ʿUmrah. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has a sacrificial animal with him, let him declare the intention for Hajj together with ʿUmrah, and then not exit iḥrām until he exits from both of them together."
I came to Makkah while I was menstruating, so I did not circumambulate the House nor perform the walk between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. I complained of that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Undo your hair and comb it, and declare the intention for Hajj, and leave the ʿUmrah."
I did so, and when I had completed the Hajj, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr to at-Tanʿīm, and I performed ʿUmrah. He said:
"This is in place of your ʿUmrah."

Those who had declared the intention for ʿUmrah circumambulated the House and walked between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then exited iḥrām; then they performed another circumambulation after returning from Minā for their Hajj. As for those who combined Hajj and ʿUmrah, they performed only one circumambulation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Makkah, he entered from its upper part and left from its lower part.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Sahl ibn Saʿd, saying, "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat white bread of fine flour?" Sahl said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never saw fine white flour from the time Allah sent him until Allah took his soul."
He said: I asked, "Did you have sieves in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never saw a sieve from the time Allah sent him until He took his soul."
He said: I asked, "How did you eat barley without sifting it?" He said, "We would grind it and blow on it,"
and what could fly off would fly away, and what remained we would moisten and eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever eats a few ʿAjwah dates every morning,
neither poison nor magic will harm him that day until the night." Another narrator said, "seven dates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey when one of the camels ran off. He said: A man shot it with an arrow and stopped it.
He said: Then he said:
"These animals have wild traits like the wild animals, so if any of them overpowers you, do this to it."
He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are on expeditions and journeys and want to slaughter, but we have no knives." He said:
"Let the blood flow, or he said, make the blood flow, and mention the name of Allah, then eat,
except for a tooth or a nail,
for a tooth is a bone,
and a nail is the knife of the Abyssinians."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Abū Mūsā when his food was brought, and in his food was chicken meat. Among the people was a man from Banū Taymillāh, reddish in complexion, who looked like a freed slave, and he did not come near. Abū Mūsā said to him, "Come closer, for I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eat from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that his mother,
when she gave birth, they took the boy to the Prophet ﷺ to perform tahnīk for him. He said: The Prophet ﷺ was in a pen, branding sheep.
Shuʿbah said: Most of what I know is that he said, "on their ears."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A maternal uncle of mine called Abū Burdah sacrificed before the prayer,
so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Your sheep is a sheep of [ordinary] meat."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have a young domestic goat, a jadhaʿah." He said:
"Slaughter it, but it will not suffice for anyone other than you." Then he said:
"Whoever slaughters before the prayer only slaughters for himself,
and whoever slaughters after the prayer has completed his sacrifice
and has met the Sunnah of the Muslims."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever drinks wine in this world
and does not repent from it,
will be deprived of it in the Hereafter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer, the thief does not steal while he is a believer, and the one who drinks wine does not drink it while he is a believer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was standing
serving the tribe, and I was the youngest of them,
younger than my uncles, a man came and said, "Wine has been prohibited."
I was standing over them, serving them drink from their fermented date-and-unripe-date drink, and they said, "Pour it out."
So I poured it out. I asked Anas, "What was it?" He said, "Unripe dates and dates."
Abū Bakr ibn Anas said, "That was their wine at that time," and Anas did not object."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār,
from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The example of the believer is like a fresh, tender plant of the crop: wherever the wind comes from, it bends it over,
and when it becomes upright, it is bent again by trials.
And the wicked person is like the cedar, rigid and upright, until Allah breaks it when He wills."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ came to visit me, neither riding a mule nor a horse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah has sent down the disease and the cure, and has made a cure for every disease, so seek treatment, but do not treat yourselves with anything forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ in command of the army of Dhāt al-Salāsil. He said: I came to him and asked, "Which of the people is most beloved to you?" He said, "ʿĀʾishah."
I asked, "And among the men?" He said, "Her father."
I asked, "Then who?" He said, "ʿUmar."
Then he named other men, and I fell silent, fearing that he would place me last among them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAlī:
"You are to me in the position of Hārūn to Mūsā, except that there is no prophet after me." This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
It has also been narrated through more than one route from Saʿd, from the Prophet ﷺ, and this hadith is considered gharīb in the narration of Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The site of the mosque of the Prophet ﷺ belonged to Banū al-Najjār. It contained date palms and graves of the polytheists. The Prophet ﷺ said to them, "Name a price to me for it."
They said, "We will never take a price for it."
He said: So the Prophet ﷺ was building it while they handed [materials] to him, and the Prophet ﷺ was saying:
"Truly, the [real] life is the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Anṣār and the Muhājirah."
He said: And before the mosque was built, the Prophet ﷺ used to pray wherever the prayer found him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Throne shook at the death of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh."
And from al-Aʿmash: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us from Jābir, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
A man said to Jābir, "But al-Barāʾ says that the bier shook."
He said, "There was ill feeling between those two tribes.
I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'The Throne of the Most Merciful shook at the death of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was asking al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, saying: Have you heard anything about staying
in Makkah? Al-Sāʾib said: I heard al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī
say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The emigrant may stay three days in Makkah after the completion of the rites."
It was as though he meant that he should not exceed that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That his father
wrote to ʿUmar ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Arqam al-Zuhrī, instructing him to go in

to Subayʿah bint al-Ḥārith al-Aslamiyyah and ask her about her case and what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to her when she sought his ruling. So ʿUmar ibn ʿAbdullāh wrote to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUtbah informing him that Subayʿah had told him that she was married to Saʿd ibn Khawlah, who was from Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy and was among those who witnessed Badr. He died while she was pregnant, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and it was not long after his death that she gave birth. When she had recovered from her postnatal bleeding, she adorned herself for suitors. Abū al-Sanābil ibn Baʿkak, a man from Banū ʿAbd al-Dār, came in to her and said to her, "Why do I see you adorned? Perhaps you are hoping to marry. By Allah, you will not be able to marry until four months and ten days have passed."

Subayʿah said: When he said that to me, I gathered my garments around me in the evening and went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about it. He gave me the ruling that I had become permitted [to marry] when I gave birth, and he instructed me to marry if I wished.
Ibn Shihāb said: I see no harm in her marrying once she has given birth, even if she is still bleeding, except that her husband should not approach her until she is pure.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥusayn, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"In a dream I saw two bracelets of gold on my hands, and their matter concerned me. Then it was revealed to me to blow on them, so I blew on them and they flew away. I interpreted them as two liars who would appear after me: one of them is called Musaylimah, the man of al-Yamāmah, and the other al-ʿAnsī, the man of Ṣanʿāʾ."
He said: This is a ṣaḥīḥ ḥasan gharīb hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were talking in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we mentioned truffles. They said, "They are the smallpox of the earth."
The talk reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Truffles are from the manna, and the ʿajwah date is from Paradise, and it is a cure for poison."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Ḥunayn, Hawāzin, Ghaṭafān and others came with their children and their livestock. The Prophet ﷺ had ten thousand with him that day, along with the Ṭulaqāʾ (those freed at the conquest of Makkah). They turned away from him until he was left alone. He said: Then he made two separate calls that day, not mixing the two at all. He turned to his right and said:
"O company of the Anṣār!"
They said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah! Rejoice, we are with you." He said: Then he turned to his left and said:
"O company of the Anṣār!"
They said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah! Rejoice, we are with you." He said: He was on a white mule, and he dismounted and said, "I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger."

Then the polytheists were routed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ obtained a great deal of spoils. He distributed them among the Muhājirūn and the Ṭulaqāʾ and gave nothing to the Anṣār. So the Anṣār said, "When there is hardship, we are called, but the spoils are given to others."
That reached him, so he gathered them in a tent and said:
"O company of the Anṣār, what is this report that has reached me from you?" They were silent. Then he said:
"O company of the Anṣār, are you not pleased that the people go away with the world while you go away with Muḥammad, taking him back to your homes?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we are pleased." He said: Then he said:
"If the people were to take one valley and the Anṣār another mountain path, I would take the path of the Anṣār."
Hishām said: I said, "O Abū Ḥamzah, were you present for that?" He said, "And where could I have been absent from it?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to Banū Jadhīmah, and he called them to Islam. They could not say well, "We have accepted Islam," and began saying, "We have changed our religion." Khālid began killing and taking captives. He said: Then each man among us was given his captive, until the morning of the next day, when Khālid ibn al-Walīd ordered each man among us to kill his captive.

Ibn ʿUmar said: I said, "By Allah, I will not kill my captive, and none of my companions will kill his captive." He said: Then we came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned to him what Khālid had done. The Prophet ﷺ raised his hands and said:
"O Allah, I declare to You that I am free of what Khālid has done."
Zakariyyā said in his narration: He mentioned this, and in the narration of Bishr: Then he said:
"O Allah, I declare to You that I am free of what Khālid has done," twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to the land of my people,
and I came while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was camped at al-Abṭaḥ. He said:
"Have you performed Hajj, O ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays?"
I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "What did you say?"
He said: I said, "At Your service, with an intention like the intention of the Messenger." He said:
"Did you bring a sacrificial animal with you?"
I said, "I did not bring one." He said:
"Then circumambulate the House, walk between Ṣafā and Marwah, and then come out of ihrām."
I did so, until a woman of the women of Banū Qays combed my hair.
We remained so until ʿUmar became caliph.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib sent from Yemen to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a small piece of gold in a tanned leather pouch, from which its soil had not yet been separated. He said: He divided it among four men: ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn, al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, Zayd al-Khayl, and the fourth was either ʿAlqamah ibn ʿUlāthah or ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl. A man among his Companions said, "We were more deserving of this than these." He said: That reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Will you not trust me, when I am trusted by the One in the heaven? News of the heaven comes to me morning and evening."

He said: Then a man with sunken eyes, prominent cheekbones, a protruding forehead, a thick beard, and a shaven head, with his garment hitched up, stood and said, "O Messenger of Allah, fear Allah!" He said:
"Woe to you! Am I not the most deserving of the people of the earth to fear Allah?"
He said: Then the man turned away, and Khālid ibn al-Walīd said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not strike his neck?" He said:
"No. Perhaps he prays."
Khālid said, "How many a person who prays says with his tongue what is not in his heart!"
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have not been commanded to search the hearts of people or to cut open their bellies."
He said: Then he looked at him as he was turning away and said:

"From the offspring of this man will come a people who recite the Book of Allah smoothly, but it does not pass beyond their throats. They pass through the religion as the arrow passes through the game. If I reach them, I will surely kill them as Thamūd were killed." He said: I think he said this.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people of Kūfah complained about Saʿd to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, so he dismissed him and appointed ʿAmmār over them.
They complained until they even said that he did not pray well.

So [ʿUmar] sent for him and said, "O Abū Isḥāq, these people claim that you do not pray well." Abū Isḥāq said, "As for me, by Allah, I used to lead them in the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, not falling short of it in anything.
I would pray the ʿIshāʾ prayer, lengthening the first two rakʿahs and shortening the last two."
He said, "That is what I thought of you, O Abū Isḥāq."
Then he sent with him a man, or men, to Kūfah,
and they asked the people of Kūfah about him.
They did not leave a mosque without asking about him, and the people spoke well of him,
until he entered a mosque of the Banū ʿAbs.
A man from among them stood up, called Usāmah ibn Qatādah, whose kunyah was Abū Saʿdah, and said, "Since you have adjured us: Saʿd would not march out with the expeditionary force,
he would not divide [the spoils] equally,
and he would not be just in judgment."
Saʿd said, "By Allah, I will make three supplications:
O Allah, if this servant of Yours is lying,
and stood up out of showing off and seeking reputation, then lengthen his life, prolong his poverty, and expose him to trials."
Afterwards, when he was asked, he would say, "An old man, tried by trials,
the supplication of Saʿd has struck me."
ʿAbd al-Malik said, "I saw him afterwards, his eyebrows drooping over his eyes from old age,
and he would accost girls in the roads and pinch them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite in the first two rakʿahs of Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr the Opening of the Book and a sūrah, and sometimes he would let us hear a verse, and in the last two rakʿahs he would recite the Opening of the Book.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite Sūrat al-Ṭūr in the Maghrib prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Ibn ʿAbbās], may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not recite to the jinn, nor did he see them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with a group of his Companions heading for the market of ʿUkāẓ. By then the devils had been barred from the news of the heavens and shooting stars had been sent against them. So the devils returned to their people, who asked, "What is wrong with you?" They said, "We have been barred from the news of the heavens and shooting stars have been sent against us."

They said, "Nothing has come between us and the news of the heavens except something that has happened. So travel through the east and west of the earth and see what it is that has come between you and the news of the heavens." He said: So they set out, travelling through the east and west of the earth, seeking what had come between them and the news of the heavens. Those of them who headed toward Tihāmah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at Nakhlah, heading for the market of ʿUkāẓ, leading his Companions in the Fajr prayer. When they heard the Qurʾān, they listened to it and said, "By Allah, this is what has come between you and the news of the heavens."
He said: Then they returned to their people and said, "O our people,
'We have heard a wondrous Qurʾān, which guides to the right path, so we believe in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.'" Then Allah revealed to His Prophet:
"Say: It has been revealed to me that a group [of jinn] listened." What was revealed to him was only the speech of the jinn.
He said, and by this chain from Ibn ʿAbbās,

he said regarding the saying of the jinn to their people, "When the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they almost became about him a compacted mass": When they saw him praying, with his Companions praying behind him, prostrating as he prostrated, they marvelled at his Companions' obedience to him, and said to their people:
"When the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they almost became about him a compacted mass."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to Ibn Masʿūd and said, "I recited the entire Mufaṣṣal last night in one rakʿah."

ʿAbdullāh said, "That is like the hurried reciting of poetry. I know the pairs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to join together." He said: Then he mentioned twenty sūrahs of the Mufaṣṣal, two sūrahs in each rakʿah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When one of you says 'Āmīn' in prayer,
and the angels in the heavens say 'Āmīn,'
and one coincides with the other, his previous sins are forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
that Abū Hurayrah
used to lead them in prayer and would say the takbīr whenever he lowered and raised [himself]. When he finished, he said, "By Allah, I am the most like you in prayer to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—his bowing, his prostration, his standing after raising his head from bowing, and his sitting between the two prostrations—was nearly equal [in length].
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was,
[and] there was among Banū ʿIjl, from Bukayr ibn Shihāb,
from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: The Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Abū al-Qāsim, tell us about thunder, what is it?" He said,
"It is one of the angels, put in charge of the clouds. He has with him whips of fire with which he drives the clouds wherever Allah wills."
They said, "Then what is this sound that we hear?" He said,
"It is his rebuke of the clouds when he rebukes them, until they reach the place where he is commanded [to take them]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ regarding the saying of Allah:
"And We make some of them better than others in food," he said:
"[Such as] the daqal [inferior dates], the Persian [dates], the sweet and the sour."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith. Zayd ibn Abī Unaysah has narrated it from al-Aʿmash in a similar form.
Sayf ibn Muḥammad is the brother of ʿAmmār ibn Muḥammad, and ʿAmmār is more reliable than him; he is the son of the sister of Sufyān al-Thawrī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a tray on which were fresh dates, and he said:

"The likeness of a good word is that of a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branches are in the sky, bearing its fruit at all times by the permission of its Lord." He said, "It is the palm tree."
"And the likeness of a bad word is that of a bad tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability." He said, "It is the colocynth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hell has seven gates. One of them is for whoever draws the sword against my Ummah," or he said, "against the Ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ regarding the saying of Allah:
"So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do," he said:
"About the saying: There is no god but Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Beware of the discernment of the believer, for he sees with the light of Allah." Then he recited:
"Indeed in that are signs for those who discern."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Four [units of prayer] before Ẓuhr, after the sun passes its zenith, are counted as equal to the like of them in the prayer before dawn."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is nothing except that it glorifies Allah at that hour." Then he recited:
"Its shadows incline to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah," the entire verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Uḥud, sixty-four men of the Anṣār and six of the Muhājirūn, among them Ḥamzah, were killed, and [the enemy] mutilated them. The Anṣār said, "If we ever get the better of them on a day like this, we will surpass them." He said: When it was the day of the conquest of Makkah, Allah revealed: "And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the equivalent of what you were afflicted with; but if you are patient, it is better for the patient." A man said, "There will be no [harm to] Quraysh after today." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Hold back from the people, except four."
He said: This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith from the narration of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the night he was taken on the Night Journey, the Prophet ﷺ was brought al-Burāq, bridled and saddled, but it was unruly toward him. Jibrīl said to it, "Do you do this to Muḥammad? No one more honored in the sight of Allah than he has ever ridden you." He said: "So it broke out in sweat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When we reached Bayt al-Maqdis, Jibrīl pointed with his finger, pierced the rock with it, and tied al-Burāq to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ regarding the saying of Allah:
"And the recitation of the dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the dawn is witnessed," he said:
"The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
ʿAlī ibn Mushir narrated from al-Aʿmash,
from Abū Ṣāliḥ,
from Abū Hurayrah and Abū
Saʿīd, from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ regarding the saying of Allah:
"On the Day We will call every people with their leader," he said:

"One of them will be called and given his record in his right hand. His body will be extended sixty cubits, his face will be whitened, and a crown of shining pearl will be placed on his head. He will go to his companions, and they will see him from afar and say, 'O Allah, bring us this one and bless us in this one,' until he comes to them. Then he will say, 'Rejoice, for each man among you will have the like of this.'

He said: As for the disbeliever, his face will be blackened and his body extended sixty cubits in the form of Adam, and he will be made to wear a crown. His companions will see him and say, 'We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this one. O Allah, do not bring us this one.'
He said: Then he will come to them and they will say, 'O Allah, disgrace him.'
He will say, 'May Allah keep you far away, for each man among you will have the like of this.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: They asked Sahl ibn Saʿd what the pulpit was made of. He said, "No one is left among the people who knows better than I do. It was from tamarisk wood of the forest,
made for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by so-and-so, the freed slave of so-and-so.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood upon it when it was made and set in place,
and he faced the qiblah and said the takbīr, while the people stood behind him.
He recited and bowed, and the people bowed behind him.
Then he raised his head,
then he stepped backwards,
and prostrated on the ground.
Then he returned to the pulpit,
then he recited and then bowed,
then he raised his head,
then he stepped backwards until he prostrated on the ground. This was how he did it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
And ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdillāh said: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, saying: Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Maymūn ibn Siyāh asked Anas ibn Mālik, saying, "O Abū Ḥamzah,

what makes a person's blood and property inviolable?" He said, "Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, faces our qiblah, prays our prayer, and eats our slaughtered animals, then he is a Muslim;
he has what the Muslim has,
and he is bound by what binds the Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, was approached at his home and told, "This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he has entered the Kaʿbah." He said: I went and found that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had already come out,
and I found Bilāl standing at the door. I said, "O Bilāl,
did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray in the Kaʿbah?" He said, "Yes."
I said, "Where?" He said, "Between these two pillars."
Then he came out and prayed two rakʿahs facing the front of the Kaʿbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you prays, he should not spit in front of him or to his right, but rather to his left or beneath his foot; otherwise..."
Then the Prophet ﷺ spat like this into his garment and rubbed it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you see my qiblah here? By Allah, neither your humility nor your bowing is hidden from me.
I truly see you from behind my back."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he remembered the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
and remembered a mouthful of water that he spat in his face from a well that was in their house.

Maḥmūd claimed that he heard ʿItbān ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī, may Allah be pleased with him, who was among those who witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: I used to lead my people, Banū Sālim, in prayer,
but a valley would come between me and them when the rains came, and it was difficult for me to cross it to reach their mosque.
So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said to him, "My eyesight has become weak,
and the valley between me and my people flows when the rains come, and it is difficult for me to cross it.
I would love for you to come and pray in my house at a place that I could take as a place of prayer."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "I will do so."

The next morning, after the day had grown hot, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came to me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked permission to enter, and I gave him permission. He did not sit until he said,
"Where would you like me to pray in your house?"
I pointed to the place where I wished him to pray.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and said the takbīr, and we lined up behind him, and he prayed two rakʿahs,
then gave the salām, and we gave the salām when he did.

I kept him back for some khazīr that was being prepared for him. The people of the neighborhood heard that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in my house, so men gathered from among them until the house was full of men.
One of them said, "What has Mālik done? I do not see him."
Another of them said, "That is a hypocrite who does not love Allah and His Messenger."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Do not say that. Do you not see that he has said, 'There is no god but Allah,'
seeking by it the Face of Allah?"
He said, "Allah and His Messenger know best.
As for us, by Allah, we see his affection and his conversation only directed toward the hypocrites."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Indeed, Allah has forbidden the Fire to whoever says, 'There is no god but Allah,'
seeking by it the Face of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim ibn ʿAbdillāh [reported] that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: We passed by al-Ḥijr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us,
"Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, unless you are weeping, out of fear that what struck them may strike you."
Then he urged his mount on and hurried until he had left it behind.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I and ʿUmar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found him taking his midday rest, so we returned to the lodging.
Then ʿUmar sent me and said, "Go and see whether he has woken up." So I came to him,
and I went in to him and gave him the pledge of allegiance.
Then I went to ʿUmar
and told him that he had woken up,
so we went to him hurrying at a quick pace, until he went in to him and pledged allegiance, and then I pledged allegiance.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr bought a saddle from ʿĀzib, and I carried it with him. ʿĀzib asked him about the journey of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Watches were set against us, so we went out at night,
and we pressed on through our night and our day until the time of noon stood still,
then a rock appeared to us,
and we came to it, and it had some shade. He said: I spread a fur I had with me for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,
then the Prophet ﷺ lay down on it, and I went off to look over the surroundings,
and suddenly I came upon a shepherd who had come with a small flock, wanting from the rock what we had wanted. I asked him, "Whose man are you, boy?" He said, "I belong to so-and-so."
I said to him, "Is there any milk among your sheep?" He said, "Yes."
I said to him, "Will you milk?" He said, "Yes."
So he took a sheep from his flock and I said to him, "Clean the udder."
He said: Then he milked a small amount of milk,
and I had with me a water-skin with a cloth over it, which I had prepared for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I poured [water] over the milk until its bottom became cool,
then I brought it to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Drink, O Messenger of Allah."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank until I was satisfied,
then we set out, with the pursuit behind us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The servant of the Prophet ﷺ said: The Prophet ﷺ came [to Madinah], and none of his Companions had graying hair except Abū Bakr,
so he covered it with henna and katam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, married a woman from Kalb called Umm Bakr,
and when Abū Bakr emigrated, he divorced her,
and her cousin married her,
this being the poet who said this poem,
lamenting the disbelievers of Quraysh: "And what is in the well, the well of Badr, of the bowls of fine wood adorned with camel humps? And what is in the well,

the well of Badr, of singing girls and noble drinking companions? Umm Bakr is greeted with peace; but is there any peace for me after my people? The Messenger tells us that we shall live again, but how can there be life for echoes of the dead and skulls?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: No one will enter Paradise who has an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart, and no one will enter the Fire"—meaning, one who has an atom's weight of faith in his heart."
A man said to him: "I like my clothes to be nice and my sandals to be nice." He said: "
Indeed Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. But arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Abū Mūsā while he was gravely ill, and his wife went to weep or to grieve over him. Abū Mūsā said to her: "Did you not hear what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said?" She said: "Yes."

He said: She fell silent. When Abū Mūsā died—Yazīd said—I met the woman and said to her: "What did Abū Mūsā mean when he said to you, 'Did you not hear what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said?' and then fell silent?" She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
He is not one of us who shaves his head, raises his voice in wailing, or tears his garments [in mourning]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Purification is half of faith, and "Al-ḥamdu lillāh" fills the scale.

And "Subḥān Allāh" and "Al-ḥamdu lillāh" fill—or it fills—what is between the heavens and the earth. Prayer is light, charity is proof, patience is illumination, and the Qur'an is an argument for you or against you. Every person goes out in the morning and sells himself, either freeing it or destroying it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah and Ibn
Ḥujr, all from Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar,
Ibn Ayyūb said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us: ʿAlāʾ informed me, from his father,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Shall I not tell you of that by which Allah erases sins and raises degrees?"
They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "
Performing ablution thoroughly despite difficulties, taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the next prayer after a prayer. That is ribāṭ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "Tell me, with what
did the Prophet ﷺ begin when he entered upon you?" She said: "When he entered, he would begin with the siwāk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked ʿĀʾishah: "May a woman eat with her husband while she is menstruating?" She said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would call me and I would eat with him while I was menstruating. He would take a bone with meat on it and insist that I take a bite from it, so I would gnaw on it and put it down; then he would take it and gnaw on it, placing his mouth where I had placed my mouth on the bone. And he would ask for a drink and insist that I drink from it before he drank; so I would take it and drink from it and put it down, then he would take it and drink from it, placing his mouth where I had placed my mouth on the cup."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Jews,

when a woman among them menstruated, would put her out of the house and would not eat with her, drink with her, or sleep with her in the house. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about that, and Allah the Exalted revealed: {They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is harm, so keep away from women during menstruation} to the end of the verse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Stay with them in the houses and do everything except intercourse."
The Jews said: "This man does not want to leave anything of our affairs without opposing us in it."

Then Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and ʿAbbād ibn Bishr came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews say such and such. Should we not have intercourse with them during menstruation?" The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed color so much that we thought he was angry with them. They left, and a gift of milk for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ met them; he sent after them and gave them a drink, so we knew that he was not angry with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUrwah said, from ʿĀʾishah:
that Umm Sulaym al-Anṣārīyah,

who is the mother of Anas ibn Mālik, said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah the Mighty and Majestic is not shy of the truth. What do you say about a woman who sees in her sleep what a man sees; must she bathe or not?" ʿĀʾishah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "
Yes, she must bathe if she finds water."
ʿĀʾishah said: I turned to her and said: "Shame on you! Does a woman see that?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to me and said: "
May your right hand be covered in dust, O ʿĀʾishah! How else would the child resemble [its mother]?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: They disputed about the bath in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Some of the people said: "As for me, I wash my head such and such way." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
As for me, I pour three handfuls of water over my head."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The stepson of the Prophet ﷺ said: When this verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ,

"Allah only intends to remove from you impurity, O members of the [Prophet's] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification" [al-Aḥzāb 33:33], in the house of Umm Salamah, he called Fāṭimah, Ḥasan and Ḥusayn and covered them with a cloak, while ʿAlī was behind his back, and he covered him with a cloak too. Then he said:
"O Allah, these are the members of my household, so remove impurity from them and purify them with [extensive] purification."
Umm Salamah said: And am I with them, O Prophet of Allah? He said:
"You are in your place, and you are on [a path of] goodness."
He said: This hadith is gharīb from this route, from the hadith of ʿAṭāʾ from ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pass by the door of Fāṭimah for six months whenever he went out to the dawn prayer, saying:
"Prayer, O members of the household!"
"Allah only intends to remove from you impurity, O members of the [Prophet's] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb from this route; we know it only from the hadith of Ḥammād ibn Salamah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her, she said: Had the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concealed anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse:
"And [remember] when you said to the one upon whom Allah bestowed favor" meaning with Islam,
"and you bestowed favor upon him" with emancipation, for you freed him,

"Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you should fear Him" up to His saying:
"And the command of Allah is always executed." And when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her, they said: He married the wife of his son. So Allah the Exalted revealed:

"Muḥammad is not the father of any of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had adopted him when he was young, and he remained so until he became a man, and he was called Zayd ibn Muḥammad. So Allah revealed:

"Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your freed slaves"; so-and-so is the freed slave of so-and-so, and so-and-so is the brother of so-and-so. "That is more just in the sight of Allah," meaning more equitable with Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
"Muḥammad is not the father of any of your men," he said: No male child of his was to live among you.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I see that everything is for the men, and I do not see women being mentioned in anything. Then this verse was revealed:
"Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women..." [al-Aḥzāb 33:35], the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: This verse was revealed about Zaynab bint Jaḥsh:

"So when Zayd had concluded his need of her, We married her to you" [al-Aḥzāb 33:37]. He said: She used to boast over the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, saying: Your families married you off, while Allah married me off from above the seven heavens.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to me, and I made my excuses to him, and he accepted my excuse. Then Allah the Exalted revealed:

"Indeed, We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation, and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you [of captives], and the daughters of your paternal uncle, the daughters of your paternal aunts, the daughters of your maternal uncle, and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet" [al-Aḥzāb 33:50], the verse. She said: So I was not lawful for him, because I had not emigrated; I was one of those set free [at the conquest of Makkah].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was forbidden [to marry] all categories of women except believing women who had emigrated. He said:

"No [other] women are lawful for you after this, nor [is it permissible] to exchange them for [other] wives, even if their beauty were to please you, except those your right hand possesses."
