So Allah made lawful your believing young women, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet, and He forbade every woman of a religion other than Islam. Then He said:
"And whoever disbelieves in faith, his work has become worthless, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers." And He said:
"O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation, and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you" up to His saying:
"This is exclusively for you, excluding the [rest of the] believers." And He forbade all other categories of women besides that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when he came to the door of a woman he had just married, and there were people with her. He went off and attended to his need, and was delayed, then he returned and there were still people with her. He went off again and attended to his need, then returned, and they had left. He said: So he entered and drew a curtain between me and him. He said: I mentioned it to Abū Ṭalḥah, and he said: If it is as you say, something will surely be revealed about this.
Then the verse of the ḥijāb was revealed.
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Among them was one of the Companions of the Tree, named Uhbān ibn Aws, who suffered from his knee,
and when he prostrated he would place a cushion under his knee.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with him, who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, of the Companions of the Tree: "Can the witr prayer be broken?" He said: "If you prayed witr at the beginning of the night,
then do not pray witr again at the end of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He entered the state of iḥrām for ʿUmrah and said: "If I am prevented from reaching it, I will do as the Prophet ﷺ did when the disbelievers of Quraysh stood between him and it."
And he recited: {Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh
and Sālim ibn ʿAbdillāh informed him that they
spoke to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar
label: machine translation

segments_en: People say that Ibn ʿUmar
accepted Islam before ʿUmar, but that is not so.
Rather, on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah ʿUmar sent ʿAbdullāh to fetch a horse of his that was with a man of the Anṣār, so that he could fight on it,
while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking pledges at the tree,
and ʿUmar did not know of that.
So ʿAbdullāh gave his pledge,
then went to the horse
and brought it to ʿUmar,
while ʿUmar was putting on his armor for battle.
He told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking pledges under the tree. He said: "Let us go," and he went with him until he gave his pledge to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
That is what people mean when they say that Ibn ʿUmar accepted Islam before ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people
were with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah,
and had dispersed into the shade of the trees.
Then, suddenly, the people were crowded around the Prophet ﷺ. ʿUmar said: "O ʿAbdullāh,
go and see what is the matter with the people, that they have crowded around the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He found them giving the pledge,
so he gave the pledge, then returned to ʿUmar, who came out and gave the pledge.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We witnessed Ḥunayn with the Prophet ﷺ.
Ibn al-Mubārak said, from Yūnus, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raided Khaybar, or he said: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out toward it, the people climbed up to overlook a valley,
and raised their voices with takbīr: "Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest,
there is no god but Allah."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Be gentle with yourselves.
You are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent.
You are calling upon One who is All-Hearing and near, and He is with you."
I was behind the riding animal of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he heard me saying: "There is no power and no strength except with Allah." He said to me:
"O ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays."
I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Shall I not guide you to a phrase that is one of the treasures of Paradise?"
I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom." He said:
"There is no power and no strength except with Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas looked at the people on the day of Friday,
and saw shawls, and said: "They look just like the Jews of Khaybar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade, on the day of Khaybar, the eating of garlic
and the meat of domestic donkeys.
The prohibition of eating garlic is from Nāfiʿ alone,
and the meat of domestic donkeys is from Sālim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was nothing in this world that made them happier, or was greater in their eyes, than what the Prophet ﷺ said to them.
Abū Burdah said: Asmāʾ said: "I saw Abū Mūsā asking me to repeat this hadith to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to the Prophet ﷺ after he had conquered Khaybar, and he gave us a share,
and he gave a share to no one who had not witnessed the conquest other than us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Khaybar was conquered, we said: "Now we will eat our fill of dates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were not satisfied with food until we conquered Khaybar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent a man of Banū ʿAdī of the Anṣār to Khaybar and appointed him governor over it.
And from ʿAbd al-Majīd, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān, from Abū Hurayrah and Abū Saʿīd, the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ʿUmrah, we shielded him from the boys of the polytheists and from them,
lest they harm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ married Maymūnah while he was in iḥrām,
and consummated the marriage when he was out of iḥrām, and she died at Sarif.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ married Maymūnah during the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
stood over Jaʿfar that day as he lay slain,
and I counted fifty wounds on him, stabs and blows,
none of them in his back.
Meaning, in his back.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The Azd are the lions of Allah on earth. People want to bring them down, but Allah refuses except to raise them up. And a time will come upon the people when a man will say: 'If only my father had been from the Azd! If only my mother had been from the Azd!'"
This hadith is gharīb; we do not know it except through this route.
This hadith was also narrated from Anas with this chain as his own statement (mawqūf), and that is more correct according to us.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If we are not from the Azd, then we are not from among the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ when a man came, whom I think was from Qays, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, curse Ḥimyar!"
He turned away from him. Then the man came from the other side, and he turned away from him again. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"May Allah have mercy on Ḥimyar: their mouths [offer] peace, their hands [offer] food, and they are people of security and faith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, the arrows of Thaqīf have burned us, so invoke Allah against them." He said:
"O Allah, guide Thaqīf."
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ died while disliking three tribes: Thaqīf, Banū Ḥanīfah, and Banū Umayyah.
This hadith is gharīb; we do not know it except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What an excellent tribe are the Asad and the Ashʿarīs: they do not flee in battle and they do not steal from the spoils. They are from me, and I am from them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, compiling the Qur'an from scraps, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Blessed is al-Shām."
We said: "For what reason, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Because the angels of the Most Merciful spread their wings over it."
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb; we only know it from the narration of Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the Jāhiliyyah and its boasting about forefathers. [A person is either] a God-fearing believer or a wretched sinner. People are the children of Adam, and Adam was from dust."
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
And this is more correct according to us than the first hadith.
Saʿīd al-Maqburī heard from Abū Hurayrah, and he narrates many things from his father from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.
Sufyān al-Thawrī and more than one other narrated this hadith from Hishām ibn Saʿd, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, like the hadith of Abū ʿĀmir from Hishām ibn Saʿd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went to relieve himself, he would go far away. He said: He went to relieve himself, during one of his journeys, and said: "Bring me water for ablution."
So I brought him water for ablution, and he performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks.
The Shaykh Ismāʿīl said: He is Ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Kathīr al-Qārī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They say that the Prophet ﷺ made a bequest to ʿAlī. Yet he called for a basin to urinate in, and he slumped, and I did not realize [he had died]. So to whom would he have made a bequest? The Shaykh Azhar said: He is Ibn Saʿd al-Sammān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade any of you from cleaning himself with a bone or dung.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When you clean yourself with stones, do so an odd number of times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when he went to the toilet and relieved himself, then said:
"O Jarīr, bring me water for purification."
So I brought him water, and he cleaned himself with water, and he made a gesture with his hand, rubbing the ground with it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin urinated in the mosque, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered a bucket of water, and it was poured over it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the mosque and urinated, and the people shouted at him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Leave him."
So they left him until he finished urinating. Then he ordered a bucket [of water], and it was poured over it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
– and the wording is his – from Ibn Wahb, from Mālik, and Yūnus,
and ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith,
that Ibn Shihāb
informed them from ʿAbbād ibn Ziyād,
from ʿUrwah ibn al-Mughīrah,
that he heard his father
say: I poured water for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he performed ablution during the expedition of Tabūk, and he wiped over his leather socks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution, washing each part once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When these two garrison cities [Kūfah and Baṣrah] were conquered, the people came to ʿUmar and said, "O Commander of the Faithful,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set Qarn as the, designated place for the people of Najd,
but it lies off our route,
and if we want to go to Qarn, it is difficult for us."
He said, "Then look for a place opposite it on your route."
So he designated Dhāt ʿIrq for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying the talbiyah while in ihrām, with his hair matted.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Usāmah ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them both) rode behind the Prophet ﷺ from ʿArafah to Muzdalifah,
then al-Faḍl rode behind him from Muzdalifah to Minā. He said: Both of them said, "The Prophet ﷺ did not cease reciting the talbiyah until he threw the pebbles at Jamrat al-ʿAqabah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ set out from Madinah,
after he had combed his hair, anointed himself with oil, and put on his lower garment and his upper garment, he and his Companions.
He did not forbid any of the upper garments or lower garments that are worn, except those dyed with saffron that leave a stain on the skin.
He spent the morning at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah,
[then] he mounted his riding animal until it stood upright with him on al-Baydāʾ,
and he and his Companions raised the voice in talbiyah, and he garlanded his sacrificial camel,
and that was five nights before the end of Dhū al-Qaʿdah.
He arrived in Makkah on the fourth night of Dhū al-Ḥijjah,
and he circumambulated the House and walked between Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah,
but he did not leave the state of ihrām because of his sacrificial camel, since he had garlanded it.
Then he camped at the upper part of Makkah near al-Ḥajūn,
while in the state of ihrām for Hajj,
and he did not go near the Kaʿbah after circumambulating it until he returned from ʿArafah,
and he commanded his Companions to circumambulate the House and walk between Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah,
then to shorten their hair and leave the state of ihrām,
and that was for whoever did not have a sacrificial camel with him that he had garlanded,
and whoever had his wife with him, she was lawful for him, as were perfume and clothing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) had prayed the morning prayer at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he would order his riding animal to be saddled, and then he would mount.
When it stood upright with him, he would face the qiblah standing,
then recite the talbiyah until he reached the sacred boundary,
then he would stop, until he came to Dhū Ṭuwā, where he would spend the night until morning.
When he had prayed the morning prayer, he would take a bath,
and he claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) intended to set out for Makkah, he would anoint himself with an oil that had no fragrant scent,
then he would come to the mosque at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, pray, and then mount.
When his riding animal stood upright with him, he would enter the state of ihrām.
Then he said, "This is how I saw the Prophet ﷺ do it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ [reported that] Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Prophet ﷺ commanded ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) to remain in his state of ihrām,
and he mentioned the statement of Surāqah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at al-Baṭḥāʾ. He said, "Have you entered ihrām for Hajj?" I said, "Yes." He said, "With what intention did you enter ihrām?"
I said, "Labbayk, with an intention like the intention of the Prophet ﷺ." He said, "You have done well.
Go, circumambulate the House and walk between Aṣ-Ṣafā and Al-Marwah."
Then I came to a woman of the Banū Qays, and she combed the lice from my head.
Then I entered ihrām for Hajj,
and I used to give people a ruling according to that,
until the caliphate of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), and I mentioned it to him.
He said, "If we follow the Book of Allah, it commands us to complete [the Hajj and ʿUmrah],
and if we follow the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not leave the state of ihrām until the sacrificial animal reached its place of slaughter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he commanded me to leave the state of ihrām.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān said: Ibn Shihāb said, "But ʿUrwah narrates from Ḥumrān,
that when ʿUthmān performed ablution he said: Shall I not tell you a hadith that I would not have told you were it not for a verse?
I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
'No man performs ablution and does it well,
and then prays the prayer, except that he will be forgiven what is between that and the [next] prayer, until he prays it.'"
ʿUrwah said: The verse is: {Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs...}
label: machine translation

segments_en: [I] read it to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, on the authority of Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd,
from Bashīr ibn Yasār,
the freed slave of Banū Ḥārithah, that Suwayd ibn al-Nuʿmān informed him that

he went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of Khaybar. When they reached al-Ṣahbāʾ, which is near Khaybar, he prayed the ʿAṣr prayer, then called for the provisions, but nothing was brought except barley meal. He ordered that it be moistened, and he ate and we ate. Then he got up for the Maghrib prayer, rinsed his mouth, and we rinsed our mouths, then he prayed and did not perform ablution.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that she used to wash semen from the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She said: Then I would see a spot or spots in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah bint Shaybah, from ʿĀʾishah, that a woman
asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: O Messenger of Allah, how should I wash after purification? He said:
"Take a piece of cotton scented with musk and purify yourself with it."
She said: How should I purify myself with it? He said, "Purify yourself with it."

She said: How should I purify myself with it? [ʿĀʾishah] said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ exclaimed "Subḥān Allāh" and turned away from her. ʿĀʾishah understood what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ meant, so she took her and pulled her toward me, and told her what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ meant.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr, from his father,
from ʿAmrah bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah,
that she said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: O Messenger of Allah, Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy has begun her menses.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Perhaps she will detain us. Did she not perform the circumambulation of the House with you?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Then depart."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ on a journey of his. We traveled through the night, until, near the break of dawn, we stopped to rest, and sleep overcame us until the sun had risen. He said: The first of us to wake was Abū Bakr, and we would not wake the Prophet of Allah ﷺ from his sleep when he slept, until he woke by himself. Then ʿUmar woke up and stood by the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and began saying "Allahu akbar" and raising his voice with the takbīr until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke. When he raised his head and saw that the sun had risen, he said: "Move on."

He traveled with us until the sun grew bright, then he dismounted and led us in the morning prayer. A man from the people withdrew and did not pray with us. When he finished, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"O so-and-so, what prevented you from praying with us?"
He said: O Prophet of Allah, I am in a state of major ritual impurity.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him, and he performed tayammum with clean earth and prayed. Then he sent me ahead of him with a party of riders to look for water, for we were extremely thirsty.
While we were traveling, we came upon a woman dangling her legs between two water-skins. We said to her: Where is the water? She said: Alas, alas! There is no water for you.
We said: How far is it between your family and the water?
She said: A day and a night's journey.
We said: Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

She said: What is the Messenger of Allah? We did not let her have any say in the matter, until we took her and brought her before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He asked her, and she told him the same as she had told us, and she told him that she was a widow with orphaned children. He ordered her water-skin brought and made to kneel, and he spat into the two upper mouths of the water-skins. Then her water-skins were sent back, and we drank, forty thirsty men, until we were satisfied. We filled every waterskin and container we had, and washed our companion, though we did not water a camel; and the two water-skins were almost bursting with water. Then he said:
"Bring what you have."
So we gathered for her some pieces of bread and dates, and tied them up in a bundle for her. He said to her:
"Go and feed this to your children, and know that we have not diminished your water."
When she came to her people, she said: I have met either the greatest sorcerer of mankind, or else he is a prophet, as they claim. Such and such happened with him.
So Allah guided that settlement through that woman; she accepted Islam and they accepted Islam.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and Marwān,
each of them confirming the account of his companion, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out at the time of al-Ḥudaybiyah,
until, when they were part of the way along the road, the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Khālid ibn al-Walīd is at al-Ghamīm with a cavalry detachment of Quraysh serving as a vanguard, so take the right-hand road."
By Allah, Khālid did not notice them until he saw the dust of the army,
so he went off galloping to warn Quraysh.
The Prophet ﷺ kept going until, when he reached the mountain pass by which one descends upon them,
his mount knelt down with him.
The people said: "Ḥal, ḥal!" [urging her on], but she persisted in refusing,
so they said: "Al-Qaṣwāʾ has become stubborn! Al-Qaṣwāʾ has become stubborn!" The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Al-Qaṣwāʾ has not become stubborn,
and that is not her nature,
but she was held back by the One who held back the elephant."
Then he said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me for any plan in which they honor the sanctities of Allah, except that I will grant it to them."
Then he urged her on, and she sprang up.
He said: So he turned away from them until he camped at the farthest point of al-Ḥudaybiyah,
at a pool with little water, which the people drew from only in small amounts.
The people did not stay long before they had drained it,
and they complained of thirst to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
So he took an arrow from his quiver,
then ordered them to put it into the pool.
By Allah, water kept welling up for them in abundance until they all left it satisfied.
While they were in that state,
Budayl ibn Warqāʾ al-Khuzāʿī came with some men of his people from Khuzāʿah,
and they were the trusted confidants of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among the people of Tihāmah.
He said: "I left Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy and ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy camped at the abundant waters of al-Ḥudaybiyah,
with them are milch camels with their young,
and they will fight you and bar you from the House."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We have not come to fight anyone,
but we have come to perform ʿUmrah,
and war has exhausted Quraysh and harmed them.
If they wish, I will agree a truce with them for a period,
and they are to leave me free to deal with the people.
If I prevail, then if they wish to enter into what the people have entered, they may do so,
and if not, they will at least have rested.
And if they refuse, then by the One in whose hand is my soul,
I will fight them over this matter of mine until my neck is severed,
and Allah will certainly carry out His command."
Budayl said: "I will convey to them what you say."
He said: So he went until he came to Quraysh and said: "We have come to you from this man,
and we heard him say something,
and if you wish, we will present it to you."
Their foolish ones said: "We have no need for you to tell us anything from him."
And those of sound judgment among them said: "Tell us what you heard him say."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to test them [the women].
And it has reached us that when Allah the Exalted revealed that they should return to the polytheists what they had spent on their wives who emigrated,
and ruled for the Muslims
that they should not hold on to the ties of disbelieving women,
ʿUmar divorced two wives: Quraybah daughter of Abū Umayyah,
and the daughter of Jarwal al-Khuzāʿī.
Muʿāwiyah then married Quraybah,
and Abū Jahm married the other.
When the disbelievers refused to acknowledge paying what the Muslims had spent on their wives,
Allah the Exalted revealed: {And if any of your wives is lost to the disbelievers and you have your turn [of gain]}. The ʿaqb is what the Muslims pay to the disbeliever whose wife has emigrated.
So he ordered that whoever lost a wife among the Muslims be given what he had spent as the dowers of the disbelieving women who emigrated.
And we do not know of any of the women emigrants who apostatized after her belief.
And it has reached us that Abū Baṣīr ibn Asīd al-Thaqafī came to the Prophet ﷺ as a believer and emigrant during the truce period,
and al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq wrote to the Prophet ﷺ asking him for Abū Baṣīr, and he mentioned the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The property used to go to the children,
and the bequest was for the parents,
then Allah abrogated from that what He willed,
and made for the male the share of two females,
and made for the parents, for each of them, a sixth or a third,
and made for the wife an eighth or a fourth,
and for the husband a half or a fourth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to Abū Ṭalḥah:
"I think you should give it to your closest relatives."
Abū Ṭalḥah said: "I will do so, O Messenger of Allah."
So Abū Ṭalḥah divided it among his relatives and his cousins.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: When {And warn your closest kinsmen} was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ began calling out:
"O Banū Fihr,
O Banū ʿAdī!" — to the clans of Quraysh.
And Abū Hurayrah said: When {And warn your closest kinsmen} was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said:
"O company of Quraysh!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people claim that this verse has been abrogated,
but no, by Allah, it has not been abrogated,
rather it is among those matters that people have treated lightly.
There are two kinds of guardians: a guardian who inherits,
and he is the one who should provide for them,
and a guardian who does not inherit,
and he is the one who should speak kindly,
saying: "I do not own anything to give you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed women who frequently visit graves.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered a grave at night, and a lamp was lit for him. He took [the body] from the direction of the qiblah and said:
"May Allah have mercy on you. You were always turning to Allah in repentance and recited the Qur'an often."
And he pronounced the takbīr over him four times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever has two children who predeceased him from among my Ummah, Allah will admit him to Paradise because of them."
ʿĀʾishah said to him: "And what about one who has one child who predeceased him from your Ummah?" He said:
"And one who has one who predeceased him, O you who have been granted success."
She said: "And what about one from your Ummah who has no child who predeceased him?" He said:
"Then I am the forerunner of my Ummah; they will never suffer a loss like [losing] me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When the dead person is buried—or he said: when one of you is buried—two black, blue-eyed angels come to him. One is called al-Munkar and the other an-Nakīr. They say: 'What did you used to say about this man?' He says what he used to say: 'He is the servant of Allah and His Messenger. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.'
They say: 'We already knew that you would say this.'
Then his grave is widened for him seventy cubits by seventy, and it is illuminated for him. Then he is told: 'Sleep.'
He says: 'Let me return to my family and inform them.' They say: 'Sleep like the sleep of a bridegroom, whom no one wakes except the dearest of his family to him,'
until Allah resurrects him from that resting place of his.
But if he was a hypocrite, he says: 'I heard people saying something, so I said the same; I do not know.'
They say: 'We already knew that you would say that.'
Then the earth is told: 'Close in on him.' So it closes in on him,
and his ribs are crushed together within it. He continues to be punished in it until Allah resurrects him from that resting place of his."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No Muslim dies on the day of Friday or the night of Friday except that Allah protects him from the trial of the grave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever consoles a woman who has lost a child will be clothed in a garment in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pronounced the takbīr over a funeral, raised his hands at the first takbīr, and placed his right hand over his left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Four are among the practices of the Messengers: modesty, wearing perfume, using the siwāk, and marriage."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade celibacy [renouncing marriage].
label: machine translation

segments_en: Similar to this.
More than one person has narrated
this hadith from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from az-Zuhrī, from Anas,
and they did not mention in it "from Wāʾil, from his son."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Food on the first day is a duty, food on the second day is a sunnah, and food on the third day is for show; and whoever does something to be heard of, Allah will make him heard of [by exposing him]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man called Abū Shuʿayb came to a servant of his who was a butcher and said: "Prepare food for me sufficient for five, for I have seen hunger in the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

He said: So he prepared food, then sent for the Prophet ﷺ and invited him and his companions who were with him. When the Prophet ﷺ got up, a man who had not been with them when they were invited followed them. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached the door, he said to the owner of the house:
"A man has followed us who was not with us when you invited us. If you permit him, he may enter."
He said: "We have permitted him; let him enter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The adulteresses are those women who marry themselves without a witness."

Yūsuf ibn Ḥammād said: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā traced this hadith back to the Prophet in the Book of Tafsīr, but in the Book of Divorce he narrated it as a statement of the Companion and did not trace it back to the Prophet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Any man who marries a woman and consummates the marriage with her, it is not lawful for him to marry her daughter. If he has not consummated it with her, then he may marry her daughter. And any man who marries a woman, whether or not he has consummated the marriage with her, it is not lawful for him to marry her mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Temporary marriage (mutʿah) was only [permitted] at the beginning of Islam. A man would arrive in a town where he had no acquaintance, so he would marry a woman for the period he thought he would stay; she would look after his belongings and take care of his affairs, until the verse was revealed:
"Except from their wives or those whom their right hands possess." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "So every private part other than these two is forbidden."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade shighār [exchange marriage].
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, we used to practice withdrawal, and the Jews claim that it is the lesser infanticide." He said:
"The Jews have lied. If Allah wants to create it, nothing can prevent Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿUthmān was besieged, he looked down on them from above his house and said: "I ask you by Allah, do you know that when Ḥirāʾ shook, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Be still, Ḥirāʾ! There is upon you only a prophet, a ṣiddīq, or a martyr'?" They said: "Yes."
He said: "I ask you by Allah, do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding the army of hardship:
'Whoever spends an expenditure that will be accepted'
while the people were exhausted and in hardship, and I equipped that army?" They said: "Yes."

Then he said: "I ask you by Allah, do you know that no one could drink from the well of Rūmah except for a price, so I bought it and made it for the rich and the poor and the traveler?" They said: "O Allah, yes," and he listed other things as well.
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb from this route, from the hadith of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿUthmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is given the kunyah Abū Muḥammad,
a freedman of the family of ʿUthmān. He said: Al-Walīd ibn Abī Hishām narrated to us,
from Farqad Abū Ṭalḥah,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khabbāb,

who said: I was present with the Prophet ﷺ while he was urging [people to give] for the army of hardship. ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I will give one hundred camels with their saddle cloths and saddles in the cause of Allah."
Then he urged [them] again for the army, and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I will give two hundred camels with their saddle cloths and saddles in the cause of Allah."

Then he urged [them] again for the army, and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I owe it to Allah to give three hundred camels with their saddle cloths and saddles in the cause of Allah."
Then I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming down from the pulpit, saying:
"Nothing will harm ʿUthmān, whatever he does after this. Nothing will harm ʿUthmān, whatever he does after this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān came to the Prophet ﷺ with a thousand dīnārs—al-Ḥasan ibn Wāqiʿ said, and it was in another place in my book: in his sleeve—when he equipped the army of hardship, and he scattered them in his lap.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ turning them over in his lap and saying:
"Nothing will harm ʿUthmān, whatever he does after today." [He said it] twice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the Pledge of Riḍwān, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān was the envoy of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the people of Makkah. He said: The people pledged allegiance. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed ʿUthmān is occupied with the business of Allah and the business of His Messenger."
Then he struck one of his hands upon the other, and the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for ʿUthmān was better than their own hands for themselves.
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"O ʿUthmān, perhaps Allah will clothe you with a shirt. If they want you to take it off, do not take it off for them."
There is a long story in the hadith.
This hadith is ḥasan gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to say, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was alive: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān.
This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb from this route; it is considered gharīb from the hadith of ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿUmar.
This hadith has also been narrated through more than one route from Ibn ʿUmar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned a tribulation and said:
"This man will be killed unjustly during it." [He meant] ʿUthmān.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The funeral of a man was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for him to pray over, but he did not pray over him. It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have never seen you leave the prayer over anyone before this." He said:
"He used to hate ʿUthmān, so Allah hated him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān said to me on the day of the house: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a covenant with me, and I am patient upon it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever he visited a sick person or one was brought to him, would say:
"Remove the harm, O Lord of the people,
and heal, for You are the Healer; there is no healing except Your healing,
a healing that leaves no illness behind."
ʿAmr ibn Abī Qays and Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān reported from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm and Abū aḍ-Ḍuḥā: "when a sick person was brought to him,"
and Jarīr said, from Manṣūr, from Abū aḍ-Ḍuḥā alone,
and he said: "when he visited a sick person."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār, from Ibn
ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the muḥrim [one in ihrām] to wear a garment dyed with saffron or wars, and he said:
"Whoever cannot find sandals, let him wear leather socks and cut them off below the ankles."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a mat which he would spread out during the day and partition off at night, and he would pray on it. The people noticed him and prayed with his prayer, while the mat was between him and them. So he said:

"Take on only as much deed as you can bear, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not grow weary until you grow weary, and the most beloved of deeds to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the most constant of them, even if it is small."
Then he left that place of prayer and did not return to it until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, took him. And whenever he did a deed, he would keep to it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The ring of the Prophet ﷺ was of silver, and its stone was part of it.
And Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb said: Ḥumayd narrated to me that he heard Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, about the hair of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The hair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was wavy, neither straight nor tightly curled,
reaching between his ears and his shoulders.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb,
who said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me,
that Abū Hurayrah
said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Every deed of the son of Ādam is for him, except fasting; it is for Me and I reward for it. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, the odor from the mouth of the fasting person is better with Allah than the scent of musk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And my eyes saw,
and my ears heard, when the Prophet ﷺ spoke, and he said:
"Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor,
and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest with his due gift."
He said: What is his due gift, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"A day and a night, and hospitality is three days,
and whatever is beyond that is charity for him,
and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ... And Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb narrated to me: Jarīr narrated to us, from ʿUmārah,
from Abū Zurʿah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among the worst of people you will find the two-faced one, who comes to these with one face and to those with another face."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say in his sermon, praising Allah and extolling Him as He deserves, then he would say:

"Whomever Allah guides, none can misguide, and whomever He misguides, none can guide. The truest speech is the Book of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muḥammad, and the worst of affairs are the newly invented ones, and every newly invented matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Fire." Then he would say:
"I was sent, I and the Hour, like these two."

And when he mentioned the Hour, his cheeks would redden, his voice would rise, and his anger would intensify, as if he were a warner of an army, saying, "It will reach you in the morning, it will reach you in the evening!" Then he said:
"Whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his family, and whoever leaves behind a debt or dependents, they are to come to me, and I am closer to the believers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-ʿArj, a poet appeared reciting verses, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Seize the devil," or "Hold back the devil. For a man's belly to be filled with pus is better for him than for it to be filled with poetry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The most abased name with Allah is a man who calls himself King of Kings."
Ibn Abī Shaybah added in his narration:
"There is no king but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
Al-Ashʿathī said: Sufyān said: like Shāhānshāh.
And Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: I asked Abū ʿAmr about "akhnaʿ," and he said: it means the lowest.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered al-Jiʿrānah and came to the mosque, where he prayed as much as Allah willed. Then he entered the state of iḥrām, then mounted his riding animal and faced the valley of Sarif until he met the road to Madinah. By morning he was in Makkah, as one who had spent the night there.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed three days during the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Zaynab bint Abī Salamah, from Umm Salamah,

—both of them narrating it from her—she said: It was my night, the one on which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would come to me, on the evening of the Day of Sacrifice. He came to me, and Wahb ibn Zamʿah entered upon me together with a man from the family of Abū Umayyah, both wearing shirts. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Wahb:
"Have you performed the Ifāḍah, Abū ʿAbdullāh?"
He said: No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Take off your shirt."
He said: So he pulled it off over his head, and his companion also pulled his shirt off over his head. Then he said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? He said:
"This is a day on which you have been given a concession: when you have stoned the Jamrah, you may come out of the state of iḥrām."
—meaning from everything that was forbidden to you except women—
"Then if evening comes upon you before you have circumambulated this House, you return to a state of iḥrām as you were before you stoned the Jamrah, until you circumambulate it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and asked him about a woman
who circumambulates the House on the Day of Sacrifice and then gets her menses. He said: Let her last contact be with the House.
He said: Al-Ḥārith said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me a ruling like that.
He said: ʿUmar said: May your hands be ruined! You asked me about something you had asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about, so that I might contradict [him]!
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered the state of iḥrām for ʿUmrah from at-Tanʿīm, then I entered [Makkah] and completed my ʿUmrah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ waited for me at al-Abṭaḥ until I had finished, and he ordered the people to depart.
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﺷ came to the House and circumambulated it, then he left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with him—meaning the Prophet ﷺ—in the second departure, and he stopped at al-Muḥaṣṣab. —Abū Dāwūd said: Ibn Bashshār did not mention the story of her being sent to at-Tanʿīm in this hadith.— She said: Then I came to him before dawn, and he gave permission among his Companions to depart, and he set out. He passed by the House before the dawn prayer and circumambulated it as he left, then went on, heading for Madinah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Rāfiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not order me to make him stop there, but I pitched his tent and he stopped there.
Musaddad said: He was in charge of the baggage of the Prophet ﷺ. And ʿUthmān said: meaning at al-Abṭaḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said when he wished to depart from Minā:
"We will be stopping tomorrow."
Then he mentioned something similar, but he did not mention its beginning, nor did he mention al-Khayf, the valley.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar
would sleep a short while at al-Baṭḥāʾ, then enter Makkah, and he claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed the Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at al-Baṭḥāʾ, then slept a short while, then entered Makkah. And Ibn ʿUmar used to do the same.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with the Prophet ﷺ on Hajj, and people kept coming to him. One would say: O Messenger of Allah, I performed the saʿy before circumambulating, or I put something forward or delayed something. And he would say:
"No harm, no harm, except for a man who wrongs the honor of a Muslim man unjustly; that is the one who is in sin and is ruined."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw the Prophet ﷺ praying near the gate of Banū Sahm while people passed in front of him, and there was no barrier between them.
Sufyān said: There was no barrier between him and the Kaʿbah.

Sufyān said: Ibn Jurayj had told us about him, saying: Kathīr told us from his father. He said: I asked him, and he said: It is not from my father that I heard it, but from some of my family, from my grandfather.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In this account, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said:

"Its grass is not to be cut, its game is not to be scared away, its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who will announce it publicly, and it is not right for a man to carry weapons in it for fighting, nor is it right to cut a tree from it, except for a man to feed his camel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Hoarding food in the Sacred Precinct is a deviation [from the truth] in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The jinn used to ascend to the heaven to listen to the revelation. When they heard a word, they would add nine more to it. The word would be true, but what they added would be false. Then, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, they were prevented from their seats. They mentioned that to Iblīs, and shooting stars had not been thrown at them before that. Iblīs said to them, "This can only be because of something that has happened on earth." So he sent out his troops, and they found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing in prayer between two mountains. I think he said: in Makkah. They came to him and told him, and he said, "This is what has happened on earth."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some of the Jews said to some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, "Does your Prophet know how many are the keepers of Hell?" They said, "We do not know until we ask our Prophet."
Then a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Muhammad, your Companions were defeated today." He said, "How were they defeated?"
He said, "The Jews asked them: Does your Prophet know how many are the keepers of Hell?" He said, "And what did they say?"
He said, "They said: We do not know until we ask our Prophet." He said,

"Were a people defeated who were asked about what they do not know and said, 'We do not know until we ask our Prophet'? But they themselves asked their Prophet and said, 'Show us Allah openly.' Bring me the enemies of Allah, for I will ask them about the soil of Paradise, which is fine white flour."
When they came, they said, "O Abū al-Qāsim, how many are the keepers of Hell?" He said, "Like this and like this,"
once ten, and once nine. They said, "Yes."
Then the Prophet ﷺ said to them,
"What is the soil of Paradise?"
He said: They were silent for a moment, then said, "Bread, O Abū al-Qāsim."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Bread is from fine white flour."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith; we know it only through this route, from the hadith of Mujālid.
label: machine translation

segments_en: This is what we presented to Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: It was revealed:

"He frowned and turned away" concerning Ibn Umm Maktūm, the blind man. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and began to say, "O Messenger of Allah, guide me," while with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was one of the great men of the polytheists. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to turn away from him and to face the other, saying, "Do you see any harm in what I say?" He would say, "No."
So it was concerning this that it was revealed
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Whoever would be pleased to look at the Day of Resurrection as if seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite: 'When the sun is rolled up,' and 'When the sky is split open,' and 'When the sky is torn apart.'"
This is a ḥasan gharīb hadith.

Hishām ibn Yūsuf and others narrated this hadith with this chain, and he said: "Whoever would be pleased to look at the Day of Resurrection as if seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite: 'When the sun is rolled up.'" He did not mention 'When the sky is split open' and 'When the sky is torn apart.'
label: machine translation

segments_en: When a servant commits a sin, a black spot is placed on his heart. If he gives it up, seeks forgiveness and repents, his heart is polished. But if he returns, it is increased until it covers his heart. That is the rust that Allah mentioned:
'No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts like rust.'"
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever is brought to account will be punished."
He said: This is a gharīb hadith; we do not know it from the hadith of Qatādah, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, except through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā,
from Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah,
from Ayyūb ibn Khālid,
from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rāfiʿ,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"The Promised Day is the Day of Resurrection, the Witnessed Day is the Day of ʿArafah, and the Witness is Friday. The sun has not risen or set on a day better than it. On it there is an hour in which no believing servant will coincide with it while supplicating Allah for good, except that Allah will answer him, and he will not seek refuge from an evil, except that Allah will protect him from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And the whisper, according to some of them, was the movement of his lips as if he were speaking. It was said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, when you pray the ʿAṣr prayer you whisper." He said,

"A prophet among the prophets was impressed by his nation and said, 'Who can stand against these?' So Allah revealed to him: give them a choice between my taking vengeance on them and my giving their enemy power over them. He chose vengeance, so He sent death upon them, and seventy thousand of them died in one day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] from the Anṣār [reported] that the Prophet ﷺ said to the Jews, beginning with them: "
Fifty men of you shall swear [an oath]."
But they refused. So he said to the Anṣār, "You are entitled [to claim it by oath]."
They said, "Should we swear about the unseen, O Messenger of Allah?" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made it a blood-money payment [to be paid] by the Jews, because [the slain man] was found among them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, addressed us and said: "I did not send my governors to strike your skins or to take your wealth. Whoever has that done to him, let him bring it to me, and I will let him take retribution." ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said, "If a man disciplines some of those under his charge, will you have retribution taken from him?" He said, "Yes, by the One in whose hand is my soul, I will have retribution taken. And I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ allow retribution against himself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that whoever kills by mistake, his blood-money is one hundred camels: thirty bint makhāḍ, thirty bint labūn, thirty ḥiqqah, and ten male ibn labūn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the value of the blood-money was eight hundred dīnārs or eight thousand dirhams, and the blood-money of the People of the Book at that time was half the blood-money of the Muslims. He said: That remained so until ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on him, became caliph. He stood up to give a sermon and said, "Indeed, the camels have become expensive."

He said: So ʿUmar set it at one thousand dīnārs for those who deal in gold, twelve thousand [dirhams] for those who deal in silver, two hundred cows for the owners of cattle, two thousand sheep for the owners of sheep, and two hundred garments for the owners of garments.
He said: And he left the blood-money of the dhimmīs and did not raise it along with what he raised of the blood-money.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled regarding blood-money: one hundred camels for the owners of camels, two hundred cows for the owners of cattle, two thousand sheep for the owners of sheep, two hundred garments for the owners of garments, and something for the owners of wheat which Muḥammad did not remember.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAṭāʾ mentioned from Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prescribed... and he mentioned the like of the narration of Mūsā.
He said: And for the people of food [staples], something which I do not remember.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ruled in the case of quasi-intentional killing: thirty ḥiqqah, thirty jadhaʿah, and forty pregnant she-camels (khalifah), between a thaniyyah and a bāzil in its ninth year.
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with him, that he said regarding quasi-intentional killing, [it is] in thirds: thirty-three ḥiqqah, thirty-three jadhaʿah, and thirty-four thaniyyah up to a bāzil in its ninth year, all of them pregnant (khalifah).
label: machine translation

segments_en: and al-Aswad,
said: ʿAbdullāh said regarding quasi-intentional killing: twenty-five ḥiqqah, twenty-five jadhaʿah, twenty-five bint labūn, and twenty-five bint makhāḍ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said regarding killing by mistake, [it is] in four parts: twenty-five ḥiqqah, twenty-five jadhaʿah, twenty-five bint labūn, and twenty-five bint makhāḍ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the case of the aggravated [blood-money]: forty pregnant jadhaʿah, thirty ḥiqqah, and thirty bint labūn. And in the case of killing by mistake: thirty ḥiqqah, thirty bint labūn, twenty male ibn labūn, and twenty bint makhāḍ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
all from Ibn
ʿUyaynah—Zuhayr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us—
from Ayyūb ibn Mūsā,
from Nubayh ibn Wahb,
from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUthmān,
who traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"A man in a state of iḥrām may not marry, nor arrange a marriage, nor propose."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her while he was not in iḥrām. He said: She was my maternal aunt and the maternal aunt of Ibn ʿAbbās.
label: machine translation

segments_en: a year after the death of Nāfiʿ, and he had a study circle at that time. He said: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Faḍl informed me, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"A woman without a husband has more right over herself than her guardian, and a virgin girl is to be consulted, and her permission is her silence."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I have married a woman of the Anṣār.
The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Did you look at her? For in the eyes of the Anṣār there is something."
He said: I have looked at her. He said:
"For how much did you marry her?"
He said: For four ūqiyyahs.
The Prophet ﷺ said to him:

"For four ūqiyyahs! It is as though you were carving silver from the side of this mountain. We have nothing to give you, but perhaps we may send you on an expedition from which you will gain something."
He said: So he sent an expedition to Banū ʿAbs, and that man was among them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among the greatest of trusts in the sight of Allah on the Day of Resurrection is a man who goes in to his wife and she goes in to him, and then he spreads her secret."
And Ibn Numayr said: "Indeed, the greatest..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He said: He traced the hadith back until he attributed it to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: Withdrawal (ʿazl) was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "What is that?"

They said: A man has a wife who is nursing, and he has relations with her but dislikes that she become pregnant by him; and a man has a slave woman and has relations with her but dislikes that she become pregnant by him. He said:
"There is no harm on you if you do not do that, for it is only the decree [of Allah]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that a woman close to giving birth was brought to him at the door of a tent, and he said:
"Perhaps he intends to have relations with her?" They said: Yes.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I had intended to curse him with a curse that would accompany him into his grave. How could he make him his heir when he is not lawful for him? How could he take him as a servant when he is not lawful for him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to see me, and I said to him: Would you be interested in my sister, the daughter of Abū Sufyān? He said: "What shall I do?" I said: Marry her. He said: "Do you like that?"
I said: I am not alone with you, and I would like the one who shares in goodness with me to be my sister. He said:
"She is not lawful for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Sālim,

the freed slave of Abū Ḥudhayfah, was with Abū Ḥudhayfah and his family in their home. So she—meaning the daughter of Suhayl—came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Sālim has reached the age that men reach and understands as they understand, and he enters upon us, and I think there is something in the heart of Abū Ḥudhayfah about that.
The Prophet ﷺ said to her:
"Nurse him, and you will become unlawful for him, and what is in the heart of Abū Ḥudhayfah will go away."
She returned and said: I have nursed him, and what was in the heart of Abū Ḥudhayfah went away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sahlah bint Suhayl ibn ʿAmr came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, Sālim—the freed slave of Abū Ḥudhayfah—is with us in our house, and he has reached what men reach and knows what men know. He said:
"Nurse him, and you will become unlawful for him."
He said: I stayed a year or about that without narrating it, out of awe of it. Then I met al-Qāsim and said to him: You narrated to me a hadith that I have not narrated since.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he married a woman during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ met him and said:
"Have you married, Jābir?"
He said: I said: Yes. He said:
"A virgin or a previously married woman?"
He said: I said: A previously married woman. He said:
"Why not a virgin, who would play with you?"
He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, I have sisters, and I feared that she would come between me and them. He said:
"Then that is it. A woman is married for her religion, her wealth, and her beauty, so take the one with religion; may your hands be covered in dust."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was serving Abū Ṭalḥah al-Anṣārī, Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb a drink made from fadīkh, which is [made from] dates. Then someone came to them and said, "Wine has been prohibited."
Abū Ṭalḥah said, "Anas, get up, go to these jars and break them."
Anas said: So I got up, took a stone mortar of ours, and struck the jars with its lower end until they broke.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿUmar], may Allah be pleased with him, said from the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "To proceed: the prohibition of wine was revealed, and it is made from five things: grapes, wheat, barley, dates and honey."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh in containers, they said, "Not everyone can find [other containers]." So he granted them permission to use jars, other than those coated with pitch.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh in the green jar.
I said, "What about the white one?" He said, "I do not know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about bādhaq.
He said, "Muḥammad ﷺ came before bādhaq [was known].
Whatever intoxicates is forbidden."
He said, "The drink [that is permitted] is what is lawful and good."
He said, "After what is lawful and good there is only what is forbidden and foul."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I brought the Prophet ﷺ a cup of milk from an-Naqīʿ, not covered, and he said:
"Why did you not cover it, even by laying a stick across it?"
Abū Ḥumayd said: He only commanded that waterskins be tied shut at night and that doors be closed at night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He prayed the Ẓuhr prayer, then sat attending to people's needs in the open space of al-Kūfah until the time of the ʿAṣr prayer came.
Then water was brought and he drank, and washed his face and hands, and he mentioned his head and feet.
Then he stood and drank what was left of it while standing, and said, "Some people dislike drinking while standing, but the Prophet ﷺ did just as I have done."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman of the Arabs was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he ordered Abū Usayd to send for her. He sent for her and she came and stayed in the fortress of Banū Sāʿidah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he came to her and entered upon her, and there was a woman with her head bowed. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke to her, she said, "I seek refuge in Allah from you." He said:
"I have given you refuge from myself."
They said to her, "Do you know who this is?" She said, "No."
They said, "This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who came to propose marriage to you." She said, "I was more wretched than that [to refuse him]."
Sahl said: On that day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and sat in the porch of Banū Sāʿidah, he and his Companions. Then he said, "Give us something to drink."
[He said this] to Sahl. He said: So I brought out this cup for them and gave them drink from it.
Abū Ḥāzim said: Sahl brought out that cup for us and we drank from it. He said: Later ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz asked him for it, and he gave it to him.
In the narration of Abū Bakr ibn Isḥāq, he said:
"Give us something to drink, Sahl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No affliction befalls a believer, even a thorn, except that some of his sins are taken away because of it, or some of his sins are expiated because of it."
Yazīd does not know which of the two ʿUrwah said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was suffering from a fever, and I touched him with my hand and said, "Messenger of Allah, you are suffering a severe fever."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Yes, I suffer fever as two men among you suffer."
He said: I said, "That is because you will have a double reward." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Yes."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no Muslim who is afflicted with harm from illness or anything else, except that Allah removes his sins because of it, as a tree sheds its leaves."
In the narration of Zuhayr, the words "and I touched him with my hand" are not present.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said to me, "Shall I show you a woman of the people of Paradise?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "This black woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'I suffer from seizures,
and I become uncovered, so pray to Allah for me.' He said:
'If you wish, be patient and Paradise will be yours; and if you wish, I will pray to Allah to cure you.' She said, 'I will be patient.'
Then she said, 'I become uncovered, so pray to Allah that I not become uncovered.' So he prayed for her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I was listening,
from Ibn al-Qāsim, who said: Mālik narrated to me,
and [another chain:] Sulaymān ibn Manṣūr informed us,
he said: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak informed us,
(and the wording is his), from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd,
from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm,
from ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqāṣ,
from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb,
may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Actions are only by intentions, and each person will only have what he intended. So whoever's migration was to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's migration was for worldly gain that he would obtain or a woman he would marry, his migration is to that for which he migrated."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And al-Ḥasan al-Ḥulwānī,
and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd,
ʿAbd said: He informed me, and he said,
while the other two said: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ,
from Ibn Shihāb,
who said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muṭīʿ ibn al-Aswad,
from Nawfal ibn Muʿāwiyah,
[who related] a hadith like this hadith of Abū Hurayrah, except that Abū Bakr adds:
"Among prayers is a prayer such that whoever misses it, it is as if he has been robbed of his family and his wealth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A virgin is not to be given in marriage until she is asked for her consent,
nor a previously married woman until she is consulted."
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is her consent?" He said: "When she remains silent."
Some people said: If the virgin is not asked for her consent and is not [properly] married off,
and a man devises a scheme and produces two false witnesses that he married her with her consent,
and the judge confirms her marriage,
while the husband knows that the testimony is false,
then there is no harm in his having intercourse with her,
and it is a valid marriage.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, which [part] of Islam is best?" He said:
"That you feed people and greet with peace those whom you know and those whom you do not know."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has three [qualities] will find the taste of faith — and Bundār said: the sweetness of faith: that he loves a person and loves him only for Allah's sake;
and that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than anything else;
and that he would rather be thrown into the Fire than return to disbelief after Allah has rescued him from it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever has four [traits] is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy in him until he gives it up: when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a covenant, he betrays; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he disputes, he behaves wickedly."
Except that in the hadith of Sufyān [it says]:
"And if there is in him one characteristic of them, there is in him a characteristic of hypocrisy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We memorized it, and what was memorized from az-Zuhrī, from Abū Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Whoever fasts Ramadān out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven;
and whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Qadr out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When dawn breaks, every night prayer and the Witr are gone, so pray the Witr before dawn breaks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to pray the Ḍuḥā prayer until we said, "He will never leave it," and he would leave it until we said, "He will never pray it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is Abū Saʿīd al-Muʾaddib, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Mujāhid,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Sāʾib,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray four [units of prayer] after the sun passed its zenith, before the Ẓuhr prayer, and he said:
"It is an hour in which the gates of heaven are opened, and I love that a righteous deed of mine ascend during it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The people closest to me on the Day of Resurrection will be those who send the most prayers upon me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed supplication remains suspended between heaven and earth; nothing of it ascends until you send prayers upon your Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: "No one may sell in our marketplace except one who has gained understanding in the religion."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"Seek the hour that is hoped for on Friday after the ʿAṣr prayer until the sun sets."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, this ḥadīth as well.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [A man] from the people of Qubāʾ, from his father, who was
one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "The Prophet ﷺ commanded us to attend the Friday prayer from Qubāʾ."
It has also been narrated from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, on this matter, but it is not authentic.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and they mentioned upon whom the Friday prayer is obligatory, but Aḥmad did not mention anything from the Prophet ﷺ about it.
Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan said: I said to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, "There is a narration about it from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ."
Aḥmad said, "From the Prophet ﷺ?" I said, "Yes."
Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan said: Ḥajjāj ibn Nuṣayr narrated to us, Muʿārik ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"Friday prayer is obligatory upon whoever can return to his family at night."
He said: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal became angry with me and said to me, "Seek forgiveness from your Lord! Seek forgiveness from your Lord!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ settled upon the pulpit, we would turn our faces toward him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī

entered on Friday while Marwān was delivering the sermon, and he stood and prayed. The guards came to make him sit, but he refused until he had prayed. When he finished, we came to him and said, "May Allah have mercy on you, they were about to attack you."
He said, "I would never leave these two [units of prayer] after something I saw from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

Then he mentioned that a man came on Friday in shabby attire while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the Friday sermon, so he commanded him, and he prayed two units while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the sermon.
Ibn Abī ʿUmar said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah used to pray two units when he came while the imam was delivering the sermon, and he used to command it; and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ held the same view.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Prophet ﷺ, after the prayer had been called, with a man speaking to him, standing between him and the qiblah, and he kept speaking to him. I even saw some of us dozing off from how long the Prophet ﷺ stood for him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah on an expedition, and it coincided with a Friday. His companions set out in the morning, but he said, "I will stay behind and pray with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then join them."
When he had prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, he saw him and said:
"What prevented you from setting out in the morning with your companions?"
He said, "I wanted to pray with you and then join them." He said:
"If you spent everything on earth, you would not attain the merit of their morning departure."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is a duty upon Muslims to bathe on Friday, and let each of them apply some of his family's perfume; if he does not find any, then water is [his] perfume."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bring out the young women, the mature girls, the women in seclusion, and the menstruating women on the two Eids. As for the menstruating women, they would keep apart from the place of prayer and witness the supplication of the Muslims. One of them said, "O Messenger of Allah, what if she has no outer garment?" He said:
"Let her sister lend her one of her garments."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the verses were revealed to the Prophet ﷺ:
"O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing," up to His saying:
"but the punishment of Allah is severe." He said: These were revealed to him while he was on a journey, and he said:
"Do you know which day that is?"
They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:

"That is the day when Allah will say to Adam: 'Send forth the delegation of the Fire.' He will say: 'My Lord, what is the delegation of the Fire?' He will say: 'Nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire and one to Paradise.'"
He said: So the Muslims began to weep, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Aim for the mean and strive for what is right, for there has never been a prophethood except that before it there was a period of ignorance. The number will be taken from the people of ignorance; if it is not completed, it will be completed from the hypocrites. Your likeness and that of the nations is only like a mark on the foreleg of an animal, or like a mole on the side of a camel." Then he said: "I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise."
So they said "Allahu akbar." Then he said:
"I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise."
So they said "Allahu akbar." Then he said:
"I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise."
So they said "Allahu akbar." He said: I do not know whether he said "two-thirds" or not.
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith, and it has been narrated through more than one route from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey, and his Companions became spread out in their travelling. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his voice with these two verses: "O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing," up to His saying:
"indeed, the punishment of Allah is severe." When his Companions heard that, they urged their mounts on, and they knew that he was about to say something. He said:
"Do you know which day that is?"
They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:
"That is the day on which Allah will call Adam, and his Lord will call to him, saying: 'O Adam, send forth the delegation of the Fire.'
He will say: 'My Lord, what is the delegation of the Fire?' He will say: 'From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire and one to Paradise.'"
The people despaired so much that they did not even smile. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw what had befallen his Companions, he said:

"Do good deeds and rejoice at the good news. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are with two creations that were never with anything except that they outnumbered it: Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj, and those of the children of Adam and the children of Iblīs who have died."
He said: Some of what the people felt was then lifted from them. He said:

"Do good deeds and rejoice at the good news. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are among the people only like a mole on the side of a camel, or like a mark on the foreleg of an animal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The House was named the Ancient House only because no tyrant has ever prevailed over it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He] may Allah be pleased with him, said: When revelation came down to the Prophet ﷺ, a sound like the buzzing of bees would be heard near his face. One day it was revealed to him, and we stayed for a while until it was lifted from him. He faced the qiblah, raised his hands, and said:

"O Allah, increase us and do not decrease us; honor us and do not humiliate us; give to us and do not deprive us; favor us and do not favor others over us; and be pleased with us and make us pleased." Then he ﷺ said:
"Ten verses have been revealed to me; whoever establishes them will enter Paradise." Then he recited:
"Certainly will the believers have succeeded," until he completed ten verses.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When it was revealed:
"And warn your closest kindred," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put his fingers in his ears and raised his voice, saying:
"O Banū ʿAbd Manāf! O, the morning alarm!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd said: Four verses were revealed concerning me.

He mentioned the story: Saʿd's mother said, "Has Allah not commanded kindness to parents? By Allah, I will not eat any food or drink any drink until I die or you disbelieve." He said: When they wanted to feed her, they would pry her mouth open. Then this verse was revealed:
"And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents," the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ regarding the saying of the Most High:
"And do you commit the evil in your meeting place?" he said:
"They used to pelt the people of the earth with pebbles and mock them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abū Bakr regarding his wager:
"Alif, Lām, Mīm. The Romans have been defeated,"
"Why did you not be more cautious, O Abū Bakr? For the biḍʿ is between three and nine."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No one spoke in the cradle except three: ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, the companion of Jurayj—Jurayj was a devout man who had built a hermitage and lived in it—his mother came to him while he was praying and said, 'O Jurayj!'
He said, 'O my Lord, my mother and my prayer!'

He turned to his prayer, and she left. The next day she came to him while he was praying and said, 'O Jurayj!' He said, 'O my Lord, my mother and my prayer!' He turned to his prayer, and she left. The next day she came to him while he was praying and said, 'O Jurayj!'
He said, 'O my Lord, my mother and my prayer!'
He turned to his prayer, and she said, 'O Allah, do not let him die until he looks upon the faces of immoral women.'

The Children of Israel then spoke about Jurayj and his worship. There was a prostitute who was known for her beauty, and she said, 'If you wish, I will tempt him for you.' He said: So she presented herself to him, but he paid her no attention.
