label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah,
from Anas ibn Mālik,
who said: We would pray the ʿAṣr prayer, then a person would go out to the Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf and find them praying ʿAṣr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"O Banū Salimah, do you not seek reward for your footsteps?"
And Mujāhid said regarding His saying {And We record what they have put forth and their traces}: He said: their steps.
And Ibn Abī Maryam said: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed us: Ḥumayd narrated to me: Anas narrated to me
that the Banū Salimah
wanted to move away from their homes
and settle near the Prophet ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that {Madīnah} be left empty, so he said:
"Do you not seek reward for your footsteps?"
Mujāhid said: Their steps are their traces, [meaning] that one walks on the earth on his feet.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"No prayer is heavier on the hypocrites than the Fajr and the ʿIshāʾ prayers,
and if they knew what is in them, they would come to them even if crawling.
I had intended to order the muʾadhdhin to call the iqāmah,
then order a man to lead the people in prayer,
then take a flame of fire and burn the houses of those who do not go out to the prayer afterwards."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the cold was severe, the Prophet ﷺ would pray early, and
when the heat was severe, he would delay the prayer until it cooled, meaning the Friday prayer.
Yūnus ibn Bukayr said: Abū Khaldah informed us, and he said "the prayer,"
and did not mention Friday.
And Bishr ibn Thābit said: Abū Khaldah narrated to us: The governor led us in the Friday prayer, then he said to Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: How did the Prophet ﷺ pray the Ẓuhr prayer?
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ which deed is best. He said:
"Belief in Allah and striving in the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ. And Aḥmad ibn Yūnus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Yaḥyā, who is Ibn Saʿīd, narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān, from ʿAmrah, from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet ﷺ would shorten the two rakʿahs before the Subḥ prayer so much that I would say: Did he recite the Mother of the Book?
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and mentioned the trial with which a person is tried in his grave. When he mentioned that, the Muslims cried out in such a clamor that it prevented me from understanding the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When their clamor subsided, I said to a man near me: May Allah bless you, what did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say at the end of his words? He said:
"It has been revealed to me that you will be tried in the graves in a way close to the trial of the Dajjāl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ibrāhīm, the son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him and said:
"He has a wet nurse in Paradise, and had he lived, he would have been a truthful prophet.
And had he lived, I would have set free his maternal relatives, the Copts, and no Copt would have been enslaved."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first to come to us were Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr and Ibn Umm Maktūm,
and they used to teach the people the Qurʾān.
Then Bilāl, Saʿd, and ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir arrived.
Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb arrived with twenty of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and after that the Prophet ﷺ arrived.
I never saw the people of Madinah rejoice over anything as they rejoiced over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ,

until even the slave girls were saying, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has arrived!" And he had not yet arrived when I had recited {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High} along with other surahs of the Mufaṣṣal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed, {"And those who hoard gold and silver"}, [the narrator] said: That weighed heavily upon the Muslims, so ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I will relieve you of it.
So he went and said: O Prophet of Allah, this verse has weighed heavily upon your Companions. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah only made zakāh obligatory so that what remains of your wealth may be purified, and He only made the laws of inheritance obligatory so that [wealth] may be for those after you."
So ʿUmar exclaimed "Allahu akbar," and then he said to him:
"Shall I not tell you of the best thing a man can hoard? The righteous woman: when he looks at her she pleases him, when he commands her she obeys him, and when he is away from her she guards him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The beggar has a right, even if he comes on a horse."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Sufyān with him, [narrating] from Fāṭimah bint Ḥusayn, from her father, from ʿAlī,
from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She, who was called Buhaysah, [narrated] from her father.

She said: My father asked permission to see the Prophet ﷺ, and he entered between him and his shirt, and began kissing and embracing him. Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the thing that it is not permissible to withhold? He said: "Water."
He said: O Prophet of Allah, what is the thing that it is not permissible to withhold? He said: "Salt."
He said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the thing that it is not permissible to withhold? He said:
"That you do good is better for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Has any of you fed a poor person today?"

Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I entered the mosque and there was a beggar asking. I found a piece of bread in the hand of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, so I took it from him and gave it to the beggar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Nothing but Paradise should be asked for by the Face of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a man came with something like an egg of gold and said: O Messenger of Allah, I got this from a mine. Take it, for it is charity; I own nothing else.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him. Then he came to him from his right side and said the same, and he turned away from him. Then he came to him from his left side, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him. Then he came to him from behind, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it and threw it at him; had it struck him it would have hurt him or wounded him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One of you brings all that he owns and says, 'This is charity,' and then sits down begging from people. The best charity is that which is given out of sufficiency."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man entered the mosque, and the Prophet ﷺ told the people to throw down some garments, so they threw them down, and he ordered two garments from them for him. Then he urged them to give charity, and the man came and threw down one of the two garments. The Prophet ﷺ shouted at him and said: "Take your garment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: O Messenger of Allah, which charity is best? He said:
"The effort of one with little, and begin with those you support."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Which charity do you like best? He said: "Water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the pledge of allegiance from the women, a dignified woman, who seemed to be from the women of Muḍar, stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, we are a burden on our fathers and our sons. Abū Dāwūd said: And I think he also mentioned, and our husbands. What is lawful for us of their wealth? He said:
"Fresh dates, which you may eat and give as gifts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is enough sin for a man that he neglects those whom he is responsible for feeding."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a sermon and said:

"Beware of miserliness, for those before you were destroyed only by miserliness. It commanded them to be stingy, and they were stingy; it commanded them to sever ties, and they severed them; it commanded them to commit immorality, and they committed it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went on a military expedition with Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah, and I found a whip. They said to me: Throw it away.

I said: No, but if I find its owner [I will return it], otherwise I will make use of it. Then I performed Hajj and passed through Madinah and asked Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. He said: I found a purse containing one hundred dinars, so I came to the Prophet ﷺ and he said: "Announce it for a year."
So I announced it for a year, then came to him, and he said: "Announce it for a year."
So I announced it for a year, then came to him, and he said: "Announce it for a year."
So I announced it for a year, then came to him and said: I have not found anyone who recognizes it. He said:
"Remember its number, its string, and its container. If its owner comes [, give it to him]; otherwise make use of it."
And he said: I do not know whether he said "Announce it" three times,
or just once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿAlī], may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood at ʿArafah and said:
"This is ʿArafah, and this is the place of standing; and all of ʿArafah is a place of standing."

Then he departed when the sun had set, with Usāmah ibn Zayd riding behind him. He kept gesturing with his hand to maintain calm while the people were rushing right and left; he would turn to them and say:
"O people, [keep to] calmness!"
Then he came to Jamʿ and led them in the two prayers together. When morning came he went to Quzaḥ, stood there and said:
"This is Quzaḥ, and it is a place of standing; and all of Jamʿ is a place of standing."

Then he departed until he reached the valley of Muḥassir. He urged his she-camel on, and she trotted until he had crossed the valley. Then he stopped, had al-Faḍl ride behind him, and came to the Jamrah and threw pebbles at it. Then he came to the place of sacrifice and said:
"This is the place of sacrifice, and all of Minā is a place of sacrifice."

A young woman of Khathʿam asked him for a ruling, saying: My father is a very old man, and the obligation of Allah concerning Hajj has come upon him. Will it suffice if I perform Hajj on his behalf? He said:
"Perform Hajj on behalf of your father."
He said: And he turned al-Faḍl's neck aside. Al-ʿAbbās said: O Messenger of Allah, why did you turn your cousin's neck aside? He said:
"I saw a young man and a young woman, and I did not feel safe from Satan [affecting] them."
Then a man came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, I departed [from ʿArafah/Minā for the Ifāḍah] before I shaved my head. He said:
"Shave or trim, and there is no harm."
He said: Another came and said: O Messenger of Allah, I slaughtered before I threw the pebbles. He said:
"Throw, and there is no harm."
He said: Then he came to the House and performed ṭawāf around it. Then he came to Zamzam and said:
"O children of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, were it not that people would overpower you in it, I would draw [water] myself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He would attribute the report [to the Prophet ﷺ]: that he would stop saying the Talbiyah
during ʿUmrah when he touched the Stone.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When we performed Hajj with the Prophet ﷺ, we would say the Talbiyah on behalf of the women and throw the pebbles on behalf of the children.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about ʿUmrah, whether it is obligatory. He said:
"No, but to perform ʿUmrah is better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ commanded ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr to take ʿĀʾishah from at-Tanʿīm to perform ʿUmrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out from al-Jiʿrānah at night to perform ʿUmrah. He entered Mecca at night and completed his ʿUmrah, then left that same night and was at al-Jiʿrānah in the morning as if he had spent the night there. When the sun passed its zenith the next day, he left from the bottom of Sarif until he joined the road, the road to Jamʿ, in the bottom of Sarif. For that reason, his ʿUmrah remained hidden from the people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is as-Salūlī al-Kūfī, from Isrāʾīl,
from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ:
that the Prophet ﷺ performed ʿUmrah in Dhū al-Qaʿdah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever performs Hajj to the House, let the last of his dealings be at the House, except for women in menstruation; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted them a concession.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever performs Hajj to this House or performs ʿUmrah, let the last of his dealings be at the House."
ʿUmar said to him: May you fall from your hands! You heard this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and did not tell us of it?
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Day of the Greater Hajj, and he said: "The Day of Sacrifice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Circumambulation around the House is like prayer, except that you speak in it; so whoever speaks in it, let him speak only what is good."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [ʿĀʾishah], may Allah be pleased with her, used to carry Zamzam water and would report that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to carry it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī took me by the hand and said: Come with us to al-Ḥasan to visit him in his illness.
We found Abū Mūsā with him. ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said: Have you come as a visitor of the sick, O Abū Mūsā, or as a mere caller? He said: No, rather as a visitor of the sick.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon Khabbāb, who had been cauterized on his belly. He said: I do not know of any of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who has suffered from affliction what I have suffered. I was [once] at the time of the Prophet ﷺ unable to find a single dirham, while in a corner of my house there are now forty thousand. And were it not that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us, or he forbade, from wishing for death, I would have wished for it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ, to that effect.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not envy anyone for an easy death after what I saw of the severity of the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said: I asked Abū Zurʿah about this hadith and said to him: Who is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-ʿAlāʾ? He said: He is Ibn al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Lajlāj.
And he is known only through this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with Zayd ibn Ḥārithah on the expedition of Mu'tah, and a man from Yemen who had come as reinforcement accompanied me, having nothing with him but his sword. A man among the Muslims slaughtered a camel, and the Yemeni asked him for a piece of its hide, so he gave it to him, and he made it like a shield. We went on and met the gathered forces of the Romans. Among them was a man on a reddish horse of his, with a gilded saddle and gilded weapons. The Roman began to attack the Muslims fiercely, so the Yemeni lay in wait for him behind a rock. When the Roman passed by him, he hamstrung his horse, and it fell; he got on top of him and killed him, and took his horse and weapons. When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, granted victory to the Muslims, Khālid ibn al-Walīd sent for him and took part of the spoils. ʿAwf said: I went to him and said, "O Khālid, do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the spoils of the slain belong to the killer?" He said, "Yes, but I thought it too much."

I said, "You will return it to him, or I will make you face this before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." But he refused to return it to him. ʿAwf said: We gathered before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I related to him the story of the Yemeni and what Khālid had done. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Khālid, what made you do what you did?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I thought it too much."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Khālid, return to him what you took from him."
ʿAwf said: I said to him, "Here you are, Khālid! Did I not do right by you?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "What is that?"
So I told him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry and said:
"O Khālid, do not return it to him. Would you leave my commanders for me? You take the best of their affairs, and they bear the worst of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Salamah ibn Yazīd al-Juʿfī asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying, "O Prophet of Allah, what do you think if rulers are set over us who demand their right from us and withhold our right from us? What do you command us?" He turned away from him. Then he asked him again, and he turned away from him. Then he asked him a second or third time, and al-Ashʿath ibn Qays pulled him aside and said, "
Listen and obey, for upon them is only what they have been charged with, and upon you is only what you have been charged with."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best of your leaders are those whom you love and who love you, and for whom you pray and who pray for you. The worst of your leaders are those whom you hate and who hate you, and whom you curse and who curse you."
They said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, should we not then oppose them?" He said:

"No, as long as they establish prayer among you. No, as long as they establish prayer among you. But whoever has a ruler set over him and sees him committing some act of disobedience to Allah, let him hate what he does of disobedience to Allah, but let him not withdraw his hand from obedience."

Ibn Jābir said: When Ruzayq told me this hadith, I said to him, "By Allah, O Abū al-Miqdām, did you really hear this from Muslim ibn Qaraẓah, who said: I heard ʿAwf say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say it?" He knelt on his knees, faced the qiblah, and said, "Yes, by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, I heard it from Muslim ibn Qaraẓah, who said: I heard ʿAwf ibn Mālik say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people dispersed from around Abū Hurayrah,
and Nātil of the people of Syria said to him, "O Shaykh, narrate to us a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said, "Yes, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'The first of people to be judged on the Day of Resurrection will be a man who died as a martyr. He will be brought, and Allah will make him recognize His blessings, and he will recognize them. He will say, "What did you do with them?" He will say, "I fought for You until I was martyred."
He will say, "You lie. Rather, you fought so that it would be said, 'He is courageous,' and so it was said."

Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is thrown into the Fire. Then a man who learned knowledge and taught it, and recited the Qur'an. He will be brought, and Allah will make him recognize His blessings, and he will recognize them. He will say, "What did you do with them?" He will say, "I learned knowledge, taught it, and recited the Qur'an for Your sake."
He will say, "You lie. Rather, you learned so that it would be said, 'He is a scholar,'
and you recited the Qur'an so that it would be said, 'He is a reciter.'
And so it was said." Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is thrown into the Fire.

Then a man whom Allah had given abundance and had granted all kinds of wealth. He will be brought, and Allah will make him recognize His blessings, and he will recognize them. He will say, "What did you do with them?" He will say, "I left no path in which You love for wealth to be spent except that I spent in it for Your sake." He will say, "You lie. Rather, you did it so that it would be said, 'He is generous.'
And so it was said." Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face and then thrown into the Fire.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"O Ibn ʿĀbis, shall I guide you—or he said, shall I inform you—to the best thing by which those who seek refuge seek refuge?"
He said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind'—these two sūrahs."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A grey mule was gifted to the Prophet ﷺ, so he rode it, and ʿUqbah took hold of it to lead it for him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿUqbah, "Recite."
He said, "What shall I recite, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Recite: 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He has created.'"
He repeated it to me until I had recited it, and he realized that I was not very pleased with it. He said:
"Perhaps you have taken it lightly."
After that, I never stood [to pray] with anything like it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he said:
"O ʿUqbah, say."
I said, "What should I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He was silent toward me, then said:
"O ʿUqbah, say."
I said, "What should I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He was silent toward me, and I said, "O Allah, make him return to me." Then he said:
"O ʿUqbah, say."
I said, "What should I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak.'" So I recited it until I reached its end. Then he said, "Say."
I said, "What should I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.'"
So I recited it until I reached its end. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said at that point:
"No one who asks has ever asked by anything like these two, and no one who seeks refuge has ever sought refuge by anything like them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Recite, O Jābir."
I said, "What should I recite, may my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah?" He said:
"Recite 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.'" So I recited them, and he said:
"Recite them, for you will never recite anything like them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"I seek refuge in Allah from disbelief and debt."
A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you equate debt with disbelief?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate with these words:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from being overwhelmed by debt, from being overpowered by the enemy, and from the gloating of enemies."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge [in Allah]. (Mursal)
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he used to say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty."
A man said, "Are the two equal?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Seek refuge in Allah from a bad neighbor in the home of permanent residence, for the neighbor of the desert moves away from you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered the mosque while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in it, so I came and sat beside him. He said:
"O Abū Dharr, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of the jinn and mankind."
I said, "Do humans have devils?" He said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"O Allah, I seek refuge in Your greatness from being swallowed up from beneath me."
Jubayr said, "That is, the earth swallowing [one] up."
ʿUbādah said, "I do not know whether it was the saying of the Prophet ﷺ or the saying of Jubayr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One night I looked for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in my bed but did not find him. I moved my hand over the head of the bed, and my hand fell on the soles of his feet, and he was in prostration, saying:
"I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your displeasure, and I seek refuge in You from You."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Unripe dates and ripe dates [mixed] are khamr (intoxicant).
label: machine translation

segments_en: Unripe dates and ripe dates [mixed] are khamr. Al-Aʿmash attributed it to the Prophet (marfūʿ).
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The Prophet ﷺ said:]
"Raisins and dates [mixed] are khamr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade [using] gourds, green jars, tarred vessels, and hollowed-out palm trunks, and forbade mixing unripe dates with ripe dates, and mixing raisins with dates. And he wrote to the people of Hajar:
"Do not mix raisins and dates together."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Unripe dates alone are forbidden, and with ripe dates they are forbidden.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to combine two things in a nabīdh, one of which overpowers the other.
He said: I asked him about faḍīkh, and he forbade it to me. He said: He disliked unripe dates that had begun to ripen from the tip, fearing they would be two things, so we would cut it off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Anas ibn Mālik brought unripe dates that had begun to ripen at the tip, and he began cutting [the ripe part] off from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Qatādah said: Anas used to order that the ripening tips be cut off.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he would not leave anything that had begun to ripen without separating it from his faḍīkh.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ash-Shaʿbī,
both said: Sukr is khamr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sukr is khamr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Ḥimyar killed a man from the enemy and wanted to take his spoils, but Khālid ibn al-Walīd, who was their commander, prevented him. So ʿAwf ibn Mālik came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him, and he said to Khālid:
"What prevented you from giving him his spoils?"
He said, "I considered it too much, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Hand it over to him."

Then Khālid passed by ʿAwf, who pulled him by his cloak and said, "Did I not fulfil for you what I mentioned to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard it and became angry, and he said:

"Do not give it to him, O Khālid! Do not give it to him, O Khālid! Will you not leave my commanders to me? Your example and theirs is that of a man who was entrusted with camels or sheep and tended them, then, when the time came to water them, he brought them to a trough and they began to drink from it. They drank its clear water and left its muddy dregs. So the clear part is for you, and the muddy part is for them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd [narrated]. Ibn Rāfiʿ said: "Ḥaddathanā," while the other two said:
"Akhbaranā ʿAbd al-Razzāq; Akhbaranā Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah,
that the Prophet ﷺ [had died], and the two of them were at that time seeking his land at Fadak and his share at Khaybar.
Abū Bakr said to them, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [say...]"

And he related the hadith with the same meaning as the hadith of ʿUqayl from al-Zuhrī, except that he said: Then ʿAlī stood up, magnified the right of Abū Bakr, mentioned his merit and his precedence, then went to Abū Bakr and pledged allegiance to him. The people turned to ʿAlī and said, "You have done right and done well."
And the people were close to ʿAlī when he drew near to what was right and customary.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And his wound was closing up for healing, and he said, "O Allah, You know that there is no one I would rather strive against for Your sake than a people who denied Your Messenger ﷺ and drove him out. O Allah, if any of the war with Quraysh remains, keep me alive so that I may strive against them for Your sake. O Allah, I think that You have ended the war between us and them. If You have ended the war between us and them, then let it burst open, and make my death in it."

So it burst open from his chest. It alarmed them only when the blood was flowing toward them, and in the mosque with him was a tent of Banū Ghifār. They said, "O people of the tent, what is this that is coming to us from your side?" And there was Saʿd, his wound gushing blood, and he died of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbbās said: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ḥunayn. Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and I stayed close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and did not leave him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on a white mule of his that Farwah ibn Nufāthah al-Judhāmī had given him as a gift. When the Muslims and the disbelievers met, the Muslims turned back in retreat, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began spurring his mule toward the disbelievers. ʿAbbās said: I was holding the bridle of the mule of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, restraining it so that it would not go fast, and Abū Sufyān was holding the stirrup of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿAbbās, call the people of the tree."

ʿAbbās, who was a man with a loud voice, said: So I called out at the top of my voice, "Where are the people of the tree?" He said: By Allah, when they heard my voice, they turned back toward me like cows turning back to their calves.

They said, "Here we are! Here we are!" He said: And they fought the disbelievers. The call went out to the Anṣār, saying, "O company of the Anṣār! O company of the Anṣār!" Then the call was limited to the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, [saying,] "O Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj! O Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, on his mule, looked toward their fighting as if stretching up over it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Now the oven has become hot."
He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took some pebbles and threw them at the faces of the disbelievers. Then he said:
"By the Lord of Muḥammad, they are defeated!"

He said: I went to look, and the fighting was still as it had been, as far as I could see. He said: By Allah, no sooner had he thrown his pebbles at them than I kept seeing their strength blunted and their affair turning to retreat.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Ḥunayn. And he related the hadith.
except that the hadith of Yūnus and the hadith of Maʿmar are longer and more complete than it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said to him, "O Abū ʿUmārah."
Then he mentioned the hadith, which is shorter than their versions, and these [others] are more complete in their narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he went out on a ship in which was ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī. When the time for one of the prayers came, we asked him to lead us in prayer and said to him, "You are the most entitled of us to that; you are a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." But he refused and said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"Whoever leads the people in prayer and gets it right,
the prayer is for him and for them.
But whoever falls short in any of that, it is against him, and not against them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The brother of Salīm al-Qārī, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, from ʿIkrimah,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Let the best of you call the adhān for you, and let those of you who are the best reciters of the Qurʾān lead you in prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Straighten the rows, align the shoulders, close the gaps, and be gentle in the hands of your brothers."
ʿĪsā did not say, "in the hands of your brothers."
"And do not leave gaps for Satan. Whoever joins a row, Allah will join him [to His mercy], and whoever cuts off a row, Allah will cut him off."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Nāfiʿ said: ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit was late for the Fajr prayer,
so Abū Nuʿaym, the muʾadhdhin, called the iqāmah for the prayer and led the people in prayer. Then ʿUbādah came, and I was with him,

until we formed a row behind Abū Nuʿaym, who was reciting aloud. ʿUbādah began to recite Umm al-Qurʾān [al-Fātiḥah]. When he finished, I said to ʿUbādah, "I heard you reciting Umm al-Qurʾān while Abū Nuʿaym was reciting aloud." He said, "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in one of the prayers in which the recitation is aloud, and the recitation became confused for him. When he finished, he turned to us with his face and said:
"Do you recite when I recite aloud?"
Some of us said, "We do that." He said:
"Do not do so. I was saying to myself, 'Why is the Qurʾān being contested with me?' So do not recite any of the Qurʾān when I recite aloud, except Umm al-Qurʾān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever among you recites {By the fig and the olive} and reaches its end, {Is not Allah the most just of judges?}, let him say, 'Yes, and to that I am among the witnesses.' And whoever recites {I swear by the Day of Resurrection} and reaches {Is He not able to bring the dead to life?}, let him say, 'Yes.' And whoever recites {By those sent forth} and reaches {Then in what statement after it will they believe?}, let him say, 'We believe in Allah.'"

Ismāʿīl said: I went back to the Bedouin man to have him repeat it and to check, and he said, "O son of my brother, do you think I did not memorize it? I have performed Hajj sixty times, and for every one of them I know the camel on which I performed Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Musāfiʿ said, from ʿUtbah ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever doubts in his prayer, let him perform two prostrations after he gives the salām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr alone [narrated] from his father, from Thawbān,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"For every mistake there are two prostrations after the salām."
No one other than ʿAmr mentioned "from his father."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Read] to him while I listened,
– and the wording is his – from Ibn Wahb,
from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from al-Jallāj,
the freed slave of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, that Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān
narrated to him from Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh,
from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
"Friday has twelve hours, in which no Muslim servant asks Allah for anything except that He gives it to him. So seek it in the last hour after ʿAṣr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for rain wearing a black khamīṣah of his. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to take hold of its lower part and make it the upper part, but when it became heavy, he turned it over onto his shoulder.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ in Ṭabaristān, and Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān was with us. He said, "Which of you prayed the fear prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" Ḥudhayfah said, "I did," and he described it, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the fear prayer with one group for one rakʿah, who formed a row behind him, while another group was between him and the enemy. He prayed one rakʿah with the group nearest him, then these withdrew to the positions of the others, and those came, and he prayed one rakʿah with them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When your rulers are the best of you, your wealthy are the most generous of you, and your affairs are decided by consultation among you, then the surface of the earth is better for you than its belly. But when your rulers are the worst of you, your wealthy are the most miserly of you, and your affairs are left to your women, then the belly of the earth is better for you than its surface."
label: machine translation

segments_en: You are in an age in which whoever among you abandons a tenth of what he has been commanded will be destroyed. Then a time will come when whoever among them acts upon a tenth of what he has been commanded will be saved."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Black banners will come out of Khurasan, and nothing will turn them back until they are planted in Īlīyā' (Jerusalem)."
This ḥadīth is gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:
"The truest dreams are those that come before dawn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The dream of a Muslim is one of forty-six parts of prophecy, and it rests on the foot of a bird as long as it is not told; when it is told, it comes to pass."
He said: This ḥadīth is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī's name is Laqīṭ ibn ʿĀmir.
Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated it from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ and said "from Wakīʿ ibn Ḥudus," while Shuʿbah, Abū ʿAwānah and Hushaym said, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Wakīʿ ibn ʿUdus, and this is more correct.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Dreams are of three kinds: a true dream; a dream in which a man talks to himself; and a distressing dream from Satan. So whoever sees something he dislikes, let him get up and pray." And he used to say:
"I like the shackle and dislike the iron collar; the shackle represents firmness in the religion." And he used to say:
"Whoever sees me, then it is truly I, for Satan cannot take my form." And he used to say:
"Do not relate a dream except to a scholar or a well-wisher."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever lies about a dream he claims to have seen will be made on the Day of Resurrection to tie a knot in a grain of barley."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about Waraqah, and Khadījah said to him: "He believed you, but he died before your mission became manifest."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I was shown him in a dream wearing white garments; had he been among the people of the Fire, he would have been wearing other than that."
He said: This ḥadīth is gharīb.
ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is not considered strong by the scholars of ḥadīth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The best of people are my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them. Then lying will spread, until a man will bear witness without being asked to testify, and a man will swear an oath without being asked to swear."
As for the meaning of the Prophet's ﷺ saying:
"The best of witnesses is the one who comes with his testimony before he is asked for it."
According to us, it is when a man has been made a witness to something: he should give his testimony and not refrain from testifying. This is how some of the people of knowledge explain the ḥadīth.
The Book of Testimonies is completed, praise be to Allah, and it is followed by the Book of Zuhd (Asceticism).
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Hasten to do good deeds before seven [things befall you]. Are you waiting for anything but poverty that makes one forget, or wealth that makes one rebellious, or sickness that corrupts, or old age that confuses the mind, or sudden death, or the Dajjāl—for he is the worst unseen thing awaited—or the Hour? And the Hour is most grievous and most bitter."

He said: This ḥadīth is ḥasan gharīb. We do not know it from the narration of al-Aʿraj from Abū Hurayrah except through the narration of Muḥarrar ibn Hārūn. Bishr ibn ʿUmar and others have also narrated from this Muḥarrar ibn Hārūn.
Maʿmar narrated this ḥadīth from someone who heard Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly. And he said: "you are waiting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man among his Companions died, and someone said, "Receive glad tidings of Paradise."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you not know? Perhaps he spoke about what did not concern him, or was stingy with something that would not have diminished him."
He said: This ḥadīth is gharīb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever a man saw a dream, he would relate it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So I wished to see a dream that I could relate to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: I was a young, unmarried man, and I used to sleep in the mosque in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. In my sleep I saw two angels take hold of me and go with me to the Fire. It was built up inside like the lining of a well, and it had two posts like the two posts of a well, and in it were people whom I recognized. I began to say: "I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire! I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire! I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire!" He said: Then another angel met them and said to me: "Do not be afraid."
I related it to Ḥafṣah, and Ḥafṣah related it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"What an excellent man ʿAbdullāh is, if only he would pray at night."
Sālim said: After that, ʿAbdullāh would sleep only a little at night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me and Fāṭimah at night and woke us for prayer. Then he returned to his house and prayed for a good part of the night, but he heard no sound from us. So he came back to us and woke us, saying: "Get up and pray."
He said: I sat up, rubbing my eyes, and said: "By Allah, we only pray what Allah has decreed for us. Our souls are in the hand of Allah.
If He wishes to raise us, He raises us." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away, striking his thigh with his hand and saying:
"We only pray what Allah has decreed for us" — {But man is, more than anything, argumentative.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah,
that she said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray the voluntary Ḍuḥā prayer.
And I pray it myself. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would leave off a deed that he loved to do, fearing that the people would act upon it and it would then be made obligatory for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about the deeds of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: He loved what was constant.
He said: I asked: At what time would he pray? She said: When he heard the crier, he would get up and pray.
label: machine translation

segments_en: My father mentioned, from Abū Salamah,
from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The pre-dawn time never found him with me except asleep. She meant the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prolonged the prayer so much that I considered doing something bad. It was asked: What did you consider doing? He said: I considered sitting down and leaving him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"O ʿAbdullāh, have I not been told that you fast during the day and stand in prayer at night?"
I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Do not do so. Fast and break your fast, stand in prayer and sleep,
for your body has a right over you,
your eyes have a right over you,
your wife has a right over you,
and your visitors have a right over you.
It is enough for you to fast three days every month,
for you will have for every good deed ten like it,
and that is fasting for a lifetime." But I was strict, so it was made strict for me.
I said: O Messenger of Allah,
I find I have strength. He said:
"Then fast the fast of the Prophet of Allah Dāwūd, peace be upon him, and do not add to it."
I asked: What was the fast of the Prophet of Allah Dāwūd, peace be upon him? He said: "Half of a lifetime."
After he grew old, ʿAbdullāh used to say: If only I had accepted the concession of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would pray two rakʿahs; if I was awake, he would talk with me, and if not, he would lie down.
I said to Sufyān: Some of them narrate it as the two rakʿahs of Fajr.
Sufyān said: That is it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hasten to any of the voluntary prayers more than to the two rakʿahs before Fajr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The night prayer of the Prophet ﷺ was thirteen rakʿahs. Of these he would pray five as Witr, not sitting in any of them except in the last of them. When the muezzin gave the call, he would get up and pray two light rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sulayk al-Ghaṭafānī came on Friday while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering the sermon, and he sat down. He said to him:
"O Sulayk, get up and pray two rakʿahs, and keep them brief." Then he said: "When one of you comes on Friday while the imam is delivering the sermon, let him pray two rakʿahs and keep them brief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Khaybar, and we travelled by night. A man among the people said to ʿĀmir ibn al-Akwaʿ, "Will you not let us hear some of your verses?" ʿĀmir was a poet, so he got down and began chanting for the people, saying: "O Allah, were it not for You we would not have been guided, nor would we have given charity, nor prayed. So forgive us, may we be ransomed for You, for what we have done, and make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy], and send down tranquility upon us. When we are called, we respond, and they have relied on shouting against us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
Who is this driver [of the camels]?" They said, "ʿĀmir." He said, "May Allah have mercy on him."
A man among the people said, "It is now obligatory [for him, martyrdom], O Messenger of Allah! If only you had let us enjoy his company longer."
He said: Then we came to Khaybar and besieged them until severe hunger afflicted us. Then he said, "
Allah has opened it for you."
He said: When evening came on the day that it was conquered for them, the people lit many fires. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "
What are these fires? Over what are you lighting them?"
They said, "Over meat." He said, "What meat?"
They said, "The meat of domestic donkeys."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Pour it out and break the pots."
A man said, "Or may we pour it out and wash them?" He said, "Or that."

He said: When the people lined up in ranks, ʿĀmir's sword was short. He reached with it for the leg of a Jew to strike him, but the edge of his sword turned back and struck ʿĀmir's knee, and he died from it. He said: When they returned, Salamah said, while holding my hand: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me silent, he said, "What is the matter with you?"
I said to him, "May my father and mother be your ransom! They claim that ʿĀmir's deeds have come to nothing." He said, "Who said that?"
I said, "So-and-so, so-and-so, and Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr al-Anṣārī." He said, "
The one who said that has lied. He will have a double reward."
And he joined his two fingers together, [and said,] "
He was truly one who strove earnestly and fought in the cause of Allah. Few Arabs have walked the earth the like of him."
Qutaybah differed from Muḥammad in the ḥadīth in two words, and in the narration of Ibn ʿAbbād [it reads]: "and send down tranquility upon us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Khaybar, a man came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the donkeys have been eaten."

Then another came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the donkeys have been wiped out." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Abū Ṭalḥah, who called out, "Allah and His Messenger forbid you the meat of donkeys, for it is filthy," or "unclean."
He said: So the pots were overturned with what was in them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the mark of a blow on the shin of Salamah,
and I said, "O Abū Muslim,
what is this blow?" He said, "This is a blow I received on the day of Khaybar,
and the people said, 'Salamah has been struck down.'
So I went to the Prophet ﷺ, and he blew on it three times,
and I have not felt any pain from it until this moment."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stayed three days with Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab on the road to Khaybar, when he consummated the marriage with her. Then she was among those for whom the veil was drawn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stayed three nights between Khaybar and Madinah, consummating his marriage with Ṣafiyyah.
I invited the Muslims to his wedding feast,
and there was neither bread nor meat in it.
All that was in it was that he commanded Bilāl to bring the leather mats, and they were spread out,
and dates, dried yogurt, and ghee were put upon them.
The Muslims said, "Is she one of the Mothers of the Believers,
or one whom his right hand possesses?" They said, "If he veils her, she is one of the Mothers of the Believers,
and if he does not veil her, she is one whom his right hand possesses."
When he set off, he seated her behind him and drew the veil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it because they were the people's beasts of burden and he disliked that their beasts of burden be lost, or whether he forbade the meat of domestic donkeys absolutely on the day of Khaybar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I met Bilāl, the muʾadhdhin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in Aleppo, and I said: "O Bilāl, tell me how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ managed his expenses." He said: "He had nothing; I was the one in charge of that for him from the time Allah sent him until he died. Whenever a person came to him as a Muslim and he saw him unclothed, he would order me, so I would go and borrow, and buy him a cloak, and clothe him and feed him. Then a man from among the polytheists confronted me and said: 'O Bilāl, I have plenty of means, so do not borrow from anyone except me.' I did so. Then one day, after I had performed ablution and stood to call the adhān for prayer, there was the polytheist approaching with a group of merchants. When he saw me, he said: 'O Abyssinian!'
I said: 'At your service.'
He scowled at me and spoke harshly to me, and said to me: 'Do you know how long remains between you and the month?' I said: 'It is near.'

He said: 'There are only four days between you and it, and then I will seize you for what you owe, and I will send you back to herding sheep as you were before.' So there took hold of me what takes hold of people. Then, when I had prayed the night prayer, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned to his family. I asked permission to see him and he permitted me. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, the polytheist from whom I used to take loans said such and such to me, and you do not have what is needed to pay on my behalf, nor do I, and he will disgrace me. So permit me to go off to some of these tribes who have accepted Islam, until Allah provides His Messenger ﷺ with what will pay on my behalf.' Then I went out until I reached my house, and I placed my sword, my bag, my sandals and my shield by my head. When the first thread of dawn split, I wanted to set off, and there was a person running and calling: 'O Bilāl, answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!' So I went until I came to him, and there were four loaded camels kneeling with their loads. I asked permission, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Rejoice, for Allah has brought you what settles your debt." Then he said:
"Did you not see the four kneeling camels?" I said: "Yes." He said:
"You have them and what is on them. On them are clothing and food, which the ruler of Fadak gave me as a gift. Take them and pay off your debt."
I did so—and he mentioned the rest of the hadith—then I went to the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the mosque. I greeted him with salām and he said:
"What has become of what you had?"
I said: "Allah has paid off everything that was owed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and nothing remains." He said: "Is there anything left over?"
I said: "Yes." He said:
"See that you relieve me of it, for I will not enter upon any of my family until you relieve me of it."
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had prayed the night prayer, he called me and said:
"What has become of what you had?"
I said: "It is still with me; no one has come to us."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spent the night in the mosque—and he related the rest of the hadith—until, when he had prayed the night prayer, meaning the next day, he called me and said:
"What has become of what you had?"
I said: "Allah has relieved you of it, O Messenger of Allah."

He said "Allāhu akbar" and praised Allah, out of fear that death might overtake him while that was still with him. Then I followed him until he came to his wives and greeted each wife in turn, until he reached the place where he would spend the night. This is what you asked me about."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the meaning of the chain of Abū Tawbah and his report. He said, at the saying:
"what will pay on my behalf."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent toward me, and I took it as a hint.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ granted him a piece of land in Hadramawt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ marked out a house for me in Medina with a bow, and said: "I will give you more, I will give you more."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One,
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī the mines of al-Qabaliyyah, which lie on the side of al-Furʿ. Nothing is taken from those mines except zakāh, to this day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ granted Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī the mines of al-Qabaliyyah, its highlands and its lowlands—and someone other than al-ʿAbbās said, its highland and its lowland—and wherever crops can be grown in Quds, and he did not give him the right of any Muslim. And the Prophet ﷺ wrote for him:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, gave to Bilāl ibn al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī: he gave him the mines of al-Qabaliyyah, its highlands and its lowlands."
And someone other than al-ʿAbbās said: "its highland and its lowland."
"And wherever crops can be grown in Quds, and he did not give him the right of any Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Any Muslim man who frees a Muslim man, it will be his ransom from the Fire, each limb of the freed man redeeming a limb of his own. And any Muslim man who frees two Muslim women, they will be his ransom from the Fire, each limb of the two redeeming a limb of his own. And any Muslim woman who frees a Muslim woman, she will be her ransom from the Fire, each limb of the freed woman redeeming a limb of her own. Abū ʿĪsā said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb from this route. Abū ʿĪsā said: In this hadith is an indication that freeing male slaves is better for men than freeing female slaves, because of the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Whoever frees a Muslim man, it will be his ransom from the Fire, each limb of the freed man redeeming a limb of his own.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people used to seek out the day of ʿĀʾishah to give their gifts. She said: My fellow wives gathered with Umm Salamah and said: O Umm Salamah, the people seek out the day of ʿĀʾishah to give their gifts, while we desire the good just as ʿĀʾishah desires it. So speak to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he orders the people to give him gifts wherever he may be. Umm Salamah mentioned that, and he turned away from her. Then he came back to her and she repeated the words. She said: O Messenger of Allah, my fellow wives have mentioned that the people seek out the day of ʿĀʾishah to give their gifts, so order the people to give gifts wherever you may be.
When it was the third time, she said that, and he said:
"O Umm Salamah, do not harm me regarding ʿĀʾishah, for the revelation did not come to me while I was in the bedcover of any woman among you except her."
Some of them have narrated this hadith from Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, as a mursal report.

This hadith is ḥasan gharīb. This hadith has also been narrated from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿAwf ibn al-Ḥārith, from Rumaythah, from Umm Salamah, something of this. And this hadith has been narrated from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah with various versions.
Sulaymān ibn Bilāl also narrated from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, similar to the hadith of Ḥammād ibn Zayd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She mentioned a number of poor people (Abū Dāwūd said: and someone else said, "or a number of charity items"), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"Give, and do not keep count, or it will be counted against you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended to travel, he would draw lots among his wives,
and whichever of them the lot came out for, he would take her with him.
He would also allot to each of his wives her day and her night,
except that Sawdah bint Zamʿah gave up her day and her night
to ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, seeking by that the pleasure of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the major sins,
or he was asked about the major sins, and he said: "Associating partners with Allah, killing a person, and disobedience to parents." Then he said:
"Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins? He said: False speech," or he said, "false testimony."
Shuʿbah said: Most of my thinking is that he said, "false testimony."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That his mother, Umm Kulthūm bint ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, who was
among the first emigrant women who pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that she heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying:
"The liar is not the one who reconciles between people, speaking good and conveying good."

Ibn Shihāb said: I have not heard that any concession was given regarding anything people say that is untrue, except in three cases: war, reconciling between people, and a man's talk with his wife and a woman's talk with her husband.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I fell ill, and the Prophet ﷺ visited me. I said: O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah not to turn me back on my heels. He said:
"Perhaps Allah will raise you up and benefit people through you."
I said: I want to make a bequest,
and I have only one daughter. I said: Shall I bequeath half? He said: "Half is too much." I said: Then a third. He said: "A third,
and a third is much," or "large."
He said: So people bequeath a third,
and that was permitted for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he met Abū Hurayrah, and Abū Hurayrah said, "I ask Allah to bring us together
in the marketplace of Paradise."
Saʿīd said, "Is there a marketplace there?" He said, "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed me:

'When the people of Paradise enter it, they settle in it according to the merit of their deeds. Then they are permitted, for a length of time equal to a Friday of this world, to visit their Lord. His Throne is made manifest to them, and He appears to them in one of the gardens of Paradise. Pulpits of light are set up for them, and pulpits of pearl, pulpits of ruby, pulpits of chrysolite, pulpits of gold, and pulpits of silver. The lowest of them, though none among them is truly low, sits upon dunes of musk and camphor, not considering that those on the chairs have a better seat than they.'"
Abū Hurayrah said, "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord?' He said:
'Yes. Do you have any doubt about seeing the sun and the moon on the night of the full moon?' We said, 'No.' He said:

'In the same way you will have no doubt about seeing your Lord. No man will remain in that gathering except that Allah will converse with him directly, until He says to one of them, "O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, do you remember the day you said such and such?" and He reminds him of some of his betrayals in the world. He says, "My Lord, have You not forgiven me?" He says, "Indeed; it was by the vastness of My forgiveness that you reached this station of yours."

While they are in that state, a cloud covers them from above and rains down upon them a fragrance the like of whose scent they had never found. Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says, "Arise to the honor that I have prepared for you, and take whatever you desire."

He said: 'Then we come to a marketplace surrounded by the angels, in which is what no eye has seen the like of, no ear has heard, and no heart has imagined. What we desire is carried for us; nothing is bought or sold in it. In that marketplace the people of Paradise meet one another. A man of high station approaches and meets one below him, though none among them is truly low, and he is amazed by the clothing he sees on him; but before the end of his conversation, something finer than it appears to him. That is because it is not fitting for anyone to feel sorrow there. Then we return to our dwellings, and our wives meet us and say, "Welcome! You have come back with even greater beauty than when you left us."
We say, "Today we sat with our Lord, the Almighty, and it is fitting for us to return as we have returned."'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When a believer desires a child in Paradise, its conception, birth, and growth to full age take place in an hour, just as he desires."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Three are loved by Allah and three are hated by Allah. As for those whom Allah loves: a man who came to some people and asked them by Allah, not by any kinship between him and them, and they refused him, so a man lagged behind them and gave him secretly, none knowing of his gift except Allah and the one who gave it; and a people who traveled through their night until, when sleep was dearer to them than anything comparable, they alighted and laid down their heads, and one of them stood up, beseeching Me and reciting My verses; and a man who was in a military detachment and met the enemy, and they were routed, and he faced them with his chest until he was killed or victory was granted to him.
And the three whom Allah hates are: the old man who commits adultery, the arrogant poor man, and the wealthy oppressor."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: {O you who believe, fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.} Then he said:
"If a single drop of zaqqūm were to fall upon the earth, it would spoil the livelihood of the people of the world. So what of the one who has no food other than it?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Fire was kindled for a thousand years until it turned red, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it turned white, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it turned black. So it is black and dark."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When you see a man who regularly attends the mosque, bear witness that he has faith, for Allah the Exalted says:
'The mosques of Allah are only maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, and give zakāh.'" [the verse]
label: machine translation

segments_en: His name is Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdullāh al-Hamdānī al-Kūfī. He said: Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad narrated to us,
from Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq,
from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī,
from Abū Juḥayfah, from ʿAlī,
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"Whoever commits an offense that carries a prescribed punishment and is punished for it promptly in this world, Allah is too just to double the punishment for His servant in the Hereafter. And whoever commits an offense that carries a prescribed punishment and Allah conceals it for him and pardons him, Allah is too generous to return to something He has already pardoned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was invited to pray over him, so he got up and went to him. When he stood over him, intending to pray, I turned and stood in front of his chest and said, "O Messenger of Allah, [are you praying] over the enemy of Allah, ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, who said on such-and-such a day such-and-such and such-and-such?" counting off his days.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was smiling, until when I had said too much to him, he said:
"Step back from me, ʿUmar.
I was given a choice and I chose. It was said to me:

'Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them.' If I knew that by adding to the seventy he would be forgiven, I would add."

He said: Then he prayed over him, walked with him, and stood at his grave until it was finished. He said: I was amazed at my boldness toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah and His Messenger know best. By Allah, it was only a short while until these two verses were revealed:

"And never pray over any of them who has died, and do not stand at his grave," to the end of the verse. He said: After that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never prayed over a hypocrite or stood at his grave until Allah took him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to Madinah, and a sickness had broken out there.

I sat with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him. A funeral procession passed by them, and the people praised its occupant well. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "It is obligatory."
Then another passed, and they praised its occupant well,
and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "It is obligatory."
Then a third passed,
and they spoke ill of its occupant, and he said, "It is obligatory."
Abū al-Aswad said: I asked, "What is obligatory, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: I said as the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Any Muslim for whom four people testify to good, Allah will admit him to Paradise."
We said, "And three?" He said, "And three."
We said, "And two?" He said, "And two."
Then we did not ask him about one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mālik [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left the slain of Badr for three days, then he came to them, stood over them and called out to them, saying:

"O Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, O Umayyah ibn Khalaf, O ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, O Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah, have you not found what your Lord promised to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true."
ʿUmar heard the words of the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, how can they hear, and how can they answer when they have become carcasses?" He said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, you do not hear what I say better than they do, but they are unable to answer."
Then he ordered that they be dragged away, and they were thrown into the well of Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out after the sun had set and heard a sound, and he said:
"Jews are being punished in their graves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And I did not hear anyone who heard from the Prophet,
ﷺ, anything other than this. She said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Give charity, for a time will come upon you when a man will walk about with his charity,
and will not find anyone to accept it. The man will say, 'If you had brought it yesterday I would have accepted it,
but today I have no need of it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were commanded to give charity.

He said: We used to carry loads for hire. He said: Abū ʿAqīl gave half a ṣāʿ in charity, and another person came with something more than that. The hypocrites said, "Allah has no need of this man's charity, and this other one only did it to show off." Then it was revealed: {Those who criticize the volunteers among the believers concerning charities, and those who find nothing except their effort} [9:79]. Bishr did not pronounce the word "al-muṭṭawwiʿīn" [as the others did].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us to give charity, and one of us would find nothing to give in charity until he went to the market and carried a load on his back, and came with a mudd, and gave it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I know today a man who has a hundred thousand, [yet] on that day he did not have a single dirham.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was informed that ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: A woman came to me with her two daughters and asked me for something, but she found nothing with me except a single date, so I gave it to her. She took it and divided it between her two daughters and did not eat any of it herself. Then she got up and left, she and her two daughters. The Prophet ﷺ then came in to me and I told him her story, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever is tested with anything through daughters and treats them well, they will be a shield for him from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A month would come upon the family of Muhammad ﷺ in which no smoke was seen in any of their houses.

I said, "Then what was their food?" She said, "The two black things: dates and water. However, we had neighbors from the Anṣār, good neighbors, who had milch animals, and they used to send him some of their milk."
Muhammad said: And they were nine households
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said this] several times: "
By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the family of Muhammad has not had in the morning a ṣāʿ of grain or a ṣāʿ of dates."
And at that time he had nine wives.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The family of Muhammad has had in the morning nothing but a mudd of food," or [he said]: "
The family of Muhammad has not had in the morning a mudd of food."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, and we stayed three nights unable—or [he] was unable—to find food.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought hot food and he ate. When he had finished, he said: "
Praise be to Allah. No hot food has entered my stomach since such and such a time."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought to me [as a bride], and our bed on the night she was brought was nothing but a ram's skin.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a domed tent at the door of a man from the Anṣār and said, "What is this?"
They said, "A dome that so-and-so built."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Every possession that is like this will be a burden on its owner on the Day of Resurrection."

The Anṣārī heard of that and tore it down. Later the Prophet ﷺ passed by and did not see it, so he asked about it and was told that he had torn it down when he heard what [the Prophet ﷺ] had said. He said: "
May Allah have mercy on him, may Allah have mercy on him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Sawāʾ,
the two sons of Khālid, said: We entered upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was working on something, so we helped him with it. He said: "
Do not despair of provision as long as your heads move, for a person is born to his mother red, without any skin on him, and then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, provides for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger ﷺ said: "

In the heart of the son of Adam there is a branch in every valley. Whoever follows his heart into all the branches, Allah will not care in which valley He destroys him; and whoever relies on Allah, He will suffice him against these branchings."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me, and be brief." He said: "
When you stand in your prayer, pray the prayer of one bidding farewell; do not say anything you will have to apologize for; and resolve to give up hope in what is in the hands of people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

The likeness of one who sits and listens to wisdom, then reports about his companion only the worst of what he hears, is that of a man who came to a shepherd and said, 'O shepherd, give me a sheep from your flock to slaughter.'
He said, 'Go and take the best of them by the ear.'
So he went and took the ear of the flock's dog."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever humbles himself for Allah, the Glorified, by one degree, Allah raises him by one degree; and whoever acts arrogantly against Allah by one degree, Allah lowers him by one degree, until He puts him in the lowest of the low."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Every religion has a characteristic, and the characteristic of Islam is modesty."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he said: "
The delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays has come to you."

Yet no one was seen. While we were like that, they came and dismounted and went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Ashajj al-ʿAṣarī stayed behind; he came later, dismounted at a lodging, made his camel kneel, put his clothes to one side, and then came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "
O Ashajj, you have two qualities that Allah loves: forbearance and deliberateness."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, is it something I was created with, or something that newly arose in me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Rather, it is something you were created with."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
There is no sip greater in reward with Allah than a sip of anger that a servant swallows, seeking the Face of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out, and we set out with him. When he reached Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, he prayed the Ẓuhr prayer, then mounted his riding animal. When it stood upright with him on al-Baydāʾ, he declared the intention for Hajj and ʿUmrah together, and we declared it with him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Makkah and we had performed the circuit of the Kaʿbah, he ordered the people to come out of iḥrām, but the people hesitated. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them:
"Had I not brought the sacrificial animal with me, I would have come out of iḥrām."

So the people came out of iḥrām, even to the point of having relations with their wives, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not come out of iḥrām, nor did he shorten his hair, until the Day of Sacrifice.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ performed only one circuit [of the Kaʿbah].
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar
used to walk briskly for three [rounds] and walk normally for four, and he maintained that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam informed us; they both said: Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from his father,
from Kathīr ibn Farqad, from Nāfiʿ,
that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar
used to walk briskly in his circuits when he arrived for Hajj or ʿUmrah, for three [rounds], and walk normally for four. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ circled the House seven times, walking briskly for three of them and walking normally for four. Then he stood at the Station [of Ibrāhīm] and prayed two rakʿahs. Then he recited: {And take the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer}, raising his voice so the people could hear. Then he turned away and touched the Stone, then went out, and said:
"We begin with what Allah began with."
So he began with Ṣafā and climbed it until the House came into view for him, and he said three times:
"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things."

He declared Allah's greatness and praised Him, then made supplication as was decreed for him. Then he came down walking until his feet descended into the bottom of the valley, and he ran until his feet climbed out of it. Then he walked until he reached Marwah and climbed it. Then the House came into view for him, and he said:
"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things."
He said that three times, then remembered Allah, glorified Him and praised Him, then made supplication there as Allah willed. He did this until he finished the circuits.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out toward Ṣafā and said:
"We begin with what Allah began with." Then he recited:
{Indeed, Ṣafā and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ climbed Ṣafā until, when he looked at the House, he declared Allah's greatness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
and the wording is his, from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Jābir,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he stood on Ṣafā, would declare Allah's greatness three times and say:
"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things."
He would do that three times and make supplication, and he would do the same on Marwah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ﷺ Then the Prophet ﷺ stood on Ṣafā, proclaiming that there is no god but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and making supplication in between.
label: machine translation

segments_en: They asked Ibn ʿUmar: Did you see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walk briskly between Ṣafā and Marwah? He said: He was among a group of people and they walked briskly, and I only saw them do so because of his walking briskly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It was] read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father,
from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh,

may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he came down from Ṣafā, would walk until, when his feet descended into the bottom of the valley, he would run until he came out of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the feet of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ descended into the bottom of the valley, he walked briskly until he came out of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Marwah and climbed it. Then the House came into view for him, and he said:
"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things."
He said that three times, then remembered Allah, glorified Him and praised Him, then made supplication as Allah willed. He did this until he finished the circuits.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Banī Isrāʾīl, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ṭā Hā, and al-Anbiyāʾ are among the earliest and finest [revelations], and they are among my oldest treasured possessions.
They are among my oldest treasured possessions.
Qatādah said: {jadhādhan} means He broke them into pieces.
Al-Ḥasan said: {in a orbit (falak)} is like the whorl of a spindle; {they swim} means they revolve.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: {nafashat} means [the sheep] grazed [at night]; {yuṣḥabūn} means they are prevented.
{This community of yours is one community}: he said, your religion is one religion. ʿIkrimah said:
