The Prophet of Allah ﷺ prayed, then gave the salām to his right and to his left until we saw the whiteness of his cheeks. Then he turned away, as Abū Rimthah turned away—meaning himself. Then the man who had caught the first takbīr with him stood up to pray additional [rakʿahs]. ʿUmar leapt to him, took him by the shoulder, shook him, and said: Sit! The People of the Book were destroyed only because there was no separation between their prayers.
So the Prophet ﷺ raised his gaze and said:
"Allah has set you right, O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer, in the same meaning as Ḥammād's entire report up to the end of his words: I was told that ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said: then he gave the salām.
He said: I asked: And the tashahhud? He said: I did not hear anything about the tashahhud, but I prefer that he recite the tashahhud. He did not mention that he used to call him Dhū al-Yadayn.
Nor did he mention: "so they gestured."
Nor did he mention the anger. And the hadith of Ḥammād from Ayyūb is more complete.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Hishām,
and Yaḥyā ibn ʿAtīq, and Ibn
ʿAwn, from Muḥammad,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, in the story of Dhū al-Yadayn, that he said the takbīr and prostrated.
Hishām, meaning Ibn Ḥassān, said: He said the takbīr, then said the takbīr again and prostrated.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said that he had committed adultery.
He turned away from him, but the man repeated it several times, and each time he turned away from him. Then he asked the man's people, "Is he insane?"
They said, "There is nothing wrong with him." He said, "Did you do it with her?" The man said, "Yes."
So he ordered that he be stoned. He was taken away and stoned, and [the Prophet ﷺ] did not pray over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Shuʿbah said: I asked Simāk about the kuthbah, and he said, "A small amount of milk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Māʿiz ibn Mālik came to the Prophet ﷺ and confessed to adultery twice, so he sent him away. Then he came and confessed to adultery twice, and [the Prophet ﷺ] said,
"You have testified against yourself four times. Take him away and stone him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ — and a second chain: Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb and ʿUqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, both saying: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us: my father narrated to us, saying: I heard Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm narrate from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said to Māʿiz ibn Mālik,
"Perhaps you kissed her, or touched her, or looked at her." He said, "No." He said, "Did you have intercourse with her?" He said, "Yes."
He said: At that point he ordered that he be stoned.
Mūsā did not mention [it] from Ibn ʿAbbās, and this is the wording of Wahb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The man of the Aslam tribe came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and testified against himself four times that he had had unlawful relations with a woman, and each time the Prophet ﷺ turned away from him. Then he came forward the fifth time, and [the Prophet ﷺ] said, "Did you have intercourse with her?" He said, "Yes." He said,
"Until that part of you disappeared into that part of her?" He said, "Yes." He said,
"As the kohl stick disappears in the kohl container, and the rope in the well?" He said, "Yes." He said,
"Do you know what adultery is?"
He said, "Yes. I did with her unlawfully what a man does with his wife lawfully." He said,
"So what do you want by this statement?"
He said, "I want you to purify me."

So he ordered that he be stoned, and he was stoned. Then the Prophet ﷺ heard two of his Companions, one of whom said to the other, "Look at this man whom Allah had concealed, yet his own self would not leave him until he was stoned like a dog."
He was silent about them. Then he walked on for a while until he passed the carcass of a donkey with its leg raised, and he said,
"Where are so-and-so and so-and-so?"
They said, "Here we are, Messenger of Allah." He said,
"Get down and eat from the carcass of this donkey."
They said, "Prophet of Allah, who would eat from this?" He said,
"What you two have just taken from the honor of your brother is worse than eating from it. By the One in whose hand is my soul, he is now in the rivers of Paradise, dipping himself in them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ ordered that Māʿiz ibn Mālik be stoned, we took him out to al-Baqīʿ. By Allah, we did not tie him, nor did we dig a pit for him, but he stood [still] for us.

Abū Kāmil said: We threw bones, clods of earth, and pieces of pottery at him, and he ran, and we ran after him until he reached the broad side of the Ḥarrah, where he stood for us, and we threw the large stones of the Ḥarrah at him until he fell silent. He said: [The Prophet ﷺ] neither asked forgiveness for him nor cursed him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ had Māʿiz's breath smelled.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, used to say that if al-Ghāmidiyyah and Māʿiz ibn Mālik had retracted after their confession, or he said, if they had not returned after their confession, he would not have pursued them; he only had them stoned at the fourth [confession].
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he
was sitting working in the market when a woman carrying a baby passed by, and the people stirred up around her, and I stirred with those who stirred. I reached the Prophet ﷺ as he was saying,
"Who is the father of this [child] with you?"
She remained silent, and a young man beside her said, "I am his father, Messenger of Allah."
Then [the Prophet ﷺ] turned to her and said,
"Who is the father of this [child] with you?"
The young man said, "I am his father, Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at some of those around him, asking them about him, and they said, "We know nothing about him except good."
The Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Are you married?" He said, "Yes."
So he ordered that he be stoned, and he was stoned.

He said: We took him out and dug a pit for him as far as we could, then we threw stones at him until he was still. Then a man came asking about the one who had been stoned, so we took him to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "This man has come asking about the wicked one."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"He is indeed better in the sight of Allah than the fragrance of musk."
It turned out that he was his father, and [the Prophet ﷺ] helped him with washing him, shrouding him, and burying him. I do not know whether he also mentioned praying over him or not.
This is the narration of ʿAbdah, and it is more complete.
label: machine translation

segments_en: from the Prophet ﷺ, with part of this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ...Hurayrah, both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Honor is His lower garment and greatness is His cloak. Whoever contends with Me over them, I will punish him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated:

"A man said, 'By Allah, Allah will not forgive so-and-so,' and Allah the Exalted said, 'Who is he who swears by Me that I will not forgive so-and-so? I have forgiven so-and-so, and I have nullified your deed.'"
Or as he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Many a person with disheveled hair, turned away from doors, would have his oath fulfilled by Allah if he swore by Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to me:
"Do not belittle any act of kindness, even if it is meeting your brother with a cheerful face."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A poor woman came to me carrying her two daughters, and I gave her three dates. She gave each of them a date, and raised one date to her mouth to eat it, but her two daughters asked her for it. So she split the date she had wanted to eat between them. Her situation amazed me, so I mentioned what she had done to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
"Allah has made Paradise obligatory for her because of it," or, "He has freed her from the Fire because of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever supports two girls until they reach maturity will come on the Day of Resurrection, he and I," and he joined his fingers together.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to some women of the Ansar:
"None of you will lose three children and be patient, hoping for reward, except that she will enter Paradise."
One of the women said, "Or two, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Or two."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were at ʿArafah when ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who was in charge of the pilgrimage season, passed by, and the people stood looking at him. I said to my father, "Father, I think Allah loves ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz."
He said, "Why is that?" I said, "Because of the love he has in people's hearts."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not mention Anas's statement, "So I love..." and what follows it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I and the Messenger of Allah,
ﷺ, were going out of the mosque, we met a man at the gate of the mosque. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"What have you prepared for it?"
The man seemed to become subdued, then said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have not prepared for it much prayer, fasting, or charity, but I love Allah and His Messenger." He said:
"Then you are with those whom you love."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Relating it from the Prophet ﷺ, he said:

"The angel enters upon the drop of fluid forty or forty-five nights after it settles in the womb and says, 'My Lord, wretched or happy?' and the two are written. Then he says, 'My Lord, male or female?' and the two are written. His deeds, his footsteps, his term, and his provision are written. Then the pages are rolled up, and nothing is added to them or taken away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wretched one is he who was wretched in his mother's womb, and the happy one is he who takes admonition from others.

He then came to a man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd al-Ghifārī and told him that, from the words of Ibn Masʿūd. He said, "How can a man be wretched without any deed?" The man said to him, "Do you find that astonishing? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"When forty-two nights have passed over the drop of fluid, Allah sends an angel to it, who shapes it and creates its hearing, its sight, its skin, its flesh, and its bones. Then
he says, 'My Lord, male or female?' and your Lord decrees what He wills, and the angel writes. Then he says, 'My Lord, his term?'
and your Lord says what He wills, and the angel writes. Then he says, 'My Lord, his provision?'
and your Lord decrees what He wills, and the angel writes. Then the angel goes out with the page in his hand, adding nothing to what he was commanded and subtracting nothing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I visited Abū Sarīḥah Ḥudhayfah ibn Asīd al-Ghifārī, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, with these two ears of mine:
"The drop of fluid remains in the womb for forty nights, then the angel forms it."
Zuhayr said: I think he said, "the one who creates it."

"He says, 'My Lord, male or female?' and Allah makes it male or female. Then he says, 'My Lord, sound or unsound?' and Allah makes it sound or unsound. Then he says, 'My Lord, what is his provision, what is his term, what is his character?' Then Allah makes him wretched or happy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade carrying weapons in the lands of Islam on the two Eids, unless they were in the presence of the enemy.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform a full bath (ghusl) on the day of Fiṭr, the day of Naḥr, and the day of ʿArafah, and al-Fākih used to command his family to bathe on these days.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"Every two units of prayer include a salām."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā,
from Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Jahḍamī,
from an-Naḍr ibn Shaybān,
Transfer of chain: and Yaḥyā ibn Ḥakīm narrated to us,
Abū Dāwūd narrated to us,
Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Jahḍamī narrated to us,
and al-Qāsim ibn al-Faḍl al-Ḥuddānī,
both of them from an-Naḍr ibn Shaybān, who said:
I met Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān and said, "Narrate to me a hadith that you heard from
your father, mentioning the month of Ramadan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The mother of Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd said to Sulaymān, 'My son, do not sleep much at night, for sleeping much at night leaves a man poor on the Day of Resurrection.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever prays much at night, his face becomes beautiful by day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ came to us after he had lost his sight. I greeted him, and he said, "Who are you?" So I told him.
He said, "Welcome, son of my brother. It has reached me that you have a beautiful voice in reciting the Qur'an. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:

'This Qur'an was revealed with sorrow, so when you recite it, weep; and if you do not weep, then force yourselves to weep. And recite it in a melodious manner, for whoever does not recite it melodiously is not one of us.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wife of the Prophet ﷺ said: I was late one night after the ʿIshāʾ prayer during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then I came, and he said, "Where were you?"
I said, "I was listening to the recitation of a man among your Companions; I have never heard the like of his recitation and his voice from anyone."
She said: So he got up and I got up with him until he listened to him. Then he turned to me and said, "This is Sālim,
the freed slave of Abū Ḥudhayfah.
Praise be to Allah who has placed among my nation the like of this man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Among the people with the finest voices in reciting the Qur'an is
the one who, when you hear him reciting,
you think that he fears Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah listens more attentively to a man with a beautiful voice reciting the Qur'an aloud than the owner of a singing girl listens to his singing girl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Beautify the Qur'an with your voices."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I memorized the Qur'an and recited all of it in one night. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I fear that time will drag on for you and that you will grow weary, so recite it in a month."
I said, "Let me enjoy my strength and my youth." He said:
"Then recite it in ten days."
I said, "Let me enjoy my strength and my youth." He said:
"Then recite it in seven days."
I said, "Let me enjoy my strength and my youth." But he refused.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed, and whenever he passed a verse of mercy, he would ask [Allah for it]; whenever he passed a verse of punishment, he would seek refuge [with Allah]; and whenever he passed a verse that glorified Allah, he would declare His glory.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, who has accepted Islam with you?" He said, "A free man and a slave."
I said, "Is there any time closer to Allah than another?" He said:
"Yes, the middle of the depth of the night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah gives respite until, when half of the night or two-thirds of it has passed, He says: 'Let none ask anyone but Me, My servants. Whoever calls upon Me, I will answer him; whoever asks Me, I will give him; whoever seeks My forgiveness, I will forgive him,' until dawn breaks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever prays twenty units of prayer between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of people from Iraq set out to ʿUmar. When they came to him, he said to them, "Where are you from?" They said, "From the people of Iraq."
He said, "Have you come with permission?" They said, "Yes."
He said: So they asked him about a man's prayer in his house.
ʿUmar said, "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said:
'As for a man's prayer in his house, it is light, so illuminate your houses.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he and some people with him went to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUkaym, a man from Juhaynah. Al-Ḥakam said: They went in while I sat at the door, then they came out to me and told me that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUkaym had informed them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to Juhaynah a month before his death: "Do not benefit from carrion, neither from its hide nor from its sinew."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a slave

stole a palm shoot from a man's orchard and planted it in his master's orchard. The owner of the shoot came looking for his shoot and found it, and he sought redress against the slave before Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam, who was the governor of Medina at that time. Marwān imprisoned the slave and wanted to cut off his hand. The slave's master went to Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj and asked him about that, and he told him that he had heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
There is no cutting of the hand for fruit or for palm pith."

The man said: Marwān has seized my slave and wants to cut off his hand, and I would like you to walk with me to him and tell him what you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj walked with him until he came to Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam, and Rāfiʿ said to him: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "
There is no cutting of the hand for fruit or for palm pith."
So Marwān gave orders concerning the slave, and he was released.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, while speaking about the pause in revelation, in his account: "
While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky, so I raised my gaze,
and there was the angel who had come to me at Ḥirāʾ, sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was frightened of him and returned, and I said: Wrap me up, wrap me up!"
So they wrapped him up, and Allah the Exalted revealed: {O you who are wrapped in your cloak, arise and warn, and your Lord magnify, and your garments purify, and uncleanness avoid.}
Abū Salamah said: That is, the idols which the people of the Jāhiliyyah used to worship.
He said: Then the revelation followed in succession.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most generous of people,
and he was most generous in Ramadan when Jibrīl met him.
Jibrīl used to meet him every night of Ramadan and study the Qurʾān with him.
So when Jibrīl met him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more generous in goodness than the blowing wind.
And from ʿAbdullāh: Maʿmar narrated to us with this chain, similarly.
Abū Hurayrah and Fāṭimah, may Allah be pleased with them both, reported from the Prophet ﷺ that Jibrīl used to review the Qurʾān with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Faith has sixty-some branches,
and modesty is a branch of faith."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sign of faith is love of the Anṣār,
and the sign of hypocrisy is hatred of the Anṣār."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and establish the prayer, and give zakāh.
If they do that, they have protected their blood and their wealth from me, except by the right of Islam,
and their reckoning is with Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When {Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing} was revealed, it was hard on the Muslims,
and they said: O Messenger of Allah,
which of us does not wrong himself? He said: "That is not it.
It is only polytheism.
Have you not heard what Luqmān said to his son while advising him: {O my son, do not associate anything with Allah; indeed, associating others with Him is a great wrong}?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Regarding Ramadan: "
Whoever stands in prayer during it out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins are forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: When My servant intends to do a good deed, I record it for him as one good deed as long as he has not done it; if he does it, I record it for him tenfold. And when he intends to do an evil deed, I forgive it for him as long as he has not done it; if he does it, I record it for him as only one like it."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
The angels said: My Lord, that servant of Yours intends to do an evil deed, though He sees him best. He said: Watch him; if he does it, record it for him as only one like it.
And if he leaves it, record it for him as a good deed, for he left it only for My sake."
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
When one of you perfects his Islam, every good deed he does is recorded tenfold, up to seven hundred times, and every evil deed he does is recorded as only one like it, until he meets Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of Ashjaʿ died at Khaybar, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Pray over your companion."
The people disapproved of that, and their faces changed. When he saw that, he said:
"Your companion defrauded [the spoils] in the way of Allah."
Zayd said: So they searched his belongings and found some beads of the Jews' beads that were not worth two dirhams.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present at Khaybar with my masters, and they spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about me and informed him that I was a slave.

He said: So he ordered that I be girded with a sword, and I was dragging it. Then he ordered that I be given something from the household goods, and I presented to him a ruqyah that I used to recite over the insane. He told me to discard part of it and keep part of it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib: Tell me what
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked or forbade of sacrificial animals.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said this with his hand, and my hand is shorter than the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

"Four are not acceptable as sacrificial animals: the one-eyed whose blindness is obvious, the sick whose sickness is obvious, the lame whose limp is obvious, and the broken-legged that has no marrow."
I said: I dislike that there be a defect in the horn and the ear.
He said: Whatever you dislike, leave it, but do not make it forbidden for anyone else.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had forbidden you from eating the meat of sacrificial animals beyond three days so that it would suffice you. Now Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has brought abundance, so eat, give in charity, and store. These days are days of eating, drinking, and remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."
A man said: We used to offer the ʿatīrah in the Pre-Islamic Period in Rajab. What do you command us? He said:
"Slaughter for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in whichever month it may be, be dutiful to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and feed [others]."
A man said: O Messenger of Allah, we used to offer the faraʿ in the Pre-Islamic Period. What do you command us? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"In every grazing flock of sheep there is a faraʿ, which your sheep nourish until, when it is strong enough to be ridden, you slaughter it and give its meat in charity to the wayfarer, for that is better."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Indeed the devils inspire their allies" He said: They used to say: What Allah's name has been mentioned over, do not eat, and what Allah's name has not been mentioned over, eat it.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "And do not eat of that over which Allah's name has not been mentioned."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He caught two hares and did not find an iron blade to slaughter them with, so he slaughtered them with a sharp stone. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I hunted two hares and did not find an iron blade to slaughter them with, so I slaughtered them with a sharp stone. May I eat them? He said: "Eat."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of them said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the faraʿ and the ʿatīrah. And the other said:
"There is no faraʿ and no ʿatīrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Every boy is held in pledge for his ʿaqīqah, which is slaughtered for him on the seventh day, his head is shaved, and he is named."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever dwells in the desert becomes harsh, whoever pursues game becomes heedless, and whoever follows the ruler is put to trial."
The wording is that of Ibn al-Muthannā.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was beneath the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, her saliva running onto me, and I heard him say:
"Indeed Allah has given every rightful person his right. Beware, there is no bequest for an heir."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I have nothing and have no wealth, but I have an orphan who has wealth. He said:
"Eat from the wealth of your orphan, without extravagance and without accumulating wealth [for yourself]."
He said: And I think he said:
"And do not protect your own wealth with his wealth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until we came to a woman of the Anṣār in al-Aswāq. The woman brought her two daughters and said: O Messenger of Allah, these are the two daughters of Thābit ibn Qays, who was killed with you on the day of Uḥud. Their paternal uncle has seized their wealth and all their inheritance, leaving them no wealth except what he took. What do you think, O Messenger of Allah? By Allah, they will never marry unless they have wealth.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah will decide in that matter."
He said: Then Sūrat an-Nisāʾ was revealed: "Allah instructs you concerning your children..." the verse.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Call for me the woman and her companion." And he said to their uncle:
"Give them two-thirds, give their mother one-eighth, and what remains is yours."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding the verse:
"It may be that your Lord will raise you to a station of praise" — he was asked about it, and he said: "It is the intercession."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was in Makkah, then he was commanded to emigrate, so this verse was revealed to him:
"And say: My Lord, cause me to enter by a sound entrance and to exit by a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Quraysh said to the Jews: "Give us something to ask this man about." They said: "Ask him about the soul (the rūḥ)." So they asked him about the soul, and Allah revealed:

"And they ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is from the affair of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little." They said: "We have been given abundant knowledge, the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good." So this was revealed:
"Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted..." to the end of the verse.
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"On the Day of Resurrection people will be gathered in three groups: a group walking, a group riding, and a group on their faces."
It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will they walk on their faces?" He said:
"Indeed, the One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces. Indeed, they will shield themselves with their faces from every mound and thorn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pray in Bayt al-Maqdis?" He said: "No." I said: "Yes, he did."
He said: "You say that, O bald one? On what basis do you say that?" I said: "On the basis of the Qur'an. The Qur'an is between me and you."
Ḥudhayfah said: "Whoever argues from the Qur'an has succeeded." Sufyān said: he means, "he has made his argument."
Sometimes he said: "he has prevailed." Then he said:
"Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the farthest mosque." He said: "Do you think he prayed in it?" I said: "No."

He said: "Had he prayed in it, prayer in it would have been prescribed for you just as prayer was prescribed in the Sacred Mosque." Ḥudhayfah said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a beast with a long back, extending like this, its stride reaching as far as its sight. The two of them did not leave the back of al-Burāq until they saw Paradise, the Fire, and all that the Hereafter has been promised. Then they returned the way they had come." He said: "They say that he tied it up. Was it going to flee from him? Rather, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed subjected it to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and this is no boast. In my hand will be the banner of praise, and this is no boast. On that Day there will be no prophet, Adam or anyone other than him, except that he will be under my banner. I am the first for whom the earth will be split open, and this is no boast." He said: "People will be terrified three times. They will come to Adam and say: 'You are our father Adam, so intercede for us with your Lord.'
He will say: 'I committed a sin for which I was sent down to the earth, but go to Noah.'
They will come to Noah, and he will say: 'I made a supplication against the people of the earth and they were destroyed, but go to Abraham.'
They will come to Abraham, and he will say: 'I told three lies.'"
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Not one of them was but in defense of the religion of Allah. But go to Moses.
They will come to Moses, and he will say: 'I killed a person, but go to Jesus.'
They will come to Jesus, and he will say: 'I was worshipped besides Allah, but go to Muhammad.'" He said: "So they will come to me, and I will go with them."
Ibn Judʿān said: Anas said: "It is as though I am looking at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said:
"I will take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise and knock it, and it will be said: 'Who is this?' It will be said: 'Muhammad.'

They will open for me and welcome me, saying: 'Welcome!' Then I will fall down in prostration, and Allah will inspire me with praise and glorification. It will be said to me: 'Raise your head. Ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted; speak and you will be heard.' That is the station of praise about which Allah said:
'It may be that your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.'"
Sufyān said: Nothing of this is from Anas except this phrase:
"I will take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise and knock it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ regarding the verse:
"And beneath it was a treasure belonging to them" — he said: "Gold and silver."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said to me: Did you hear your father narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the hour of Friday? He said:
I said: Yes, I heard him say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"It is between the time the imam sits down until the prayer is concluded."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUmārah ibn Ruʾaybah saw Bishr ibn Marwān raising his hands in supplication on a Friday, so ʿUmārah said: May Allah disfigure these two hands.
Zāʾidah said: Ḥuṣayn said: ʿUmārah narrated to me, saying: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the minbar, and he did not do more than this, meaning the index finger, the one next to the thumb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the prayer of the eclipse, from ʿAṭāʾ,
from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿĀʾishah,
that the Prophet ﷺ prayed six rakʿahs with four prostrations.
I said to Muʿādh: [Is this] from the Prophet ﷺ? He said: Without doubt or uncertainty.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over a grave after [the deceased] had been buried, and he said the takbīr over it four times.
Al-Shaybānī said: I asked al-Shaʿbī: Who narrated this to you? He said: The trustworthy one, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās.

This is the wording of a ḥasan hadith. In the narration of Ibn Numayr he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to a fresh grave and prayed over it, and they lined up behind him, and he said the takbīr four times.
I asked ʿĀmir: Who narrated to you? He said: The trustworthy one who witnessed it, Ibn ʿAbbās.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Shall I not narrate to you about myself and about the Prophet ﷺ? We said: Yes. She said:
When it was my night, the night he was with me, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, he turned over and placed his sandals by his feet,
and spread the edge of his lower garment over his bed,
and he stayed only as long as he thought I had fallen asleep,
then he put on his sandals gently and took his cloak gently,
then he opened the door gently and went out gently. I put my shift over my head, wrapped myself in my headscarf, and drew my lower garment over me,
and I set out after him until he came to al-Baqīʿ,
where he raised his hands three times, at length,
then he turned away and I turned away; he hurried and I hurried; he ran and I ran;
he went faster and I went faster, and I reached there before him and entered.
I had only just lain down when he came in and said: "
What is the matter, ʿĀʾishah? Why are you out of breath?" She said: Nothing. He said: "
Either you tell me, or the Subtle, the All-Aware will inform me." I said:
O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom! And I told him the matter. He said: "
So you were the dark figure I saw ahead of me?" She said: Yes.
He struck me on the chest with a blow that pained me, then said: "
Did you think that Allah and His Messenger would wrong you?" I said:
However much people conceal, Allah knows it. He said: "
Gabriel came to me when you saw [me], but he did not enter while you had your clothes off. He called me,
and I concealed it from you, so I answered him and concealed it from you,
and I thought you had fallen asleep, and I disliked waking you,
and I feared that you would be frightened to be alone,
and he commanded me to go to al-Baqīʿ and seek forgiveness for them." I said:
How should I say it, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "
Say: Peace be upon the people of these abodes, among the believers and the Muslims,
may Allah have mercy on those of us who have gone before and those who come later,
and we will, Allah willing, join you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That ʿAbdullāh

recited the talbiyah when he departed from Jamʿ. It was said: Is this a bedouin? ʿAbdullāh said: Have the people forgotten, or have they gone astray? I heard the one upon whom Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed say in this place: "
Labbayka Allāhumma labbayk (Here I am, O Allah, here I am)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the ifāḍah on the Day of Sacrifice, then returned and prayed Ẓuhr at Minā.
Nāfiʿ said: Ibn ʿUmar used to perform the ifāḍah on the Day of Sacrifice, then return and pray Ẓuhr at Minā, and he mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ had done so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were walking with the Prophet ﷺ when he passed by Ibn Ṣayyād, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him,
"I have concealed something for you in my mind." He said, "Dukh."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Be gone! You will never go beyond your limit."
ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah, let me strike his neck." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Leave him. If he is the one you fear, you will not be able to kill him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"None of you should curse time, for Allah is time, and none of you should call the grape vine 'al-karm'.
For the true 'karm' is the Muslim man."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A boy was born to a man among us and he named him al-Qāsim. We said, "We will not call you Abū al-Qāsim, and we will not give you the delight of your eye."
So he went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said,
"Name your son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Mundhir ibn Abī Usayd was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he was born, and the Prophet ﷺ placed him on his thigh while Abū Usayd was sitting there. The Prophet ﷺ became occupied with something in front of him, so Abū Usayd ordered that his son be picked up from the thigh of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was taken away. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to himself and said, "Where is the boy?"
Abū Usayd said, "We sent him back, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "What is his name?"
He said, "So-and-so, O Messenger of Allah." He said,
"No, rather his name is al-Mundhir."
So that day he named him al-Mundhir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā, "Did you see Ibrāhīm, the son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "He died when he was young. Had it been decreed that there would be a prophet after Muhammad ﷺ, his son would have lived. But there is no prophet after him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"A believer is not one who curses excessively."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Teach me something, but do not give me too much, so that I may remember it." He said, "Do not become angry."
The man repeated his request several times, and each time he said, "Do not become angry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whenever a young man honors an elderly person because of his age, Allah appoints for him someone who will honor him when he reaches that age."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Modesty and reticence in speech are two branches of faith, while obscenity and loquacious eloquence are two branches of hypocrisy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no one forbearing except one who has stumbled, and no one wise except one who has experience."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When Allah loves a servant, He protects him from the world, just as one of you keeps his sick person away from water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of what you can use for treatment is snuff, medicine poured into the side of the mouth, cupping, and a laxative."
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill, his Companions poured medicine into the side of his mouth. When they had finished, he said, "Give them the same medicine."
He said: So they all had the medicine poured into their mouths, except al-ʿAbbās.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The best of what you can use for treatment is medicine poured into the side of the mouth, snuff, cupping, and a laxative. And the best of what you can apply as kohl is antimony, for it clears the sight and makes the hair grow."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a kohl container with which he would apply kohl at bedtime, three times to each eye.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ cauterized Asʿad ibn Zurārah for erysipelas (a thorn-like infection).
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās had three young slaves who were cuppers. Two of them earned a daily payment for him and his family, and one would perform cupping on him and his family.
He said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said:
"What an excellent servant is the cupper: he removes the blood, lightens the back, and clears the sight."
He also said that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken up on the Night Journey, he did not pass by any company of angels except that they said, "Upon you is cupping." And he said:
"The best days on which you can have cupping done are the seventeenth, the nineteenth, and the twenty-first." And he said:
"The best of what you can use for treatment is snuff, medicine poured into the side of the mouth, cupping, and a laxative."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had medicine poured into the mouth of al-ʿAbbās and his Companions, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who gave me this medicine?" They all held back, so he said:
"No one in the house will be left without having this medicine poured into his mouth."
except for his uncle al-ʿAbbās. ʿAbd said: Al-Naḍr said: Ladūd is the same as wajūr (medicine poured into the mouth).
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no omen in the owl, and the evil eye is real."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I took three, five, or seven truffles, squeezed them, and put their juice in a bottle. Then I applied it as kohl to a girl of mine, and she was cured.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Black seed is a remedy for every disease except death.

Qatādah said: One takes twenty-one seeds each day and puts them in a piece of cloth and soaks it, then uses it as snuff each day: on the first day, two drops in the right nostril and one in the left; on the second day, two drops in the left and one in the right; and on the third day, two drops in the right and one in the left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I visited ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUkaym Abū Maʿbad al-Juhanī to visit him while he was ill with erysipelas. We said, "Will you not hang something [as an amulet]?" He said, "Death is nearer than that. The Prophet ﷺ said:
'Whoever hangs something [for protection] will be entrusted to it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I wanted to forbid ghīlah (intercourse with a nursing mother), but then I saw that the Persians and the Romans do it, and it does not harm their children."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to prescribe olive oil and wars (a plant dye) for pleurisy.
Qatādah said: And it is poured into the mouth from the side that he complains of.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to treat pleurisy with sea costus and olive oil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever acquires a branch of knowledge from the stars has acquired a branch of sorcery; the more he adds, the more it increases."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was a slave of Umm Salamah, and she said, "I will free you, and I stipulate that you serve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for as long as you live."
I said, "Even if you did not stipulate that on me, I would not part from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for as long as I live." So she freed me and stipulated that upon me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever frees a slave who owns property, the slave's property belongs to him, unless the master stipulates that the property is his, in which case it belongs to him."
Ibn Lahīʿah said: "unless the master excepts it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: This verse, {It is not for a prophet to take [something] unjustly from the spoils}, was revealed concerning a red velvet cloak that went missing on the day of Badr. Some people said, "Perhaps the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {It is not for a prophet to take [something] unjustly from the spoils}, to the end of the verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he recited "qad balaghta min ladunnī ʿudhran" with the nūn doubled.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me to recite: {Indeed, it is Allah who is the Provider, the Possessor of power, the Firm.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man bathing in the open ground without a waist wrapper. So he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, and then said ﷺ:
"Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Modest and Concealing; He loves modesty and concealment. So when one of you bathes, let him cover himself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Jarhad said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by Jarhad in the mosque while his thigh was uncovered, and he said:
"The thigh is ʿawrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The sleeve of the shirt of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached to the wrist.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd said: I saw a man in Bukhārā on a white mule, wearing a black silk turban, and he said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ clothed me with it."
This is the wording of ʿUthmān, and the reports are in his narration.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with a companion of mine,

called Abū ʿĀmir, a man from al-Maʿāfir, to pray in Īliyāʾ. Their storyteller was a man from al-Azd called Abū Rayḥānah, one of the Companions. Abū al-Ḥuṣayn said: My companion reached the mosque before me, then I followed and sat beside him. He asked me, "Have you caught the talk of Abū Rayḥānah?" I said, "No."

segments_en: He came to the Prophet ﷺ in shabby clothing, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Do you have wealth?"
He said, "Yes, of every kind of wealth." He said:
"Of which kind of wealth?"
He said, "Allah has given me camels, sheep, horses, and slaves." He said:
"Then when Allah has given you wealth, let the effect of Allah's blessing and generosity be seen upon you."

segments_en: We descended with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from a mountain pass, and he turned to me while I was wearing a light garment dyed with safflower, and said:
"What is this garment you are wearing?"
I understood what he disliked, so I went to my family while they were heating their oven, and I threw it into it. Then I came to him the next day, and he said:
"ʿAbdullāh, what did you do with the garment?" I told him, and he said:
"Why did you not give it to one of your family to wear? There is no harm in it for women."

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever drinks wine, Allah does not accept his prayer for forty mornings. If he repents, Allah accepts his repentance. If he returns, Allah does not accept his prayer for forty mornings; if he repents, Allah accepts his repentance. If he returns, Allah does not accept his prayer for forty mornings; if he repents, Allah accepts his repentance. If he returns a fourth time, Allah does not accept his prayer for forty mornings, and if he repents, Allah will not accept his repentance, and He will give him to drink from the River of Khabāl."
It was said: O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, what is the River of Khabāl? He said: A river of pus of the people of the Fire.

Then we stood with him on the twenty-fifth night until half of the night. Then we stood with him on the twenty-seventh night until we thought that we would not reach al-falāḥ, and they used to call it as-suḥūr.

segments_en: That a man

from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: I said, while I was on a journey with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: By Allah, I will watch the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in prayer until I see what he does. When he prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer, which is al-ʿatamah, he lay down for a while of the night, then woke up and looked at the horizon and said: {Our Lord, You did not create this in vain} until he reached {Indeed, You do not fail in [Your] promise}.

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached for his bed, drew out a siwāk from it, poured water into a cup from a water skin he had by him, and cleaned his teeth. Then he stood and prayed until I said, "He has prayed as long as he slept." Then he lay down until I said, "He has slept as long as he prayed." Then he woke up and did as he had done the first time and said the same as he had said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did so three times before dawn.

segments_en: We never wished to see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying at night except that we saw him, and we never wished to see him sleeping except that we saw him.

Ibn Abī Mulaykah informed me
that Yaʿlā ibn Mamlak informed him that he
asked Umm Salamah about the prayer of

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: He would pray the ʿatamah [ʿIshāʾ], then glorify Allah, then pray after it as much as Allah willed of the night, then finish and sleep for as long as he had prayed, then wake from that sleep and pray for as long as he had slept. And that last prayer of his would continue until the morning.

segments_en: Al-ʿAbbās and ʿAlī came to ʿUmar disputing with one another, and al-ʿAbbās said, "Judge between me and this man."
The people said, "Decide between them."
ʿUmar said, "I will not decide between them. They both know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'We [prophets] are not inherited from; whatever we leave is charity (ṣadaqah).'"

Al-Zuhrī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took charge of it, took from it the sustenance of his family, and put the rest to the use of public funds. Then Abū Bakr took charge of it after him. Then I took charge of it after Abū Bakr and did with it what he used to do. Then the two of them came to me and asked me to hand it over to them, on condition that they manage it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ managed it, as Abū Bakr managed it, and as I managed it. So I handed it over to them and took their pledges on that. Then they came to me, one saying, "Give me my share from my nephew,"
and the other saying, "Give me my share from my wife."

If they wish, I will hand it over to them on condition that they manage it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ managed it, as Abū Bakr managed it, and as I managed it; but if they refuse, they are spared that. Then he recited: {And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, one-fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger, for relatives, orphans, the needy and the traveler} — this is for those. {Charity is only for the poor, the needy, those who work to collect it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, for freeing slaves, for those in debt, and in the cause of Allah} — this is for those. {And what Allah gave as spoil to His Messenger from them, for which you did not spur any horses or camels} — al-Zuhrī said: This was specifically for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: the Arab towns of Fadak and such-and-such. {What Allah gave as spoil to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah, the Messenger, relatives, orphans, the needy and the traveler}, and {for the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth}, {and those who were settled in the abode and in faith before them}, {and those who came after them}. This verse encompassed all the people, so there is no Muslim who does not have a right in this wealth — or he said, a share — except some of those slaves whom you own. If I live, Allah willing, every Muslim will receive his right — or he said, his share.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, which emigration is best?" He said:
"That you abandon what your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, dislikes."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Emigration is of two kinds: the emigration of the town-dweller and the emigration of the desert-dweller. As for the desert-dweller, he responds when called and obeys when commanded. As for the town-dweller, his trial is greater and his reward is greater."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar were among the Emigrants because they abandoned the polytheists. Among the Helpers there were also emigrants, because Medina had been a land of polytheism, so they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of al-ʿAqabah.

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me of a deed
that I may remain steadfast in and perform."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:

segments_en: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a delegation, each of us seeking a need, and I was the last of them to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I left behind me people who claim that emigration has ended." He said:
"Emigration does not end as long as the disbelievers are fought."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. My companions entered and he fulfilled their needs, and I was the last of them to enter. He said, "Your need?"

segments_en: Jarīr said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was taking pledges. I said, "O Messenger of Allah, stretch out your hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you, and set conditions for me, for you know best." He said:
"I take your pledge that you worship Allah, establish prayer, give zakāh, give sincere advice to the Muslims, and separate from the polytheists."

the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I said, "O Messenger of Allah, a woman helped me in mourning during the Jāhiliyyah; may I go and help her, then come to you and pledge allegiance?" He said, "Go and help her."
She said: So I went and helped her, then I came and pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

"The one who strives to help the widow and the poor is like the one who strives in the cause of Allah — and I think he also said —
(al-Qaʿnabī was unsure) like the one who stands in prayer without tiring,
and like the one who fasts without breaking his fast."

segments_en: I was a boy under the care of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and my hand used to wander around the dish. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"Boy, mention the name of Allah,
eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you."
And that remained my way of eating ever after.

segments_en: I entered the house of al-Ḥakam ibn Ayyūb with my grandfather Anas ibn Mālik, and there were some people who had set up a hen and were shooting at it. Anas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade tying up animals to be shot at.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no contagion and no bad omen, and I love the good omen."
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the good omen?" He said: "A good word."

segments_en: I asked ʿĀʾishah about silk,
and she said: "Go to Ibn ʿAbbās and ask him."
He said: So I asked him, and he said: "Ask Ibn ʿUmar."
He said: So I asked Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: Abū Ḥafṣ, meaning ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, informed me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Only one who has no share in the Hereafter wears silk in this world."
I said: "He spoke the truth, and Abū Ḥafṣ did not lie about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
ʿAbdullāh ibn Rajāʾ said: Ḥarb narrated to us from Yaḥyā, who said: ʿImrān narrated to me, and he related the hadith.

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. Transfer of the chain: And Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us,
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us,
from ʿAlī ibn Mudrik,
from Abū Zurʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarīr,

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once led his Companions in prayer. When he had finished the prayer, he turned his face to the people and said:
"What is the matter with people who raise their eyes to the sky
[in prayer]?" His words grew severe on this point, until he said:
"They must stop this, or Allah will snatch away their sight."

segments_en: A man
entered the mosque while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in a corner of the mosque, and he prayed.
Then he came and greeted him with salām, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"And upon you be peace. Go back and pray, for you have not prayed." So he went back and prayed,
then he came and greeted him with salām. [The Prophet ﷺ] said:
"And upon you be peace. Go back and pray,
for you have not prayed."
The second time, or the time after it, the man said: "Teach me, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"When you stand up for prayer, perform the ablution fully,
then face the qiblah and say the takbīr,
then recite whatever is easy for you of the Qurʾān,
then bow until you are at ease in bowing,
then rise until you stand upright,
then prostrate until you are at ease in prostration,
then rise until you are at ease sitting,
then prostrate until you are at ease in prostration,
then rise until you are at ease sitting,
then do that throughout all of your prayer."
Abū Usāmah said at the end:
"until you stand upright."
label: machine translation

"Glory be to You, my Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me."

segments_en: When we sat with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in prayer, we used to say: "Peace be upon Allah before His servants; peace be upon so-and-so and so-and-so." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not say, 'Peace be upon Allah,' for Allah is Himself As-Salām. Rather, when one of you sits, let him say: 'All greetings, prayers and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah.' For when you say that, it reaches every righteous servant in the heavens and the earth, or between the heavens and the earth. 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.' Then let each of you choose whichever supplication pleases him most and supplicate with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Abū Bakr said] to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Teach me a supplication with which I may supplicate in my prayer." He said:
"Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You, so grant me forgiveness from Yourself and have mercy on me. Indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful."
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb hadith, and it is the hadith of Layth ibn Saʿd. Abū al-Khayr's name is Marthad ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Yazanī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "None of you should give the Devil a share of his prayer by thinking that he must turn away only to his right. I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turn away most often to his left."
ʿUmārah said: Later I came to Madinah and saw that the houses of the Prophet ﷺ were on his left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever performs the ritual bath of janābah on Friday and then goes out early, it is as if he offered a camel [in sacrifice].
Whoever goes in the second hour, it is as if he offered a cow.
Whoever goes in the third hour, it is as if he offered a horned ram.
Whoever goes in the fourth hour, it is as if he offered a chicken.
Whoever goes in the fifth hour, it is as if he offered an egg.
Then when the imam comes out, the angels are present, listening to the reminder."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first call to prayer on Friday used to be when the imam sat on the pulpit on Friday, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both. Then in the caliphate of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, when the people had become numerous,
ʿUthmān ordered a third call to prayer on Friday,
and it was called out at az-Zawrāʾ.
And the matter remained established on that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Ṭufayl ibn ʿAmr al-Dawsī

came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, do you want a strong fortress and protection?" – a fortress that the tribe of Daws had in the pre-Islamic period. The Prophet ﷺ declined that because of what Allah had stored up for the Anṣār. Then, when the Prophet ﷺ emigrated to Medina, al-Ṭufayl ibn ʿAmr emigrated to him, and a man from his people emigrated with him. They found the climate of Medina unhealthy, and the man fell ill and became impatient. He took a broad-headed arrowhead of his and cut his knuckles with it, so his hands bled profusely until he died. Al-Ṭufayl ibn ʿAmr saw him in a dream, and saw him in a good state, but saw him covering his hands. He said to him, "What did your Lord do with you?" He said, "He forgave me because of my emigration to His Prophet ﷺ." He said, "Why do I see you covering your hands?" He said, "I was told: We will not repair of you what you yourself have ruined."
Al-Ṭufayl related it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Allah, and forgive his hands as well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah will send a wind from Yemen softer than silk, and it will leave no one who has in his heart – Abū ʿAlqamah said: the weight of a grain, and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: the weight of an atom – of faith, except that it will take his soul."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When this verse was revealed: "O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet," to the end of the verse, Thābit ibn Qays sat in his house and said, "I am one of the people of the Fire."
He kept away from the Prophet ﷺ, so the Prophet ﷺ asked Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, saying:
"O Abū ʿAmr, what is the matter with Thābit? Is he ill?"
Saʿd said, "He is my neighbor, and I do not know of any illness of his."

He said: So Saʿd went to him and mentioned to him what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said. Thābit said, "This verse was revealed, and you know that I am among those with the loudest voices over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I am one of the people of the Fire."
Saʿd mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Rather, he is one of the people of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were present with ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ as he was in the throes of death.

He wept for a long time and turned his face to the wall. His son began to say, "O father, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not give you glad tidings of such and such? Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not give you glad tidings of such and such?" He said: Then he turned his face toward us.

He said, "The best thing we can count on is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I have lived through three stages. I saw myself when there was no one who hated the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than I did, and nothing dearer to me than to have power over him and kill him. Had I died in that state, I would have been among the people of the Fire. Then, when Allah put Islam in my heart, I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'Stretch out your right hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you.'
He stretched out his right hand – he said – and I withdrew my hand. He said:
'What is the matter, O ʿAmr?'
He said: I said, "I want to make a condition." He said, "What condition do you want to make?"
I said, "That I be forgiven." He said:
'Do you not know that Islam wipes out what came before it, that emigration wipes out what came before it, and that Hajj wipes out what came before it?'

And no one was dearer to me than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor greater in my eyes. I could not bring myself to fill my eyes with him out of reverence for him, and if I were asked to describe him I could not, because I never filled my eyes with him. Had I died in that state, I would have hoped to be among the people of Paradise. Then we were put in charge of certain matters, and I do not know what my state is in them. So when I die, let no wailing woman or fire accompany me. When you bury me, pour the earth over me gently, then stay around my grave for as long as it takes to slaughter a camel and distribute its meat, so that I may take comfort in your company and see how I should answer the messengers of my Lord."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muhammad ibn Sīrīn said to me: Ask al-Ḥasan from whom he heard his hadith about the ʿaqīqah.
So I asked him about that,
and he said: I heard it from Samurah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the farʿ?" He said:

"It is a right. But if you leave it until it grows into a young camel, and then you load it for the cause of Allah or give it to a widow, that is better than slaughtering it so that its flesh sticks to its fur, and you spill your vessel and leave your she-camel bereft."
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the ʿatīrah?" He said: "The ʿatīrah is a right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the Farewell Pilgrimage while he was on his she-camel al-ʿAḍbāʾ. I approached him from one side and said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, ask forgiveness for me." He said:
"May Allah forgive you."
Then I came to him from the other side, hoping that he would single me out apart from them, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." He said, gesturing with his hand:
"May Allah forgive you."
Then a man among the people said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the ʿatāʾir and the farāʾiʿ?" He said:
"Whoever wishes may sacrifice an ʿatīrah, and whoever wishes need not; whoever wishes may sacrifice a farʿ, and whoever wishes need not. Among sheep, there is the sacrificial animal (uḍḥiyah)."
And he closed his fingers except for one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, we used to slaughter animals in the Jāhiliyyah in Rajab, and we would eat and feed whoever came to us."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no harm in it."
Wakīʿ ibn ʿUdus said: So I do not give it up.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked Ibn ʿAbbās, saying: "We go on expeditions in this western land, and they are idol-worshippers who have waterskins in which there is milk and water." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Tanning is purification."
Ibn Waʿlah said: "Is this your own opinion, or something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Rather, it is from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: During the expedition of Tabūk, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ asked for water from a woman. She said: "I have only what is in a waterskin of mine made from a dead animal." He said:
"Have you not tanned it?" She said: "Yes." He said:
"Then its tanning is its slaughter."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the hides of dead animals and said: "Their tanning is their purification."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The slaughter of a dead animal is its tanning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The slaughter of a dead animal is its tanning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In Egypt, it was read to him while I listened,
from Suwayd ibn Naṣr,
who said: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak informed us, from ʿĀṣim, from ash-Shaʿbī,
from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim,
that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about hunting, and he said:

"When you send out your dog, mention the name of Allah over it. If you reach the game and it has not been killed, slaughter it and mention the name of Allah over it. If you find it already killed and the dog has not eaten from it, eat, for it has caught it for you. But if you find that it has eaten from it, do not eat any of it, for it only caught it for itself. And if your dog mixes with other dogs and they kill the game without eating, do not eat any of it, for you do not know which of them killed it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about hunting, and he said:
"When you send out your dog and other dogs over which the name of Allah was not mentioned mix with it, do not eat, for you do not know which of them killed it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, the like of that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about hunting. He said:

"When you send out your dog and mention the name of Allah over it, and it kills the game without eating, then eat. But if it eats from it, do not eat, for it only caught it for itself and did not catch it for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have trained hunting dogs; give me a ruling about them." He said:
"Eat what your dogs catch for you."
I said: "Even if they kill it?" He said: "Even if they kill it."
He said: "Give me a ruling about my bow." He said:
"Eat what your arrow returns to you."
He said: "And if it disappears from me?" He said:
"Even if it disappears from you, so long as you do not find on it the mark of an arrow other than yours, or find that it has spoiled."
meaning, it has begun to stink.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:

"By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one of this nation, Jew or Christian, hears of me and then dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the people of the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ. (Another chain:) And Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us:
Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dhakwān,
from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ. (Another chain:) And Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ narrated to us:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us: Maʿmar narrated to us,
from Hammām ibn Munabbih,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to the hadith of al-ʿAlāʾ from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said one day:
"Do you know where this sun goes?"
They said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said:

"This sun runs until it reaches its resting place beneath the Throne, where it falls down in prostration. It remains so until it is said to it, 'Rise, return from where you came,' and it returns and rises from its place of rising. Then it runs until it reaches its resting place beneath the Throne, where it falls down in prostration, and it remains so until it is said to it, 'Rise, return from where you came,' and it returns and rises from its place of rising. Then it runs, and people notice nothing unusual in it, until it reaches that resting place of its beneath the Throne, and it is said to it, 'Rise, and rise from your place of setting,' and it rises from its place of setting."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you know when that will be? That will be when belief will not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned some good through its belief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said: "Then he returned to Khadījah, his heart trembling," and he related the hadith like the hadith of Yūnus and Maʿmar, but he did not mention the beginning of their narration, namely his words: "The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was started of revelation was the true dream."
And Yūnus concurred with him in the words: "By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you."
And he mentioned the words of Khadījah: "O son of my uncle, listen to your nephew."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said, 'I will surely give charity.' So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a thief. In the morning people were saying, 'Charity was given to a thief!' He said, 'O Allah, to You belongs all praise. [I gave] to a thief! I will surely give charity.' So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of an adulteress. In the morning people were saying, 'Charity was given last night to an adulteress!' He said, 'O Allah, to You belongs all praise. [I gave] to an adulteress! I will surely give charity.' So he went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a rich man. In the morning people were saying, 'Charity was given to a rich man!' He said, 'O Allah, to You belongs all praise, [for my charity going] to an adulteress, to a thief, and to a rich man.' Then he was visited [in a dream] and told: 'As for your charity, it has been accepted. As for the adulteress, perhaps she will abstain from her adultery because of it; perhaps the thief will abstain from his theft; and perhaps the rich man will take heed and spend from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best charity is that which is given from surplus, or given while one remains self-sufficient. And begin with those you are responsible for supporting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The trustworthy Muslim treasurer who carries out—and perhaps he said, 'gives'—what he is commanded, giving it in full and complete, with a willing heart, handing it to the one for whom he was commanded to give it, is one of the two who give charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The example of the one who spends in charity and the miser is like two men wearing two iron cloaks or two coats of mail, from their breasts to their collarbones. When the spender wishes to spend, the coat expands over him, or stretches, until it covers his fingertips and erases his tracks. But when the miser wishes to spend, it contracts and every ring clings to its place, until it grips him at his collarbone or his neck."
Abū Hurayrah said: I bear witness that he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ trying to widen it, but it would not widen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Charity is due from every Muslim."
It was asked, "What if he does not find [anything to give]?" He said:
"He works with his hands, benefiting himself and giving in charity."
It was asked, "What if he is unable?" He said:
"He helps the needy person in distress."
It was asked, "What if he is unable?" He said:
"He enjoins what is right or good."
He was asked, "What if he does not do that?" He said:
"He refrains from evil, for that is charity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not harm his neighbor;
and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest;
and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak what is good or remain silent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
asked permission to see the Prophet ﷺ, and when he saw him, he said:
"What an evil brother of the clan,
and what an evil son of the clan!"
Then when the man sat down, the Prophet ﷺ was cheerful toward him and received him warmly.
When the man left, ʿĀʾishah said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, when you saw the man you said such and such about him,
and then you were cheerful toward him and received him warmly." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿĀʾishah, when have you ever known me to be vulgar?
Indeed, the worst of people in standing with Allah on the Day of Resurrection is the one whom people leave alone out of fear of his evil."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from Anas ibn Mālik,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, and do not turn away from one another. Be servants of Allah, brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man keeps speaking the truth and striving for truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as truthful. And beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man keeps lying and striving to lie until he is recorded with Allah as a liar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb among a group of riders while he was swearing by his father,
so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out to them:
"Indeed, Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers.
Whoever must swear, let him swear by Allah, or else let him remain silent."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"A believer is not stung from the same hole twice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥayyiṣah ibn Masʿūd
and ʿAbdullāh ibn Sahl

set out toward Khaybar and separated among the date palms, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Sahl was killed. They accused the Jews. Then his brother ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sahl and his two cousins, Ḥuwayyiṣah and Muḥayyiṣah, came to the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān began to speak about his brother's case, though he was the youngest of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "The elder, the elder!" or he said, "Let the eldest begin."
So the two spoke about the matter of their companion, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Fifty of you shall swear against one man of them, and he will be handed over [to you] with his rope."
They said, "It is a matter we did not witness; how can we swear?" He said:
"Then the Jews will clear you by the oaths of fifty of them."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, they are a people of disbelievers."
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid the blood money from his own funds.
He said: Sahl said, "One day I entered one of their camel pens, and one of those camels kicked me with its leg."
Ḥammād said, "It was this or something like it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade throwing pebbles.
Ibn Jaʿfar said in his narration: And he said, "It does not harm the enemy and does not kill game, but it breaks a tooth and puts out an eye."
Ibn Mahdī said, "It does not harm the enemy,"
and he did not mention putting out an eye.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When one of you sneezes, let him say, 'Praise be to Allah.'
And let his brother or his companion say to him, 'May Allah have mercy on you.'
Then when he says to him, 'May Allah have mercy on you,'
let him say, 'May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting in a gathering with Ubayy ibn Kaʿb when Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī came, angry, and stood there. He said, "I ask you by Allah, did any of you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Asking permission is three times; if you are given permission, [enter], and if not, then go back'?"

Ubayy said, "What is that about?" He said, "I asked permission to see ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb yesterday three times and was not given permission, so I went back. Then I came to him today and entered, and I told him that I had come yesterday, greeted him with salām three times, and then left." He said, "We heard you, but we were busy at the time. Why did you not keep asking until you were given permission?" He said, "I asked permission just as I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [instruct]." He said, "By Allah, I will beat your back and your belly,
or you must bring someone who will testify for you to this."
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said, "By Allah, only the youngest of us will go with you. Get up, Abū Saʿīd."
So I got up and went to ʿUmar and said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no charity (ṣadaqah) due on fewer than five camels, and nothing is due on four. When they reach five, one sheep is due, up to nine. When they reach ten, two sheep are due, up to fourteen. When they reach fifteen, three sheep are due, up to nineteen. When they reach twenty, four sheep are due, up to twenty-four. When they reach twenty-five, a bint makhāḍ (a female camel in its second year) is due, up to thirty-five. If there is no bint makhāḍ, then a male ibn labūn (a camel in its third year). If they exceed that by one camel, a bint labūn is due, up to forty-five. If they exceed that by one camel, a ḥiqqah is due, up to sixty. If they exceed that by one camel, a jadhaʿah is due, up to seventy-five. If they exceed that by one camel, two bint labūn are due, up to ninety.
