If they exceed that by one camel, two ḥiqqahs are due, up to one hundred and twenty. Then for every fifty, a ḥiqqah, and for every forty, a bint labūn."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim had me read a document that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had written concerning the charities (ṣadaqāt) before Allah took him in death, and I found in it:

"For forty sheep, one sheep is due, up to one hundred and twenty. If they exceed that by one, two sheep are due, up to two hundred. If they exceed that by one, three sheep are due, up to three hundred. If they increase beyond that, then for every hundred, one sheep." And I found in it:
"What is separate is not to be combined, and what is combined is not to be separated." And I found in it:
"No billy goat, no old animal, and no defective animal is to be taken as charity (ṣadaqah)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The charities (ṣadaqāt) of the Muslims are to be taken at their watering places."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he
and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb were discussing charity (ṣadaqah) one day, and ʿUmar said, "Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he mentioned misappropriation of charity (ṣadaqah):
'Whoever misappropriates from it a camel or a sheep will be brought on the Day of Resurrection carrying it.'"
He said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Unays said, "Yes."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only established zakāh on these five: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, and corn.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to send someone to the people to estimate the yield of their vineyards and fruits.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have bees." He said, "Pay the tenth."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, protect it for me." So he protected it for me.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he took the tenth from honey.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Bahrain, or to Hajar, and I would come to an orchard shared among brothers, one of whom had become Muslim. I would take the tenth from the Muslim and the kharāj (land tax) from the polytheist.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The wasq is sixty ṣāʿ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The wasq is sixty ṣāʿ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Who will accept one thing from me, and I will accept Paradise for him?" I said, "I will." He said:
"Do not ask people for anything."
He said: Thawbān's whip would fall while he was riding, and he would not say to anyone, "Hand it to me," until he dismounted and took it himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Marriage is part of my sunnah, so whoever does not act on my sunnah is not from me. Marry, for I will boast of your numbers before the other nations. Whoever has the means, let him marry; and whoever does not find the means, let him fast, for fasting is a protection for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"We have not seen anything like marriage for two who love one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That a man
asked the Prophet ﷺ, "What is the right of a wife over her husband?" He said:
"That he feed her when he eats, clothe her when he clothes himself, not strike the face, not revile her, and not forsake her except within the house."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While a young woman was on a she-camel carrying some of the people's belongings, she caught sight of the Prophet ﷺ, and the mountain pass became narrow for them. She said, "Ḥall!" [a word to urge on a camel] and then, "O Allah, curse her."
He said: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"A she-camel that carries a curse must not accompany us."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not fitting for a truthful person (ṣiddīq) to be one who curses much."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Malik

ibn Marwān sent some jewelry from his own possessions to Umm al-Dardāʾ. Then one night ʿAbd al-Malik got up in the night and called his servant, who seemed to be slow in coming to him, so he cursed him. When morning came, Umm al-Dardāʾ said to him, "I heard you last night cursing your servant when you called him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, invoke [Allah] against the polytheists." He said:
"I was not sent as one who curses; I was only sent as a mercy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke to him about something I do not know what, and they angered him, so he cursed them and reviled them. When they left, I said, "O Messenger of Allah, whoever receives any good, these two have not received it!" He said, "And what is that?"
She said: I said, "You cursed them and reviled them." He said,
"Do you not know the condition I made with my Lord? I said: O Allah, I am only a human being, so whichever Muslim I curse or revile, make that a purification and a reward for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the chain of transmission of ʿAbdullāh ibn Numayr,
[narrated] the same as his report, except that in
the report of ʿĪsā he put "and a reward."
In the report of Abū Hurayrah he put "and a mercy."
In the report of Jābir
label: machine translation

segments_en: Umm Sulaym, who is the mother of Anas, had an orphan girl with her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the orphan girl and said:
"Is it you? You have grown up! May your age not grow older!"

The orphan girl went back to Umm Sulaym weeping. Umm Sulaym said, "What is the matter with you, my little daughter?" The girl said, "The Prophet of Allah ﷺ has invoked against me that my age should not grow older, so now my age will never grow older", or she said, "my generation." Umm Sulaym went out in haste, wrapping her head covering around her, until she met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her:
"What is the matter, Umm Sulaym?"
She said, "O Prophet of Allah, did you invoke against my orphan girl?" He said,
"And what is that, Umm Sulaym?"
She said, "She claims that you prayed that her age should not grow older and her generation should not grow older." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, then said,

"O Umm Sulaym, do you not know that my condition with my Lord is that I made a condition with my Lord, saying: I am only a human being; I am pleased as human beings are pleased, and I become angry as human beings become angry. So whichever of my community I invoke against with an invocation that he does not deserve, make it for him a purification, a purity, and a means of nearness by which You bring him close to You on the Day of Resurrection."
Abū Maʿn said: "yutaymah"
in the diminutive form in all three places in the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was playing with the boys when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, so I hid behind a door. He said: He came and gave me a pat on the back of the neck, and said:
"Go and call Muʿāwiyah for me."
He said: I went and said, "He is eating." He said: Then he said to me,
"Go and call Muʿāwiyah for me."
He said: I went and said, "He is eating." So he said:
"May Allah not fill his stomach."
Ibn al-Muthannā said: I asked Umayyah what "ḥaṭāni" meant. He said, "He slapped me on the back of the neck with a slap."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ﷺ said:
"Shall I not inform you what al-ʿaḍh is? It is slander (namīmah), the spreading of talk between people."
And Muḥammad ﷺ said:
"A man keeps speaking the truth until he is recorded as truthful (ṣiddīq), and he keeps lying until he is recorded as a great liar."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When Allah fashioned Adam in Paradise, He left him as long as Allah willed to leave him. Iblīs began to go around him, looking at what he was. When he saw that he was hollow, he knew that he had been created as a creature that could not control itself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw a man moving about in Paradise because of a tree he cut down from the middle of the road, which used to harm people."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "O Messenger of Allah, I do not know; perhaps you will pass away and I will remain after you, so give me some provision by which Allah will benefit me."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do such and such, do such and such" (Abū Bakr forgot it) "and remove harmful things from the road."
label: machine translation

segments_en: That al-Miswar ibn Makhramah
informed him from ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf,

who was an ally of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy and had witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ to Bahrain to bring its jizyah. The Prophet ﷺ had made a treaty with the people of Bahrain and had appointed al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Ḥaḍramī over them. Abū ʿUbaydah came back with money from Bahrain, and the Anṣār heard of Abū ʿUbaydah's arrival, so they attended the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he turned away, and they presented themselves to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled when he saw them, then said:
"I think you have heard that Abū ʿUbaydah has come with something from Bahrain."
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:

"Rejoice, and hope for that which pleases you. By Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but I fear that the world will be spread out for you as it was spread out for those before you, and you will compete for it as they competed for it, and it will destroy you as it destroyed them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Beware! Whoever kills a person under a covenant, who has the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger, has broken the protection of Allah, and he will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance can be detected from a distance of seventy years' travel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Allah created the creation, He wrote in His Book—He writes upon Himself,
and it is placed with Him upon the Throne—: 'Indeed My mercy prevails over My wrath.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed the angels do not enter a house in which there is a picture."

Busr said: Then Zayd fell ill afterward and we visited him, and there on his door was a curtain with a picture on it. He said: I said to ʿUbaydullāh al-Khawlānī, the stepson of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ: Did Zayd not tell us about pictures the other day? ʿUbaydullāh said: Did you not hear him when he said, "except a design on a cloth"?
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.'"

Abū Hurayrah said: "Besides what Allah has already made known to you. Recite, if you wish: {No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do.}" He said: Abū Hurayrah used to recite it as "qurrāti aʿyun" (comforts of eyes)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A piece of silk cloth was gifted to the Prophet ﷺ,
and the people began passing it around among themselves,
marveling at its beauty and softness.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Do you marvel at it?"
They said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, the handkerchiefs of Saʿd in Paradise are better than this."
Shuʿbah and Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, did not say:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel for a hundred years,
and recite, if you wish: {And extended shade}."
"And a place in Paradise the size of the bow of one of you is better than all that the sun rises upon or sets upon."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I recited to Mālik, from Sumayy,
from Abū Ṣāliḥ,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things,'
a hundred times in a day,

it will be for him equal to freeing ten slaves, a hundred good deeds will be written for him, a hundred bad deeds will be erased from him, and it will be a protection for him from Satan on that day until evening; and no one will bring anything better than what he brought, except someone who did more than that.
And whoever says: 'Glory be to Allah and with His praise,' a hundred times in a day, his sins will be wiped away even if they were like the foam of the sea."
label: machine translation

segments_en: may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said:

"When you hear the crowing of roosters, ask Allah for His bounty, for they have seen an angel; and when you hear the braying of a donkey, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed, for it has seen a devil."
He said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not come until two great groups fight one another,
with great slaughter between them, though their claim is one;
and until deceitful impostors are sent forth,
close to thirty of them,
each of whom claims that he is the messenger of Allah;
and until knowledge is taken away, earthquakes become frequent, time draws closer together, and trials appear,
and harj increases, which is killing;
and until wealth becomes so abundant among you that it overflows,
so that the owner of the wealth worries about who will accept his charity,
and until he offers it, and the one to whom he offers it says, 'I have no need of it.'
And until people compete in constructing tall buildings,
and until a man passes by another man's grave and says, 'I wish I were in his place.'
And until the sun rises from the west.
When it rises and the people see it, meaning they all believe,
that is the time when belief will not benefit a soul that had not believed before,
or had not earned some good through its belief.
And the Hour will come while two men have spread out their cloth between them,
and they will neither complete their sale nor fold it up.
And the Hour will come while a man has gone off with the milk of his she-camel, and he will not drink it.
And the Hour will come while he is plastering his trough, and he will not water [his animals] from it.
And the Hour will come while a man has raised his morsel to his mouth, and he will not eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with Ṣafwān, Jundab, and his companions while he was advising them, and they said, "Have you heard anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "I heard him say:

'Whoever does deeds to be heard, Allah will expose him on the Day of Resurrection.' He also said: 'Whoever causes hardship, Allah will cause hardship to him on the Day of Resurrection.'" They said, "Advise us." So he said:
"The first part of a person to rot is his belly,
so whoever is able to eat only what is good, let him do so,
and whoever is able to ensure that nothing stands between him and Paradise but a handful of blood he has shed, let him do so."
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh, "Who is it that says, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ'?" He said, "Yes, Jundab."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent him, and then sent Muʿādh after him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
had accepted Islam and then reverted to Judaism.
Then Muʿādh ibn Jabal came while [the man] was with Abū Mūsā, and he said, "What is this?" [Abū Mūsā] said, "He accepted Islam and then reverted to Judaism."
He said, "I will not sit down until I have him killed,
for that is the judgment of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sālim, the freed slave of Abū Ḥudhayfah, used to lead the first Emigrants and the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ in prayer at the mosque of Qubāʾ,
among them Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, Abū Salamah, Zayd, and ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Muslims gave permission regarding freeing the captives of Hawāzin, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I do not know which of you has given permission and which of you has not,
so go back until your leaders report your decision to us."
So the people went back and their leaders spoke with them,
then they returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him that the people were pleased and had given permission.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people said to Ibn ʿUmar, "We enter upon our ruler and say to them the opposite of what we say when we leave them." He said, "We used to count that as hypocrisy."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ ordered him to learn the writing of the Jews,
until I wrote letters for the Prophet ﷺ,
and I read their letters to him when they wrote to him.

ʿUmar said, while ʿAlī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and ʿUthmān were with him, "What does this woman say?" ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥāṭib said, "I said: She is telling you about their companion who did that to the two of them."
Abū Jamrah said, "I used to translate between Ibn ʿAbbās and the people."
And some people said, "A judge must have translators."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Heraclius sent for him with a group of riders from Quraysh,
then he said to his translator, "Tell them that I am going to question this man,
and if he lies to me, then call him a liar."
He then mentioned the hadith, and [Heraclius] said to the translator, "Tell him: If what you say is true, he will soon rule the place where my two feet are standing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the people pledged allegiance to ʿAbd al-Malik, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar wrote to him: "To the servant of Allah ʿAbd al-Malik, Commander of the Faithful: I acknowledge hearing and obeying the servant of Allah ʿAbd al-Malik, Commander of the Faithful,
according to the way of Allah and the way of His Messenger, as far as I am able,
and my sons have acknowledged that as well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū Sahm set out with Tamīm ad-Dārī and ʿAdī ibn Baddāʾ, and the man from Sahm died in a land where there was no Muslim. When the two came back with his belongings, they found a silver bowl inlaid with gold missing, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the two of them swear an oath. Then the bowl was found in Makkah, and it was said, "We bought it from ʿAdī and Tamīm." So two men from the next of kin of the man from Sahm stood up and swore by Allah: "Our testimony is more truthful than their testimony, and the bowl belongs to their companion."
He said: Concerning them was revealed:
"O you who have believed, [let there be] testimony among you..." This hadith is ḥasan gharīb, and it is the hadith of Ibn Abī Zāʾidah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which deed is best?" He said:
"Prayer at its proper time."
I said, "Then which?" He said:
"Then dutifulness to parents."
I said, "Then which?" He said:
"Striving in the cause of Allah."
Then he fell silent—[meaning] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—and had I asked for more, he would have given me more.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sulaymān said, "Tonight I will go around to ninety women,
each of whom will bear a boy who fights in the cause of Allah."
His companion—Sufyān said: meaning the angel—said to him, "Say, 'If Allah wills.'" But he forgot, and he went around to them,
and not one of the women brought a child,
except one, [who bore] half a boy.
Abū Hurayrah, relating it, said that he ﷺ said:
"Had he said, 'If Allah wills,'
he would not have broken his oath, and it would have fulfilled his need."
And once he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Had he made the exception."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Saʿd used to teach his sons these words as a teacher teaches boys, and he would say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge with them after prayer:

"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from cowardice, and I seek refuge in You from miserliness, and I seek refuge in You from being returned to the worst stage of life, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the world and the punishment of the grave."

ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān said: Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī was inconsistent in this hadith; he would say, "from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿUmar," and he would say, "from someone else," and was inconsistent in it. Abū ʿĪsā said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ by this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Anas ibn Mālik said to me, "What did Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿAmrah die of?" She said: I said, "The plague."
She said: He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The plague is martyrdom for every Muslim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever spends a pair [of something] in the cause of Allah, the gatekeepers of Paradise will call him from the gates of Paradise: 'O so-and-so, come, enter!'"
Abū Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, that is the one who will have no loss."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I hope that you will be among them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of al-Aḥzāb:
"Who will bring us news of the people?"
Az-Zubayr said, "I will." Then he said:
"Who will bring us news of the people?"
Az-Zubayr said, "I will." Then he said:
"Who will bring us news of the people?"
Az-Zubayr said, "I will." Then he said:
"Every prophet has a disciple,
and my disciple is az-Zubayr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of the Trench, the Prophet ﷺ called for volunteers, and az-Zubayr volunteered.
Then he called for them again, and az-Zubayr volunteered.
Then he called for them again, and az-Zubayr volunteered. Then he said:
"Every prophet has a disciple, and my disciple is az-Zubayr."
Sufyān said: I memorized it from Ibn al-Munkadir.
Ayyūb said to him, "O Abū Bakr, narrate to them from Jābir,
for the people are pleased when you narrate to them from Jābir."
So in that gathering he said, "I heard Jābir," and he repeated one report after another, [saying,] "I heard Jābir."
I said to Sufyān, "But ath-Thawrī says it was the day of Qurayẓah." He said, "I memorized it as [the day of the Trench], just as you are sitting [here]."
Sufyān said, "It was one day." And Sufyān smiled.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Blessing is in the forelocks of horses."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The hadith of one of them has entered into the hadith of the other, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Jābir, from Yaḥyā ibn Jābir aṭ-Ṭāʾī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from his father Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from an-Nawwās ibn Samʿān al-Kilābī, who said: One morning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the Dajjāl, sometimes lowering his voice about him and sometimes raising it, until we thought he was among the cluster of date palms.
He said: We left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then returned to him, and he noticed that in us and said, "What is the matter with you?"
He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, this morning you mentioned the Dajjāl, lowering your voice about him and raising it, until we thought he was among the cluster of date palms." He said,

"Something other than the Dajjāl is what I fear more for you. If he emerges while I am among you, I will contend with him on your behalf; and if he emerges while I am not among you, then each man must contend for himself, and Allah is my successor over every Muslim. He is a young man with tightly curled hair and one eye protruding, resembling ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Qaṭan. Whoever among you sees him, let him recite the opening verses of Sūrat al-Kahf." He said, "He will emerge between Syria and Iraq and will spread corruption to the right and to the left. O servants of Allah, remain steadfast!"
He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, how long will he remain on the earth?" He said,
"Forty days: a day like a year, a day like a month, a day like a week, and the rest of his days like your days."
He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, regarding that day which is like a year, will the prayer of one day suffice for us in it?" He said,
"No, but estimate its length [and pray accordingly]."
He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, how fast will he travel through the earth?" He said,

"Like rain driven by the wind behind it. He will come to a people and call them, and they will deny him and reject his words; so he will leave them, and their wealth will follow him, and by morning they will have nothing in their hands. Then he will come to another people and call them, and they will respond to him and believe him. He will command the sky to rain, and it will rain; and he will command the earth to grow, and it will grow. Their grazing livestock will come back to them in the evening with humps taller than ever, udders full of milk, and flanks stretched [with fullness]. Then he will come to a ruin and say to it, 'Bring forth your treasures,' and its treasures will follow him like swarms of bees. Then he will call a man brimming with youth, strike him with the sword and cut him into two pieces, then call him, and he will come forward, his face beaming and laughing. While he is in that state, Allah will send down ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, at the white minaret in the east of Damascus, wearing two garments dyed with saffron, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, drops fall from it, and when he raises it, beads like pearls cascade from it. No disbeliever can smell his breath without dying, and his breath reaches as far as his sight. He will pursue him until he catches him at the gate of Ludd and kills him. Then he will remain so for as long as Allah wills."
He said: Then Allah will reveal to him, 'I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one has the power to fight; so take My servants safely to aṭ-Ṭūr.'
He said: And Allah will send Yājūj and Mājūj, and they are as Allah said:
"They descend from every elevation."

He said: The first of them will pass by Lake Tiberias and drink what is in it. Then the last of them will pass by it and say, 'There was once water here.' Then they will travel until they reach the mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis and say, 'We have killed those on earth; come, let us kill those in the sky.'

They will shoot their arrows toward the sky, and Allah will return their arrows to them stained red with blood. ʿĪsā ibn Maryam and his companions will be besieged until the head of an ox will be better for one of them than a hundred dinars are for one of you today.

He said: Then ʿĪsā ibn Maryam and his companions will turn to Allah in supplication. He said: Allah will send upon them worms in their necks, and by morning they will lie dead like the death of a single soul. He said: Then ʿĪsā and his companions will descend and find not a handspan of ground that is not filled with their rot, stench and blood. He said: Then ʿĪsā and his companions will turn to Allah in supplication, and Allah will send birds like the necks of Bactrian camels. He said: They will carry them and throw them where Allah wills. And the Muslims will burn their bows, arrows and quivers as fuel for seven years. He said: Then Allah will send rain upon them that no house of hair or clay will keep out. He said: It will wash the earth and leave it like a smooth mirror. He said: Then the earth will be told, 'Bring forth your fruit and restore your blessing.'

On that day a group of people will eat from a single pomegranate and shelter beneath its rind. Milk will be blessed, so that a large group of people will be satisfied with one milch camel, a tribe with one milch cow, and a clan with one milch sheep. While they are like that, Allah will send a wind that will take the soul of every believer, and the rest of the people will remain, copulating openly like donkeys. Upon them the Hour will come."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Mā'iz ibn Mālik al-Aslamī
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have wronged myself and committed adultery, and I want you to purify me."
He turned him away. The next day he came to him again and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed adultery."
He turned him away a second time, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent word to his people, saying:
"Do you know of anything wrong with his mind? Do you find anything objectionable in him?"

They said, "We know nothing of him except that his mind is sound, and that he is among our righteous ones, as far as we can see." Then he came a third time, and again he sent word to them and asked about him, and they told him that there was nothing wrong with him or with his mind. When the fourth time came, a pit was dug for him, then he gave the order and he was stoned.
He said: Then the woman of Ghāmid came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed adultery, so purify me."
He turned her away. The next day she said, "O Messenger of Allah, why do you turn me away? Perhaps you are turning me away as you turned Mā'iz away. By Allah, I am pregnant." He said:
"If you insist, then go until you have given birth."
When she gave birth, she came to him with the child wrapped in a cloth and said, "This is the one I have given birth to." He said:
"Go and nurse him until you have weaned him."
When she had weaned him, she came to him with the child, who had a piece of bread in his hand, and said, "O Prophet of Allah, here he is; I have weaned him and he is eating food."

The child was given to one of the Muslims. Then he gave the order concerning her, and a pit was dug for her up to her chest, and he commanded the people, and they stoned her. Khālid ibn al-Walīd came forward with a stone and struck her head, and blood spurted onto Khālid's face, so he cursed her. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ heard him cursing her and said:
"Gently, O Khālid! By the One in whose hand is my soul, she has repented with such a repentance that if a tax collector were to repent with it, he would be forgiven."
Then he gave the order concerning her, and the funeral prayer was performed over her, and she was buried.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ stoned a man from Aslam, and a man from the Jews and his wife.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the slave woman.
[He narrated] the like of their hadith, and he did not mention the statement of Ibn Shihāb, "And the ḍafīr is the rope."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Through the chain of al-Layth, the like of his hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged on the basis of an oath and one witness.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed, Allah is pleased with three things for you and dislikes three things for you. He is pleased for you that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and that you hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah and do not become divided. And He dislikes for you gossip ("it was said and he said"), excessive questioning, and wasting wealth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And Qutaybah, and Ibn
Ḥujr. Ibn Ḥujr said: Ismāʿīl informed us; and the other two said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
who is Ibn Jaʿfar, from Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Yazīd,
the freed slave of al-Munbaʿith, from Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, that a man
asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a lost item that is found, and he said:
"Publicize it for a year, then learn its container and its binding. Then spend it. If its owner comes, give it to him."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about a stray sheep?" He said:
"Take it, for it is for you, or for your brother, or for the wolf."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about a stray camel?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry until his cheeks turned red, or his face turned red, and then he said:
"What do you want with it? It has its water-skin and its hooves; it will reach water and eat from trees until its owner finds it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I went out with Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah, and I found a whip.
And he related the hadith, like it, up to his words, "and I made use of it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:
"Whoever shelters a stray animal is astray, so long as he does not publicize it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and saw,
my eyes, and my heart retained it when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke it.
Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of al-Layth, and he mentioned in it:
"It is not lawful for any of you to stay with his brother until he makes him fall into sin."
Like what is in the hadith of Wakīʿ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Each of you is a shepherd."
Al-Layth added: Yūnus said: Ruzayq ibn Ḥakīm wrote to Ibn Shihāb, while I was with him that day in Wādī al-Qurā: "Do you think I should hold the Friday prayer?"
Ruzayq was in charge of land that he worked,
and on it was a group of Sudanese people and others,
and Ruzayq was at that time in Aylah.
So Ibn Shihāb wrote, while I was listening, instructing him to hold the Friday prayer,
and informing him that Sālim had told him that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Each of you is a shepherd,
and each of you is responsible for his flock.
The leader is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock;
a man is a shepherd over his family and is responsible for his flock;
a woman is a shepherd in her husband's house and is responsible for her flock;

and a servant is a shepherd over his master's property and is responsible for his flock." He said: I think he also said: "A man is a shepherd over his father's property and is responsible for his flock. Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock."
label: machine translation

segments_en: It is a right owed to Allah upon every Muslim to wash himself every seven days, washing his head and his body."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] to his muezzin on a rainy day: "When you say, 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' do not say, 'Come to prayer.' Say, 'Pray in your homes.'" He said: It seems the people disapproved of that, so he said: "Are you surprised at this? One who was better than me did this. Indeed, Friday prayer is an obligation, and I disliked making it hard for you, so that you would walk in mud and slippery ground."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbāyah ibn Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ caught up with me as I was walking
to the Friday prayer, and he said: "Rejoice, for these steps of yours are in the cause of Allah. I heard Abū ʿAbs say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever's feet become dusty in the cause of Allah, the Fire is forbidden to them.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The one who
added the third call to prayer on Friday was ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, when the people of Medina had become numerous,
whereas the Prophet ﷺ had only one muezzin,
and the call to prayer on Friday was made when the imam sat,
that is, on the pulpit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Prophet ﷺ used to deliver two sermons, sitting for a short while between them.
Bishr added: while standing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When it is Friday,
at every door of the mosque there are angels recording the people according to their ranks, the first and then the next.
When the imam comes out, they fold up the scrolls and listen to the sermon.
The one who goes early to the prayer is like one who offers a camel.
Then the one after him is like one who offers a cow.
Then the one after him is like one who offers a ram."
[The narrator continued] until he mentioned the chicken and the egg. Sahl added in his narration:
"Whoever comes after that, he comes only for what is due to the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ was delivering the Friday sermon when people stood up to him and called out, saying: "O Prophet of Allah, the rain has failed and the animals are dying. Pray to Allah to give us rain." He said:
"O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain."

He said: By Allah, we did not see in the sky even a wisp of cloud. He said: Then a cloud arose and spread, and then it rained, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came down and prayed, and the people left. It continued to rain until the next Friday. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to deliver the sermon, they called out to him, saying: "O Prophet of Allah, the houses have collapsed and the roads are cut off. Pray to Allah to hold it back from us."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled and said:
"O Allah, around us and not upon us."
Then it cleared away from Medina and rained around it, while not a drop fell on Medina. I looked at Medina and it was like a crown."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the Friday sermon standing, a caravan arrived in Medina, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hurried to it until none remained except twelve men, among them Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. Then the verse was revealed:
"But when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush to it and leave you standing."
He said: This is a good and sound hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed [from Minā] at the end of that day after he had prayed the Ẓuhr prayer, then returned to Minā and stayed there for the nights of the days of Tashrīq. When the sun had passed its zenith, he would stone each of the pillars with seven pebbles, saying the takbīr with each pebble. He would stand at the first and the second, prolonging his standing and supplicating humbly, and he would stone the third and not stand at it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned Jamrat al-ʿAqabah on the Day of Sacrifice, then returned to his dwelling in Minā and called for his sacrificial animal, and it was slaughtered. Then he called for the barber, took hold of the right side of his head and shaved it, and began distributing the hairs, one or two at a time, to those near him. Then he took the left side of his head and shaved it, and then said:
"Is Abū Ṭalḥah here?"
And he gave it to Abū Ṭalḥah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Women are not required to shave their heads; women are only required to trim."
label: machine translation

segments_en: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only had ʿĀʾishah perform ʿUmrah in Dhū al-Ḥijjah in order to put an end to the practice of the polytheists. For this tribe of Quraysh and those who followed their religion used to say: "When the camels' fur has grown back, the sores on their backs have healed, and Ṣafar has come, then ʿUmrah becomes permissible for whoever wishes to perform it."
So they used to forbid ʿUmrah until Dhū al-Ḥijjah and Muḥarram had ended.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The messenger of Marwān, whom he had sent to Umm Maʿqil, informed me that she said: Abū Maʿqil was going for Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he arrived, Umm Maʿqil said: "You know that I owe a Hajj." So the two of them set off walking until they came to him, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, I owe a Hajj, and Abū Maʿqil has a young camel."
Abū Maʿqil said: "She is right, but I have devoted it in the cause of Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Give it to her so that she may perform Hajj on it, for that too is in the cause of Allah."
So he gave her the young camel. Then she said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a woman who has grown old and ill. Is there any deed that would suffice for me in place of my Hajj?" He said:
"An ʿUmrah in Ramadan suffices in place of a Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the Farewell Hajj, we had a camel, which Abū Maʿqil had devoted in the cause of Allah. Illness struck us and Abū Maʿqil died. The Prophet ﷺ set out, and when he had finished his Hajj, I came to him, and he said:
"O Umm Maʿqil, what prevented you from going out with us?"
She said: "We had prepared, but Abū Maʿqil died. We had a camel that we used to perform Hajj on, and Abū Maʿqil bequeathed it for the cause of Allah." He said:
"Why did you not go out on it? For Hajj is in the cause of Allah. But since you missed this Hajj with us, then perform ʿUmrah in Ramadan, for it is like a Hajj."
She used to say: "Hajj is Hajj and ʿUmrah is ʿUmrah, yet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said this to me. I do not know whether it was specifically for me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended to perform Hajj, and a woman said to her husband: "Let me perform Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on your camel."
He said: "I have nothing on which to send you for Hajj."
She said: "Let me perform Hajj on your camel so-and-so."
He said: "That one is endowed for the cause of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

So he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "My wife sends you greetings of peace and the mercy of Allah, and she asked me to let her perform Hajj with you. She said: 'Let me perform Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'
I said: 'I have nothing on which to send you for Hajj.'
She said: 'Let me perform Hajj on your camel so-and-so.'
I said: 'That one is endowed for the cause of Allah.'" He said:
"Had you sent her for Hajj on it, it would have been in the cause of Allah."
He said: "She also told me to ask you what is equal to a Hajj with you."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Give her my greetings of peace, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings, and inform her that it is equal to a Hajj with me."
He meant an ʿUmrah in Ramadan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ʿUmrah twice: one ʿUmrah in Dhū al-Qaʿdah and one in Shawwāl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar was asked how many times the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ʿUmrah, and he said: "Twice."
ʿĀʾishah said: "Ibn ʿUmar knows that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ʿUmrah three times, besides the one he combined with the Farewell Hajj."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān:
"O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, have your sister ʿĀʾishah ride behind you and have her perform ʿUmrah from Tanʿīm. When you descend with her from the rise, she should enter iḥrām, for it is an accepted ʿUmrah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the mosque when Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr appeared before us, wearing nothing but a cloak of his that was patched with fur. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he wept because of the comfort he had once enjoyed and the state he was in that day. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"How will you be when one of you goes out in the morning in one set of clothes and goes out in the evening in another, when a dish is set before him and another is taken away, and you cover your houses as the Kaʿbah is covered?"
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, on that day we will be better off than we are today; we will be free to devote ourselves to worship and will be spared the burden of providing for ourselves."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"You are better today than you will be on that day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Building is all a burden. I said, "What about what is unavoidable?" He said, "There is no reward and no sin in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever abandons [fine] clothing out of humility before Allah, while he is able to wear it, Allah will call him on the Day of Resurrection before all of creation until He lets him choose whichever of the garments of faith he wishes to wear."
This is a good hadith. As for his saying "the garments of faith",
it means what the people of faith will be given of the garments of Paradise.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"All spending is in the cause of Allah, except building, for there is no good in it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A beggar came and asked Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn ʿAbbās said to the beggar, "Do you testify that there is no
god but Allah?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "And do you fast Ramadan?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "You have asked, and the one who asks has a right. It is indeed our duty to give to you."
So he gave him a garment, then said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'No Muslim clothes another Muslim with a garment except that he is in Allah's protection as long as any piece of it remains on him.'"
He said: This is a good hadith, gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shall I not tell you who is forbidden to the Fire, or for whom the Fire is forbidden? Every person who is close [to people], easygoing, gentle, and agreeable."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the Day of Resurrection the arrogant will be gathered like tiny ants in the forms of men, covered with humiliation from every side. They will be driven to a prison in Hell called Būlas, overpowered by the fire of fires, and made to drink the discharge of the people of the Fire, the mud of khabāl."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever has three [qualities], Allah will spread His protection over him and admit him into His Paradise: gentleness toward the weak, compassion toward parents, and kindness to those under his authority."
He said: This is a good hadith, gharīb.
And Abū Bakr ibn al-Munkadir is the brother of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Kifl of the Children of Israel did not refrain from any sin. A woman came to him and he gave her sixty dinars so that he could have relations with her. When he sat before her as a man sits with his wife, she trembled and wept. He said, "What makes you weep? Did I force you?" She said, "No, but this is something I have never done, and only need drove me to it." He said, "You do this, and I have never done it? Go, the money is yours."
And he said, "No, by Allah, I will never disobey Allah after this."
He died that night, and in the morning it was written on his door: 'Allah has forgiven al-Kifl.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever keeps silent is saved."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever taunts his brother for a sin will not die until he commits it."
Aḥmad said: [meaning] a sin from which [his brother] has repented.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not show malicious joy at your brother's misfortune, for Allah may have mercy on him and afflict you."
He said: This is a good hadith, gharīb.
Makḥūl heard from Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ, Anas ibn Mālik, and Abū Hind al-Dārī, and it is said that he did not hear from any of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ except these three.
Makḥūl the Syrian has the kunyah Abū ʿAbd Allāh; he was a slave who was freed. Makḥūl al-Azdī was from Basra; he heard from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, and ʿUmārah ibn Zādhān narrates from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He is of the descendants of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, from ʿUthmān ibn Muhammad al-Akhnasī,
from Saʿīd al-Maqburī,
from Abū Hurayrah,
that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Beware of discord among people, for it is the shaver [of religion]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from the Anṣār came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, why do I see your face looking pale?" He said, "Hunger."
So the Anṣārī went to his dwelling but found nothing there. He went out searching and came upon a Jew watering date palms. The Anṣārī said to the Jew, "Shall I water your palms?" He said, "Yes."
He said, "For every bucket, a date."
The Anṣārī stipulated that he would not take any rotten date, nor any dried-up one, nor any poor-quality one, and that he would take only good, firm ones.
So he drew water for about two ṣāʿ [of dates] and brought it to the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to practice crop-sharing and saw nothing wrong with it, until we heard Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden it. So we abandoned it because of what he said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade muḥāqalah.
And muḥāqalah is renting out land [for a share of its crop].
label: machine translation

segments_en: When he heard how much people were saying
about renting out land, he said, "Glory be to Allah! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said:
'Would that one of you lend it to his brother.'
He did not forbid renting it out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿādh ibn Jabal
rented out land during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, for a third and a quarter, and he still acts upon it to this day of yours.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said:
'For one of you to lend his brother the land is better for him than to take a fixed rent for it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to practice muḥāqalah during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he related that some of his uncles came to them and said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
'Whoever has land should not rent it out for a specified amount of food.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave Khaybar to its people on the basis of half [the produce], both its palms and its land.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Khaybar, he gave it [to its people] for half [the produce].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ heard some voices and said,
"What is this sound?"
They said, "The date palms are being pollinated." He said,
"If they did not do it, it would still be fine."
So they did not pollinate that year, and the dates came out poor. They mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said,
"If it is something of your worldly affairs, then it is your concern; but if it is something of your religion, then refer it to me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Three things must not be withheld: water, pasture, and fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the thing that it is not permissible to withhold?" He said, "Water, salt, and fire."
She said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we know about water, but what about salt and fire?" He said,
"O Ḥumayrāʾ, whoever gives fire is as if he had given in charity everything that fire cooks; and whoever gives salt

is as if he had given in charity everything that salt makes good; and whoever gives a Muslim a drink of water where water is found is as if he had freed a slave; and whoever gives a Muslim a drink of water where water is not found is as if he had given him life."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He asked [the Prophet ﷺ] to grant him the salt that is called the salt of the Mārib dam.

So he granted it to him. Then al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis at-Tamīmī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I used to go to that salt in the Jāhiliyyah. It lies in a land with no water, and whoever comes to it takes it; it is like flowing water that never runs dry."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked Abyaḍ ibn Ḥammāl to relinquish his grant of the salt.
He said, "I will relinquish it on the condition that you count it as a charity from me."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"It is a charity from you, and it is like flowing water that never runs dry; whoever comes to it may take it."
Faraj said: And today it remains so; whoever comes to it takes it.
He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ granted him land and palms at al-Jurf, the Jurf of Murād, in its place when he released him from it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Surplus water must not be withheld, nor the water left in a well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled concerning the watering of palm trees from a flood stream that the higher ones are watered first, before the lower ones, and the water is held until it reaches the ankles; then the water is released to the next lower one, and so on until the orchards are finished or the water runs out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Begin with the horses on the day they come to water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever digs a well has forty cubits around it as a resting place for his livestock."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to say "prayer is better than sleep" in the Fajr call, and he forbade me from saying it in the ʿIshāʾ call.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to the Prophet ﷺ to inform him that it was time for the Fajr prayer, and it was said, "He is asleep."
So he said, "Prayer is better than sleep, prayer is better than sleep." This was then established in the call to the Fajr prayer, and the practice remained so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When he was with her on her day and night and heard the muʾadhdhin giving the call to prayer, he would say what the muʾadhdhin said.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Saʿīd said to me, "When you are in the desert, raise your voice with the call to prayer, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'No jinn, human, tree, or stone hears it except that it will testify for him.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The muʾadhdhins will have the longest necks of all people on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever gives the call to prayer for twelve years, Paradise becomes due for him, and for his call to prayer sixty good deeds are recorded for him each day, and for each iqāmah thirty good deeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The call to prayer of Bilāl was in pairs of phrases, and his iqāmah was in single phrases.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw Bilāl giving the call to prayer in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in pairs of phrases, and he would give the iqāmah once.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is in the mosque when the call to prayer reaches him and then leaves, not leaving for a need and not intending to return, he is a hypocrite."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I see that after me you will adorn your mosques lavishly, just as the Jews adorned their synagogues and the Christians adorned their churches."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"No people ever fall into evil deeds except that they adorn their mosques."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Filth is thrown into it. So he said:
"When it has been watered several times, pray in it."
He attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are things that are not fitting in the mosque: it is not to be taken as a thoroughfare, weapons are not to be drawn in it, a bow is not to be twanged in it, arrows are not to be scattered in it, raw meat is not to be carried through it, no legal punishment is to be carried out in it, no retaliation is to be taken from anyone in it, and it is not to be made a marketplace."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Keep your mosques free of your children, your insane, your wicked, your buying and selling, your disputes, the raising of your voices, the carrying out of your legal punishments, and the drawing of your swords. Put purification places at their doors, and perfume them with incense on Fridays."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
one of the People of the Ṣuffah. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us, "Set off."
So we went to the house of ʿĀʾishah, and we ate and drank. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us,
"If you wish you may sleep here, and if you wish you may go to the mosque."
He said: We said, "Rather, we will go to the mosque."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from the Anṣār sent word to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Come and mark out a place of prayer for me in my house so that I may pray in it," and this was after he had gone blind. So he came and did so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of my uncles prepared food for the Prophet ﷺ and said to the Prophet ﷺ, "I would like you to eat in my house and pray in it."
He said: So he came to him, and in the house was a male palm tree of these male palms. He ordered a part of it to be swept and sprinkled with water, and he prayed, and we prayed with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever removes something harmful from the mosque, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The first to light lamps in the mosques was Tamīm ad-Dārī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ scraped off spittle from the qiblah wall of the mosque.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade announcing a lost item in the mosque.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever goes out from his house to prayer and says: 'O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask You, and I ask You by the right of this walking of mine; I did not come out in arrogance, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I came out to guard against Your displeasure and to seek Your pleasure. So I ask You to protect me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins, for none forgives sins except You,' Allah turns His face towards him, and seventy thousand angels seek forgiveness for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are three things about which I swear, and I will tell you a hadith, so memorize it." He said:

"The wealth of a servant never decreases because of charity (ṣadaqah). No servant is wronged by an injustice and bears it patiently except that Allah increases him in honor. And no servant opens a door of begging except that Allah opens for him a door of poverty," or a similar word. "And I will tell you a hadith, so memorize it." He said:

"This world is only for four types of people: a servant whom Allah has given wealth and knowledge, so he fears his Lord regarding it, maintains his family ties with it, and knows the right of Allah in it; this one is in the best of positions. And a servant whom Allah has given knowledge but not wealth; he is sincere in his intention and says, 'If I had wealth, I would do as so-and-so does.' He is [rewarded] according to his intention, so their reward is equal. And a servant whom Allah has given wealth but not knowledge; he squanders his wealth without knowledge, does not fear his Lord regarding it, does not maintain his family ties with it, and does not know the right of Allah in it; this one is in the worst of positions. And a servant whom Allah has given neither wealth nor knowledge; he says, 'If I had wealth, I would do with it as so-and-so does.' He is [judged] according to his intention, so their burden of sin is equal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not acquire estates, lest you become fond of this world."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
said, "O Messenger of Allah, which of the people is best?" He said:
"The one whose life is long and whose deeds are good."
He said, "And which of the people is worst?" He said:
"The one whose life is long and whose deeds are bad."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The Hour will not come until time becomes close, so that a year is like a month, a month like a week, a week like a day, a day like an hour, and an hour like the blaze of a fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed every nation has a trial, and the trial of my nation is wealth."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"The son of Adam has no right to anything besides these things: a house in which he lives, a garment with which he covers his nakedness, and a crust of bread and water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There were two brothers in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. One of them would come to the Prophet ﷺ, and the other worked at a trade. The one who worked complained about his brother to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"Perhaps you are being provided for because of him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"He has succeeded who has submitted [to Islam], whose provision is just enough, and whom Allah has made content with it."
He said: This hadith is hasan ṣaḥīḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Blessed is the one who is guided to Islam, whose living is just enough, and who is content."
He said: Abū Hāniʾ's name is Ḥumayd ibn Hāniʾ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said to the Prophet ﷺ, "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I love you." He said:
"Consider what you are saying."
He said, "By Allah, I love you." He said:
"Consider what you are saying."
He said, "By Allah, I love you."
three times. Then he said:
"If you love me, then prepare a covering for poverty, for poverty comes faster to the one who loves me than a flood to its end."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The poor among the Muslims will enter Paradise forty years before their rich."
This hadith is hasan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah and she called for food for me and said, "I never eat my fill of food and wish to weep except that I weep."
He said, I asked, "Why?" She said, "I remember the state in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed from this world. By Allah, he never ate his fill of bread and meat twice in a day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his family never ate their fill of wheat bread three days in a row until he departed from this world.
This hadith is ṣaḥīḥ ḥasan gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Barley bread would never be left over from the family of
the house of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would not store anything for the next day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led the people in prayer, some men would collapse from their standing in prayer because of hunger. They were the People of the Bench (Aṣḥāb al-Ṣuffah), so that the Bedouins would say, "These are madmen." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he turned to them and said:
"If you knew what you have with Allah, you would love to increase in poverty and need."
Faḍālah said, "And I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on that day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until, on part of the road to Makkah, he lagged behind with some companions of his who were in the state of iḥrām, while he himself was not in iḥrām.
Then he saw a wild donkey and mounted his horse.
He asked his companions to hand him his whip, but they refused.
He asked them for his spear, but they refused.
So he took it himself, charged at the donkey, and killed it.
Some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ ate from it, and some refused.
When they caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they asked him about that, and he said:
"It is only a meal that Allah fed you."
And from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Qatādah, concerning the wild donkey, similar to the hadith of Abū al-Naḍr; he said:
"Do you have any of its meat with you?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
"O Messenger of Allah, shall I go out to fight in jihād?" He said: "Do you have parents?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then strive in jihād by [serving] them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the prophets stopped to rest beneath a tree, and an ant stung him. He ordered that their dwelling be burned with everything in it. Then Allah revealed to him: "Could it not have been just one ant?"
And al-Ashʿath said, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, the same, and added: "For they glorify [Allah]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From al-Aʿmash,
from Zayd ibn Wahb,
from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd,
who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the truthful and the one declared truthful, narrated to us:

"Each of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days; then he becomes a clinging clot for a similar period; then a lump of flesh for a similar period. Then Allah sends the angel to him, who breathes the soul into him, and he is commanded to write four matters: his provision, his life span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or blessed. By the One besides Whom there is no god, one of you may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only a cubit between him and it, then what is written overtakes him, and he ends with the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And one of you may do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only a cubit between him and it, then what is written overtakes him, and he ends with the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that he was sitting on the cushions of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz during his governorship of Madinah, with ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr present. ʿUmar delayed the ʿaṣr prayer somewhat, so ʿUrwah said to him: "Indeed, Jibrīl came down and led the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in prayer."
ʿUmar said to him: "Be careful about what you say, O ʿUrwah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or a picture."
He means statues of living beings.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Ādam bears a share of its [burden]" and Sufyān sometimes said, "of its blood" "because he was the first to establish the practice of killing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Mūsā said: 'My Lord, show us Ādam, who brought us and himself out of Paradise.' So Allah showed him Ādam, and he said: 'You are our father Ādam?' Ādam said to him: 'Yes.'
He said: 'You are the one into whom Allah breathed of His spirit, whom He taught all the names, and for whom He commanded the angels to prostrate, and they prostrated?' He said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'What made you bring us and yourself out of Paradise?' Ādam said to him: 'And who are you?' He said: 'I am Mūsā.'
He said: 'You are the prophet of the Children of Israel, to whom Allah spoke from behind a veil, placing no messenger from His creation between you and Him?' He said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'Did you not find that this was in the Book of Allah before I was created?' He said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'Then why do you blame me for something that Allah, the Exalted, had decreed before me?'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said at that point:
"So Ādam prevailed over Mūsā; so Ādam prevailed over Mūsā."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with her, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me one day, delighted, and said:

"O ʿĀʾishah, did you not see that Mujazziz al-Mudlijī came in to me while Usāmah ibn Zayd was with me? He saw Usāmah ibn Zayd and Zayd, who were covered with a sheet, their heads covered and their feet showing, and he said: 'These feet are from one another.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to let his hair hang down loose,
while the polytheists used to part their hair; and the People of the Book used to let their hair hang down,
and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ liked to follow the People of the Book in matters about which he had not been commanded anything.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ parted his hair.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was at sea and met two men from the people of Yemen, Dhū Kalāʿ and Dhū ʿAmr,
and I began to tell them about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Dhū ʿAmr said to me, "If what you mention about your companion is true,
then his term has already run out three days ago."

They both set out with me, and when we were part of the way along the road, a party of riders from the direction of Madinah appeared to us. We asked them, and they said, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been taken in death, Abū Bakr has been appointed as successor, and the people are well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went on the expedition of the Army of the Khabaṭ, and Abū ʿUbaydah was made the commander.
We became extremely hungry, and then the sea cast up a dead whale,
the like of which we had never seen,
called al-ʿAnbar.
We ate from it for half a month,
and Abū ʿUbaydah took one of its bones, and a rider passed beneath it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to worship a stone,
and when we found a stone better than it, we threw it away and took the other.
When we could not find a stone, we would gather a heap of earth,
then bring a sheep and milk it over that heap,
then circle around it.
When the month of Rajab began, we would say, "The remover of spearheads."
So we would not leave any spear with an iron head or any arrow with an iron head except that we pulled it off and put it aside during the month of Rajab.
And I heard Abū Rajāʾ
say: On the day the Prophet ﷺ was sent, I was a boy tending camels for my family.
When we heard of his emergence, we fled to the Fire, to Musaylimah the Liar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah said: It reached us that Musaylimah the Liar came to Madinah,
and stayed in the house of Bint al-Ḥārith.
Married to him was the daughter of al-Ḥārith ibn Kurayz,
who was the mother of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿĀmir.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him, with Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās,
who is the one called the orator of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was a stick.
He stood before him and spoke with him. Musaylimah said to him, "If you wish, you may leave the matter between us and you,
and then make it ours after you." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Even if you asked me for this stick, I would not give it to you. And I see that you are the one about whom I was shown what I was shown.
And this is Thābit ibn Qays, and he will answer you on my behalf." Then the Prophet ﷺ left.
ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh said: I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās about the dream of
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which he mentioned. Ibn ʿAbbās said: It was mentioned to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"While I was sleeping, I was shown that two bracelets of gold were placed in my hands, and I found them dreadful and disliked them.
Then I was permitted, so I blew on them and they flew away.
I interpreted them as two liars who would appear."
ʿUbaydullāh said: One of them is al-ʿAnsī, whom Fayrūz killed in Yemen,
and the other is Musaylimah the Liar.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were sitting with Ibn Masʿūd,
when Khabbāb came and said, "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān,
can these young men recite as you recite?" He said, "If you wish, I will order one of them to recite to you." He said, "Yes."
He said, "Recite, O ʿAlqamah."

Zayd ibn Ḥudayr, the brother of Ziyād ibn Ḥudayr, said, "Do you order ʿAlqamah to recite when he is not the best reciter among us?" He said, "If you wish, I will tell you what the Prophet ﷺ said about your people and his people."
So I recited fifty verses from Sūrah Maryam,
and ʿAbdullāh said, "How do you see it?" He said, "He has done well."
ʿAbdullāh said, "I do not recite anything except that he recites it."
Then he turned to Khabbāb, who was wearing a gold ring, and said, "Has the time not come for this ring to be thrown away?" He said, "You will not see it on me after today." And he threw it away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to ʿUmar in a delegation,
and he began calling the men one by one, naming them. I said, "Do you not know me, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said, "Yes,
you embraced Islam when they disbelieved,
you advanced when they turned back,
you were faithful when they betrayed,
and you recognized when they denied."
ʿAdī said, "Then I do not care now."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said in his sermon:
"The burden of proof is upon the claimant, and the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made."
This is a hadith whose chain of narration is open to criticism.
Muhammad ibn ʿUbaydillāh al-ʿArzamī is considered weak in hadith on account of his memory; Ibn al-Mubārak and others declared him weak.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ sent the Prophet ﷺ some food in a bowl, and ʿĀʾishah struck the bowl with her hand and spilled what was in it. So the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Food for food, and a vessel for a vessel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ borrowed a bowl, and it was lost, so he made himself liable to compensate them for it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The partner has the right of pre-emption, and pre-emption applies to everything."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ granted him a piece of land in Ḥaḍramawt.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from a practice that had been beneficial to us: that when one of us had land, he would give it out for a portion of its yield or for some dirhams. And he said:
"If one of you has land, let him lend it to his brother or cultivate it himself."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not forbid sharecropping, but he commanded that they be kind to one another.
label: machine translation

segments_en: If the people of the heavens and the people of the earth were to share in shedding the blood of a believer, Allah would cast them all headlong into the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he had retaliation carried out against a father for [killing] his son, but he did not have retaliation carried out against a son for [killing] his father.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ paid the blood money for the two men of Banū ʿĀmir at the rate of blood money for Muslims, for they had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr, and whoever takes a handspan of land unjustly will have it hung around his neck on the Day of Resurrection from seven earths."
Ḥātim ibn Siyāh al-Marwazī added in this hadith: Maʿmar said: It reached me from az-Zuhrī, and I did not hear it from him, that he added in this hadith:
"Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr."
Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamzah likewise narrated this hadith from az-Zuhrī, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Sahl, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ.
Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated it from az-Zuhrī, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ, and Sufyān did not mention ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Sahl in it.
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Ward off the prescribed punishments from the Muslims as much as you can. If there is a way out for him, then let him go on his way, for it is better for the leader to err in pardoning than to err in punishing."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ carried out stoning, Abū Bakr carried out stoning, and I have carried out stoning. Were it not that I dislike adding to the Book of Allah, I would write it in the Muṣḥaf, for I fear that people will come and not find it in the Book of Allah and so disbelieve in it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a Jewish man and a Jewish woman stoned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ had a Jewish man and a Jewish woman stoned.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ administered the prescribed punishment of forty [strokes] with two sandals.
Misʿar said: I think it was for wine.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The prescribed punishment for the sorcerer is a strike with the sword."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If a man says to another man, 'O Jew,' strike him twenty [lashes]; and if he says, 'O effeminate one,' strike him twenty [lashes]; and whoever has relations with a woman within the prohibited degrees of kinship, kill him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said: O Messenger of Allah, we are people of hunting. He said:
"If you send your dog and mention the name of Allah over it, and it catches [the game] for you, then eat."
I said: Even if it kills? He said: "Even if it kills."
I said: We are people of archery. He said:
"Whatever your bow brings back to you, eat it."
I said: We are people who travel, passing by Jews, Christians and Magians, and we find nothing but their vessels. He said:
"If you do not find anything else, then wash them with water, and then eat and drink in them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The dog of the Magians.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about hunting with a falcon, and he said:
"Whatever it catches for you, eat it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
from his people hunted a hare, or two, and slaughtered them with a sharp stone. He hung them up until he met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him, and he commanded him to eat them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating the animal that has been made a target, which is the one that is held captive and shot with arrows.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A son of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās died, and he said to me, "O Kurayb, go and see whether any people have gathered for my son." I said, "Yes."
He said, "Woe to you! How many do you see? Forty?" I said, "No,
there are more." He said:
"Then bring my son out, for I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'There is no group of forty believers who intercede for a believer except that Allah accepts their intercession.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar did not permit as much latitude in anything as they permitted in the prayer over the dead.
Meaning, he did not set a fixed limit.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed over ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn and said the takbīr four times over him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I prayed with ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā al-Aslamī, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, over the funeral of a daughter of his. He said the takbīr four times over her, and after the fourth he remained for a while.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said the takbīr four times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbīr five times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The funeral prayer is to be offered for a child."
