label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Pray over your children, for they are your forerunners."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When al-Qāsim, the son of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, died, Khadījah said, "O Messenger of Allah, al-Qāsim's milk was flowing for him. If only Allah had kept him alive until he completed his nursing!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"His nursing will be completed in Paradise."
She said, "If I knew that, O Messenger of Allah, it would make the matter easier for me."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If you wish, I will call upon Allah, the Exalted, to let you hear his voice."
She said, "O Messenger of Allah, rather I believe Allah and His Messenger."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The martyrs were brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uḥud, and he prayed over them ten at a time, while Ḥamzah remained as he was; the others were carried away, while he stayed where he was placed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowered a man into his grave at night, and a lamp was lit in his grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not bury your dead at night unless you are compelled to."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Pray over your dead, by night and by day."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Pray over every dead person, and fight in jihad alongside every ruler."
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he was
older than Zayd. He said: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ, and when he reached al-Baqīʿ, there was a new grave. He asked about it, and they said, "So-and-so, a woman."
He said: He recognized her and said:
"Why did you not inform me of her?"
They said, "You were resting at midday and fasting, so we disliked to disturb you." He said:
"Do not do that. Let me not know of any one of you who dies while I am among you without your informing me of it, for my prayer over him is a mercy for him."
Then he came to the grave, and we formed rows behind him, and he said the takbīr over it four times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was a black woman who used to sweep the mosque. She died at night, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ awoke he was told of her death, and he said:
"Why did you not inform me of her?"
Then he went out with his Companions and stood at her grave, and he said the takbīr over her with the people behind him, and he supplicated for her, then departed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ went out with them and said:
"Pray over a brother of yours who has died in a land other than yours." They asked, "Who is he?" He said, "The Negus."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I missed him, meaning the Prophet ﷺ, and he was at al-Baqīʿ. He said:
"Peace be upon you, abode of believing people. You are our forerunners and we will join you. O Allah, do not deprive us of their reward, and do not put us to trial after them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew Saʿd into the grave smoothly, and sprinkled water over his grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the body from the side of the qiblah, received it from that direction, and drew it out smoothly into the grave.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muʿāwiyah delivered a sermon in Ḥimṣ and mentioned in his sermon that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wailing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Wailing is from the matters of the Jāhiliyyah, and if the wailing woman dies without repenting, Allah will cut for her garments of tar and a coat of flaming fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr on the hill of Madīnah. The Quraysh and the people kept passing by him, until ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar passed by him and stopped before him and said, "Peace be upon you, Abū Khubayb! Peace be upon you, Abū Khubayb! Peace be upon you, Abū Khubayb! By Allah, I used to forbid you from this. By Allah, I used to forbid you from this. By Allah, I used to forbid you from this. By Allah, as far as I knew, you were one who fasted much, stood much in prayer, and maintained the ties of kinship. By Allah, a community of which you are the worst would be a good community."

Then ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar went on. What ʿAbdullāh had stood and said reached al-Ḥajjāj, so he sent for the body and it was taken down from its trunk and thrown into the graves of the Jews. Then he sent for his mother, Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr, but she refused to come to him. The messenger repeated to her, "You will come to me, or I will send someone to drag you by your hair." She refused and said, "By Allah, I will not come to you until you send someone to drag me by my hair." He said, "Give me my sandals."

He took his sandals and set off, striding proudly, until he entered upon her and said, "How did you see how I dealt with the enemy of Allah?" She said, "I saw that you ruined his worldly life, and he ruined your Hereafter. It has reached me that you say to him, 'O son of the woman of the two waist-wraps.' By Allah, I am the woman of the two waist-wraps. As for one of them, I used to carry with it the food of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the food of Abū Bakr to keep it from the animals. As for the other, it is the waist-wrap of a woman, which she cannot do without. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told us:
'In Thaqīf there will be a great liar and a destroyer.'
As for the liar, we have seen him. As for the destroyer, I think you can only be him." He then got up and left her and did not reply to her.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If religion were at the Pleiades, a man from Persia — or he said, from the sons of Persia — would reach it until he obtained it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "I pledge allegiance to you for emigration and jihad, seeking reward from Allah." He said:
"Is either of your parents still alive?"
He said, "Yes, indeed, both of them." He said:
"Are you seeking reward from Allah?" He said, "Yes." He said:
"Then return to your parents and keep good company with them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man

from the Bedouin met him on the road to Makkah, and ʿAbdullāh greeted him with peace, mounted him on a donkey that he had been riding, and gave him a turban that had been on his head. Ibn Dīnār said: We said to him, "May Allah set you right! They are Bedouins, and they are satisfied with little."
ʿAbdullāh said, "The father of this man was a friend of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'The greatest act of righteousness is for a son to maintain ties with the loved ones of his father.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: When he went out to Makkah, he had a donkey on which he would rest when he grew tired of riding the camel, and a turban with which he would wrap his head. One day, while he was on that donkey, a Bedouin passed by him and said, "Are you not the son of so-and-so, son of so-and-so?" He said, "Yes, indeed."
So he gave him the donkey and said, "Ride this," and [gave him] the turban, and said, "Wrap your head with it."
Some of his companions said to him, "May Allah forgive you! You gave this Bedouin a donkey on which you used to rest, and a turban with which you used to wrap your head."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The womb is suspended from the Throne, saying: 'Whoever joins me, Allah will join him; and whoever cuts me off, Allah will cut him off.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah [reported] that a man

said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have relatives; I maintain ties with them, but they cut me off; I do good to them, but they do wrong to me; I am forbearing toward them, but they act ignorantly toward me." He said:
"If it is as you say, then it is as though you are feeding them hot ashes, and you will continue to have a supporter from Allah against them as long as you remain so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. And Ḥarmalah ibn Yaḥyā narrated it to me:
Ibn Wahb informed me; Yūnus informed me
from Ibn Shihāb, from Anas,
from the Prophet ﷺ, like the hadith of Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: with the chain of Mālik and like his hadith, except for his words:
"This one turns away and that one turns away."
For all of them said in their narrations, other than Mālik:
"This one avoids and that one avoids."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not cut off from one another, do not turn your backs on one another, do not spy on one another, and do not outbid one another in a sale; and be, O servants of Allah, brothers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "O Ubayy!"
He was praying. Ubayy turned but did not answer him, and he prayed briefly, then went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"And upon you be peace. What prevented you, O Ubayy, from answering me when I called you?"
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I was in prayer." He said,
"Did you not find among what Allah revealed to me: 'Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life'?"
He said, "Yes indeed, and I will not do it again, if Allah wills." He said,
"Would you like me to teach you a sūrah the like of which has not been revealed in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqān?"
He said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"How do you recite in prayer?"
He said: So he recited Umm al-Qurʾān [al-Fātiḥah], and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"By the One in whose hand is my soul, nothing like it has been revealed in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqān. It is the seven oft-repeated verses and the Great Qurʾān which I have been given."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Everything has a peak, and the peak of the Qurʾān is Sūrat al-Baqarah. In it is a verse that is the chief of the verses of the Qurʾān: it is Āyat al-Kursī."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever recites Ḥā Mīm al-Muʾmin up to:

'To Him is the final return,' and Āyat al-Kursī when he rises in the morning will be protected by them until the evening; and whoever recites them when he enters the evening will be protected by them until the morning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He had a storeroom in which there were dates, and a ghoul would come and take from it. He complained of that to the Prophet ﷺ, who said,
"Go, and when you see her, say: In the name of Allah, answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said: So he seized her, and she swore that she would not return, so he let her go. Then he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said,
"What did your captive do?"
He said, "She swore that she would not return." He said,
"She lied, and she is prone to lying again."
He said: So he seized her another time, and she swore that she would not return, so he let her go. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ, who said,
"What did your captive do?"
He said, "She swore that she would not return." He said,
"She lied, and she is prone to lying again."
So he seized her and said, "I will not let you go until I take you to the Prophet ﷺ."
She said, "I will tell you something: Āyat al-Kursī. Recite it in your house and neither Satan nor anyone else will come near you."
He said: Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ, who said,
"What did your captive do?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah wrote a book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and sent down two verses from it with which He concluded Sūrat al-Baqarah. They are not recited in a house for three nights without Satan coming near it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: In the explanation of the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, he said: Allah has not created any heaven or earth greater than Āyat al-Kursī.
Sufyān said: Because Āyat al-Kursī is the speech of Allah, and the speech of Allah is greater than what Allah created of the heavens and the earth.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While a man was reciting Sūrat al-Kahf, he saw his mount bolting. He looked and saw something like a cloud or a mist. He went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. The Prophet ﷺ said,
"That is the tranquility that descended with the Qurʾān," or, "that descended upon the Qurʾān."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said,
"Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qurʾān is Yā Sīn. Whoever recites Yā Sīn, Allah records for him by its recitation the reward of reciting the Qurʾān ten times."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ [said],
"Whoever recites Ḥā Mīm ad-Dukhān during a night will wake in the morning with seventy thousand angels asking forgiveness for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Whoever recites Ḥā Mīm ad-Dukhān on the night of Friday will be forgiven."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some people,
in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said, "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Yes." Then he said,

"Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun at midday when the sky is clear and there is no cloud with it? And do you have any difficulty seeing the moon on the night of the full moon when the sky is clear and there is no cloud?"
They said, "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said,

"You will have no more difficulty seeing Allah, Blessed and Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection than you have in seeing either of these. When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will announce that every nation should follow what it used to worship.

So no one who used to worship anything other than Allah, Glorified is He, of idols and stone altars, will remain, but they will fall into the Fire, until, when no one remains except those who used to worship Allah, whether righteous or sinful, and the remnants of the People of the Book, the Jews will be called and it will be said to them, 'What did you use to worship?' They will say, 'We used to worship ʿUzayr, the son of Allah.'
It will be said, 'You have lied. Allah has taken neither a consort nor a son. So what do you want?' They will say, 'We are thirsty, our Lord, so give us a drink.'

Then it will be signaled to them, 'Will you not go to the water?' So they will be gathered to the Fire, which will look like a mirage, its parts crushing one another, and they will fall into the Fire.
Then the Christians will be called and it will be said to them, 'What did you use to worship?' They will say, 'We used to worship the Messiah, the son of Allah.'
It will be said to them, 'You have lied.
Allah has taken neither a consort nor a son.'
It will be said to them, 'What do you want?' They will say, 'We are thirsty, our Lord, so give us a drink.'

He said: Then it will be signaled to them, 'Will you not go to the water?' So they will be gathered to Hell, which will look like a mirage, its parts crushing one another, and they will fall into the Fire. Until, when no one remains except those who used to worship Allah, the Exalted, whether righteous or sinful, the Lord of the worlds, Glorified and Exalted is He, will come to them in a form closest to that in which they had seen Him.
He will say, 'What are you waiting for? Every nation follows what it used to worship.'
They will say, 'Our Lord, we separated from the people in the world when we needed them most, and we did not keep company with them.'
He will say, 'I am your Lord.'
They will say, 'We seek refuge in Allah from you. We associate nothing with Allah,' twice or three times, so that some of them will almost turn back.
He will say, 'Is there a sign between you and Him by which you would recognize Him?' They will say, 'Yes.'

Then the Shin will be uncovered, and everyone who used to prostrate to Allah willingly will be permitted by Allah to prostrate, and no one who used to prostrate out of fear or for show will remain, but Allah will make his back one rigid plank, so that whenever he tries to prostrate he falls on his back.
Then they will raise their heads, and He will have changed into the form in which they saw Him the first time, and He will say, 'I am your Lord.'
They will say, 'You are our Lord.'
Then the bridge will be set over Hell, and intercession will be permitted, and they will say, 'O Allah, grant safety, grant safety.'"
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the bridge?" He said, "A slippery place where feet slide.

On it are hooks, grappling irons, and thorns, broad at one end, like those found in Najd, with a thorny plant called as-Saʿdān. The believers will pass over it like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like birds, and like the finest horses and riding camels. Some will be safe and unharmed, some will be scratched but released, and some will be piled up in the Fire of Hell.

Until, when the believers have been saved from the Fire, by the One in whose hand is my soul, none of you pleads with Allah more earnestly in demanding what is due than the believers will plead with Allah on the Day of Resurrection for their brothers who are in the Fire. They will say, 'Our Lord, they used to fast with us, pray, and perform Hajj.'
It will be said to them, 'Bring out those whom you recognize.'

Their forms will be forbidden to the Fire, so they will bring out many people, whom the Fire had seized up to the middle of their shins and up to their knees. Then they will say, 'Our Lord, none of those whom You commanded us to bring out remains in it.'
He will say, 'Go back, and whoever you find in whose heart is the weight of a dinar of good, bring him out.'
They will bring out many people, then they will say, 'Our Lord, we have not left in it anyone of those whom You commanded us to bring out.'
Then He will say, 'Go back, and whoever you find in whose heart is the weight of half a dinar of good, bring him out.'
They will bring out many people, then they will say, 'Our Lord, we have not left in it anyone of those whom You commanded us to bring out.'
Then He will say, 'Go back, and whoever you find in whose heart is the weight of an atom of good, bring him out.'
They will bring out many people, then they will say, 'Our Lord, we have left in it no one with any good.'"

Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī used to say, "If you do not believe me about this hadith, then recite, if you wish: {Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.}"

"Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say, 'The angels have interceded, the prophets have interceded, and the believers have interceded, and none remains but the Most Merciful of the merciful.' So He will take a handful from the Fire and bring out from it people who never did any good at all, who have returned as charcoal. He will cast them into a river at the entrances of Paradise called the River of Life, and they will come out like a seed sprouting in the silt carried by a flood. Do you not see it growing beside a rock or a tree? What is toward the sun is yellowish and greenish, and what is toward the shade is white."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, it is as if you used to tend flocks in the desert." He said,

"So they will come out like pearls, with seals on their necks, and the people of Paradise will recognize them: 'These are the freed ones of Allah, whom Allah has admitted to Paradise without any deed they did or any good they sent ahead.' Then He will say, 'Enter Paradise, and whatever you see is yours.'
They will say, 'Our Lord, You have given us what You have not given to anyone among the worlds.'
He will say, 'I have for you something better than this.' They will say, 'Our Lord, what is better than this?'
He will say, 'My pleasure, so I will never be angry with you after it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿUmar

used to lease out his farmland during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and during the leadership of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, and in the early part of the caliphate of Muʿāwiyah, until at the end of Muʿāwiyah's caliphate word reached him that Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj was narrating a prohibition on this from the Prophet ﷺ. So he went to see him, and I was with him, and he asked him. Rāfiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid the leasing of farmland.
After that Ibn ʿUmar gave it up.
And whenever he was asked about it afterwards, he would say: Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj claims that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a drink,
and he drank from it. On his right was a boy and on his left were elders. He said to the boy:
"Do you permit me to give it to these men?"
The boy said: No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I will not give anyone preference over me in my share from you.
He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed it in his hand.
label: machine translation

segments_en: By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will certainly drive men away from my Basin, just as a stray camel is driven away from the water trough."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no protected pasture except for Allah and His Messenger."
He said: It has reached us that the Prophet ﷺ protected an-Naqīʿ,
and that ʿUmar protected as-Sarif and ar-Rabadhah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever takes people's wealth intending to repay it, Allah will repay it for him;
and whoever takes it intending to destroy it, Allah will destroy him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dharr said: I was walking with the Prophet ﷺ in the lava field of Madinah in the evening, and we were looking at Uḥud. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
"O Abū Dharr."
I said: At your service, O Messenger of Allah. He said:

"I would not like to have this Uḥud as gold, with three nights passing while any of it remained with me, except a dīnār that I would set aside for a debt, unless I give it away among the servants of Allah like this, like this and like this," scooping with his hands in front of him, then to his right, then to his left.
He said: Then we walked on, and he said:
"O Abū Dharr."
I said: At your service, O Messenger of Allah. He said:
"Indeed, those who have the most will be the least on the Day of Resurrection, except for the one who says [does] like this, like this and like this."
He did as he had done the first time. He said: Then we walked on, and he said:
"O Abū Dharr, stay where you are until I come back to you."

He said: He went off until he disappeared from me. I heard a commotion and a voice. I said: Perhaps something has befallen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I intended to follow him, but then I remembered his words:
"Do not leave until I come back to you."
So I waited for him, and when he came I mentioned to him what I had heard. He said:
"That was Jibrīl. He came to me and said: Whoever of your nation dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise."
I said: Even if he commits adultery and steals? He said:
"Even if he commits adultery and steals."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The people were unsure about whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was fasting on the Day of ʿArafah,
so I sent him a vessel containing milk, and he drank.
Sufyān would sometimes say: The people were unsure about the fasting of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of ʿArafah, so Umm al-Faḍl sent to him.
But when he paused to settle the matter, he said: It is from Umm al-Faḍl.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ commanded him to take charge of his sacrificial camels, and commanded him to distribute all of them, their meat, their hides, and their coverings, among the poor, and not to give anything from them as payment to the butcher.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Mālik: Did Sumayy narrate to you from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Travel is a piece of torment: it keeps one of you from his sleep, his food, and his drink. So when one of you has finished his business on his journey, let him hurry back to his family." He said: Yes.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I was listening,
from Ibn Wahb,
who said: Yūnus informed me,
from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim,

who said: Ibn ʿUmar used to disapprove of making a stipulation in Hajj, and he would say: Is the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not enough for you? If one of you is prevented from Hajj, he circumambulates the House and goes between Ṣafā and Marwah, then comes out of the sacred state from everything until he performs Hajj the following year, and he offers a sacrificial animal, or fasts if he cannot find one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A woman
came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: My mother vowed to perform Hajj but died before performing it. Should I perform Hajj on her behalf? He said:
"Yes, perform Hajj on her behalf.
Do you not see that if your mother had a debt, you would pay it?" She said: Yes. He said:
"Then pay what is owed to Him,
for Allah is more deserving that what is owed to Him be fulfilled."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said to Anas ibn Mālik: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ declare Medina sacred? He said: Yes, from such-and-such to such-and-such. Whoever introduces an innovation in it. He said: Then he said to me: This is serious. [He said:]
"Whoever introduces an innovation in it, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people. Allah will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any obligatory or voluntary act."
He said: Ibn Anas said: Or gives shelter to an innovator.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He heard] a man saying: Tonight is the night of the fifteenth. He said to him: How do you know that tonight is the fifteenth? I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
"The month is like this and like this."
And he gestured with all ten fingers twice, "and like this,"
the third time, and he gestured with all his fingers but held back or folded his thumb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
both from Sufyān,
Abū Bakr said: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
from ʿUbaydullāh ibn Abī Yazīd,
that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās,
may Allah be pleased with them both, when he was asked about fasting on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.
He said: I do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fasted any day seeking its merit over other days except this day, nor any month except this month, meaning Ramadan.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Nāfiʿ,
from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that some men
among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ were shown Laylat al-Qadr in dreams in the last seven nights, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I see that your dreams have agreed on the last seven nights, so whoever is seeking it, let him seek it in the last seven nights."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying, and in his chest was a sound like the creaking of a millstone from weeping, ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O ʿAlī, do not correct the imam during prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With this report he said: and he took a coarse woolen garment that had belonged to Abū Jahm. It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, the embroidered cloak was better than the coarse woolen one."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The call was made for prayer, meaning the dawn prayer, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to pray while looking toward the mountain pass.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: While we were waiting for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the Ẓuhr or ʿAṣr prayer, and Bilāl had called him to prayer, he came out to us with Umāmah bint Abī al-ʿĀṣ, his daughter's daughter, on his neck. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood in his place of prayer and we stood behind him, while she remained where she was. He said: He said the takbīr and we said the takbīr. He said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to bow, he took her and put her down, then bowed and prostrated. When he finished his prostration and stood up, he took her and returned her to her place. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept doing this with her in every rakʿah until he finished his prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no ghirār in prayer, nor in the greeting of salām."
Aḥmad said: I think this means that you should not give the salām nor be given the salām, and that a man should not shortchange his prayer, leaving it while in doubt about it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I learned matters of Islam, and among what I learned was that he said to me:
"When you sneeze, praise Allah, and when someone sneezes and praises Allah, say: 'May Allah have mercy on you.'"

He said: While I was standing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in prayer, a man sneezed and praised Allah, so I said, "May Allah have mercy on you," raising my voice with it. The people fixed their eyes on me until it became too much for me, and I said, "What is the matter with you, that you stare at me with sidelong glances?" He said: They glorified Allah. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said: "Who was the one who spoke?"
It was said, "This bedouin." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called me and said to me:
"Prayer is only for the recitation of the Qurʾān and the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So when you are in it, let that be your concern."
I never saw a teacher more gentle than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said "Āmīn" aloud and gave the salām to his right and to his left, until I saw the whiteness of his cheek.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "O Messenger of Allah, do not get ahead of me in saying 'Āmīn.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to sit with Abū Zuhayr al-Numayrī, who was one of the Companions, and he would relate the best of talk. When one of us made a supplication, he would say, "Seal it with 'Āmīn,' for 'Āmīn' is like the seal on a document."
label: machine translation

She strikes the palm of her left hand with two fingers of her right.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came to al-Raqqah, and one of my companions said to me, "Would you like to meet a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ?" I said, "A real gain!" So we were directed to Wābiṣah. I said to my companion, "Let us first observe his appearance." He wore a low cap with two ear flaps and a dusty-colored silk burnous, and he was leaning on a staff in his prayer. After we had given the salām, we said:
label: machine translation

segments_en: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad
showed them the manner of sitting in the tashahhud, and then he mentioned the hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ sat in prayer, he would spread out his left foot until the top of his foot turned dark.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was sitting with a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with this hadith, but he did not mention Abū Qatādah. He said: When he sat after the two rakʿahs, he sat on his left foot, and when he sat in the last rakʿah, he brought his left foot forward and sat on his buttocks.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was in a gathering in which his father was present, and he mentioned in it: He prostrated, resting firmly on his palms, his knees, and the fronts of his feet. Then, while sitting, he sat in tawarruk and set up his other foot. Then he said the takbīr and prostrated, then said the takbīr and stood up without sitting in tawarruk. Then he returned and bowed in the other rakʿah, saying the takbīr likewise. Then he sat after the two rakʿahs, and when he wanted to rise to stand, he stood with a takbīr, then performed the last two rakʿahs. When he gave the salām, he gave it to his right and to his left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to open the prayer with the takbīr, and the recitation with {Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds}. When he bowed, he would neither raise his head high nor lower it, but keep it between the two. When he raised his head from bowing, he would not prostrate until he stood upright. When he raised his head from prostration, he would not prostrate again until he sat upright. He would recite the tahiyyah (the greeting) after every two rakʿahs. He would lay his left foot flat and set his right foot upright. He forbade the sitting of the devil, and he forbade a man from spreading his forearms on the ground like a predatory animal. And he would conclude the prayer with the salām.
In the narration of Ibn Numayr from Abū Khālid: and he used to forbid the heel of the devil.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis. When this verse was revealed: {So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you may be, turn your faces toward it}, a man from Banū Salimah passed by them while they were bowing in the Fajr prayer, still facing Bayt al-Maqdis. He called out: "Indeed, the direction of prayer has been changed to the Kaʿbah!" — twice. So they turned, just as they were in bowing, toward the Kaʿbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me while he was setting out toward Banū al-Muṣṭaliq. I came to him while he was praying on his camel, and I spoke to him. He gestured to me with his hand like this — and Zuhayr gestured with his hand — then I spoke to him again, and he gestured to me like this — and Zuhayr again gestured with his hand toward the ground — and I heard him reciting, nodding with his head. When he had finished, he said:
"What did you do about the matter for which I sent you? Nothing prevented me from speaking to you except that I was praying."

Zuhayr said: Abū az-Zubayr was sitting facing the Kaʿbah, and Abū az-Zubayr gestured with his hand toward Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, saying that he gestured with his hand toward a direction other than the Kaʿbah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to pray, and we heard him say:
"I seek refuge in Allah from you." Then he said:
"I curse you with the curse of Allah,"

three times, and he stretched out his hand as if taking hold of something. When he finished the prayer, we said: O Messenger of Allah, we heard you say something in the prayer that we had not heard you say before, and we saw you stretch out your hand. He said:

"The enemy of Allah, Iblīs, came with a flame of fire to put it in my face. So I said, 'I seek refuge in Allah from you,' three times. Then I said, 'I curse you with the curse of Allah,' and he did not withdraw, three times. Then I wanted to seize him. By Allah, were it not for the supplication of our brother Sulaymān, he would have been bound, and the children of the people of Madinah would be playing with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw phlegm on the qiblah wall of the mosque. He turned to the people and said:

"What is the matter with one of you that he stands facing his Lord and clears phlegm in front of him? Would any of you like to be faced and then have phlegm spat in his face? When one of you needs to clear phlegm, let him do so to his left, beneath his foot. If he cannot, let him do like this."
And al-Qāsim described it: he spat into his garment, then rubbed one part of it against another.
label: machine translation

segments_en: That he prayed with the Prophet ﷺ. He said: Then he cleared phlegm and rubbed it away with his left sandal.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
announced in the mosque, saying: "Who will call me to the red camel?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "May you not find it!
The mosques were only built for that for which they were built."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat in the prayer, he would place his left foot under his right thigh and shin, lay his right foot flat, place his left hand on his left knee, place his right hand on his right thigh, and point with his finger.
And ʿAbd al-Wāḥid showed us, pointing with the index finger.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while a Jewish woman was with me, and she was saying: "Do you know that you will be tested in the graves?" She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was alarmed and said:
"Only the Jews will be tested."
ʿĀʾishah said: We stayed for some nights, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you know that it has been revealed to me that you will be tested in the graves?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge from the punishment of Hell, the punishment of the grave, and the Antichrist (al-Masīḥ ad-Dajjāl).
label: machine translation

segments_en: We memorized it from the mouth of al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿUbaydullāh informed me that he heard Abū Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khālid say: We were with the Prophet ﷺ when a man stood up and said, "I adjure you by Allah to judge between us by the Book of Allah."
His opponent, who was more knowledgeable than he, stood up and said, "Judge between us by the Book of Allah, and give me permission [to speak]." He said, "Speak."
He said, "My son was a hired worker for this man, and he committed adultery with his wife.
So I ransomed him [my son] with one hundred sheep and a servant.
Then I asked some men of knowledge,
and they informed me that my son must receive one hundred lashes and a year of exile,
and that this man's wife must be stoned." The Prophet ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will judge between you both by the Book of Allah, mighty is His mention.
The one hundred sheep and the servant are to be returned,
and your son must receive one hundred lashes and a year of exile.
And go in the morning, O Unays, to the wife of this man,
and if she confesses, stone her."
So he went to her in the morning, and she confessed, and he stoned her.
I said to Sufyān: Did he not say, "and they informed me that my son must be stoned"?
He said: I am unsure about it from al-Zuhrī,
so sometimes I said it and sometimes I stayed silent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Yaḥyā said: And I think [it was] from Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj,

that they both said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sahl ibn Zayd and Muḥayyiṣah ibn Masʿūd ibn Zayd went out until, when they were at Khaybar, they separated in some part of it. Then Muḥayyiṣah found ʿAbdullāh ibn Sahl killed, having been murdered, so he buried him. Then he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, together with Ḥuwayyiṣah ibn Masʿūd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sahl, who was the youngest of the group. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān went to speak before his two companions, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Let the elder speak first."
So he fell silent and his two companions spoke, then he spoke with them. They told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the killing of ʿAbdullāh ibn Sahl, and he said to them:
"Will you swear fifty oaths so that you establish your claim against your companion's killer?"
They said, "How can we swear when we did not witness it?" He said:
"Then the Jews will clear themselves of you by fifty oaths."
They said, "How can we accept the oaths of a disbelieving people?" So when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw that, he paid the blood-money himself.
label: machine translation

segments_en: that al-Rubayyiʿ, who was the daughter of al-Naḍr, broke the front tooth of a girl,
so they [her family] sought compensation and sought pardon,
but they refused, so they came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ordered retaliation.
Anas ibn al-Naḍr said, "Will al-Rubayyiʿ's tooth be broken, O Messenger of Allah? No, by the One who sent you with the truth, her tooth will not be broken!" He said:
"O Anas, the Book of Allah [decrees] retaliation."
Then the people were content and pardoned. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Among the servants of Allah are those who, if they swore an oath by Allah, He would fulfil it for them."
Al-Fazārī added from Ḥumayd from Anas: The people were content and accepted the compensation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not right for a Muslim who has something to bequeath to let two nights pass without having his will written down with him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, they say that none will enter Paradise except a emigrant." He said:
"There is no emigration after the conquest of Makkah, but [there is] jihad and intention. So when you are called to go out, go out."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"No one is wounded in the cause of Allah, and Allah knows best who is wounded in His cause, except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound as it was on the day he was wounded: the colour is the colour of blood, and the scent is the scent of musk."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ used to say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from laziness, helplessness, and miserliness."
And with this chain of narration from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to seek refuge from extreme old age and the punishment of the grave.
He said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ twisting the forelock of a horse between his two fingers, and saying:
"Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection: the reward and the spoils of war."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The properties of Banū al-Naḍīr were among what Allah granted as spoils to His Messenger, for which the Muslims had not urged on horses or camels. They belonged exclusively to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would spend on his family from them. Ibn ʿAbdah said: he would spend on his family their provision for a year. Whatever remained he would put toward horses and equipment in the cause of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Ibn ʿAbdah said: toward horses and weapons.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [May Allah be pleased with him] said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the rich to keep sheep and commanded the poor to keep chickens, and he said:
"When the rich take to keeping chickens, Allah permits the destruction of the towns."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are sending me while I am young, to judge between them, and I do not know what judging is?" He struck my chest with his hand, then said:
"O Allah, guide his heart and make his tongue firm."
He said: After that I never doubted in judging between two people.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"There is no ruler who judges between people except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection with an angel holding him by the nape of his neck. Then the angel will raise his head to the sky, and if Allah says, 'Cast him down,' the angel will cast him into a pit for forty years' fall."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever helps in a dispute through wrongdoing, or helps in wrongdoing, will remain under Allah's wrath until he desists."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"If a man's goods are lost or stolen, and he finds them in the hand of a man who is selling them, he has a greater right to them, and the buyer may return to the seller for the price."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man from Banū Sawāʾah said: I said to ʿĀʾishah: "Tell me about the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

She said: "Do you not read the Qur'an: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}?" She said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with his Companions, and I made food for him, and Ḥafṣah also made food for him.

She said: Ḥafṣah was ahead of me, so I said to the servant girl: 'Go and overturn her dish.' I caught up with her just as she was about to place it before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I overturned it, so the dish broke and the food spilled.
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered it and the food that was in it onto a leather mat, and they ate. Then he sent my dish and gave it to Ḥafṣah, and said:
'Take a vessel in place of your vessel.'
She said: And I did not see any sign of that on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that:
"There is to be no harm and no reciprocating harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A group of people

brought a dispute before the Prophet ﷺ about a reed hut that was between them. He sent Ḥudhayfah to judge between them, and he ruled in favor of those on whose side the binding ropes were. When he returned to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, he said: "You were right and you did well."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If something is sold to two men, the sale belongs to the first."
Abū al-Walīd said: In this hadith is the invalidation of the khalāṣ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Quraysh
came to a woman soothsayer and said to her: "Tell us which of us most resembles in footprint the one of the Station [of Ibrāhīm]."
She said: "If you drag a cloak over this level ground and then walk over it, I will inform you."
He said: They dragged a cloak, then the people walked over it, and she looked at the footprints of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She said: "This one is the closest of you to him in resemblance."
Then they stayed for twenty years after that, or as long as Allah willed, and then Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: His parents
brought a dispute before the Prophet ﷺ, one of them a disbeliever and the other a Muslim. He let the boy choose, and he turned toward the disbeliever, so he said: "O Allah, guide him."
Then he turned toward the Muslim, so he ruled in his favor to have him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And ʿĀʾishah
[reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever seeks a right, let him seek it with propriety, whether he receives it in full or not."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed the best of you, or among the best of you, are those who are best in repaying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ demanding a debt or a right owed to him, and he spoke some harsh words, so the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were about to act against him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Leave him! The one owed a debt has the right to press his debtor until he repays it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I used to sell camels at al-Baqīʿ. I would sell for dinars and take dirhams, and sell for dirhams and take dinars, taking this in place of that and giving that in place of this. So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in the house of Ḥafṣah, and I said, "O Messenger of Allah, take your time, let me ask you: I sell camels at al-Baqīʿ. I sell for dinars and take dirhams, and sell for dirhams and take dinars, taking this in place of that and giving that in place of this."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There is no harm in taking them at the rate of that day, as long as you do not part while anything remains between you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of fruit until it ripens, the sale of grapes until they turn black, and the sale of grain until it hardens.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmmār, Saʿd, and I went into partnership
in what we might gain on the day of Badr. He said: Saʿd came with two captives, while ʿAmmār and I brought nothing.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever plants crops in the land of a people without their permission has no share of the crops, and his expenses are to be returned to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [The brother of Banū Ḥārithah reported] from his father,
that he asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to take payment for cupping, but he forbade him from it. He kept asking him and seeking his permission until he said:
"Feed it to your water-carrying camel and feed it to your slaves."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade meeting the incoming caravans [to trade]. If a buyer meets them and buys from them, then the owner of the goods has the option [to cancel] when he comes to the market.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Prices rose during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so they said, "O Messenger of Allah, prices have risen, so fix prices for us." He said:
"Indeed, Allah is the One Who fixes prices, Who withholds, Who extends, and Who provides. I truly hope to meet my Lord without anyone demanding of me any wrong done regarding blood or property."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The two parties to a sale have the option as long as they have not parted, except in a sale made with an option. And it is not permissible for one of them to part from his companion for fear that he may ask to cancel the deal."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever makes two sales in one sale will have the lesser of the two, or else it is usury (ribā)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ forbade the price of a cat.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Malik said: [He forbade] eating a cat and eating its price.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Until he mentioned ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is not lawful to combine a loan and a sale, nor two conditions in one sale, nor profit on what you have not taken responsibility for, nor to sell what you do not possess."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The neighbor has more right to the right of pre-emption (shufʿah) of his neighbor; it is to be awaited for him even if he is absent, if their road is one."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is appointed to judgeship, or is made a judge among the people, has been slaughtered without a knife."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes it in judgment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the dawn prayer, and when he finished he stood up and said:
"False testimony has been made equal to associating partners with Allah."
He said it three times, then recited: {So avoid the filth of idols and avoid false speech, [being] upright for Allah, not associating anything with Him.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ detained a man on suspicion, then released him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:
"Whoever harms [others], Allah will harm him; and whoever makes things hard [for others], Allah will make things hard for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever conceals knowledge by which Allah benefits people in their religious affairs, Allah will bridle him on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the prohibition of wine was revealed, ʿUmar said, "O Allah, make the ruling on wine clear to us with a satisfying clarification." Then the verse in Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed: {They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, 'In both is great sin'} the verse. He said: ʿUmar was summoned and it was recited to him. He said, "O Allah, make the ruling on wine clear to us with a satisfying clarification." Then the verse in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ was revealed: {O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated}. So when the prayer was called, the announcer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would call out: "Let no intoxicated person approach the prayer." ʿUmar was summoned and it was recited to him. He said, "O Allah, make the ruling on wine clear to us with a satisfying clarification." Then this verse was revealed: {So will you not desist?} ʿUmar said, "We have desisted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abū Ṭalḥah:
"Find me one of your boys to serve me."
So Abū Ṭalḥah took me out, having me ride behind him, and I would serve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whenever he stopped. I often heard him say:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from old age, grief, incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, the burden of debt, and being overpowered by men."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
"Allah has commanded me to recite to you." Then he recited to him:
"Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book..." [Sūrat al-Bayyinah], and he recited in it:
"Indeed, the true religion with Allah is the upright, submitting faith (ḥanīfiyyah), not Judaism and not Christianity. Whoever does good will not be denied its reward." And he recited to him:

"If the son of Adam had a valley of wealth, he would seek a second one; and if he had a second, he would seek a third. Nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust. And Allah turns in mercy to whoever repents."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ told us two narrations; I have seen one of them, and I am waiting for the other. He told us:
"Trustworthiness descended into the roots of men's hearts,"
– aṭ-Ṭanāfisī said, meaning the middle of men's hearts – "and then the Qurʾān was revealed, so we learned from the Qurʾān and we learned from the Sunnah."
Then he told us about its being taken away, and said:

"A man will sleep a sleep, and trustworthiness will be taken from his heart, and its trace will remain like the trace of a dark spot. Then he will sleep another sleep, and trustworthiness will be taken from his heart, and its trace will remain like the trace of a blister, like an ember you roll over your foot: it swells, and you see it raised, yet there is nothing inside it."
Then Ḥudhayfah took a handful of pebbles and rolled it over his shin. He said:
"Then people will be in the morning trading with one another, and hardly anyone will fulfill the trust, until it is said, 'In the tribe of so-and-so there is a trustworthy man.'
And until it is said to a man, 'How intelligent he is, how strong, how refined!'
Yet in his heart there is not a mustard seed's weight of faith."

And there was a time when I did not care with which of you I made a transaction: if he was a Muslim, his Islam would make him return it to me, and if he was a Jew or a Christian, his official would make him return it to me. But today, I would not trade except with so-and-so and so-and-so.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most untrue of speech. Do not pry, do not spy, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another,
and be, O servants of Allah, brothers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him: The Prophet ﷺ sent a man from Banū Makhzūm to collect charity, and he said to Abū Rāfiʿ, "Accompany me so that you may get some of it." He said, "No,
not until I go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him."
So he went to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and he said:
"Charity is not lawful for us, and the freed slaves of a people are from among them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He claimed that a man

from the Anṣār, called Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathmah, informed him that a group of his people went to Khaybar and dispersed there, and then found one of them killed. They said to those near whom they found him, "You killed our companion." They said, "We did not kill him, and we do not know who killed him."
So they went to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Prophet of Allah, we went to Khaybar and found one of us killed."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "The eldest, the eldest!" Then he said to them:
"Bring proof against the one who killed him."
They said, "We have no proof." He said, "Then they will swear an oath to you."
They said, "We are not satisfied with the oaths of the Jews."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that his blood should go unavenged, so he paid the blood money for him: one hundred camels from the charity camels.
ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb differed from them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to Khabbāb to visit him, and he had been cauterized seven times. He said, "My illness has been prolonged, and had I not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Do not wish for death,' I would have wished for it." And he said:
"A man is rewarded for all that he spends, except for dust," or he said, "except for building."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two men
each claimed a camel or an animal before the Prophet ﷺ, and neither of them had proof, so the Prophet ﷺ made it between the two of them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, I am going to ask you about a matter which you know and of which I am ignorant." He said, "What is it?"
He said, "Is there any time of the night or day in which prayer is disliked?" He said, "Yes.
When you have prayed the Fajr prayer,
leave off prayer until the sun rises,
for it rises between the two horns of Satan.
Then pray, for prayer is witnessed and accepted until the sun is straight above your head like a spear.
When it is above your head like a spear, leave off prayer,
for at that time Hell is fueled and its gates are opened,
until the sun declines from your right eyebrow.
When it has passed its zenith, prayer is witnessed and accepted until you pray the ʿAṣr prayer.
Then leave off prayer until the sun sets."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There will be rulers who are distracted by other things and delay the prayer from its proper time. So make your prayer with them a voluntary prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ led his Companions in the fear prayer (ṣalāt al-khawf). He bowed with all of them, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the row right behind him prostrated while the others stood. When he rose, those [who had prostrated] stood, and the others prostrated by themselves two prostrations. Then the front row moved back until they stood in the place of the others, and the others moved forward until they stood in the place of the front row. The Prophet ﷺ then bowed with all of them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the row right behind him prostrated. When they raised their heads, the others prostrated two prostrations. So all of them bowed with the Prophet ﷺ, and one group prostrated by themselves two prostrations. The enemy was in the direction of the qiblah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have come to you from a people whose shepherd has no provisions and whose stallion does not even swish its tail."
So he ascended the pulpit, praised Allah, and then said,
"O Allah, give us rain, helpful, wholesome, abundant, pasture-giving, plentiful, quick and not delayed."
Then he came down, and no one came to him from any direction except that they said, "We have been revived."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for rain [raising his hands] until I saw—or it was seen—the whiteness of his armpits.
Muʿtamir said: I think it was during the prayer for rain.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He performed Hajj and said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ delivering a sermon on his camel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would say the takbīr between the parts of the sermon; he would say the takbīr often in the sermons of the two Eids.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the day of Fiṭr or Aḍḥā and delivered a sermon standing, then sat for a short while, then stood up again.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not pray anything before the Eid prayer, and when he returned to his house he would pray two rakʿahs.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would go out to the Eid prayer on foot and return on foot.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ went out to the two Eid prayers, he would pass by the houses of Saʿīd ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ, then by the people of the tents, then return by the other road, the road of Banū Zurayq, then go out by the house of ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and the house of Abū Hurayrah to al-Balāṭ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He would go out to the Eid prayer by one road and return by another, and he claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would come to the Eid prayer on foot and return on foot, by a road other than the one by which he had set out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿIyāḍ al-Ashʿarī attended an Eid in al-Anbār and said: Why do I not see you performing the qalas as it was performed in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
label: machine translation

segments_en: There was nothing in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except that I saw it, except one thing: the qalas was performed for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Fiṭr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the Eid prayer at the prayer ground, using a short spear as a screen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to bring out his daughters and his wives for the two Eids.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Two Eids coincided in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He led the people in prayer and then said,
"Whoever wishes to come to the Friday prayer may come, and whoever wishes to stay behind may stay behind."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"One who severs the ties of kinship will not enter Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever visits a sick person remains in the khurfah of Paradise."
It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the khurfah of Paradise?" He said, "Its harvested fruit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He] said, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Nothing afflicts a believer, whether fatigue, grief, illness, or even worry that concerns him, except that Allah expiates some of his sins by it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the verse {Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it} was revealed, it weighed very heavily upon the Muslims, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Aim for what is right and stay close to it, for in everything that afflicts a Muslim there is expiation, even a calamity that strikes him or a thorn that pricks him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do you know who the bankrupt person is?"
They said, "The bankrupt person among us, O Messenger of Allah, is the one who has no dirham and no property."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The bankrupt one of my nation is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with his prayer, fasting, and zakāh, but he comes having insulted this person, slandered that one, consumed the wealth of another, shed the blood of another, and struck yet another. So he is made to sit, and this one is given from his good deeds and that one from his good deeds. If his good deeds run out before what he owes is settled, some of their sins are taken and cast upon him, and then he is thrown into the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Rights will certainly be returned to their owners on the Day of Resurrection, until even the hornless sheep will be given retribution against the horned sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Charity does not decrease wealth; Allah increases a servant in nothing for his pardoning except honor; and no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah does not conceal the faults of a servant in this world except that Allah will conceal them on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Those who curse a great deal will not be witnesses or intercessors on the Day of Resurrection."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Hishām ibn Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām passed by some of the Nabatean people in Syria who had been made to stand in the sun. He said, "What is the matter with them?" They said, "They have been detained over the jizyah."
Hishām said, "I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Allah will punish those who punish people in this world.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, guide me to a deed by which I may benefit." He said:
"Remove harmful things from the path of the Muslims."
label: machine translation

segments_en: My close friend ﷺ advised me:
"When you cook a broth, add plenty of water to it, then look to a household among your neighbors and give them a share of it with kindness."
label: machine translation

segments_en: al-Nakhaʿī, Abū Ghiyāth, from Abū Zurʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarīr,
from Abū Hurayrah,
who said: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ with a son of hers and said, "O Messenger of Allah, he is ill, and I fear for him. I have already buried three." He said:
"You have fortified yourself with a strong barrier against the Fire."
Zuhayr said, from Ṭalq.
And he did not mention the kunyah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, "What do you say about a man who does a good deed and people praise him for it?" He said:
"That is the immediate glad tidings for the believer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Surāqah ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, explain our religion to us as though we were created just now. What is the deed today: is it for what the pens have dried upon and the decrees have run, or for what lies ahead?" He said, "No.
Rather, it is for what the pens have dried upon and the decrees have run."
He said, "Then what is the point of deeds?" Zuhayr said: Then Abū al-Zubayr said something I did not understand, so I asked what he said, and he said:
"Act, for everyone is eased [toward what he was created for]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Allah wrote the decrees of the creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." He said, "And His Throne was upon the water."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not give up. If something afflicts you, do not say, 'If only I had done such and such, it would have been so and so.'
Rather, say, 'Allah decreed, and what He willed, He did,' for 'if only' opens the door to the work of Satan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We responded to the call (talbiyah) for Hajj until, when we were at Sarif, I began to menstruate. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while I was weeping, and he said:
"What makes you weep, ʿĀʾishah?"
I said, "I have started to menstruate. I wish I had not come for Hajj." He said:
"Glory be to Allah! This is something Allah has decreed for the daughters of Adam." He said:
"Perform all the rites, except that you must not circumambulate the House."
When we entered Makkah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever wishes to make it an ʿUmrah, let him make it an ʿUmrah, except for the one who has brought the sacrificial animal with him."

She said: On the Day of Sacrifice, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ slaughtered cows on behalf of his wives. Then on the night of al-Baṭḥāʾ, when ʿĀʾishah had become pure, she said, "O Messenger of Allah, will my companions return with both Hajj and ʿUmrah while I return with Hajj only?" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, and he took her to at-Tanʿīm, and she responded to the call (talbiyah) for ʿUmrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell from his horse,
and his leg or his shoulder was scraped,
and he swore an oath to stay away from his wives for a month,
so he sat in an upper room of his,
whose steps were made of palm trunks.
His Companions came to visit him,
and he led them in prayer sitting,
while they were standing. When he finished the prayer, he said:
"The imam is appointed only to be followed,
so when he says the takbīr, say the takbīr;
when he bows, bow;
when he prostrates, prostrate;
and if he prays standing, pray standing."
He came down on the twenty-ninth day, and they said, "O Messenger of Allah, you swore a oath for a month." He said:
"The month is twenty-nine days."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal, from ʿUrwah,
from Zaynab bint Abī Salamah,
from Umm Salamah,
who said: I complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that I was ill, and he said:
"Circumambulate behind the people while riding."
So I circumambulated while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying beside the House, reciting {By the Mount, and by a Book inscribed}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
Zuhayr said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father,
that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say; (another chain:) and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us,
— and the wording is his — Sufyān narrated to us, ʿAmr narrated to us, from Ṭāwūs,
from Ibn ʿUmar;
and (another chain:) al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from Sālim, from his father, that a man
asked the Prophet ﷺ about the night prayer, and he said:
"Two by two; and if you fear the dawn, pray one rakʿah as witr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Let not the call to prayer of Bilāl prevent any one of you from his pre-dawn meal,
for he calls the adhān (or calls out) during the night,
so that the one among you who is praying may return and the one who is sleeping may be awakened,
and it is not that dawn or morning has come."
And he gestured with his fingers, raising them upward and then lowering them downward, until he said like this.
Zuhayr said, with his two index fingers, one above the other, and then he extended them to his right and left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Prayer in congregation equals twenty-five prayers. If one prays it in an open desert and completes its bowing and prostration, it reaches fifty prayers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"When the evening meal of one of you has been served and the prayer is called, let him not get up until he has finished."
Musaddad added: When ʿAbdullāh's evening meal was served or was present, he would not get up until he had finished, even if he heard the iqāmah and even if he heard the imam's recitation.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to straighten our rows until it was as though he were straightening arrows with them, until he saw that we had understood from him. Then one day he came out and stood, and was about to say the takbīr, when he saw a man whose chest was protruding from the row, and he said:
"Servants of Allah, you will straighten your rows, or Allah will set your faces against one another."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We would take the midday rest and eat the midday meal only after the Friday prayer — Ibn Ḥujr added — in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to stand in prayer at night until his feet swelled. ʿĀʾishah said, "Why do you do this, O Messenger of Allah, when Allah has forgiven you your earlier and later sins?" He said:
"Should I not love to be a grateful servant?"
When he grew heavier in body, he would pray sitting, and when he wished to bow, he would stand,
recite, and then bow.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He saw ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr lead them in prayer, gesturing with his palms when he stood, when he bowed, when he prostrated, and when he rose to stand, gesturing with his hands. So I went to Ibn ʿAbbās and said, "I saw Ibn al-Zubayr pray a prayer the like of which I have not seen anyone pray," and I described this gesturing to him. He said, "If you would like to look at the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then follow the prayer of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar
used to raise his hands level with his shoulders when he began the prayer, and when he raised his head from bowing he raised them to a lesser height than that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said, "If you were in front of the Prophet ﷺ, you would see his armpits."
Ibn Muʿādh added: Lāḥiq said, "Do you not see that he is in prayer and cannot be in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" And Mūsā added: meaning, when he said the takbīr he raised his hands.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began the prayer, he raised his hands to close to his ears, and then he did not repeat it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Lining up the feet and placing the hand on the hand is from the sunnah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He was praying and placed his left hand on his right. The Prophet ﷺ saw him and placed his right hand on his left.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Hurayrah said, "Placing the palms on the palms in prayer is below the navel."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, holding his left hand with his right on the wrist, above the navel.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to place his right hand on his left hand, then clasp them firmly together on his chest while he was in prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, Ibn Abī Farwah, and others among the jurists of Madinah said to me, "When you say that, then say:"
"And I am among the Muslims," meaning His saying:
"And I am the first of the Muslims."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There is no harm in making supplication in prayer, at its beginning, its middle, and its end, in the obligatory prayer and others.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the night prayer, used to say after saying "Allahu akbar":
Then he mentioned its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A young man of the Anṣār sneezed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in prayer, and he said, "Praise be to Allah, abundant, good, blessed praise, until our Lord is pleased, and after He is pleased, in the affairs of this world and the next." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said:
"Who said those words?"
The young man stayed silent. Then he said:
"Who said those words? For he did not say anything wrong."
The young man said, "O Messenger of Allah, I said them; I intended nothing by them but good." He said:
"They did not stop short of the Throne of the Most Merciful, blessed and exalted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to keep silent twice, when he began the prayer and when he finished the recitation entirely.
Then he mentioned the meaning of the hadith of Yūnus.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And she mentioned the slander,
and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat down, uncovered his face, and said:
"I seek refuge in the All-Hearing, All-Knowing from the accursed Satan: {Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you}." The verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ did not know the end of a sūrah until {In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful} was revealed to him.
This is the wording of Ibn al-Sarḥ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He came to Muʿādh ibn Jabal while he was leading a people in the Maghrib prayer. In this report he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"O Muʿādh, do not be a cause of trial, for behind you pray the old, the weak, the one with a need, and the traveler."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man may finish his prayer and have recorded for him only a tenth of it, a ninth, an eighth, a seventh, a sixth, a fifth, a quarter, a third, or a half."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We thought he meant by that that the people would catch the first rakʿah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ used to stand in the first rakʿah of the Ẓuhr prayer so long that no sound of footsteps could be heard.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the sun had passed its zenith, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would pray Ẓuhr and recite about as much as {By the night when it covers}; likewise in ʿAṣr, and likewise in the other prayers, except Ṣubḥ, which he would lengthen.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ prostrated in the Ẓuhr prayer, then stood up and bowed, and we thought that he had recited Tanzīl al-Sajdah.
Ibn ʿĪsā said: No one mentioned Umayyah except Muʿtamir.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr prayers or not.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ cursed women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed, and women who pluck their eyebrows, [those] who seek beauty [and] change the creation of Allah.
He said: This hadith is hasan ṣaḥīḥ.
It was also narrated by Shuʿbah and more than one of the Imams from Manṣūr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Some women,
from the people of Ḥimṣ or from the people of Syria, entered upon ʿĀʾishah, and she said: "You are the ones whose women enter the public baths. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Any woman who takes off her clothes in a place other than her husband's house has torn the veil between herself and her Lord.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gold ring, the red saddle-cloth (mīthara), qassī garments, and jaʿah, a drink made from barley and wheat, and he mentioned how strong it is.
ʿAmmār ibn Ruzayq differed from him; he narrated it from Abū Isḥāq, from Ṣaʿṣaʿah, from ʿAlī.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us wearing two green garments.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me with a trace of khalūq [perfume] on me, and he said:
"O Yaʿlā, do you have a wife?" I said: No. He said:
"Wash it off, then do not do it again; then wash it off, then do not do it again; then wash it off, then do not do it again."
He said: So I washed it off and did not do it again; then I washed it and did not do it again; then I washed it and did not do it again.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah for the ʿUmrah of al-Qaḍāʾ, with ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah walking in front of him, saying: "Clear the way, O sons of the disbelievers! Today we will strike you over its revelation, a blow that removes heads from their resting places and makes friend forget friend." ʿUmar said to him: "O Ibn Rawāḥah, in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and in the sanctuary of Allah, you recite poetry?" The Prophet ﷺ said to him:
