So we began looking through the trees in the pass, and there he was, arriving until he stood before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He greeted him with salām and said:
"I went until I was at the top of this pass, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me. When morning came, I looked out over both passes and looked, but I saw no one."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "
Did you dismount at all during the night?" He said:
"No, except to pray or to relieve myself."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "
You have made [Paradise] binding upon yourself, so it will not matter if you do no further deeds after this."
label: machine translation

segments_en: {If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment} and {It was not for the people of Madīnah} up to His words {they used to do} were abrogated by the verse that follows it: {And it is not for the believers to go forth all together}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about this verse,
{If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment}. He said:
The rain was withheld from them, and that was their punishment.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The worst thing in a man is panicky greed and crippling cowardice."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man said:
"O Messenger of Allah,
a man wants to fight in the cause of Allah while seeking some of the goods of this world." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
He has no reward."
The people found this a grave matter and said to the man:
"Go back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, perhaps you did not make him understand." So he said:
"O Messenger of Allah,
a man wants to fight in the cause of Allah while seeking some of the goods of this world." He said: "
He has no reward." They said to the man:
"Go back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
He said it to him a third time, and he said to him: "
He has no reward."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A hadith that pleased me. Then he mentioned its meaning.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĪsā will be taught his argument, and Allah will teach it to him, as in His saying:

"And [beware the Day] when Allah will say, 'O ʿĪsā, son of Maryam, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'" Abū Hurayrah said, from the Prophet ﷺ: So Allah will teach him [to say]:
"Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to [say]" — the whole verse.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The last surah to be revealed was Sūrat al-Māʾidah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: [They said] to the Prophet ﷺ: "We do not call you a liar, but we deny what you have brought." So Allah revealed:
"Indeed, they do not call you a liar, but the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever would be pleased to look at the document bearing the seal of Muhammad ﷺ, let him read these verses:
"Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden to you..." the verse, up to His saying: "...so that you may become mindful of Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
"Or that some of the signs of your Lord come" he said: "The rising of the sun from its place of setting."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ recited this verse:

"So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust." Ḥammād said: Like this, and Sulaymān held the tip of his thumb on the top joint of his right finger. He said: The mountain sank down, "and Mūsā fell unconscious."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"When Allah created Ādam, He wiped his back, and from his back fell every soul that He would create from his offspring until the Day of Resurrection. He placed a gleam of light between the eyes of each person among them. Then He presented them to Ādam and he said: 'My Lord, who are these?' He said: 'These are your offspring.' He saw one man among them and the gleam between his eyes impressed him, so he said: 'My Lord, who is this?' He said: 'This is a man from the last of the nations among your offspring, called Dāwūd.'
He said: 'My Lord, how long have You made his life?' He said: 'Sixty years.' He said: 'My Lord, add forty years to him from my life.'

When Ādam's lifespan came to an end, the Angel of Death came to him and he said: 'Do I not have forty years remaining of my life?' He said: 'Did you not give them to your son Dāwūd?' He said: Ādam denied it, so his offspring deny; Ādam forgot, so his offspring forget; and Ādam erred, so his offspring err."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When Ḥawwāʾ became pregnant, Iblīs went around with her, and none of her children would live. He said: 'Name him ʿAbd al-Ḥārith.'
So she named him ʿAbd al-Ḥārith, and he lived. That was from the suggestion of Satan and his command."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"When Ādam was created..." — the hadith [continues].
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished with Badr, it was said to him: "[Go after] the caravan; there is nothing to stop you." Then al-ʿAbbās, who was in his bonds, called out to him: "That is not proper, because Allah promised you one of the two parties, and He has given you what He promised you." He said: "You have spoken truly."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah revealed to me two securities for my nation:

'But Allah would not punish them while you are among them' and 'nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.' When I am gone, I will have left seeking forgiveness among them until the Day of Resurrection."
This is a gharīb hadith.
And Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir is considered weak in hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Spoils of war were not made lawful for any of the black-headed people before you. A fire would come down from the sky and consume them."
Sulaymān al-Aʿmash said: Who would say this now except Abū Hurayrah? Then on the day of Badr, they fell upon the spoils before they had been made lawful for them, so Allah the Exalted revealed:

"Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took." Abū ʿĪsā said: This hadith is ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb from the narration of al-Aʿmash.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The day of the Greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

He said: This hadith is more authentic than the hadith of Muhammad ibn Isḥāq, because this hadith has been narrated through more than one route from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī as his own statement [mawqūf], and we do not know anyone who attributed it to the Prophet ﷺ except what was narrated from Muhammad ibn Isḥāq. Shuʿbah also narrated this hadith from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī as his own statement [mawqūf].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent [the surah] Barāʾah with Abū Bakr, then called him back and said:
"It is not proper for anyone to convey this except a man from my family."
So he called ʿAlī and gave it to him.
He said: This hadith is ḥasan gharīb from the narration of Anas ibn Mālik.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Allah will admit the people of Paradise into Paradise, admitting whom He wills by His mercy, and He will admit the people of the Fire into the Fire. Then He will say: 'Look for whoever you find has in his heart faith equal to the weight of a mustard seed, and bring him out.'
So they will come out of it as burnt coals.
They will be thrown into the river of life, or the river of rain, and they will sprout in it as a seed sprouts beside the bank of a torrent. Have you not seen how it comes out yellow and twisted?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a group of men [some wealth] while I was sitting among them. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left out one man from among them and did not give him anything,
and he was the one I liked best of them.
So I got up and went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke to him privately, and I said: "Why do you overlook so-and-so? By Allah, I consider him a believer." He said: "Or a Muslim."
He said: I stayed silent for a little while, then what I knew about him overcame me, so I said: "O Messenger of Allah,
why do you overlook so-and-so? By Allah, I consider him a believer." He said: "Or a Muslim."
He said: I stayed silent for a little while, then what I knew about him overcame me, so I said: "O Messenger of Allah, why do you overlook so-and-so? By Allah, I consider him a believer." He said:
"Or a Muslim?" Then he said: "I give to a man while another is dearer to me than he is,
for fear that he would be thrown on his face into the Fire."

And from his father, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad, who said: I heard my father narrate this, and he said in his narration: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck with his hand and gathered the muscle between my neck and my shoulder, then said:
"Come closer, O Saʿd! I give to a man..."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This religion is ease, and no one makes the religion a hardship except that it overcomes him. So be steadfast, stay close [to what is right], receive good news, make things easy, and seek help through the morning journey, the afternoon journey, and a part of the night journey."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell behind us on a journey we were making, then he caught up with us when prayer, the ʿAṣr prayer, was nearly out of time, and we were performing ablution.
So we began wiping over our feet,
and he called out at the top of his voice:
"Woe to the heels from the Fire!"
Twice or three times.
label: machine translation

segments_en: And a man,
who was better in my estimation than ʿAbd al-Raḥmān — Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Prophet ﷺ addressed us on the Day of Sacrifice. He said:
"Do you know what day this is?"
We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."
He was silent until we thought he would give it a name other than its name. He said:
"Is it not the Day of Sacrifice?" We said: "Yes." He said:
"What month is this?"
We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."
He was silent until we thought he would give it a name other than its name. Then he said:
"Is it not Dhū al-Ḥijjah?" We said: "Yes." He said:
"What city is this?"
We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."
He was silent until we thought he would give it a name other than its name. He said:
"Is it not the Sacred City?" We said: "Yes." He said:
"Indeed, your blood and your wealth are sacred to you,
like the sacredness of this day of yours,
in this month of yours,
in this city of yours,
until the day you meet your Lord.
Have I not conveyed [the message]?" They said: "Yes." He said: "O Allah, bear witness.
Let the one who is present convey it to the one who is absent,
for perhaps one to whom it is conveyed will retain it better than one who hears it.
So do not return to disbelief after me, striking one another's necks."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn Abī Najīḥ said to me, from Mujāhid,
who said: I accompanied Ibn ʿUmar to Madinah and did not hear him narrate anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except one hadith.
He said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ when some palm pith was brought, and he said:
"Among the trees there is a tree whose likeness is that of the Muslim."
I wanted to say it was the palm tree,
but since I was the youngest of the people, I remained silent. The Prophet ﷺ said: "It is the palm tree."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I saw a man whose opinion people were following;
he did not say anything except that they acted on it. I asked, "Who is this?" They said, "This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
I said, "Upon you be peace, O Messenger of Allah," twice. He said,
"Do not say, 'Upon you be peace,'
for 'Upon you be peace' is the greeting for the dead. Say, 'Peace be upon you.'"
He said: I said, "Are you the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said,

"I am the Messenger of Allah, the One who, when harm touches you and you call upon Him, removes it from you; and if a year of drought afflicts you and you call upon Him, He makes the crops grow for you; and when you are in a barren land or a desert and your mount is lost, and you call upon Him, He returns it to you."
I said, "Give me advice." He said,
"Do not insult anyone."
He said: After that I never insulted a free man, a slave, a camel, or a sheep. He said,

"And do not belittle anything of good, even if you speak to your brother with a cheerful face; that is part of what is good. Raise your lower garment to the middle of the shin; if you refuse, then to the ankles. And beware of letting the lower garment trail, for that is from arrogance, and Allah does not love arrogance. And if a man insults you and shames you with something he knows about you, do not shame him with something you know about him, for the evil consequence of that falls upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Allah, glorified is He, says: 'Pride is My cloak and greatness is My lower garment. Whoever contends with Me over either of them, I will throw him into Hell.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: She said that

she was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, along with Maymūnah. She said: While we were with him, Ibn Umm Maktūm came and entered upon him, and this was after we had been commanded to observe the veil. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Veil yourselves from him."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah, is he not blind? He cannot see us and does not recognize us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Are you two blind? Do you not see him?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted the Mothers of the Believers to let their garments trail a handspan. Then they asked him for more, so he added another handspan for them. So they would send [their garments] to us, and we would measure out a cubit for them.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I had sheep at Uḥud, and death befell them. So I went to Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and mentioned that to her. Maymūnah said to me, "If only you had taken their hides and benefited from them."
He said, "Is that permissible?" She said, "Yes.
Some men of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dragging a sheep of theirs, [bloated] like a donkey. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them,
'If only you had taken its hide.'
They said, 'It is carrion.'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
'Water and qaraẓ [acacia pods] purify it.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"When you dress and when you perform ablution, begin with your right sides."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ in his house and saw him reclining on a cushion. Ibn al-Jarrāḥ added: on his left side.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Her bed was directly opposite the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,

"Jibrīl came to me and said: 'I came to you last night, and nothing prevented me from entering the house you were in except that at the door of the house there was a statue of men, and in the house there was a curtain with images on it, and in the house there was a dog. So order that the head of the statue at the door be cut off so that it becomes like the shape of a tree; order that the curtain be cut and made into two cushions, set aside, to be trodden upon; and order that the dog be taken out.'"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did so. That dog was a puppy belonging to al-Ḥasan or al-Ḥusayn, under a couch of his, so he ordered that it be taken out.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade combing the hair [regularly] except every other day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: From his mother's side, Abū Dhubāb, from his grandfather,
he said: The ring of the Prophet ﷺ was of iron with silver wound around it.
He said: Sometimes it was on his hand. He said: Al-Muʿayqīb was in charge of the ring of the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"How will you be, and a time...?" or

"A time is about to come when people will be sifted thoroughly, leaving behind the dregs of people, whose covenants and trusts have become corrupted and who have fallen into disagreement, and they will be like this,"
and he interlaced his fingers. They said, "What should we do, O Messenger of Allah?" He said,
"Take what you recognize, leave what you reject, attend to the affair of your own special circle, and leave the affair of the general public."
label: machine translation

segments_en: There are lingering [words] whose sayer—or doer—will not be disappointed after every obligatory prayer: thirty-three glorifications (tasbīḥ), thirty-three praises (taḥmīd), and thirty-four declarations of Allah's greatness (takbīr)."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

"Whoever glorifies Allah after every prayer thirty-three times, praises Allah thirty-three times, and declares Allah's greatness thirty-three times—that makes ninety-nine—and then says, to complete the hundred, 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things,' his sins will be forgiven, even if they are like the foam of the sea."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
and Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb,
they said: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us,
(transfer of chain) He said: and Abū Kurayb narrated to us,
Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, from Maʿmar and al-Awzāʿī,
and Mālik ibn Anas, and Yūnus,
(transfer of chain) He said: and Ibn Numayr narrated to us,
my father narrated to us, (transfer of chain)
He said: and Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us,
ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us,
all of them from ʿUbaydullāh,
all of these from al-Zuhrī,
from Abū Salamah,
from Abū Hurayrah,
from the Prophet ﷺ, like the hadith of Yaḥyā from Mālik, though in none of their narrations is "with the imam."
And in the narration of ʿUbaydullāh he said:
"He has caught the entire prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Knowledge cannot be attained with bodily comfort.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the ʿAṣr prayer. When he finished, a man from Banū Salimah came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we wish to slaughter a camel of ours, and we would like you to be present." He said, "Yes."
So he set out and we set out with him, and we found the camel had not yet been slaughtered. It was slaughtered, then cut up, then some of it was cooked, and we ate it before the sun set.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAmr said: He traces it back [to the Prophet ﷺ].
label: machine translation

segments_en: And he would say: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said:

"You will indeed see your Lord just as you see this moon, with no difficulty in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in [performing] a prayer before sunrise and before sunset, then do so."
He meant ʿAṣr and Fajr. Then Jarīr recited: {And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.}
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the prayers much like your prayer, but he would delay the ʿIshāʾ a little later than your prayer, and he would make the prayer light.
And in the narration of Abū Kāmil: he would shorten [it].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not mind delaying the ʿIshāʾ prayer somewhat, until the middle of the night, and he did not like sleeping before it nor talking after it.
Shuʿbah said: Then I met him another time and he said: or a third of the night.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "A little over twenty"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned several hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I have considered ordering my young men to gather bundles of firewood for me, then ordering a man to lead the people in prayer, and then burning down the houses upon those inside them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said about people who stayed away from the Friday prayer:
"I have considered ordering a man to lead the people in prayer, and then burning the houses down upon the men who stay away from the Friday prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh said: I have seen us [in the past], and no one stayed away from the prayer except a hypocrite whose hypocrisy was known, or a sick person. Even a sick man would walk between two men until he reached the prayer. And he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught us the ways of guidance, and among the ways of guidance is praying in the mosque in which the call to prayer is given.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān entered the mosque after the Maghrib prayer and sat alone, so I sat beside him. He said, "O son of my brother, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever prays the ʿIshāʾ in congregation, it is as if he had stood in prayer for half the night; and whoever prays the Fajr in congregation, it is as if he had prayed the whole night.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ, with this [wording], but he did not mention:
"and he will be thrown on his face into the Fire of Hell."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the best of people in character. Sometimes the time for prayer would arrive while he was in our house, and he would order the mat beneath him to be swept and then sprinkled with water. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would lead, and we would stand behind him, and he would pray with us. Their mat was made of palm fronds.
label: machine translation

segments_en: He entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found him praying on a mat, prostrating upon it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought some wealth or captives, and he distributed it.
He gave some men and left others, then word reached him that those he had left out were displeased.
So he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said, "To proceed:
By Allah, I give one man and leave another,
and the one I leave is dearer to me than the one I give. But I give [to] people because of the anxiety and impatience I see in their hearts,
and I entrust other people to the richness and goodness that Allah has placed in their hearts,
and among them is ʿAmr ibn Taghlib."
By Allah, I would not exchange that statement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for red camels.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up one evening after the prayer,
recited the testimony of faith and praised Allah as He deserves, then said, "To proceed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We used to rejoice on the day of Friday.

We had an old woman who would take some roots of beet greens that we planted in our small irrigation channels, and put them in a pot of hers, and add some grains of barley. I only know that he said there was no fat or grease in it.
When we had prayed the Friday prayer, we would visit her and she would bring it near
to us, so we used to rejoice on Friday for that reason. And we did not eat the midday meal or take the midday nap except after Friday [prayer].
label: machine translation

segments_en: [It is] similar to the statement of Mujāhid: when they are intermingled, [they pray] standing.
Ibn ʿUmar added, from the Prophet ﷺ:
"And if they are more than that, let them pray standing or riding."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the dawn prayer in the darkness, then mounted and said,
"Allah is the Greatest! Khaybar is ruined.
When we descend upon the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned."

They came out running through the streets, saying, "Muḥammad and the khamīs!" He said: the khamīs is the army. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ overcame them, killed the fighters and took the children captive.
Ṣafiyyah fell to Diḥyah al-Kalbī,
then she became [the share] of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He then married her and made her emancipation her dowry.
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said to Thābit, "O Abū Muḥammad,
did you ask Anas what he gave her as dowry?" He said, "He gave her herself as her dowry." And he smiled.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not go out on the day of al-Fiṭr until he had eaten some dates.
Murajjā ibn Rajāʾ said: ʿUbaydullāh narrated to me, he said: Anas narrated to me from the Prophet ﷺ: and he would eat them in an odd number.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray on [the days of] al-Aḍḥā and al-Fiṭr,
then deliver the sermon after the prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with Ibn ʿUmar when the point of a spear struck the arch of his foot,
and his foot became stuck to the stirrup.
I dismounted and pulled it out, and that was at Minā.
Word reached al-Ḥajjāj, so he began to visit him, and al-Ḥajjāj said, "If only we knew who struck you."
Ibn ʿUmar said, "You are the one who struck me."
He said, "How is that?" He said, "You carried weapons on a day when they are not carried,
and you brought weapons into the Sanctuary, though weapons were not brought into the Sanctuary."
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar
used to give the salutation [to end the prayer] between one rakʿah and two rakʿahs in the Witr prayer,
until he would instruct [someone] about some need of his.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Prophet ﷺ raised his head from the last rakʿah, he would say:
"O Allah, save ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah.
O Allah, save Salamah ibn Hishām.
O Allah, save al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd.
O Allah, save the oppressed among the believers.
O Allah, press down Your tread hard upon Muḍar.
O Allah, make it years like the years of Yūsuf."
And the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Ghifār, may Allah forgive them,
and Aslam, may Allah keep them safe."
Ibn Abī al-Zinād said, from his father: All of this was in the dawn prayer.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd Allāh said: This was only because, when Quraysh rebelled against the Prophet ﷺ, he supplicated against them for years like the years of Yūsuf.
So drought and hardship struck them until they ate bones.
A man would look at the sky and see between himself and it something like smoke because of the hardship.

So Allah the Exalted revealed: {Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke * Covering the people; this is a painful punishment.} He said: Then [a man] came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah for rain for Muḍar,
for they have perished." He said,
"For Muḍar? You are indeed bold." So he prayed for rain, and they were given rain.
Then it was revealed: {Indeed, you will return [to disbelief]}. When ease came to them, they returned to their former state when ease had come to them.
So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {On the Day We seize [them] with the greatest seizure, We will take retribution.} He said: That is, the Day of Badr.
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ pitched his tent over a grave, not realizing that it was a grave. Suddenly there was a person in it reciting Sūrah Tabārak alladhī bi-yadihi al-mulk until he completed it. So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I pitched my tent over a grave without realizing it was a grave, and suddenly there was a person in it reciting Sūrat Tabārak al-Mulk until he completed it."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"It is the preventer; it is the saver. It saves him from the punishment of the grave."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ would not sleep until he had recited:
"Alif Lām Mīm. The revelation of..." [Sūrat as-Sajdah] and "Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion" [Sūrat al-Mulk].
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever recites 'When the earth is shaken', it equals for him half of the Qur'an. Whoever recites 'Say: O disbelievers', it equals for him a quarter of the Qur'an. And whoever recites 'Say: He is Allah, the One', it equals for him a third of the Qur'an."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to a man among his Companions:
"Have you married, O so-and-so?"
He said, "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, and I do not have the means to marry." He said:
"Do you not have 'Say: He is Allah, the One'?" He said, "Yes." He said, "That is a third of the Qur'an." He said:
"Do you not have 'When the help of Allah comes and the victory'?" He said, "Yes." He said, "That is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said:
"Do you not have 'Say: O disbelievers'?"
He said, "Yes." He said, "That is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said:
"Do you not have 'When the earth is shaken'?" He said, "Yes." He said, "That is a quarter of the Qur'an. Marry, marry!"
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever recites 'Say: He is Allah, the One' two hundred times every day, the sins of fifty years will be erased for him, unless he has a debt."
And with this chain of narration, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:

"Whoever wants to sleep on his bed and lies down on his right side, then recites 'Say: He is Allah, the One' one hundred times, then on the Day of Resurrection the Lord will say to him: O My servant, enter Paradise on your right."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I passed through the mosque and found the people engrossed in idle talk. So I went in to see ʿAlī and said, "O Commander of the Faithful, do you not see that the people have plunged into idle talk?"
He said, "Have they really done so?" I said, "Yes."
He said, "Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Beware, there will be trials.'
I said, 'What is the way out of them, O Messenger of Allah?' He said:

'The Book of Allah. In it is the account of those before you, the news of what comes after you, and the judgment of what is between you. It is the decisive word, not a jest. Whoever abandons it out of tyranny, Allah will break him; and whoever seeks guidance in other than it, Allah will lead him astray. It is the firm rope of Allah, the wise Reminder, and the straight path. It is that by which desires do not swerve, tongues do not become confused, and scholars are never satiated with it. It does not wear out from much repetition, and its wonders never end. It is that which the jinn did not cease from when they heard it, until they said: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an which guides to the right course, so we believed in it." Whoever speaks by it speaks truthfully, whoever acts by it is rewarded, whoever judges by it is just, and whoever calls to it is guided to a straight path.'"
Take it to yourself, O one-eyed one.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever recites a letter from the Book of Allah will have a good deed for it, and a good deed is multiplied tenfold. I do not say that 'Alif Lām Mīm' is one letter, but Alif is a letter, Lām is a letter, and Mīm is a letter."

This hadith is also narrated through another route from Ibn Masʿūd. Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated it from Ibn Masʿūd; some of them traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ and some of them made it a statement of Ibn Masʿūd.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Allah has not permitted a servant anything better than two rakʿahs that he prays. Indeed, righteousness is poured over the head of the servant as long as he is in his prayer. And the servants do not draw near to Allah with anything like that which came out from Him."
Abū an-Naḍr said, "That is, the Qur'an."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"You will never return to Allah with anything better than that which came out from Him." That is, the Qur'an.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Indeed, one who has nothing of the Qur'an in his heart is like a ruined house."
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Ask Allah for His bounty, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loves to be asked, and the best act of worship is awaiting relief."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The closest that the Lord is to the servant is in the depth of the last part of the night. So if you are able to be among those who remember Allah at that hour, then be so."
He said: This is a hadith that is ḥasan, ṣaḥīḥ, gharīb from this route.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'My servant, the true servant of Mine, is the one who remembers Me while he is meeting his opponent.'"
That is, during battle.
He said: This is a gharīb hadith; we do not know it except from this route, and its chain is not strong.
And we do not know of any narration from the Prophet ﷺ by ʿUmārah ibn Zaʿkarah except this one hadith.
As for the meaning of his saying, "while he is meeting his opponent,"
it only means during battle, that is, that he remembers Allah at that hour.
label: machine translation

segments_en: No angel rises from the earth except that he says: There is no might and no power except with Allah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I bear witness that I heard Abū Saʿīd narrate, adding to it:
"As you see a setting star on the eastern and western horizon."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"No one will enter Paradise except that he is shown his seat in the Fire, had he done evil, so that he may increase in gratitude;
and no one will enter the Fire except that he is shown his seat in Paradise, had he done good,
so that it may be a source of regret for him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: "This is for you, and ten times the like of it."
Abū Hurayrah said: I memorized "the like of it with it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He used to narrate about the Companions of the Prophet
ﷺ, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Men from my Companions will come to me at the Pond, and they will be driven away from it. I will say: 'My Lord, my Companions!'
He will say: 'You have no knowledge of what they introduced after you.
They turned back on their heels, retreating.'"
Shuʿayb said, from al-Zuhrī: Abū Hurayrah used to narrate from the Prophet ﷺ, "fa-yujallawn."
ʿUqayl said: "fa-yuḥalliʾūn."
Al-Zubaydī said, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr said: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"My Pond is a month's journey across;
its water is whiter than milk,
its fragrance is better than musk,
and its cups are like the stars of the sky;
whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty again."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Sahl said: I said, "Yes."
He said: I bear witness about Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that I heard him adding to it:
"I will say: 'They are of me.'
It will be said: 'You do not know what they introduced after you.'
I will say: 'Away, away with whoever changed [things] after me!'"
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Suḥqan means "far away."
It is said "saḥīq" means far; and "asḥaqahu" means he removed it far away.
label: machine translation

segments_en: While I was standing, there was a group,
and when I recognized them, a man came out from between me and them and said: 'Come along.'
I said: 'Where to?' He said: 'To the Fire, by Allah.'
I said: 'What is their matter?' He said: 'They turned back after you on their heels, retreating.'
Then there was another group, and when I recognized them, a man came out from between me and them and said: 'Come along.'
I said: 'Where to?' He said: 'To the Fire, by Allah.'
I said: 'What is their matter?' He said: 'They turned back after you on their heels, retreating.'
And I do not see any of them escaping except like stray camels."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not swear by your fathers."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh, from the account
of ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, when the people of the slander said about her what they said, and Allah cleared her,
each of them narrated to me a portion of the account: The Prophet ﷺ stood and asked to be excused regarding ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy,
then Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr stood and said to Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah: By the life of Allah, we will surely kill him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: She said: It was revealed concerning [a person's saying] "No,
by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: and ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn ʿUtbah, from the account
of ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, when the people of the slander said about her what they said,

and Allah cleared her of what they said, each of them narrated to me a portion of the account: Then Allah revealed {Indeed, those who came with the slander}, the ten verses, all of them about my innocence.
Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, who used to spend on Misṭaḥ because of his kinship to him, said: By Allah, I will never spend anything on Misṭaḥ again,
after what he said about ʿĀʾishah.
So Allah revealed {And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give to their relatives} the verse.
Abū Bakr said: Yes, by Allah, I love that Allah forgive me.
So he returned to Misṭaḥ the spending he used to give him and said: By Allah, I will never take it away from him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When death came to Abū Ṭālib, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and said:
"Say: There is no god but Allah, a word
with which I can plead for you before Allah."
label: machine translation

segments_en: He vowed that no day
would come upon him except that he would fast it,
and it coincided with the day of Aḍḥā or Fiṭr.
He said: "There is indeed in the Messenger of Allah a good example for you."
He did not fast on the day of Aḍḥā and Fiṭr,
and he did not consider fasting them [permissible].
label: machine translation

segments_en: and others,
from our brothers, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī,
from Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Namir,
that he heard Anas ibn Mālik

say: While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the mosque, a man entered riding a camel. He made it kneel in the mosque, then tied it, and then said, "Which of you is Muhammad?"—while the Prophet ﷺ was reclining among them. We said to him, "This fair-complexioned man who is reclining." The man said to him, "O son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "I have answered you."
The man said, "O Muhammad, I am going to ask you, and I will be harsh in questioning you." He said,
"Ask whatever you wish."
He said, "I ask you by your Lord and the Lord of those before you: did Allah send you to all the people?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "By Allah, yes."
He said, "Then I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you to fast this month of the year?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "By Allah, yes."
He said, "Then I ask you by Allah: did Allah command you to take this charity (ṣadaqah) from our rich and distribute it among our poor?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "By Allah, yes."
The man said, "I believe in what you have brought, and I am the messenger of those of my people who are behind me. I am Ḍimām ibn Thaʿlabah, of the Banū Saʿd ibn Bakr."
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar differed with him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I will narrate to you a hadith that no one will narrate to you after me.
I heard it from the Prophet ﷺ; I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:

"The Hour will not come"—or he said, "Among the signs of the Hour are that knowledge will be taken away and ignorance will appear, wine will be drunk, fornication will appear, men will become few and women will become many,
until there will be one man to take care of fifty women."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I read to Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb,
from ʿĪsā ibn
Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ,

who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped at Minā during the Farewell Pilgrimage for the people to ask him questions. A man came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I did not realize, and I shaved my head before sacrificing." He said,
"Sacrifice, and there is no harm."
Then another man came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I did not realize, and I sacrificed before casting the pebbles." He said,
"Cast, and there is no harm."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not asked about anything done earlier or later except that he said,
"Do it, and there is no harm."
label: machine translation

segments_en: "Time will draw closer, deeds will diminish, miserliness will be cast [into hearts], trials will appear, and harj will increase."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is it?" He said, "Killing, killing."
Shuʿayb, Yūnus, al-Layth, and the son of al-Zuhrī's brother said, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥumayd,
from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿUqbah [said]: But I remember the hadith of ʿUbayd better. He said: I married a woman,
and a black woman came to us and said, "I nursed both of you."
So I went to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "I married so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so, and a black woman came to us and told me, 'I nursed both of you.'"
But she was lying. So he turned away from me,
and I came to him from the front of his face
and said, "She is lying." He said,
"What can be done, when she has claimed that she nursed both of you? Leave her."
And Ismāʿīl pointed with his two fingers, the index and the middle finger, narrating from Ayyūb.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Any man who has a slave girl, and teaches her and teaches her well,
and disciplines her and disciplines her well,
then frees her and marries her, will have a double reward.
And any man from the People of the Book who believes in his prophet and believes in me will have a double reward.
And any slave who fulfills the right of his masters and the right of his Lord will have a double reward."
Al-Shaʿbī said: Take it without anything [in return]; a man used to travel to Medina for less than this.
And Abū Bakr said, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Abū Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ:
"Free her, then give her a dowry."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I passed by and found Abū Jahl lying struck down, his leg cut off. I said, "O enemy of Allah, O Abū Jahl! Allah has disgraced the other one."
He said: And at that moment I did not fear him.

He said, "Is there anyone further removed [from honor] than a man whose own people killed him?" Then I struck him with a sword that was of no use, and it did nothing for me until his sword fell from his hand, so I struck him with it until he was dead.
label: machine translation

segments_en: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ obtained war booty, he would order Bilāl to announce it among the people, and they would bring their spoils. He would take the fifth and distribute the rest. Afterwards a man came with a halter made of hair and said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is from the booty we took." He said, "
Did you hear Bilāl announcing it?" three times. He said, "Yes." He said, "
Then what prevented you from bringing it?"
So he made an excuse to him, and he said, "
You be the one to bring it on the Day of Resurrection, for I will never accept it from you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We went on a campaign with al-Walīd ibn Hishām, and with us were Sālim ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. A man stole some of the spoils, so al-Walīd ordered that his belongings be burned, and he was paraded around, and he was not given his share.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar burned the belongings of one who stole from the spoils, and they beat him.
label: machine translation

segments_en: To proceed: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say, "
Whoever conceals a thief of the spoils is like him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on that day, meaning the day of Ḥunayn, "
Whoever kills a disbeliever, his belongings are his."

On that day Abū Ṭalḥah killed twenty men and took their belongings. Abū Ṭalḥah met Umm Sulaym, who had a dagger with her, and he said, "O Umm Sulaym, what is this with you?" She said, "By Allah, I intended, if any of them came near me, to rip open his belly with it."
Abū Ṭalḥah informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of that.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Thawr about this hadith,
and he narrated to me from Khālid ibn Maʿdān,
from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father,
from ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī, similarly.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the slain man's belongings go to the killer, and he did not take the fifth from those belongings.
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Badr the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted me as an extra award the sword of Abū Jahl, whom he had killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, meaning on the day of Badr, and said, "
ʿUthmān has gone off on a task for Allah and a task for His Messenger, and I pledge allegiance on his behalf."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ allotted him a share, and he allotted none to anyone else who was absent.
label: machine translation

segments_en: and such and such, and he mentioned
things, and about the slave,
whether he has any share in the spoils, and about the women,

whether they used to go out with the Prophet ﷺ and whether they had a share. Ibn ʿAbbās said, "Were it not that he would fall into foolishness, I would not have written to him. As for the slave, he would be given a small gift. As for the women, they used to treat the wounded and give water to drink."
label: machine translation

segments_en: She went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the expedition of Khaybar as the sixth of six women. News of this reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he sent for us and we came, and we saw anger in him. He said, "
With whom did you go out, and with whose permission did you go out?"

We said, "O Messenger of Allah, we went out to spin hair and to assist with it in the cause of Allah. We have medicine for the wounded, we hand out arrows, and we serve barley meal." He said, "Stay [then]."
Until, when Allah gave him victory at Khaybar, he gave us a share just as he gave a share to the men.
He said: I said to her, "Grandmother, what was that?" She said, "Dates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: On the day of Badr I used to draw water for my companions.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, four men with a horse among us. He gave each person among us one share and gave the horse two shares.
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were present at al-Ḥudaybiyah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When we left it, the people were urging on their camels, and some of the people said to others, "What is wrong with the people?" They said, "Revelation has come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

So we went out with the people, hurrying, and we found the Prophet ﷺ standing on his mount at Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm. When the people had gathered around him, he recited to them: {Indeed, We have given you a clear victory}. A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, is it a victory?" He said, "
Yes, by the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, it is indeed a victory."

Then Khaybar was divided among the people of al-Ḥudaybiyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided it into eighteen shares. The army was one thousand five hundred, among them three hundred horsemen. He gave the horseman two shares and the foot soldier one share.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim, and it is not lawful for a Muslim who sells his brother a defective item to sell it without making the defect clear to him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever sells a defective item without making the defect clear remains in the displeasure of Allah, and the angels continue to curse him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: When captives were brought to the Prophet ﷺ, he would give them to the members of a household all together, disliking that they be separated from one another.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who separates a mother from her child, or a brother from his brother.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Silver for silver, gold for gold, barley for barley, and wheat for wheat, like for like."

segments_en: He had retracted that [view], so I met him in Makkah and said, "It has reached me that you retracted."
He said, "Yes. That was only an opinion of mine, and this is Abū Saʿīd, who narrates from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he forbade currency exchange [with unequal amounts]."

segments_en: I used to sell camels, and I would take gold for silver and silver for gold, and dinars for dirhams and dirhams for dinars.
So I asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
"If you take one of them and give the other, do not part from your companion while anything remains unsettled between you and him."

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ bought Ṣafiyyah for seven heads [of slaves].
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said, "From Diḥyah al-Kalbī."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I came upon a people whose bellies were like houses, with snakes inside them that could be seen from outside their bellies. I said, 'Who are these, Jibrīl?' He said, 'These are those who consume usury.'"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Usury has seventy degrees of sin, the least of which is that a man marries his own mother."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Usury has seventy-three categories."
label: machine translation

segments_en: No one gains much through usury except that the end result of his affairs is scarcity."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "The people of so-and-so," referring to a group of Jews, "have become Muslims, and they have become hungry, and I fear they may apostatize." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Does anyone have anything?"
A man from among the Jews said, "I have such-and-such," naming something, and I think he said three hundred dinars, "at the price of such-and-such, from the orchard of so-and-so."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"At the price of such-and-such, for such-and-such a term, and not from the orchard of so-and-so."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when a Bedouin said, "Repay me my young camel."
So he gave him an older camel, and the Bedouin said, "Messenger of Allah, this is older than my camel."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The best of people are those best in repaying."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [He said] to the Prophet ﷺ, "You were my partner in the pre-Islamic period, and you were the best of partners: you did not try to placate me, and you did not argue with me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"There are three things in which there is blessing: sale on deferred payment, partnership in investment, and mixing wheat with barley for the household, not for sale."
label: machine translation

segments_en: If you come upon a shepherd, call him three times. If he answers you, [well and good]; otherwise drink, without causing damage. And if you come upon the wall of an orchard, call the owner of the orchard three times. If he answers you, [well and good]; otherwise eat, without causing damage."
label: machine translation

segments_en: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, we saw camels tied up with the thorny branches of trees, and we rushed toward them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called us, so we returned to him, and he said:

"These camels belong to a household of Muslims; they are their sustenance and, after Allah, their source of blessing. Would it please you if you returned to your provision bags and found what was in them gone? Would you consider that just?" They said, "No." He said:
"Then this is the same."
We said, "What if we need food and drink?" He said:
"Eat, but do not carry away; drink, but do not carry away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said to her:
"Keep sheep, for there is blessing in them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: May Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"The sheep is among the animals of Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Concerning the saying of the Exalted, {The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger...} [al-Māʾidah 5:33], the verse: He said, "This verse was revealed about the polytheists. Whoever among them repents before he is overpowered, there is no way against him. This verse is not for the Muslim man: whoever kills and spreads corruption in the land and wages war against Allah and His Messenger, then joins the disbelievers before he is overpowered, that does not prevent the prescribed punishment from being applied to him for what he committed."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:
"When a slave runs away, no prayer of his is accepted, and if he dies, he dies a disbeliever."
A slave of Jarīr ran away, so [Jarīr] seized him and struck off his neck.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Any slave who runs away from his masters and joins the enemy has made himself lawful to be killed.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever changes his religion, kill him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ sent him to Yemen, and after that sent Muʿādh ibn Jabal. When [Muʿādh] arrived, he said, "O people, I am the envoy of the Messenger of Allah to you."

Abū Mūsā laid down a cushion for him to sit on. Then a man was brought who had been a Jew, then became Muslim, then disbelieved again. Muʿādh said, "I will not sit until he is killed; this is the judgment of Allah and His Messenger," three times.
When he was killed, he sat down.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of the Anṣār became Muslim, then apostatized and joined the polytheists, then regretted it. He sent word to his people: "Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me whether I have any repentance." His people came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "So-and-so has regretted it, and he told us to ask you whether he has any repentance." Then was revealed: {How shall Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief...} up to His saying {Forgiving, Merciful}.
So he sent for him, and he became Muslim.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man spoke harshly to Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq. I said, "Shall I kill him?" He rebuked me and said, "This is not for anyone after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Bakr became angry at a man, and [another] said, "If you had ordered me, I would have done it."
He said, "By Allah, that was not for any human being after Muḥammad ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I came upon Abū Bakr when he had spoken harshly to a man and the man had answered him back. I said, "Shall I not strike off his neck?" and he rebuked me.
Then he said, "That is not for anyone after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever ties a knot and then blows into it has practiced sorcery, and whoever practices sorcery has associated partners with Allah, and whoever attaches himself to something is left to it."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man of the Jews bewitched the Prophet ﷺ, and he was ill from it for some days. Then Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came to him and said, "A man of the Jews has bewitched you; he tied knots for you in such-and-such a well." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent [people] and they took them out and brought them. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose as if he had been released from a bond. He never mentioned it to that Jewish man, nor did he ever show it in his face.
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [Another chain:] And ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī informed me, he said: Khalaf ibn Tamīm narrated to us, he said: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, he said: Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from Qābūs ibn Mukhāriq, from his father. He said: I heard Sufyān ath-Thawrī narrating this hadith: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "A man comes to me wanting my property." He said, "Remind him of Allah."
He said, "And if he does not take heed?" He said:
"Seek help against him from the Muslims around you."
He said, "And if there are no Muslims around me?" He said:
"Seek help against him from the ruler."
He said, "And if the ruler is far from me?" He said:
"Fight for your property until you are among the martyrs of the Hereafter, or you protect your property."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man
came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if someone attacks my property?" He said, "Plead with him in the name of Allah."
He said, "And if they refuse me?" He said, "Plead with him in the name of Allah."
He said, "And if they refuse me?" He said, "Plead with him in the name of Allah."
He said, "And if they refuse me?" He said:
"Then fight. If you are killed, you will be in Paradise, and if you kill, he will be in the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever is killed unjustly defending his property, his is Paradise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever draws his sword and then lays it down, his blood is forfeit."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With a meaning similar to the hadith of Hishām, and with its chain of narration.
And the wording of the hadith of Hishām, Shaybān, and Muʿāwiyah ibn Sallām agrees in this hadith.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf
married a woman for the weight of a date-stone in gold, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
"Hold a wedding feast, even if with a single sheep."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ṣafiyyah fell to Diḥyah as his share, and they began to praise her in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: They were saying, "We have not seen the like of her among the captives." He said: So he sent for Diḥyah and gave him what he wanted for her. Then he handed her over to my mother and said, "Prepare her."
He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Khaybar, until, when he had put it behind him, he stopped and pitched a tent over her. When morning came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has any surplus provisions, let him bring them to us."

He said: So a man began to come with surplus dates and another with surplus barley flour, until they made a heap of it, a ḥays. They began to eat from that ḥays and to drink from basins beside them filled with rain water. Anas said: That was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for her. He said: Then we set out, and when we saw the walls of Madinah, we were delighted to see it, so we urged our mounts on, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ urged his mount on. He said: Ṣafiyyah was behind him, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seated her behind him. He said: Then the mount of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stumbled, and he fell and she fell. He said: None of the people looked at him or at her until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and covered her. He said: We came to him and he said, "We are not hurt."
He said: Then we entered Madinah, and the young women of his wives came out to look at her and gloated over her fall.
label: machine translation

segments_en: This is the hadith of Bahz. He said: When the waiting period of Zaynab had ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd, "Mention me to her."

He said: So Zayd went until he came to her while she was kneading her dough. He said: When I saw her, she became so great in my chest that I could not look at her, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mentioned her. So I turned my back to her and stepped back on my heels, and said, "O Zaynab, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has sent me to mention you."
She said, "I will not do anything until I consult my Lord."

So she stood in her place of prayer, and the Qurʾān was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered upon her without permission. He said: I remember that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fed us bread and meat when the day had grown long. The people left, while some men remained in the house talking after the meal. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and I followed him. He went around to the rooms of his wives, greeting them with peace, and they said, "O Messenger of Allah, how did you find your family?" He said: I do not know whether I told him that the people had left or he told me. He said: Then he went on until he entered the house, and I went to enter with him, but he let the curtain fall between me and him, and the verse of the veil was revealed. He said: And the people were admonished with what they were admonished.
Ibn Rāfiʿ added in his hadith: {Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission for a meal, without waiting for its time} up to His words: {And Allah is not shy of the truth}.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ said:
"If you are invited to a trotter, respond."
label: machine translation

segments_en: A man divorced his wife three times, then another man married her and divorced her before consummating the marriage. Her first husband wanted to marry her again, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about that, and he said:
"No, not until the other has tasted her sweetness as the first had tasted."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is my soul, there is no man who calls his wife to his bed and she refuses him, except that the One who is in the heaven is displeased with her until he is pleased with her."
label: machine translation

segments_en: With the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Bishr, meaning the hadith about withdrawal (ʿazl). He said, "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Bishr narrated it to me."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We said to Abū Saʿīd, "Did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention anything about withdrawal?" He said, "Yes."
And he related the hadith with a meaning similar to the hadith of Ibn ʿAwn, up to the words "destiny."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about withdrawal, and he said:
"Not all water produces a child, and when Allah wills to create something, nothing can prevent Him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and he was fasting.
When the sun had set, he said to one of the men:
"O so-and-so, get up and mix [the drink] for us."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would wait until evening." He said, "Get down and mix [the drink] for us."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, if only you would wait until evening." He said, "Get down and mix [the drink] for us."
He said, "There is still daylight upon you." He said, "Get down and mix [the drink] for us."
So he got down and mixed [the drink] for them,
and the Prophet ﷺ drank, then said:
"When you see the night approaching from over there,
then the fasting person has broken his fast."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Prophet ﷺ set out from Madinah in Ramadan,
with ten thousand men,
and that was at the beginning of the eighth year and a half after his arrival in Madinah.
He and the Muslims with him travelled to Makkah,
he fasting and they fasting, until he reached al-Kadīd, a watering place between ʿUsfān and Qudayd, [where] he broke his fast and they broke their fast.
Az-Zuhrī said: The latest command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is what is followed, then the one after it.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever dies owing fasts, his guardian should fast on his behalf."
label: machine translation

segments_en: We broke our fast one day in Ramadan on a cloudy day during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and then the sun appeared. Abū Usāmah said: I asked Hishām, "Were they commanded to make up the fast?" He said, "Is there any way around that?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: It reached the Prophet ﷺ that I was fasting continuously and praying through the night. Either he sent for me or I met him, and he said:

"Was I not told that you fast and do not break your fast, and that you pray through the night? Do not do so, for your eyes have a right over you, your self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you.
Fast and break your fast, pray and sleep, and fast one day out of every ten days, and you will have the reward of nine."
He said, "I find myself stronger than that, O Prophet of Allah." He said:
"Then fast the fast of Dāwūd, peace be upon him."
He said, "And how did Dāwūd fast, O Prophet of Allah?" He said:
"He would fast one day and break his fast the next, and he would not flee when he met [the enemy]."
He said, "Who will grant me [the ability for] this, O Prophet of Allah?" ʿAṭāʾ said: I do not know how perpetual fasting came to be mentioned. Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no fast for one who fasts perpetually; there is no fast for one who fasts perpetually; there is no fast for one who fasts perpetually."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:

"O ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, you fast all the time and pray through the night, and if you do that, your eyes sink in and your self becomes exhausted. There is no fast for one who fasts perpetually. Fasting three days of the month is [like] fasting the whole of time."
I said, "I am able to do more than that." He said:
"Fast the fast of Dāwūd: he would fast one day and break his fast the next, and he would not flee when he met [the enemy]."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered with your father Zayd upon ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, and he related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was told about my fasting, so he came in to see me. I threw him a small leather cushion stuffed with palm fibre, but he sat on the ground and the cushion was between him and me. He said:
"Is it not enough for you to fast three days of each month?"
I said, "O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Five."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Seven."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Nine."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah." He said, "Eleven."
I said, "O Messenger of Allah." Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
"There is no fasting greater than the fast of Dāwūd: half of time, fasting one day and breaking the fast the next."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ:
that he asked him, or asked a man while ʿImrān was listening, and said:
"O Abū so-and-so, did you not fast the last days of this month?"
He said: I think he meant Ramadan.
The man said, "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said:
"Then when you have broken your fast, fast two days."
Aṣ-Ṣalt did not say, "I think he meant Ramadan."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh while I was circumambulating the House:
Did the Prophet ﷺ forbid fasting on Friday? He said:
Yes, by the Lord of this House.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked the Mother of the Believers, ʿĀʾishah. I said, "O Mother of the Believers, how was the practice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Did he single out any particular days?" She said, "No.
His practice was constant, and which of you is able to do what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was able to do?"
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say when he went to his bed:

"Praise be to Allah, who sufficed me, gave me shelter, fed me and gave me drink; who has been gracious to me and bestowed favor, who has given me and been generous. Praise be to Allah in every circumstance. O Allah, Lord of everything and its Sovereign, and God of everything, I seek refuge in You from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Narrated] by ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he woke up during the night, would say:

"There is no god but You. Glory be to You, O Allah. I seek Your forgiveness for my sin, and I ask You for Your mercy. O Allah, increase me in knowledge, and do not let my heart deviate after You have guided me, and grant me mercy from Yourself. Truly, You are the Bestower."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Prophet ﷺ with this report, in which ʿAlī said: "I have not abandoned them since I heard them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, except on the night of Ṣiffīn, for I remembered them at the end of the night and said them."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever says, when he enters the morning or the evening: 'O Allah, I have entered the morning bearing witness to You, and I call as witnesses the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all Your creation, that You are Allah, there is no god but You, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger,' Allah will free a quarter of him from the Fire. Whoever says it twice, Allah will free half of him. Whoever says it three times, Allah will free three quarters of him. And if he says it four times, Allah will free him from the Fire."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever says when he enters the morning: 'O Allah, whatever blessing has come to me this morning is from You alone, You have no partner; so to You is the praise and to You is the thanks,'
he has fulfilled his thanks for that day. And whoever says the like of that when he enters the evening, he has fulfilled his thanks for that night."
label: machine translation

segments_en: One of the daughters of the Prophet ﷺ who served [him] reported that a daughter of the Prophet,
ﷺ, told her that the Prophet ﷺ used to teach her, saying:

"Say when you enter the morning: 'Glory be to Allah and with His praise; there is no power except with Allah; what Allah wills happens, and what He does not will does not happen. I know that Allah has power over all things, and that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge.' For whoever says these when he enters the morning will be protected until the evening, and whoever says them when he enters the evening will be protected until the morning."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said:

"Whoever says when he enters the morning: {So glory be to Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. And to Him is all praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you are at noon} up to {and thus will you be brought out,} he will attain what he missed that day. And whoever says them when he enters the evening will attain what he missed that night."
Ar-Rabīʿ said, from al-Layth:
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he confided to him and said:
"When you finish the sunset prayer, say: 'O Allah, protect me from the Fire,'

seven times. For if you say that and then die during your night, protection from it will be recorded for you. And when you pray the morning prayer, say likewise, for if you die during your day, protection from it will be recorded for you."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Whoever says, when he enters the morning and when he enters the evening, "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne," seven times, Allah will suffice him in whatever concerns him, whether he was sincere in it or not.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and asked her, "With what did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ begin when he got up during the night?" She said, "You have asked me about something no one has asked me before you. When he got up during the night, he would say 'Allāhu akbar' ten times, say 'Praise be to Allah' ten times, and say:
'Glory be to Allah and with His praise,' ten times, and say:
'Glory be to the Sovereign, the Most Holy,'
ten times. He would seek forgiveness ten times and say 'There is no god but Allah' ten times. Then he would say:
'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of this world and the hardship of the Day of Resurrection,'
ten times. Then he would begin the prayer."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Abū Dharr used to say: Whoever says when he enters the morning: "O Allah, whatever oath I have sworn, or word I have spoken, or vow I have made, Your will is before all of that; what You will happens, and what You do not will does not happen. O Allah, forgive me and overlook it for me. O Allah, whomever I have invoked blessings upon, then upon him be my blessing, and whomever I have cursed, then upon him be my curse," he will be covered by an exception for that day, or he said: that day.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate in prayer, saying:
"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sin and from debt."
Someone said to him, "How often you seek refuge from debt, O Messenger of Allah!" He said:
"When a man falls into debt, he speaks and lies, and he promises and breaks his promise."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned some hadith, among them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By Allah, I return to my family and find a date fallen on my bed—or in my house—and I pick it up to eat it, then I fear that it may be charity—or from charity—so I throw it away."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Whoever has wronged another person in regard to his honor or anything else, let him seek his forgiveness today,
before the time comes when there will be neither dinar nor dirham.
If he has righteous deeds, they will be taken from him in proportion to his wrongdoing,
and if he has no good deeds, some of the evil deeds of his opponent will be taken and laden upon him."
label: machine translation

segments_en: [Regarding the verse] "And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or turning away", she said: This is the woman who is with a man,
who does not find much in her to like, so he wants to divorce her and marry another.
She says to him: Keep me and do not divorce me,
and then marry someone else;
you are free of any obligation to spend on me and of any share of your time due to me.
That is the saying of the Exalted: "There is no blame on them if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best."
label: machine translation

segments_en: Arwā bint Uways
claimed against Saʿīd ibn Zayd that he had taken some of her land, and she brought her dispute with him to Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam.

Saʿīd said, "Would I take any of her land after what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He asked, "And what did you hear from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
'Whoever takes a handspan of land unjustly, it will be hung around his neck down through seven earths.'"
Marwān said to him, "I will not ask you for any proof after this."
Saʿīd said, "O Allah, if she is lying, blind her sight and kill her on her land."
[The narrator] said: She did not die until she lost her sight, and then, while she was walking on her land, she fell into a pit and died.
label: machine translation

segments_en: Ibn al-Zubayr used to provide us with dates. [The narrator] said: People were in hardship at that time. We were eating, and Ibn ʿUmar passed by us while we were eating and said, "Do not eat two dates together, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade eating two at a time, unless a man asks permission of his brother."
Shuʿbah said: I think this phrase [about permission] is only from the words of Ibn ʿUmar. He means the asking of permission.
label: machine translation

segments_en: ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: Hind bint ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah came
and said, "O Messenger of Allah, Abū Sufyān is a stingy man.
Is there any blame on me if I feed our household from what belongs to him?" He said:
"There is no blame on you if you feed them in a reasonable manner."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I was serving drink to the people on the day when wine was prohibited, in the house of Abū Ṭalḥah, and their drink was only fadīkh, [made from] unripe dates and ripe dates.

Then a caller was calling out. He said, "Go out and see." I went out, and there was a caller announcing: "Indeed, wine has been prohibited!" He said: It flowed in the streets of Madinah. Abū Ṭalḥah said to me, "Go out and pour it out."

So I poured it out. They said—or some of them said—"So-and-so was killed, so-and-so was killed, while it was in their stomachs." [The narrator] said: I do not know whether this is from the hadith of Anas. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "There is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten, when they are mindful of Allah and believe and do righteous deeds."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I entered upon him and he handed me some perfume.
He said: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, would not refuse perfume.
He said: And Anas claimed that the Prophet ﷺ would not refuse perfume.
label: machine translation

segments_en: I sold a camel to the Prophet ﷺ on a journey.
When we came to Madinah, he said:
"Go to the mosque and pray two rakʿahs."
Then he weighed [the price]—Shuʿbah said: I think [he said] he weighed it out for me and gave extra—
and some of it remained with me until the people of Syria seized it on the day of al-Ḥarrah.
label: machine translation

segments_en: The delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays
said, "O Messenger of Allah, in what should we drink?" He said:
"Do not drink in gourds, nor in tarred jars, nor in hollowed palm-trunks, but make nabīdh in waterskins."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, and if it becomes strong in the waterskins?" He said:
"Then pour water over it."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah."
Then, on the third or fourth time, he said to them, "Pour it out." Then he said:
"Indeed Allah has forbidden to me—or: has forbidden—wine, gambling, and the kūbah." He said:
"And every intoxicant is forbidden."
Sufyān said: I asked ʿAlī ibn Badhīmah about the kūbah, and he said, "The drum."
label: machine translation

segments_en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the containers: gourds, green jars, tarred jars, and hollowed palm-trunks. A Bedouin said, "We have no [other] vessels." So he said:
"Drink what is lawful."
label: machine translation

segments_en: I asked Umm Salamah what the Prophet ﷺ used to forbid. She said, "He used to forbid us from soaking date pits by boiling them, or from mixing raisins and dates."
label: machine translation

segments_en: From the Banū Asad, from ʿĀʾishah,
may Allah be pleased with her: Raisins would be soaked for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and she would put dates into it, and dates [would be soaked] and she would put raisins into it.
label: machine translation
